   > How: Press R on the Coke Oven in JEI or open the MI guidebook to see the 3D layout: a 3x3x3 cube of brick blocks with the controller in one face. Swap wall bricks for hatches: item in, item out, steam in, and a fluid output for creosote.
   > Tip: Pipe steam from your boiler into the fluid input hatch. Click the checkmark once the controller shows it's formed.
5. **A Way Out for Tar**: `modern_industrialization:bronze_fluid_output_hatch` *(after: Hatches)*
   > What: Coking coal also drives out a liquid. Without a fluid output hatch it has nowhere to go.
   > Chemistry: The volatile part of coal leaves as gas and condenses into tar as it cools. Real coke works collect it, because coal tar is a feedstock, not waste.
   > How: A bronze machine casing on top of a bronze tank. Swap one wall brick of the Coke Oven for it.
   > Tip: Pipe it straight into a tank or a boiler so it never fills up.
6. **Coke**: 16x `modern_industrialization:coke` *(after: Build the Coke Oven)*
   > What: Coke is exactly what a blast furnace needs: strong, porous, nearly pure carbon.
   > Chemistry: With the hydrogen, sulfur and tars baked out, what's left is a carbon skeleton that burns hot and clean.
   > How: Feed coal into the item input hatch. Each coal becomes 1 coke in 30 seconds.
   > Tip: Coal dust works too and comes out as coke dust, which saves a grinding step later.
7. **Byproduct: Creosote**: `modern_industrialization:creosote_bucket` *(after: Build the Coke Oven, A Way Out for Tar)*
   > What: Half the time, coking a coal also yields 500 mB of creosote. Nothing is wasted in chemistry: creosote is a boiler fuel.
   > Chemistry: Coal-tar creosote is a mix of phenols, cresols and ring-shaped hydrocarbons, the same family of compounds that makes tar smell the way it does.
   > How: Pipe it out of the fluid output hatch into a tank, or straight into a boiler.
8. **Lubricant**: `modern_industrialization:lubricant_bucket` *(after: Byproduct: Creosote)*
   > What: The Steam Cutting Machine needs lubricant as cutting fluid. Now you can finally run it.
   > How: In the Steam Mixer, 500 mB of creosote and 1 redstone make 500 mB of lubricant.
   > Tip: Each cut uses only 1 mB, so one bucket lasts a very long time. The Cutting Machine now makes your steel rods and bolts.
9. **Coke Dust**: 4x `modern_industrialization:coke_dust` *(after: Coke)*
   > What: Steel is mixed as dust, so the carbon has to be a powder too.
   > Chemistry: Coke is the reducing agent in a real blast furnace: it pulls oxygen out of iron ore and supplies the carbon that becomes steel.
   > How: Grind coke in the Steam Macerator, or coke coal dust directly in the Coke Oven.
10. **Iron Dust**: 14x `modern_industrialization:iron_dust` *(after: Coke Dust)*
   > What: The other ingredient of steel.
   > How: Grind iron ingots in the Steam Macerator or the Forge Hammer (1 ingot makes 1 dust).
   > Tip: Macerating iron ore gives 2 raw iron per ore, which smelts into more ingots than mining alone.
11. **Uncooked Steel**: 7x `modern_industrialization:uncooked_steel_dust` *(after: Iron Dust)*
   > What: A blend of iron and carbon, ready for the blast furnace.
   > Chemistry: Real steel holds far less carbon than this mix suggests, but the idea is right: carbon is the ingredient that turns soft iron into steel.
   > How: Craft 7 iron dust with 2 coke dust to get 7 uncooked steel dust.
12. **Blast Furnace Materials**: 32x `modern_industrialization:fire_clay_bricks`; `minecraft:blast_furnace` *(after: Coke)*
   > What: The Steam Blast Furnace is a tower of fire clay bricks, hotter than anything you've built.
   > How: Make fire clay bricks as in Chapter I (the Steam Macerator grinds bricks into brick dust now). A vanilla blast furnace is 5 iron, a furnace and 3 smooth stone.
   > Tip: Automate it: macerator → crafting → steam furnace. You'll want a lot of these.
13. **The Steam Blast Furnace**: `modern_industrialization:steam_blast_furnace` *(after: Blast Furnace Materials)*
   > What: A multiblock that gets hot enough to melt iron and dissolve carbon into it.
   > How: Craft the controller from 8 fire clay brick blocks around a blast furnace. Check the structure in JEI: a 3x3 tower, four blocks tall, with bronze hatches for items and steam.
   > Tip: Some later recipes in this furnace need a steel hatch. Steel itself only needs bronze ones.
14. **Steel**: 16x `modern_industrialization:steel_ingot` *(after: The Steam Blast Furnace, Uncooked Steel)*
   > Iron that bends without breaking. You once forged weapons for gods out of something very like this.
   > What: Iron with a small, controlled amount of carbon (about 0.2-2%) is steel: strong, tough, and the backbone of every machine to come.
   > Chemistry: Carbon atoms sit in the gaps between iron atoms and stop the layers sliding. Too much carbon and you get brittle cast iron. Chemistry is about the right ratio.
   > How: Put uncooked steel dust in the blast furnace's item input hatch. Each dust becomes 1 steel ingot in 30 seconds.
15. **Steel Paxel**: `mekanismtools:steel_paxel` *(after: Steel)*
   > What: Mekanism's steel tools are diamond tier: a steel paxel mines obsidian, which the Combiner needs, and lasts far longer than iron.
   > Chemistry: A little carbon in iron makes it much harder: carbon atoms in the gaps of the iron lattice pin it so the layers can't slip.
   > How: A steel pickaxe, axe and shovel with 2 sticks (check JEI).
   > Tip: No diamonds needed for obsidian now. Save your diamonds for the Combiner itself.
16. **Steel Boiler**: `modern_industrialization:steel_boiler` *(after: Steel)*
   > What: More steam per tick than the bronze boiler.
   > How: Steel plates, a steel tank, a furnace and 3 fire clay brick blocks (check JEI).
   > Tip: Steel versions of the steam machines (macerator, compressor and others) run faster too.
17. **Steel Plates**: 16x `modern_industrialization:steel_plate` *(after: Steel)*
   > What: The Dissolver and Combiner are framed in steel plates, and steel gears need them too.
   > How: The Steam Compressor presses 1 steel ingot into 1 plate.
   > Tip: You need at least 8 for the Dissolver and Combiner, plus more for gears. Keep the compressor busy.
18. **Steel Gears**: 2x `modern_industrialization:steel_gear` *(after: Steel Plates, Lubricant)*
   > What: Steel machine casings (the core of every LV machine in Chapter IV) and item pipes need steel gears.
   > How: Same pattern as bronze: 4 steel plates, 4 steel bolts and 1 steel ring (check JEI).
   > Tip: Steel rods, bolts and rings come from the Forge Hammer, or from the Cutting Machine now that you have lubricant.
19. **Item Pipes**: 16x `modern_industrialization:item_pipe` *(after: Steel Gears)*
   > What: MI item pipes move items between machines, so dust, ingots and coke flow on their own.
   > How: 6 bronze curved plates and 2 steel gears make 16 pipes.
   > Tip: Right-click a pipe end with an empty hand to switch it between insert and extract.
20. **A Simple Generator**: `generatorgalore:copper_generator` *(after: Blocks of Redstone)*
   > What: Generator Galore's Copper Generator burns solid fuel into FE (Forge Energy) and pushes it into machines it touches.
   > Chemistry: Burning releases the chemical energy stored in carbon bonds as heat; the generator turns that heat into electricity.
   > How: Copper ingots around a furnace, with a block of redstone (check JEI).
21. **Forge Energy**: `generatorgalore:iron_generator` *(after: A Simple Generator)*
   > What: Some machines run on FE instead of steam. You'll need it for the Dissolver.
   > How: Upgrade the Copper Generator: surround it with iron ingots and a block of redstone to make the Iron Generator.
   > Tip: A Mekanism Heat Generator or Powah Furnator also works. Burn coke for long runs.
22. **Heat and Pressure**: 2x `minecraft:magma_block`; 2x `minecraft:piston` *(after: Steel Plates)*
   > What: Besides steel plates and a bronze machine casing, the Dissolver needs 2 magma blocks and 2 pistons.
   > Chemistry: Magma blocks are rock hot enough to glow, a fitting heat source for a machine that tears compounds apart.
   > How: Magma blocks generate in underwater ravines and caves, or can be crafted from 4 magma cream. Pistons need iron, redstone, cobblestone and planks.
23. **Pressure and Precision**: `minecraft:diamond`; 2x `minecraft:obsidian` *(after: Steel Plates, Steel Paxel)*
   > What: The Combiner needs a diamond, 2 obsidian and a piston, plus steel plates and a casing.
   > Chemistry: Obsidian is volcanic glass: lava that cooled too fast for crystals to form.
   > How: Pour water onto a lava source to make obsidian. Your steel paxel is diamond tier, so it mines obsidian; no diamond pickaxe needed. Diamonds are most common near the bottom of the world.
24. **The Dissolver**: `alchemistry:dissolver` *(after: Heat and Pressure, Forge Energy)*
   > Your first gift returns: look at anything and know what it's made of.
   > What: The Dissolver breaks any item into the elements and compounds it's made of.
   > How: Steel plates, pistons, magma blocks and a Bronze Machine Casing (check JEI). Power it with FE, insert anything, and collect the elements.
   > Tip: Some things dissolve into compounds first. Put those back in to break them down further.
25. **The Combiner**: `alchemistry:combiner` *(after: Pressure and Precision, Forge Energy)*
   > And the other half of the gift: what you can take apart, you can put back together.
   > What: The reverse: arrange elements and the Combiner builds them back into items and blocks.
   > How: Steel plates, a diamond, obsidian, a piston and a Bronze Machine Casing (check JEI). It runs on FE too.
   > Tip: Its first real job comes in Chapter IV: sulfuric acid for the lead-acid redstone battery. Taking the world apart and rebuilding it is what this pack is about.
26. **Wood, Undone**: 4x `chemlib:cellulose` *(after: The Dissolver)*
   > What: Your first compound out of the Dissolver.
   > Chemistry: Cellulose is a chain of glucose units, (C₆H₁₀O₅)ₙ. It's the most common organic compound on Earth and gives wood its strength.
   > How: Dissolve logs: each log gives 1 cellulose. Dissolve the cellulose again to get 6 carbon, 10 hydrogen and 5 oxygen.
27. **Graphite**: 4x `chemlib:graphite` *(after: The Dissolver)*
   > What: Coal and charcoal dissolve into graphite, a pure form of carbon.
   > Chemistry: In graphite, carbon atoms form flat sheets of hexagons that slide over each other. That's why pencil 'lead' leaves a mark.
   > How: Dissolve coal or charcoal: each gives 2 graphite. Each graphite dissolves into 4 carbon.
28. **First Entries in the Periodic Table**: 16x `chemlib:hydrogen`; 16x `chemlib:carbon`; 16x `chemlib:oxygen`; 16x `chemlib:iron` *(after: Wood, Undone, Graphite, The Combiner)*
   > What: Dissolve whatever you have lying around and collect your first elements: H (1), C (6), O (8), Fe (26).
   > Chemistry: The number is the atomic number: how many protons are in the nucleus. Change it and you have a different element.
   > How: Cellulose gives carbon, hydrogen and oxygen; graphite gives carbon. Each iron ingot gives 16 iron.
   > Tip: The Periodic Table chapter tracks every element from here on.
29. **Your First Synthesis**: 4x `chemlib:water` *(after: First Entries in the Periodic Table)*
   > Two hydrogen, one oxygen. You once filled oceans with this; today it's a few drops. It's a start, and it's yours.
   > What: Build water from its elements in the Combiner. It's a trivial compound, but you made it from scratch. That's the point.
   > Chemistry: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. Hydrogen and oxygen share electrons in covalent bonds, and the bent shape of the molecule makes it polar.
   > How: Pick water as the target in the Combiner's GUI, then supply 2 hydrogen and 1 oxygen per water.
30. **Blocks of Redstone**: 2x `minecraft:redstone_block` *(after: Steel)*
   > What: The Copper Generator and its Iron upgrade each have a block of redstone in their recipe, so make two.
   > How: 9 redstone dust make 1 block. Redstone ore sits deep, mostly below Y 16, and needs an iron pickaxe.
   > Tip: Ultimine a redstone vein: one gives plenty, and lubricant needs dust too.
31. **Fuel Reserve**: 4x `modern_industrialization:coke_block` *(after: Coke)*
   > What: A stockpile of coke for boilers, generators and future steel.
   > Chemistry: Coke is porous. Air flows through it, which is why it burns so hot and steadily in a furnace.
   > Tip: A full Coke Oven running overnight fills these quickly.
32. **Steel Upgrades**: `modern_industrialization:steel_upgrade`; `modern_industrialization:steel_macerator` *(after: Steel)*
   > What: A Steel Upgrade turns a bronze steam machine into its faster steel version.
   > How: Craft Steel Upgrades from a steel machine casing, bronze parts, fluid pipes and fire clay bricks (check JEI), then combine one with the Bronze Macerator.
   > Tip: Upgrade the machines that bottleneck you first, usually the macerator.
33. **Proof of Composition**: 16x `chemlib:copper`; 16x `chemlib:tin` *(after: First Entries in the Periodic Table)*
   > What: Dissolve a copper ingot and a tin ingot to see the two elements that make bronze.
   > Chemistry: Copper is element 29 and tin is element 50. Every bronze ingot you made in Chapter I was these two, mixed.
   > How: Each copper or tin ingot dissolves into 16 of its element.
34. **Sweet Chemistry**: `chemlib:sucrose` *(after: First Entries in the Periodic Table)*
   > What: Dissolve sugar into sucrose, then sucrose into its elements.
   > Chemistry: Sucrose is glucose and fructose joined together. Dissolved, it gives 12 carbon, 22 hydrogen and 11 oxygen.
   > How: Sugar cane makes sugar; the Dissolver turns 1 sugar into 1 sucrose.
35. **Carbon Is Carbon**: 128x `chemlib:graphite` *(after: First Entries in the Periodic Table)*
   > What: A diamond dissolves into 128 graphite. Expensive, but it proves a point.
   > Chemistry: Diamond and graphite are both pure carbon, called allotropes. In diamond every atom bonds to four neighbours in 3D; in graphite, to three in flat sheets.
   > Tip: Don't dissolve your last diamond. You'll need them for machines.
36. **Steel Hatches**: `modern_industrialization:steel_item_input_hatch`; `modern_industrialization:steel_item_output_hatch`; `modern_industrialization:steel_fluid_input_hatch` *(after: Steel Gears)*
   > What: Steel hatches hold more than bronze ones, and a steam multiblock with at least one steel hatch is upgraded to steel tier: twice as fast, as long as the recipe stays within 4 EU/t.
   > How: Each is a steel machine casing (8 steel plates around a steel gear) with a hopper or a steel tank on top (check JEI for the output versions).
   > Tip: Swap one hatch on your Coke Oven and Steam Blast Furnace and both run at double speed.
37. **Packer and Unpacker**: `modern_industrialization:steel_packer`; `modern_industrialization:steel_unpacker` *(after: Item Pipes)*
   > What: The Packer does small crafts on its own: blocks, double ingots and pipes. The Unpacker takes blocks back apart. Both exist only in steel.
   > How: A steel machine casing with bronze gears, fluid pipes and item pipes (check JEI; the Unpacker also needs bronze rods).
   > Tip: Pipe ingots into the Packer and store your metal as blocks: nine times fewer slots.
38. **Steel Alloy Smelter**: `extended_industrialization:steel_alloy_smelter` *(after: Steel Gears)*
   > What: An Extended Industrialization machine that melts metals together and pours alloy ingots directly: bronze, invar, cupronickel, electrum, battery alloy, brass and more.
   > Chemistry: Alloying in the melt is how bronze was really made: liquid copper and tin mix atom by atom, then freeze together.
   > How: Invar plates, a bronze rotor, fluid pipes and a steel machine casing (check JEI). Invar is iron and nickel; mix the dusts and smelt. Feed the smelter nuggets or tiny dusts.
   > Tip: 27 copper and 9 tin nuggets make 4 bronze ingots: the same 3:1 ratio as the dust, with no mixing step.
39. **The Steam Quarry**: `modern_industrialization:steam_quarry`; 4x `modern_industrialization:bronze_drill` *(after: Item Pipes)*
   > What: A steam multiblock that wears out bronze drills to bring up ore from deeper than bedrock. Slow, but you never have to dig.
   > How: The controller takes steel large plates, steel gears, item pipes, an invar rotary blade and a steel machine casing (check JEI for the shape and its ore table). Drills come 4 at a time from a bronze drill head, iron gears and pipes.
   > Tip: It eats a lot of steel, so build it once your Steam Blast Furnace runs on its own. Quarry ore still obeys the 2x cap until acids.

### III. Divine Ascent

*Walk through fire, brew in the dark, and take back the sky. Flight needs the Nether and your first Alchemistry machine: fire and chemistry together.*

1. **A Door of Fire**: 10x `minecraft:obsidian`; `minecraft:flint_and_steel` *(after: Iron Pickaxe)*
   > You remember the sky. Not looking up at it: standing in it.
   > What: a Nether portal is a 4x5 frame of obsidian (corners optional), lit with flint and steel.
   > Chemistry: obsidian is volcanic glass. Lava cooled so fast its atoms never had time to form crystals.
   > How: mine obsidian with a diamond pickaxe (or a steel paxel, which is diamond tier), or pour water over still lava to make it in place.
   > Tip: a bucket of water and a bucket of lava let you cast the frame block by block.
2. **Into the Fire**: visit `minecraft:the_nether` *(after: A Door of Fire)*
   > What: the Nether is a chemistry lab: quartz (SiO₂), blaze powder and nether wart all come from here.
   > How: bring food, armour, blocks and a way home. NetherPortalFix keeps portals linked properly.
   > Tip: water evaporates instantly here and beds explode. Bring a respawn plan, not a bed.
3. **Blaze Rods**: 4x `minecraft:blaze_rod` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: blaze rods craft the brewing stand, and blaze powder fuels it.
   > How: blazes spawn around spawners in Nether Fortresses. Explorer's Compass can point you to one.
   > Tip: snowballs hurt blazes, and fire resistance makes the fight easy.
4. **Nether Wart**: 8x `minecraft:nether_wart` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: the base reagent for almost every potion.
   > How: it grows on soul sand in fortress stairwells. Bring some soul sand home and replant it; it grows in the Overworld too.
   > Tip: one stack of wart grown at home covers every brew in this chapter.
5. **Nether Quartz**: 16x `minecraft:quartz` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: Nether quartz ore is everywhere in Nether netherrack. The Infusion Pylon needs it.
   > Chemistry: quartz is silicon dioxide, SiO₂. Much later you'll reduce it with carbon to get pure silicon for circuits.
   > Tip: keep a spare stack. Quartz dust plus coke becomes silicon in Chapter V.
6. **Blackstone**: 16x `minecraft:blackstone` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: the Infusion Pylon is framed in blackstone.
   > Chemistry: blackstone is a basalt-like volcanic rock, rich in dark iron and magnesium minerals.
   > How: it fills basalt deltas and bastion remnants. Any pickaxe mines it.
7. **The Brewer's Art**: `minecraft:brewing_stand` *(after: Blaze Rods, Nether Wart)*
   > What: a brewing stand turns water bottles into potions, one ingredient at a time.
   > Chemistry: brewing is extraction and reaction: each ingredient changes what's dissolved in the bottle.
   > How: 1 blaze rod + 3 cobblestone. Blaze powder in the top-left slot fuels 20 brews. Then brew an Awkward Potion: three water bottles in the stand, nether wart on top. Almost every potion starts from it.
   > Tip: look up Potion of Flying in JEI (from Apothic Attributes). The next quests walk the whole chain.
8. **Slow Falling**: 4x `minecraft:phantom_membrane` *(after: The Brewer's Art)*
   > What: step 1 toward flight. Awkward Potion + phantom membrane = Potion of Slow Falling.
   > How: phantoms appear at night when someone in the world hasn't slept for three or more days. Fight them on a roof.
   > Tip: one membrane brews three bottles, so four membranes go a long way.
9. **Levitation**: 4x `minecraft:fermented_spider_eye` *(after: Slow Falling)*
   > What: step 2. Slow Falling + fermented spider eye = Potion of Levitation (Apothic Attributes).
   > Chemistry: fermentation is yeast turning sugar into alcohol and acids. Here it 'corrupts' the effect into its opposite.
   > How: fermented spider eye = spider eye + sugar + brown mushroom (shapeless).
10. **Lifting Gas**: 2x `chemlib:hydrogen` *(after: Levitation, Lighter than Air)*
   > What: step 3. In this pack, Flying is made with hydrogen instead of End chorus fruit, so you can fly before the End.
   > Chemistry: hydrogen (H₂) is the lightest gas there is, about 14 times lighter than air. It lifted the first passenger balloons in 1783.
   > How: get hydrogen from the Alchemistry Dissolver (dissolve water or plants). In a crafting grid, 1 Potion of Levitation + 2 hydrogen make a Potion of Flying: 8 minutes of creative-style flight (check JEI).
   > Tip: don't drink it yet; the next step makes it last longer. The brewing-stand route (popped chorus fruit) also works once you reach the End.
11. **Extended Flight**: 8x `minecraft:redstone` *(after: Lifting Gas)*
   > What: redstone stretches a potion's duration. Flying + redstone = Long Flying (15 min). Add redstone again for Extra Long Flying (30 min).
   > How: brew redstone into your Flying potions, then into the Long ones.
   > Tip: a Potion Filter needs a full hour, which is just two Extra Long potions. Brew at least two.
12. **Potion Filter**: `pylons:potion_filter` *(after: Extended Flight)*
   > What: a Potion Filter holds a potion effect for the Infusion Pylon.
   > How: drink a potion, then right-click the filter to store the effect. It activates once it holds 1 hour of Flying: two Extra Long (30 min each), four Long (15 min) or about eight regular potions.
   > Tip: drink and load one potion at a time so none of the effect runs out first. Two filters with the same effect combine: hold one in each hand and right-click.
13. **Lighter than Air**: 8x `chemlib:hydrogen` *(after: The Dissolver)*
   > What: your flight pylon needs hydrogen, and only the Dissolver can pull it out of matter as an item.
   > Chemistry: H is element 1: one proton, one electron. Hydrogen balloons carried people aloft in 1783.
   > How: dissolve water, plants or wood and collect the hydrogen.
   > Tip: feed the Dissolver from a hopper and it runs while you're in the Nether.
14. **Wings of a God**: `pylons:infusion_pylon` *(after: Potion Filter, Nether Quartz, Blackstone, Lighter than Air)*
   > Your second gift returns, and the sky is yours again. You had forgotten how small the world looks from here.
   > What: the Infusion Pylon applies a filter's effect to you anywhere. With a Flying filter, that's creative-style flight.
   > How: craft it from Nether quartz, blackstone and hydrogen from your Dissolver (see JEI), place it, and put the full (one-hour) filter inside.
   > Tip: the pylon only works while its chunk is loaded. Force-load it (see the next quest).
15. **Keep It Running**: checkmark *(after: Wings of a God)*
   > What: if the pylon's chunk unloads, your flight stops. Over a long trip that means a long fall.
   > How: open the FTB Chunks map (press M), claim the chunk with the pylon, then right-click it again to force-load it.
   > Tip: force-load your Dissolver and brewing setup too, so they keep working while you travel.
16. **Netherite**: `minecraft:netherite_ingot` *(after: Ancient Debris)*
   > What: The toughest metal in the game: netherite gear doesn't burn in lava and outlasts diamond.
   > Chemistry: Netherite isn't on the periodic table. In game terms it's an alloy: scrap from ancient debris fused with gold.
   > How: Smelt ancient debris into netherite scrap, then craft 4 scrap with 4 gold ingots. A smithing table and an upgrade template turn diamond gear into netherite.
   > Tip: Keep this in mind for later: calorite ore on Venus needs a netherite-tier pickaxe.
17. **Eyes of Ender**: 4x `minecraft:ender_pearl`; 2x `minecraft:ender_eye` *(after: Blaze Rods)*
   > What: An Eye of Ender, thrown, flies towards the nearest stronghold, and twelve of them open the way to the End.
   > How: Endermen drop ender pearls; they spawn in every dimension but crowd the Nether's warped forests. Craft 1 pearl with 1 blaze powder (shapeless) for an eye.
   > Tip: No rush. Flight here runs on hydrogen, so the End can wait until you want its chorus fruit.
18. **Fortress Found**: 32x `minecraft:nether_brick` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: Nether Fortresses hold blazes, wither skeletons and nether wart.
   > How: Explorer's Compass points to structures. Mine nether bricks from the fortress walls.
   > Tip: build a small portal near the fortress and your next trip is much shorter.
19. **Fire Resistance**: 4x `minecraft:magma_cream` *(after: The Brewer's Art)*
   > What: Fire Resistance makes lava and blaze fire harmless. Swimming in lava becomes a shortcut.
   > How: magma cubes drop magma cream in basalt deltas, or craft it from blaze powder + slimeball. Brew it into an Awkward Potion.
   > Tip: add redstone for an 8-minute version before any lava-heavy trip.
20. **Ghast Tears**: 2x `minecraft:ghast_tear` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: ghast tears brew Regeneration and drop rarely, since the ghast must die over solid ground.
   > How: reflect a fireball back with a punch or arrow, then catch the tear before it burns in lava.
   > Tip: a bow and patience beat chasing ghasts across lava lakes.
21. **Ancient Debris**: 2x `minecraft:ancient_debris` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: ancient debris smelts into netherite scrap, the base of netherite gear.
   > How: it hides deep in the Nether (around Y 8-22) and resists explosions, so bed or TNT mining works.
   > Tip: try the Dissolver on a scrap later and see what this 'element' really is.
22. **Fire into Source**: `ars_nouveau:volcanic_sourcelink` *(after: Whispers of Magic)*
   > What: the Volcanic Sourcelink turns burning fuel into Source, the energy behind Ars Nouveau.
   > How: craft it from source gems, gold and a lava bucket, place it near a Source Jar and give it fuel. The Worn Notebook explains the details.
   > Tip: it suits a Nether-themed base: blaze rods and lava-adjacent fuels keep it going.
23. **Archwood**: 8x `ars_nouveau:blue_archwood_log` *(after: Whispers of Magic)*
   > What: archwood is Ars Nouveau's magic wood, used for its jars, tables and rituals.
   > How: look for brightly coloured trees in archwood forests; any colour works, but this quest wants blue.
   > Tip: archwood saplings grow at home, so a few logs become a farm.
24. **Whispers of Magic**: `ars_nouveau:worn_notebook`; 4x `ars_nouveau:source_gem` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: the Worn Notebook teaches Ars Nouveau spellcrafting. Source gems are its basic magical material.
   > How: the notebook is a book + lapis lazuli (shapeless). Source gems come from the Imbuement Chamber (lapis or amethyst + Source).
   > Tip: its Ritual of Flight is a second way to fly near your base. See the Ars Nouveau page (Magic and Relics).

### IV. The Electric Age

*Electricity is the tool that splits compounds apart. First you have to make it, and build the circuits that use it.*

1. **Oil from Coal**: `modern_industrialization:raw_synthetic_oil_bucket` *(after: Steel)*
   > Lightning used to come when you called it. Now you'll have to build it a road, and the road starts in a coal pit.
   > What: Raw synthetic oil is the first step to rubber, and rubber is what keeps electricity in its wires.
   > Chemistry: Hot carbon and steam react into syngas, C + H₂O → CO + H₂, and the Fischer-Tropsch process builds that up into longer hydrocarbon chains. Coal-to-oil really was done this way.
   > How: In the Steam Mixer, 1 coke dust and 100 mB of water make 200 mB of raw synthetic oil. Fill a bucket from the mixer's output.
   > Tip: Grind coke in the Steam Macerator for the dust. One coke dust is a fifth of a bucket of oil.
2. **Synthetic Oil**: `modern_industrialization:synthetic_oil_bucket` *(after: Oil from Coal)*
   > What: Raw oil is a messy mixture. Heat refines it into synthetic oil, the input for rubber.
   > Chemistry: Heating a crude hydrocarbon mix breaks up the unstable pieces and drives off the light ones, leaving a cleaner, more uniform oil.
   > How: Pipe raw synthetic oil into a fluid input hatch on your Steam Blast Furnace: 100 mB in, 100 mB out. It needs a fluid output hatch too.
   > Tip: A tank between mixer and furnace keeps both busy.
3. **Rubber**: 8x `modern_industrialization:rubber_sheet` *(after: Synthetic Oil)*
   > What: rubber sheets insulate cables and form circuit boards. Here rubber is synthetic, made from coal, not tree sap.
   > Chemistry: rubber is a polymer: long, tangled hydrocarbon chains. Cross-linked with sulfur (vulcanisation), the chains become a tough, flexible insulator.
   > How: Mixer: synthetic oil + paper → 2 rubber sheets, or + sulfur dust → synthetic rubber fluid (12 sheets per paper). Check JEI.
   > Tip: the sulfur route gives six times more sheets per oil, but its mixer needs more power (check JEI for sulfur dust sources).
4. **Steel Wiremill**: `modern_industrialization:steel_wiremill` *(after: Steel Machine Casing)*
   > What: Copper wire can't be crafted by hand. The Wiremill draws plates into wire, and wire into fine wire.
   > Chemistry: Metals are ductile: their atoms slide past each other without the bonds breaking, so a plate can be pulled through a die into a thin wire.
   > How: A steel machine casing with bronze gears, bronze rotors and fluid pipes (check JEI). It runs on steam like your other machines.
   > Tip: 1 copper plate makes 2 wire. Keep it fed from your Steam Compressor.
5. **Wires and Cables**: 8x `modern_industrialization:copper_wire`; 8x `modern_industrialization:tin_cable` *(after: Steel Wiremill)*
   > What: copper wire goes into every component. Tin cable carries LV power between machines.
   > Chemistry: copper's single outer electron moves freely between atoms, which is why it conducts so well.
   > How: the Steel Wiremill pulls plates into wire. Cables combine wire with rubber sheets.
   > Tip: tin cable is rated for LV (32 EU/t). Higher tiers need better cable.
6. **Battery Alloy**: 4x `modern_industrialization:battery_alloy_ingot` *(after: Steel)*
   > What: battery alloy makes the casing and grids of redstone batteries.
   > Chemistry: lead hardened with antimony is the grid metal of real lead-acid batteries. Pure lead is too soft.
   > How: mix lead and antimony dust (check JEI), then smelt. Lead deposits sit around Y -24 to 16.
7. **Analog Circuit Board**: 2x `modern_industrialization:analog_circuit_board` *(after: Rubber)*
   > What: the base every analog circuit is soldered onto.
   > How: rubber sheet, copper plate, rubber sheet stacked in a column.
   > Tip: once you have an Assembler, it makes these automatically.
8. **Capacitor**: 2x `modern_industrialization:capacitor` *(after: Rubber, Wires and Cables)*
   > What: capacitors store a small charge and smooth out the current.
   > Chemistry: two conductors (gold plates) separated by an insulator (rubber): charge builds up on each side.
   > How: gold plates, copper wire and a rubber sheet (see JEI).
9. **Fine Copper Wire**: 8x `modern_industrialization:copper_fine_wire` *(after: Wires and Cables)*
   > What: Thinner wire for small components. Resistors need it first.
   > Chemistry: A thinner wire has more resistance: current has less metal to flow through. Useful when you want to limit current, not carry it.
   > How: Put copper wire back into the Wiremill: 1 wire makes 4 fine wire.
10. **Resistor**: 3x `modern_industrialization:resistor` *(after: Fine Copper Wire)*
   > What: resistors limit current so the rest of the circuit doesn't burn out.
   > Chemistry: carbon conducts, but poorly. A pinch of coal dust between fine copper wires makes a carbon resistor.
   > How: paper, copper fine wire and coal dust. One craft gives three.
11. **Inductor**: 2x `modern_industrialization:inductor` *(after: Wires and Cables)*
   > What: inductors resist sudden changes in current. The Polarizer also needs them.
   > Chemistry: current through a coil makes a magnetic field; changing the current fights that field.
   > How: copper wire wound around a steel rod.
12. **Battery Acid**: 2x `chemlib:sulfuric_acid` *(after: The Combiner)*
   > What: the redstone battery is a real lead-acid battery, and its electrolyte is sulfuric acid. The Combiner from Chapter II makes it from elements.
   > Chemistry: H₂SO₄ is the most-produced chemical in the world. In a car battery it reacts with the lead plates (Pb + PbO₂ + 2H₂SO₄ → 2PbSO₄ + 2H₂O) and releases electrons; charging runs the reaction backwards.
   > How: pick sulfuric acid in the Combiner and supply 2 hydrogen, 1 sulfur and 4 oxygen. Dissolve gunpowder for sulfur (1 gunpowder → 8 S) and water or cellulose for hydrogen and oxygen.
   > Tip: every LV hull needs two batteries, so keep a stack of acid ready.
13. **Redstone Battery**: 2x `modern_industrialization:redstone_battery` *(after: Battery Alloy, Wires and Cables, Battery Acid)*
   > What: a rechargeable lead-acid battery. Every LV hull holds two.
   > Chemistry: lead-antimony grids, sulfuric acid electrolyte: the same chemistry as the battery under a car's bonnet.
   > How: battery alloy plate and curved plates, tin cable, redstone and sulfuric acid from the Combiner (check JEI for the exact recipe).
   > Tip: the LV Storage Unit is built from six of these, so make spares.
14. **Analog Circuit**: 2x `modern_industrialization:analog_circuit` *(after: Analog Circuit Board, Capacitor, Resistor, Inductor)*
   > What: the LV circuit. Mekanism's Basic Control Circuit also needs one, so MI and Mekanism advance together.
   > How: 2 resistors, 1 inductor, 2 capacitors, the board, and 3 copper wire (see JEI for the layout).
   > Tip: make four or five now. The hull, turbine and each machine all eat them.
15. **Steel Machine Casing**: `modern_industrialization:steel_machine_casing` *(after: Steel Gears)*
   > What: a steel frame. The LV hull is built around it.
   > How: 8 steel plates around a steel gear, the same shape as the bronze one.
   > Tip: the LV hull uses one casing each, and every LV machine needs a hull. Make a few.
16. **LV Machine Hull**: `modern_industrialization:basic_machine_hull` *(after: Analog Circuit, Redstone Battery, Steel Machine Casing)*
   > Your hands remember wiring this. Your mind is still catching up.
   > What: LV (Low Voltage) is the first electric tier. Every LV machine is built on this hull.
   > How: steel machine casing + analog circuit + 2 redstone batteries + 3 tin cable.
17. **Magnetic Steel Rod**: 2x `modern_industrialization:steel_rod_magnetic` *(after: Steel)*
   > What: the core of an electric motor.
   > Chemistry: iron-based alloys hold magnetism because their electron spins line up in domains.
   > How: a steel rod ringed by redstone. Later the Polarizer magnetises rods with electricity.
18. **Electric Motor**: 2x `modern_industrialization:motor` *(after: Magnetic Steel Rod, Wires and Cables)*
   > What: motors drive turbines, pistons, conveyors and robot arms. Nearly every LV machine needs one.
   > Chemistry: current in a coil next to a magnet creates a force; that's the motor effect. Run it backwards and it's a generator.
   > How: magnetic steel rod, steel rods, copper wire and tin cable (see JEI).
19. **Steam to Electricity**: `modern_industrialization:lv_steam_turbine` *(after: LV Machine Hull, Electric Motor)*
   > What: a turbine turns your boiler's steam into EU, MI's electricity.
   > How: pipe steam in, and run tin cable from the turbine to your machines.
   > Tip: watch the turbine's steam input. If machines stall, add boilers before adding turbines.
20. **Piston**: 2x `modern_industrialization:piston` *(after: Electric Motor)*
   > What: MI's piston component, used in the macerator, compressor and robot arm.
   > How: steel plates, steel rods, steel gear, tin cable and a motor.
   > Tip: the Electric Macerator and Electric Compressor each need pistons, so make four.
21. **Conveyor**: 2x `modern_industrialization:conveyor` *(after: Electric Motor, Rubber)*
   > What: conveyors move items inside machines. The Assembler, Packer and Cutting Machine need them.
   > How: rubber sheets, two motors and tin cable.
   > Tip: motors are the bottleneck here. Keep a few spare.
22. **Electric Compressor**: `modern_industrialization:electric_compressor` *(after: Steam to Electricity, Piston)*
   > What: plates, curved plates and rings for every part you'll build next.
   > How: LV hull, two pistons, analog circuits and tin cable.
   > Tip: it doubles as a second plate source while the steam compressor keeps running.
23. **Electric Wiremill**: `modern_industrialization:electric_wiremill` *(after: Steam to Electricity)*
   > What: copper wire and fine wire in bulk. Circuits use a lot of it.
   > How: LV hull, motors and analog circuits (see JEI).
   > Tip: feed it from your compressor's plate output.
24. **Polarizer**: `modern_industrialization:polarizer` *(after: Steam to Electricity, Inductor)*
   > What: magnetic steel rods for motors, and magnetic cupronickel wire for heating coils.
   > Chemistry: a strong field lines up the magnetic domains in the metal, and they stay lined up.
   > How: LV hull, inductors, tin wire and tin cable.
25. **Electric Mixer**: `modern_industrialization:electric_mixer` *(after: Steam to Electricity)*
   > What: mixing dusts into alloys (bronze, invar, cupronickel, battery alloy) and fluids into mixtures.
   > How: LV hull, motor, tin rotor, glass, a fluid pipe and analog circuits.
   > Tip: you'll need it for cupronickel (copper + nickel) and invar (iron + nickel) right away.
26. **Electric Macerator**: `modern_industrialization:electric_macerator` *(after: Piston, Steam to Electricity)*
   > What: ore to crushed dust, ingots back to dust. Still capped at 2x per ore until acids.
   > How: needs an invar rotary blade (invar gear + diamond dust). Invar is iron + nickel; mix the dusts.
   > Tip: the hull quest reward included one. Build a second for throughput.
27. **Electric Furnace**: `modern_industrialization:electric_furnace` *(after: Magnetic Cupronickel Wire)*
   > What: fast, fuel-free smelting.
   > Chemistry: current through a resistive wire turns into heat (Joule heating), the same idea as a toaster.
   > How: LV hull wrapped in magnetic cupronickel wire, with analog circuits.
28. **Robot Arm**: 2x `modern_industrialization:robot_arm` *(after: Piston)*
   > What: robot arms move parts inside the Assembler and Packer.
   > How: two motors, a piston, steel rods, tin cable and an analog circuit.
   > Tip: the Assembler takes two and the Packer two more.
29. **Cutting Machine**: `modern_industrialization:electric_cutting_machine` *(after: Conveyor, Steam to Electricity)*
   > What: cutting ingots into rods and bolts, and logs into more planks.
   > How: it uses an invar rotary blade, motors and a conveyor. Its cuts use a little lubricant, the creosote + redstone mix from Chapter II.
   > Tip: logs give six planks here instead of four.
30. **Magnetic Cupronickel Wire**: 8x `modern_industrialization:cupronickel_wire_magnetic` *(after: Polarizer, Electric Mixer)*
   > What: the heating wire for the Electric Furnace and Electric Blast Furnace.
   > Chemistry: cupronickel (copper + nickel) resists current more than copper and survives heat. Coins and ship pipes use it too.
   > How: mix copper and nickel dust, smelt, draw into wire, then magnetise it in the Polarizer.
31. **Assembler**: `modern_industrialization:assembler` *(after: Robot Arm, Conveyor)*
   > What: circuits and machine parts, automatically, from a stocked input.
   > How: LV hull, two robot arms, two conveyors and two analog circuits.
   > Tip: MI shows every assembler recipe in JEI. Feed it sheets, wire and plates and leave it running.
32. **Packer**: `modern_industrialization:electric_packer` *(after: Robot Arm, Conveyor)*
   > What: compacting ingots into blocks and double ingots, and assembling a few parts. You'll want bauxite blocks next chapter.
   > How: robot arms, conveyors, analog circuits and tin cable on an LV hull.
   > Tip: unpacking is a separate machine, the Unpacker. Build one if you store metal as blocks.
33. **Electric Blast Furnace**: `modern_industrialization:electric_blast_furnace`; 8x `modern_industrialization:cupronickel_coil` *(after: Magnetic Cupronickel Wire)*
   > Fire you can measure in volts. You used to do this without the volts.
   > What: MI's big furnace multiblock. With cupronickel coils it reaches the heat for aluminum and silicon.
   > How: the controller is an LV hull wrapped in magnetic cupronickel wire. Check the structure in JEI or the MI guidebook, then add an LV energy input hatch and item hatches.
   > Tip: hold a hatch or wrench near the controller to see the valid positions highlighted.
34. **Osmium**: 8x `mekanism:raw_osmium` *(after: LV Machine Hull)*
   > What: Mekanism builds almost everything from osmium: its infuser, casings and circuits.
   > Chemistry: real osmium is the densest natural element, 22.6 g/cm³. A litre of it weighs about as much as a big dog.
   > How: osmium ore is common in small veins underground. Smelt the raw osmium into ingots.
35. **Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser**: `mekanism:metallurgic_infuser` *(after: Osmium)*
   > What: Mekanism's entry machine. It infuses metals with other materials.
   > How: iron ingots, redstone, an osmium ingot and two furnaces.
   > Tip: it runs on FE. Your Chapter II generator works, or a Mekanism Heat Generator (Power chapter).
36. **Infused Alloy**: 4x `mekanism:alloy_infused` *(after: Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser)*
   > What: Mekanism's basic alloy. The Enrichment Chamber and many basic machines need it.
   > Chemistry: a real alloy mixes metals at the atomic level. Here redstone plays the part of the second element.
   > How: put redstone in the infuser's left slot (it becomes an infusion buffer), then feed copper ingots.
37. **Mekanism Circuits**: 2x `mekanism:basic_control_circuit`; `mekanism:steel_casing` *(after: Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser, Analog Circuit)*
   > What: in this pack, a Basic Control Circuit is MI Analog Circuit + osmium. Each Mekanism circuit tier needs the matching MI circuit.
   > How: the Steel Casing (steel, glass and osmium) is the frame for most Mekanism machines.
   > Tip: make several casings at once. Every Mekanism machine in the next chapter needs one.
38. **Enrichment Chamber**: `mekanism:enrichment_chamber` *(after: Mekanism Circuits, Infused Alloy)*
   > What: ore → 2 dust. It also turns dirty dust into clean dust in the higher-tier lines.
   > How: steel casing, infused alloy, iron and a basic control circuit.
   > Tip: 3x, 4x and 5x need gases and acids: that's the next chapter.
39. **Crusher**: `mekanism:crusher` *(after: Mekanism Circuits)*
   > What: crushes ingots to dust and, later, ore clumps into dirty dust in the 3x+ lines.
   > How: steel casing, basic control circuits, redstone and lava buckets.
   > Tip: it also turns ingots back into dust, handy for alloy recipes.
40. **Pipe Config Card**: `modern_industrialization:config_card` *(after: LV Machine Hull)*
   > What: saves an item or fluid pipe connection's settings and pastes them onto other connections.
   > How: sneak + use on a configured pipe connection to save; use on another connection to apply. Sneak + use on air clears it.
   > Tip: it can also camouflage pipes as any block. The card's tooltip explains how.
41. **LV Storage Unit**: `modern_industrialization:lv_storage_unit` *(after: Steam to Electricity, Redstone Battery)*
   > What: stores EU, so machines keep running when the turbine can't keep up for a moment.
   > How: six redstone batteries, battery alloy plates and an LV hull.
   > Tip: put it between turbine and machines so short dips don't stop anything.
42. **Electric Water Pump**: `modern_industrialization:electric_water_pump` *(after: Steam to Electricity)*
   > What: pumps water from nothing but power, for boilers and (soon) electrolysis.
   > How: an LV hull with a pump, tin rotor, pipes and an analog circuit.
   > Tip: next chapter, water becomes hydrogen and oxygen. You'll want lots of it.
43. **The Spectrometer**: `warbuckscore:spectrometer` *(after: Analog Circuit)*
   > Once you could see the colours inside things, the light every element gives off. This is a fair copy.
   > What: a hand-held scanner (Warbucks Core, made for this pack). Right-click to read the ore signal in the loaded chunks around you.
   > Chemistry: heated atoms give off light only at certain wavelengths, an emission spectrum unique to each element. That's how helium was found in the Sun before anyone found it on Earth.
   > How: amethyst prism, steel plates, copper wire and an analog circuit (check JEI). It lists each element with its strength, direction, distance and depth.
   > Tip: a "strong" signal is usually a rich deposit. Walk towards it and scan again.
44. **A Rich Lead Deposit**: 64x `modern_industrialization:lead_ore` *(after: Steel)*
   > What: rich ore deposits hold hundreds of ores in one chunk, at a metal-specific depth. Lead's sits around Y -24 to 16.
   > How: strip-mine at that depth and check ore with Jade. FTB Ultimine clears a vein in one go.
   > Tip: galena (lead sulfide, PbS) is the world's main lead ore, and it often carries silver.
45. **Osmium Hoard**: 32x `mekanism:ingot_osmium` *(after: Osmium)*
   > What: every Mekanism machine, casing and circuit costs osmium. A stockpile saves trips.
   > How: smelt or enrich raw osmium into ingots.
   > Tip: the Enrichment Chamber doubles osmium ore, so process it there once it's built.

### V. Electrochemistry and Acids

*Electricity splits compounds into elements. Acids dissolve what fire can't. Ore processing becomes chemistry.*

1. **Mekanism Gases**: `mekanism:electrolytic_separator` *(after: Mekanism Circuits)*
   > Once a word was enough to pull water apart. Now it takes a machine and a cable, and that will have to do.
   > What: the Electrolytic Separator makes hydrogen and oxygen as gases you can pipe and store.
   > Chemistry: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂. Current drives the reaction backwards from burning hydrogen.
   > How: feed it water and FE. Gases leave from the coloured sides (configure them with the Configurator).
2. **Pressurized Tubes**: 16x `mekanism:basic_pressurized_tube` *(after: Mekanism Gases)*
   > What: gases need sealed tubes. Item pipes and fluid pipes won't carry them.
   > How: craft basic pressurized tubes (see JEI) and run them from the separator's outputs.
   > Tip: vent what you don't need yet. A full output tank stops the whole separator.
3. **A Source of Sulfur**: 8x `modern_industrialization:sulfur_dust` *(after: Electric Macerator)*
   > What: sulfur is where sulfuric acid starts.
   > Chemistry: S is element 16. Volcanoes and fossil fuels are full of it; most industrial sulfur is stripped out of oil and gas.
   > How: macerate crushed lignite coal (about half the time you get sulfur dust), or centrifuge lava later. Press U on Sulfur Dust in JEI for all sources.
4. **Contact Process 1: SO₂**: `mekanism:chemical_oxidizer` *(after: Pressurized Tubes, A Source of Sulfur)*
   > What: the Chemical Oxidizer turns a solid into a gas. Sulfur dust becomes sulfur dioxide.
   > Chemistry: S + O₂ → SO₂. It's the sharp smell of a struck match.
   > How: one sulfur dust gives 100 mB of SO₂. Pipe it out with pressurized tubes.
5. **Contact Process 2: SO₃**: `mekanism:chemical_infuser` *(after: Contact Process 1: SO₂)*
   > What: the Chemical Infuser combines two gases. SO₂ plus oxygen from your separator gives sulfur trioxide.
   > Chemistry: 2SO₂ + O₂ → 2SO₃. Real plants pass the gases over a vanadium oxide (V₂O₅) catalyst at about 450 °C: the 'contact' in the name.
   > How: SO₂ in one side, O₂ in the other.
6. **Water Vapor**: `mekanism:rotary_condensentrator` *(after: Contact Process 2: SO₃)*
   > What: the Rotary Condensentrator converts fluids to gases and back. It turns water into water vapor.
   > How: set it to gas mode (the toggle in its GUI), pipe water in and pressurized tube out.
   > Tip: it also turns Mekanism gases into buckets, which is handy for storage and trading.
7. **Contact Process 3: H₂SO₄**: checkmark *(after: Contact Process 2: SO₃, Water Vapor)*
   > What: a second Chemical Infuser combines SO₃ with water vapor into sulfuric acid gas. Tick this when acid is flowing.
   > Chemistry: SO₃ + H₂O → H₂SO₄. Real plants dissolve SO₃ in existing acid first (oleum), because SO₃ and water alone make a corrosive mist.
   > Tip: store the acid in a chemical tank. The 5x ore line drinks it.
8. **Salt**: 16x `modern_industrialization:salt_dust` *(after: Electric Macerator)*
   > What: salt is the start of the chlor-alkali industry: chlorine, sodium and everything made from them.
   > Chemistry: NaCl is an ionic crystal: Na⁺ and Cl⁻ held together by charge. Split it and you get a soft, reactive metal and a toxic green gas.
   > How: MI salt ore is found underground and drops salt dust.
9. **Brine**: checkmark *(after: Salt, Contact Process 1: SO₂)*
   > What: brine is salty water, and Mekanism splits it into chlorine. Tick this when you have brine.
   > How: put salt dust in a Chemical Oxidizer (15 mB brine per dust), or build a Thermal Evaporation Plant (see the side quest).
   > Tip: a second oxidizer just for salt saves you from swapping inputs.
10. **Chlorine**: checkmark *(after: Brine, Mekanism Gases)*
   > What: the Electrolytic Separator also takes brine. Out come chlorine and sodium. Tick this when chlorine is flowing.
   > Chemistry: real brine electrolysis gives Cl₂ at one electrode and H₂ + NaOH at the other. Mekanism simplifies it to sodium + chlorine.
   > Tip: use a second separator so your hydrogen and oxygen line keeps running.
11. **Hydrogen Chloride**: checkmark *(after: Chlorine, Contact Process 2: SO₃)*
   > What: hydrogen chloride drives the 4x ore line. Tick this when HCl is flowing.
   > Chemistry: H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl. Dissolved in water it's hydrochloric acid, the same acid in your stomach.
   > How: hydrogen in one side of a Chemical Infuser, chlorine in the other.
12. **3x Ore: Oxygen**: `mekanism:purification_chamber` *(after: Mekanism Gases, Enrichment Chamber, Crusher, Electronic Circuit)*
   > What: before acids, every route caps at 2x per ore. Purifying ore with oxygen gives 3x. The chamber needs advanced control circuits, which are built on MI's electronic circuit.
   > How: ore + O₂ → 3 clumps. Crusher: clumps → dirty dust. Enrichment Chamber: dirty dust → dust.
   > Tip: Mekanism shows each step in JEI. Chain them with pipes and side configuration.
13. **4x Ore: Hydrogen Chloride**: `mekanism:chemical_injection_chamber` *(after: 3x Ore: Oxygen, Hydrogen Chloride)*
   > What: injecting hydrogen chloride splits ore into shards: 4x.
   > How: ore + HCl → 4 shards. Purification Chamber: shards → clumps, then on through your 3x line.
   > Tip: your 3x machines are now the back half of the 4x line. Nothing is wasted.
14. **Dissolving Ore**: `mekanism:chemical_dissolution_chamber` *(after: 4x Ore: Hydrogen Chloride, Contact Process 3: H₂SO₄)*
   > What: the Dissolution Chamber dissolves ore in sulfuric acid, giving a dirty slurry.
   > Chemistry: acid leaching: H₂SO₄ turns metal minerals into soluble sulfates, leaving the rock behind.
   > How: feed it ore and sulfuric acid gas. The slurry comes out as a chemical.
15. **Washing Slurry**: `mekanism:chemical_washer` *(after: Dissolving Ore)*
   > What: the Chemical Washer rinses impurities out of the slurry.
   > Chemistry: washing removes the dissolved gangue (waste rock) so only the metal salt is left to crystallise.
   > How: slurry in, water in, clean slurry out. An MI electric water pump keeps the water coming.
16. **5x Ore: Dissolution**: `mekanism:chemical_crystallizer` *(after: Washing Slurry)*
   > Five from one. You used to call that a small miracle. Now you call it hydrometallurgy.
   > What: the Chemical Crystallizer turns clean slurry into crystals: 5x per ore.
   > Chemistry: this is hydrometallurgy, the way most of the world's copper is really refined.
   > How: crystals → Injection Chamber (shards) → Purification Chamber (clumps) → Crusher → Enrichment Chamber.
17. **Ore Byproducts**: `modern_industrialization:centrifuge`; 4x `modern_industrialization:silver_dust` *(after: 5x Ore: Dissolution, Electronic Circuit)*
   > What: real ores are never pure. Send Mekanism's dirty dust through MI's Centrifuge instead of the Enrichment Chamber for the same dust plus a chance at a bonus metal.
   > Chemistry: iron → nickel, copper → gold, gold → silver, lead → silver (galena), tin → tungsten, osmium → iridium, uranium → lead (decay).
   > How: the Centrifuge needs an electronic circuit. Route dirty dust to it, and rare metals arrive as a bonus.
18. **Bauxite**: 16x `modern_industrialization:bauxite_dust` *(after: Electric Blast Furnace)*
   > An emperor once served his finest guests on this metal. You knew even then it was never rare, only stubborn.
   > What: bauxite is the only practical aluminum ore. MI bauxite ore drops bauxite dust.
   > Chemistry: bauxite is mostly aluminium hydroxides, Al(OH)₃ and AlO(OH), stained red by iron oxide.
   > How: rich bauxite deposits sit around Y -16 to 24. No furnace will free the metal: it goes through the Bayer process first.
19. **Lye for the Digester**: `modern_industrialization:sodium_hydroxide_bucket` *(after: Electric Mixer, The Combiner)*
   > What: the Bayer process dissolves bauxite in hot lye, so you need sodium hydroxide solution first.
   > Chemistry: NaOH is a strong base: it fully splits into Na⁺ and OH⁻ in water, and OH⁻ is what pulls aluminium into solution.
   > How: combine Na + O + H in the Alchemistry Combiner (check JEI on Sodium Hydroxide), then Mixer: 1 crystal + 250 mB water → 250 mB lye.
   > Tip: the digester gives most of the lye back, so a few crystals go a long way. Later the Chemical Reactor makes it in bulk.
20. **Bayer Digestion**: `modern_industrialization:sodium_aluminate_solution_bucket` *(after: Bauxite, Lye for the Digester)*
   > What: the first step of every aluminium refinery since 1888: hot lye dissolves the aluminium out of bauxite.
   > Chemistry: Al(OH)₃ + NaOH → NaAl(OH)₄ (sodium aluminate). Iron and titanium oxides don't dissolve; they settle out as 'red mud'.
   > How: Mixer: 4 bauxite dust + 1000 mB lye → 1000 mB sodium aluminate solution + 2 tiny iron dust + 1 tiny titanium dust.
   > Tip: pipe the solution straight into the next Mixer; a bucket is only needed for this quest.
21. **Precipitation**: 8x `chemlib:aluminum_hydroxide_dust` *(after: Bayer Digestion)*
   > What: pure aluminium hydroxide, crystallised back out of the solution, with the lye recovered.
   > Chemistry: NaAl(OH)₄ → Al(OH)₃ + NaOH. Diluting the liquor makes the reaction run backwards; the impurities stayed behind in the red mud.
   > How: Mixer: 1000 mB sodium aluminate + 1000 mB water → 4 aluminium hydroxide dust + 900 mB lye.
   > Tip: loop the 900 mB of lye back into the digester. That loop is why the Bayer process is cheap.
22. **Alumina**: 4x `chemlib:aluminum_oxide_dust` *(after: Precipitation)*
   > What: alumina (aluminium oxide) is the white powder that actually goes into the smelter.
   > Chemistry: calcination: 2Al(OH)₃ → Al₂O₃ + 3H₂O at around 1000 °C. Alumina also makes sapphire and ruby, coloured by traces of iron, titanium or chromium.
   > How: Electric Blast Furnace: 2 aluminium hydroxide dust → 1 alumina dust.
23. **The Hall-Héroult Cell**: `modern_industrialization:hall_heroult_cell` *(after: Alumina)*
   > What: a multiblock smelter that splits alumina with electricity. It's built from steel and LV parts, because it's what makes your first aluminium.
   > Chemistry: alumina melts at 2072 °C, far too hot. Dissolved in molten cryolite it melts near 950 °C. Current then splits it: 2Al₂O₃ + 3C → 4Al + 3CO₂, burning the carbon anode away.
   > How: controller from steel large plates, analog circuits, cupronickel coils and an LV hull. Check JEI (press U on the controller) for the 3x3x3 shape: steel casings top and bottom, a ring of cupronickel coils with the controller in the middle layer.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > History: Charles Martin Hall (USA) and Paul Héroult (France) found the process independently in 1886, both in their early twenties. Within about ten years the price of aluminium fell by more than 90%.
   > Note: every primary aluminium smelter on Earth still uses it, and the cells draw a few percent of the world's electricity.
24. **Aluminum**: 8x `modern_industrialization:aluminum_ingot` *(after: The Hall-Héroult Cell)*
   > The metal comes away bright and light in your hand. Some part of you is pleased it still had to work for it.
   > What: aluminum is the metal of the MV tier: boards, rotors, casings, the Chemical Reactor and the Electrolyzer.
   > Chemistry: aluminium is the most common metal in the crust but clings to oxygen, so only electricity can pull it free.
   > How: Hall-Héroult Cell (LV power): 1 alumina dust + coke dust (the anode, used half the time) + a pinch of fluorite flux → 1 aluminum ingot.
   > Tip: 4 bauxite dust becomes 2 ingots. The cell only takes refined alumina dust, and no furnace will smelt aluminium dust: the Bayer line is the way in.
25. **Fun Fact: No Shortcut**: checkmark *(after: Alumina)*
   > What: for decades aluminium cost more than silver, because nobody could pull it off its oxygen cheaply. Tick this once you've read why.
   > Chemistry: 4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃ releases so much energy that thermite (Al + iron oxide) burns white-hot. Carbon grabs oxygen far less strongly, so coke in a furnace can't take it back from alumina.
   > How: that's why this pack has no furnace route for aluminium: the Hall-Héroult cell feeds in electricity instead, and it only accepts refined alumina dust from your Bayer line.
   > Tip: Napoleon III reportedly served his most honoured guests on aluminium plates. Everyone else made do with gold.
26. **Electrum**: 4x `modern_industrialization:electrum_ingot` *(after: Electric Mixer)*
   > What: electrum cable and fine wire go into every MV component.
   > Chemistry: electrum is a natural gold-silver alloy. The first coins, in Lydia around 600 BC, were struck from it.
   > How: mix gold and silver dust, then smelt. Check JEI (press R on Silver Dust) for silver ore in this pack.
27. **Silicon**: 4x `modern_industrialization:silicon_ingot` *(after: Electric Blast Furnace, Nether Quartz)*
   > What: silicon is the semiconductor every transistor and diode is built on.
   > Chemistry: SiO₂ + 2C → Si + 2CO. Carbon pulls the oxygen off quartz at furnace heat: carbothermic reduction.
   > How: macerate quartz into dust, then EBF: quartz dust + coke dust → silicon dust. Smelt it into ingots.
   > Tip: this is the only source of silicon in the pack. AE2's certus smelting and Mekanism's sand crushing are removed, so AE2 runs on this silicon too.
28. **Electronic Circuit Board**: `modern_industrialization:electronic_circuit_board` *(after: Aluminum, Electrum)*
   > What: the base for MV circuits.
   > How: an analog circuit board with aluminum plates, electrum cable and a redstone battery (see JEI).
   > Tip: the Assembler can make these too, once you stock it.
29. **Transistors and Diodes**: 2x `modern_industrialization:transistor`; 2x `modern_industrialization:diode` *(after: Silicon, Electrum)*
   > What: diodes let current flow one way; transistors are switches controlled by current.
   > Chemistry: a pure silicon crystal barely conducts. Tiny amounts of other elements ('doping') make it conduct in controllable ways.
   > How: silicon plates, steel plates and electrum fine wire (diodes add glass).
30. **Electronic Circuit**: 2x `modern_industrialization:electronic_circuit` *(after: Electronic Circuit Board, Transistors and Diodes)*
   > What: the MV circuit. The Electrolyzer, Chemical Reactor and Centrifuge all need it, even though they sit on an LV hull.
   > How: electronic circuit board, 4 analog circuits, 2 diodes and 2 transistors.
   > Tip: set an Assembler to make these. You'll need dozens.
31. **Electrolysis**: `modern_industrialization:electrolyzer` *(after: Electronic Circuit, Pumps, Large and Small)*
   > What: pass current through a compound and it splits. This is electrochemistry.
   > Chemistry: water → H₂ + O₂ (3000 mB water → 2000 mB H₂ + 1000 mB O₂). Salt → sodium + chlorine.
   > How: magnetic cupronickel wire, aluminum rods, an LV hull, an electronic circuit and a large pump.
32. **The Chemical Reactor**: `modern_industrialization:chemical_reactor` *(after: Electronic Circuit, Pumps, Large and Small)*
   > What: combines items and fluids into new compounds. You'll use it constantly from here to the end.
   > How: glass, a large pump, aluminum rotors, an LV hull, electronic circuits and electrum cable.
   > Tip: MI fluids go in through pipes. A Configurable Tank holds spare H₂ and O₂.
33. **Sodium**: 4x `modern_industrialization:sodium_dust` *(after: Electrolysis, Salt)*
   > What: sodium goes into the HV tier's sodium battery. The chlorine is a bonus.
   > Chemistry: 2NaCl → 2Na + Cl₂. Real sodium is made this way from molten salt (the Downs cell). It reacts violently with water.
   > How: Electrolyzer: 2 salt dust → 1 sodium dust + 125 mB chlorine.
34. **Sulfuric Acid**: `modern_industrialization:sulfuric_acid_bucket` *(after: The Chemical Reactor, A Source of Sulfur)*
   > Acid opens what fire cannot. You learned that once, the hard way, and the lesson has come back intact.
   > What: sulfuric acid, as an MI fluid you can bucket. The Undergarden portal and many MI recipes need it.
   > Chemistry: S + O₂ + H₂O → H₂SO₄, the whole contact process in one vessel. Industry makes more of it than any other chemical.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: 1 sulfur dust + 200 mB O₂ + 200 mB water → 500 mB sulfuric acid.
35. **Silicon Battery**: 2x `modern_industrialization:silicon_battery` *(after: Silicon, Electrum)*
   > What: the MV battery. Every MV hull holds two.
   > How: battery alloy plates, electrum cable and silicon dust.
   > Tip: make four. The Advanced (MV) hull uses two, and you'll want a second hull soon.
36. **MV: Aluminum**: `modern_industrialization:electronic_circuit`; `modern_industrialization:advanced_machine_hull` *(after: Electronic Circuit, Silicon Battery)*
   > The circuits are getting smaller and the power larger. So are you.
   > What: the MV hull is the base for every MV machine, and Powah, Hostile Neural Networks and Extended Crafting all want MV circuits.
   > How: advanced machine casing (an LV hull wrapped in aluminum plates) + electronic circuit + 2 silicon batteries + electrum cable.
37. **Uranium**: 4x `modern_industrialization:uranium_dust` *(after: Electric Macerator)*
   > What: uranium is the fuel of Powah's reactors and, much later, fission.
   > Chemistry: U is element 92, the heaviest element found in quantity in nature. It slowly decays into lead.
   > How: rich uranium deposits sit deep, around Y -56 to -24. Macerate the ore into dust.
38. **Uranium Dioxide**: `powah:energizing_orb`; 4x `powah:uraninite` *(after: MV: Aluminum, The Chemical Reactor, Uranium)*
   > What: uraninite fuels Powah's reactors. Powah's Energizing Orb needs an MV circuit.
   > Chemistry: uraninite is UO₂, the main ore of uranium in nature. Here you make it: U + O₂ → UO₂.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: uranium dust + 500 mB oxygen → uraninite. Powah's own uraninite ore is turned off.
39. **The Undergarden**: `undergarden:catalyst`; visit `undergarden:undergarden` *(after: Sulfuric Acid, Contact Process 3: H₂SO₄)*
   > A world beneath the world, and the key to its door is a bottle of acid. You are trusted with more every day.
   > What: a strange underground dimension. Its portal catalyst needs a bucket of sulfuric acid: MI's, Mekanism's or ChemLib's all work.
   > How: the quickest bucket is your Mekanism contact process: a Rotary Condensentrator in liquid mode turns the acid gas into fluid you can bucket. MI's Chemical Reactor acid works too. Then build a stone-brick portal frame and right-click it with the catalyst.
   > Tip: bring torches and food. It is dark down there.
40. **Thermal Evaporation**: `mekanism:thermal_evaporation_controller`; `mekanism:thermal_evaporation_valve`; 16x `mekanism:thermal_evaporation_block` *(after: Mekanism Gases)*
   > What: a tall multiblock that boils water down into brine, and brine down into lithium.
   > Chemistry: evaporation concentrates dissolved salts. Salt flats and lithium ponds in Chile work the same way.
   > How: see Just Enough Mekanism Multiblocks in JEI for the layout. Taller towers run faster; heat speeds it up.
41. **Bottled Gases**: 3x `mekanism:basic_chemical_tank` *(after: Pressurized Tubes)*
   > What: chemical tanks store gases and keep them when broken, so you can carry them around.
   > How: fill one tank each with hydrogen, oxygen and chlorine.
   > Tip: a tank of hydrogen also fuels the Gas-Burning Generator (Power chapter).
42. **Fun Fact: Oleum**: checkmark *(after: Contact Process 3: H₂SO₄)*
   > What: SO₃ hitting water directly forms a fine acid mist that's hard to capture.
   > Chemistry: plants absorb SO₃ into concentrated H₂SO₄ to make oleum (H₂S₂O₇), then dilute: H₂S₂O₇ + H₂O → 2H₂SO₄.
   > Tip: you've now run, in miniature, a process that makes over 250 million tonnes a year.
43. **Five for Everything**: checkmark *(after: 5x Ore: Dissolution)*
   > What: a challenge: put at least five different ores through the full 5x line.
   > How: one Dissolution Chamber handles every metal, but each slurry needs its own washer and crystallizer pass. Tick this when five ores are done.
   > Tip: Mekanism factories (upgraded machines) run several ores at once.
44. **A Red Mountain**: 128x `modern_industrialization:bauxite_dust` *(after: Bauxite)*
   > What: rich deposits hold hundreds of ores in one chunk. Find bauxite's and the MV tier stops feeling slow.
   > How: strip-mine around Y -16 to 24 and look for red ore with Jade. FTB Ultimine helps a lot.
   > Tip: Fortune works on bauxite ore, since it drops dust.
45. **A Hint of Titanium**: 9x `modern_industrialization:titanium_tiny_dust` *(after: Bayer Digestion)*
   > What: Bayer digestion leaves a little titanium behind with the iron. Save it for much later.
   > Chemistry: bauxite carries titanium dioxide (TiO₂) as an impurity. It doesn't dissolve in lye, so it ends up in the 'red mud'.
   > How: every Bayer digestion (4 bauxite dust) gives 1 tiny titanium dust. Nine of them pack into a full dust.
46. **Hydrochloric Acid, MI Style**: `modern_industrialization:hydrochloric_acid_bucket` *(after: The Chemical Reactor, Sodium)*
   > What: MI makes hydrochloric acid as a fluid, the alternative to Mekanism's HCl gas.
   > Chemistry: H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl. 1000 mB of each gas gives 2000 mB of acid.
   > How: chlorine from salt electrolysis, hydrogen from water electrolysis, both into the Chemical Reactor.
47. **Lye**: `modern_industrialization:sodium_hydroxide_bucket` *(after: The Chemical Reactor, Sodium)*
   > What: sodium hydroxide (NaOH, lye) is the strong base to sulfuric acid's strong acid. Soap is made with it.
   > Chemistry: acid + base → salt + water. H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: sodium dust + 1000 mB oxygen + 1000 mB hydrogen → 2000 mB sodium hydroxide.
   > Tip: this is the bulk lye supply for the Bayer digester, so you can stop feeding it Combiner crystals.
48. **Pumps, Large and Small**: 3x `modern_industrialization:pump`; `modern_industrialization:large_motor`; `modern_industrialization:large_pump` *(after: Electronic Circuit, Aluminum)*
   > What: the Electrolyzer and the Chemical Reactor each need a Large Pump, and a Large Pump is three small pumps driven by a Large Motor.
   > How: Large Motor: an electronic circuit, 2 aluminum rods and 6 motors. Large Pump: 2 electronic circuits, 3 aluminum rotors, a Large Motor and 3 pumps (Assembler or crafting table; check JEI).
   > Tip: pumps are the part you'll run short of. Keep an Assembler stocked with motors and rotors.
49. **Doping Silicon**: `modern_industrialization:silicon_n_doped_plate`; `modern_industrialization:silicon_p_doped_plate` *(after: Transistors and Diodes, The Chemical Reactor)*
   > What: silicon plates with a trace of another element, used in cheaper recipes for transistors and diodes.
   > Chemistry: silicon has four outer electrons. Antimony has five, so it adds a spare electron (n-type); aluminium has three, so it leaves a 'hole' (p-type). Where n meets p, current flows one way only: a diode.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: 1 silicon plate + 1 tiny antimony dust → n-doped plate; 1 silicon plate + 1 tiny aluminum dust → p-doped plate. JEI shows the doped transistor and diode recipes.
50. **Machine Upgrades**: 4x `modern_industrialization:basic_upgrade`; `modern_industrialization:overdrive_module` *(after: Electronic Circuit Board)*
   > What: Upgrades go in a machine's upgrade slot and raise how much EU/t it may draw, so it overclocks harder. The Overdrive Module keeps a machine's efficiency up while it waits for input.
   > How: Assembler: 2 conveyors, 4 motors, 2 robot arms and an analog circuit board → 4 basic upgrades. Overdrive Module: 2 diodes, 2 transistors, 4 electrum fine wire and an electronic circuit board.
   > Tip: hover over an upgrade for its exact bonus. Some late recipes ask for more EU/t than a plain machine allows; upgrades are the answer.
51. **Electric Helpers**: `extended_industrialization:electric_alloy_smelter`; `modern_industrialization:electric_unpacker` *(after: Mekanism Gases)*
   > What: the electric versions of two steam-age helpers: the Electric Alloy Smelter (Extended Industrialization) pours alloys from nuggets, the Electric Unpacker breaks blocks and double ingots back down.
   > How: both sit on an LV machine hull with analog circuits. The Alloy Smelter adds a tin rotor and magnetic cupronickel wire, the Unpacker motors and conveyors (check JEI).
   > Tip: they run on the same LV cable as everything else, so your steam boilers can finally rest.

### VI. Petrochemistry

*Crude oil is a mixture. Separate it by boiling point, then build polymers from the pieces.*

1. **Black Gold**: `modern_industrialization:oil_drilling_rig`; `modern_industrialization:crude_oil_bucket` *(after: MV: Aluminum)*
   > Before there were people, you watched forests grow, fall and sink, and the ages press them into oil. Time to take some of that sunlight back.
   > What: crude oil is a soup of hydrocarbons, from tiny gas molecules to long waxy chains.
   > Chemistry: hydrocarbons are just carbon and hydrogen (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ and friends). Chain length decides whether one is a gas, a fuel or a tar.
   > How: put the Oil Drilling Rig in an MI Quarry over an oil-rich area (check JEI). It slowly wears out aluminum drills.
   > Tip: pipe the crude straight into a tank. You'll need a lot of it.
2. **Fractional Distillation**: `modern_industrialization:distillation_tower` *(after: Black Gold, Pipe Casings)*
   > What: the Distillation Tower is a multiblock that splits one fluid into several fractions at once.
   > Chemistry: heat the crude and each fraction boils off at its own temperature. Light molecules rise to the top, heavy ones stay low.
   > How: the 3D layout is in JEI and the MI guidebook. Each extra layer adds one more output.
   > Tip: every other mod gets its fuel and plastic from here, so build it with room to grow.
3. **Sour Fractions**: `modern_industrialization:sulfuric_light_fuel_bucket`; `modern_industrialization:sulfuric_heavy_fuel_bucket`; `modern_industrialization:sulfuric_naphtha_bucket` *(after: Fractional Distillation)*
   > What: 1000 mB of crude gives 500 light fuel, 200 heavy fuel and 300 naphtha, but all three are 'sour'.
   > Chemistry: natural oil carries sulfur compounds. Burn them and you get SO₂, the gas behind acid rain.
   > How: run crude through the Distillation Tower and catch each output in its own tank or bucket.
4. **Sweetening the Oil**: `modern_industrialization:light_fuel_bucket`; `modern_industrialization:heavy_fuel_bucket`; `modern_industrialization:naphtha_bucket` *(after: Sour Fractions)*
   > What: hydrotreating removes the sulfur and gives clean light fuel, heavy fuel and naphtha.
   > Chemistry: hydrogen reacts with sulfur compounds to form H₂S. Real refineries turn that into sulfur and then acid; MI hands you sulfuric acid directly.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: 12 B of a sour fraction + 2 B hydrogen → 12 B clean fraction + 2 B H₂SO₄.
   > Tip: feed the acid back into your ore line. Nothing is wasted.
5. **Diesel Power**: `modern_industrialization:diesel_bucket`; `modern_industrialization:lv_diesel_generator` *(after: Sweetening the Oil)*
   > What: diesel runs MI generators, tools and, later, your rockets (Ad Astra burns MI diesel).
   > Chemistry: diesel is a blend of C₁₀ to C₂₀ hydrocarbons: mostly light fuel, with heavy fuel for energy density.
   > How: Mixer: 5 B light fuel + 1 B heavy fuel → 6 B diesel.
   > Tip: a Large Diesel Generator is far more efficient than a row of small ones.
6. **Steam Cracking**: `modern_industrialization:steam_cracked_naphtha_bucket` *(after: Sweetening the Oil)*
   > What: naphtha is too big to make plastic from. Cracking breaks it into the small building blocks chemists actually want.
   > Chemistry: at high temperature with steam, long chains snap apart into short, reactive molecules with double bonds (alkenes).
   > How: Chemical Reactor: 1000 mB naphtha + 100 mB steam → 1000 mB steam-cracked naphtha.
7. **Ethylene**: `modern_industrialization:ethylene_bucket` *(after: Steam Cracking)*
   > What: distilling cracked naphtha gives eight products: methane, acetylene, ethylene, propene, butadiene, benzene, toluene and ethylbenzene.
   > Chemistry: ethylene's C=C double bond can open up and link to its neighbours. That is how plastics are born.
   > How: send steam-cracked naphtha through the Distillation Tower (more layers give more outputs; all eight need the full tower).
   > Tip: store every fraction. Each one has a use later in this chapter.
8. **Polymerisation**: `modern_industrialization:polyethylene_bucket` *(after: Ethylene)*
   > What: polyethylene, (C₂H₄)ₙ, is the plastic in bags and bottles, and the laminate on HV circuit boards.
   > Chemistry: a metal catalyst opens each double bond so the molecules join head to tail. Real plants use chromium (Phillips) or titanium catalysts.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: 500 mB ethylene + 4 tiny lead or chromium dust → 300 mB polyethylene.
9. **HDPE**: 8x `mekanism:hdpe_pellet` *(after: Polymerisation)*
   > What: high-density polyethylene pellets become Mekanism's plastic sheets, rods and later the MekaSuit.
   > Chemistry: HDPE has straight chains that pack tightly, so it's stiffer than ordinary polyethylene.
   > How: Pressurized Reaction Chamber with ethylene, water and substrate (check JEI).
10. **Chromium and Manganese**: 4x `modern_industrialization:chromium_dust`; 4x `modern_industrialization:manganese_dust` *(after: MV: Aluminum)*
   > What: stainless steel needs chromium, nickel and manganese on top of iron.
   > Chemistry: chromium is leached with acid: crushed chromium + HCl → chromium chloride solution, then electrolysis splits out the metal plus H₂ and Cl₂.
   > How: Chemical Reactor (chromium crushed dust + 9 B HCl), then Electrolyzer. Check JEI for manganese.
11. **Stainless Steel Dust**: 9x `modern_industrialization:stainless_steel_dust` *(after: Chromium and Manganese)*
   > What: the mixed powder that becomes stainless steel.
   > Chemistry: at 10.5% chromium or more, the surface forms an invisible Cr₂O₃ film that stops rust spreading.
   > How: Mixer: 6 iron dust + 1 chromium + 1 nickel + 1 manganese → 9 stainless steel dust.
12. **Hot Ingots**: `modern_industrialization:vacuum_freezer`; `modern_industrialization:stainless_steel_hot_ingot` *(after: Stainless Steel Dust)*
   > What: the Electric Blast Furnace melts the dust into a hot ingot that must be cooled before use.
   > How: EBF turns 1 stainless steel dust into 1 hot ingot. Build the Vacuum Freezer multiblock (layout in JEI) to cool it.
   > Tip: later, the Heat Exchanger cools hot ingots too and gives argon and helium back.
13. **Stainless Steel**: 8x `modern_industrialization:stainless_steel_ingot` *(after: Hot Ingots, Electric Blast Furnace)*
   > What: stainless steel resists corrosion, so it can hold acids and hot fluids.
   > Chemistry: if the surface is scratched, chromium re-forms the oxide film at once. The steel heals itself.
   > How: cool hot ingots in the Vacuum Freezer. HV circuit boards need 4 stainless plates each.
   > Tip: automate the whole line: mixer → EBF → freezer → compressor.
14. **Digital Circuit Board**: `modern_industrialization:digital_circuit_board` *(after: Polymerisation, Stainless Steel)*
   > What: the base of every HV circuit.
   > Chemistry: polyethylene is an excellent insulator, so it separates the copper layers of the board.
   > How: Assembler: electronic circuit board + 4 stainless steel plates + silicon battery + 6 aluminum cable + 750 mB polyethylene.
15. **Sodium Battery**: 2x `modern_industrialization:sodium_battery` *(after: Sodium)*
   > What: the HV hull needs two sodium batteries.
   > Chemistry: sodium metal gives up its one outer electron very easily (it fizzes in water), which is what makes it a good battery material.
   > How: sodium dust from the Electrolyzer (2 salt dust → 1 sodium dust + chlorine), as in Electrochemistry. Then craft the battery (check JEI).
   > Tip: keep the chlorine. It's needed for HCl and, next chapter, PVC.
16. **HV: Digital Circuits**: `modern_industrialization:digital_circuit`; `modern_industrialization:turbo_machine_hull` *(after: Digital Circuit Board, Sodium Battery, Logic Gates)*
   > Logic gates, clicking into place. You used to think this fast.
   > What: digital circuits unlock HV machines, AE2, the Angel Ring and elite jetpack coils.
   > How: Assembler: digital circuit board + 4 electronic circuits + AND, OR and NOT gates. The Turbo hull adds 2 sodium batteries and aluminum cable.
   > Tip: set up a dedicated assembler for circuits. You'll make hundreds.
17. **Fallen Stars**: `ae2:meteorite_compass`; `ae2:engineering_processor_press`; `ae2:silicon_press` *(after: HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > What: AE2's inscriber presses are only found in the core of meteorites.
   > How: craft a Meteorite Compass, follow it, and dig to the centre of the sky stone crater. Each meteorite's mysterious cube holds one press.
   > Tip: once you have one press, the Inscriber can copy it with an iron block.
18. **Fluix**: `ae2:charger`; 8x `ae2:fluix_crystal` *(after: HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > What: fluix crystals carry the ME network's signal. The ME Controller needs them.
   > How: charge certus quartz in the Charger, then drop charged certus, redstone and Nether quartz in water together (check JEI).
   > Tip: budding certus quartz grows new crystals, so certus is renewable once you find some.
19. **The Inscriber**: `ae2:inscriber`; 2x `ae2:engineering_processor` *(after: HV: Digital Circuits, Fallen Stars)*
   > What: every AE2 processor is printed in the Inscriber. In this pack it's built on a Turbo hull.
   > Chemistry: engineering processors print a circuit onto silicon, the same element your HV boards depend on.
   > How: press a diamond into a printed engineering circuit, silicon into printed silicon, then combine them with redstone.
   > Tip: the silicon is your MI silicon from the EBF. AE2's certus-to-silicon smelting is removed in this pack.
