28. **A Breath of Noble Gas**: 64x any of `or(item(chemlib:helium)item(chemlib:neon)item(chemlib:argon)item(chemlib:krypton)item(chemlib:xenon)item(chemlib:radon))` *(after: A New World)*
   > What: any 64 noble gas items from ChemLib, in any mix.
   > Chemistry: noble gases have full outer electron shells, so they almost never react. Neon glows red in a discharge tube; xenon glows blue; radon is radioactive.
   > How: Alchemistry Dissolver on air-rich or gas-bearing items, or the Fusion Chamber (check JEI for which inputs give which gas).
   > Tip: helium is the lightest: fuse two hydrogen and you're there.
29. **The Rare Earths**: 64x any of `or(item(chemlib:lanthanum)item(chemlib:cerium)item(chemlib:praseodymium)item(chemlib:neodymium)item(chemlib:promethium)item(chemlib:samarium)item(chemlib:europium)item(chemlib:gadolinium)item(chemlib:terbium)item(chemlib:dysprosium)item(chemlib:holmium)item(chemlib:erbium)item(chemlib:thulium)item(chemlib:ytterbium)item(chemlib:lutetium))` *(after: A Breath of Noble Gas)*
   > What: any 64 lanthanide items from ChemLib: lanthanum through lutetium.
   > Chemistry: the lanthanides fill the 4f electron shell, which sits deep inside the atom. That's why they're so alike and so hard to separate.
   > How: Fusion Chamber (pairs that add up to 57-71) or the Dissolver on rare-earth-bearing items (check JEI).
   > Tip: neodymium makes the strongest permanent magnets; europium makes red phosphors in screens.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Deep dive: why 'rare' earths?
   > They aren't rare. Cerium is about as common as copper in the Earth's crust. They're 'rare' because they never form rich deposits on their own.
   > Separating them took chemists over a century. Their outer electrons are nearly the same, so their chemistry is nearly the same; only the slow shrinking of the atoms across the row (the lanthanide contraction) tells them apart.
   > Industry separates them by solvent extraction, hundreds of stages long. Your Fusion Chamber skips all that.
30. **Island of Stability**: 64x any of `or(item(chemlib:oganesson)item(chemlib:tennessine)item(chemlib:livermorium)item(chemlib:moscovium)item(chemlib:flerovium)item(chemlib:nihonium))` *(after: The Rare Earths)*
   > What: any 64 of the six newest elements: nihonium, flerovium, moscovium, livermorium, tennessine and oganesson.
   > Chemistry: all six were made in the last 25 years, a few atoms at a time, and decay within seconds or less.
   > How: Alchemistry Fusion Chamber. Automate the inputs and let it run.
   > Tip: physicists predict an 'island of stability' near 114 protons and 184 neutrons, where superheavy nuclei might last much longer. No one has reached it yet.
31. **Demigod**: checkmark *(after: The Terraformer, Quantum Armour, A Stack of Atomic Alloy, Your First Singularity, Other Skies, Island of Stability, Echoes)*
   > You don't remember being this any more. You simply are.
   > What: you've planted the Seed, walked every world, built armour from a collapsed star, and held the whole periodic table.
   > Now: build. A city, a garden on Mars, a pocket world for every friend on the server. The tools are yours.
   > The new world is waiting. It's whatever you make it.
32. **Pressure Not Required**: 64x `minecraft:diamond` *(after: Nucleosynthesis)*
   > What: the Nucleosynthesizer turns coal into diamond with 4 mB of antimatter. You found it.
   > Chemistry: both are carbon. Graphite and diamond differ only in how the atoms bond: sheets of rings versus a rigid 3D lattice. Nature needs about 50,000 atmospheres to make the change.
   > Tip: 64 diamonds from 64 coal. Your younger self, swinging an iron pickaxe, would be furious.
33. **Where It Began**: find biome `biomesoplenty:origin_valley` *(after: Rare Ground)*
   > What: Biomes O' Plenty's Origin Valley, built to look like the very first versions of Minecraft.
   > Bright grass, roses, plain old trees. You remember a world this simple. It was the first one you made.
   > Tip: it's rare. If you found it by chance, consider it a gift.
34. **Ultradense Metal Ball**: `modern_industrialization:ultradense_metal_ball` *(after: A New World)*
   > What: the core that 64 nukes crush into a singularity.
   > Chemistry: tungsten, lead and iridium are among the densest metals there are. Iridium and osmium tie for the record at about 22.6 g/cm³, twice as dense as lead.
   > How: Assembler: 4 tungsten large plates, 4 lead plates and 1 iridium plate.
35. **Quantum Sword**: `modern_industrialization:quantum_sword` *(after: Quantum Upgrade)*
   > What: MI's quantum sword: the MI guidebook claims it vaporises anything it hits.
   > How: MI Packer: netherite sword + 1 quantum upgrade, at the same huge draw as the armour (check JEI).
   > Tip: a quantum upgrade is a lot to spend on a sword. Finish the armour first.

## The Demigod's Market

### The Demigod's Market

*Spend your Demigod Tokens: supplies and comforts, never shortcuts.*

1. **The Market**: checkmark *(after: Demigod Tokens)*
   > You remember offerings left at your altar. Now the world pays you in coins instead.
   > What: Demigod Tokens are the reward currency of this book. You trade them for supplies by crafting, with no shopkeeper and no server plugin.
   > How: every shop trade is a shapeless crafting recipe: put tokens in a crafting grid and the item appears.
   > How: the price list is JEI: search Demigod Token and press U (uses). Every trade shows as a crafting recipe. Do the same for the Greater Demigod Token.
   > Tip: the crafting shop sells raw supplies and comforts, never anything that skips a tier. Copies of machines you have already built are in the Machine Shop quests.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > What tokens never buy: the shop skips boring gathering (sand, gravel, string, torches), never learning. If a trade seems missing, it was left out on purpose.
   > Chemistry: a bag of raw ore is not a refinery. Raw tin still needs your crusher, raw titanium still needs your blast furnace.
2. **Where Tokens Come From**: `kubejs:demigod_token` *(after: The Market)*
   > What: almost every quest pays tokens, scaled by tier: 1 per quest at the start, 2 in the steam and Nether chapters, 3 at LV and MV, 4 at HV, 5 at EV, 8 in space.
   > How: milestone quests (the big ones) pay double and also roll that tier's reward table. Optional side quests pay 1 or 2.
   > Tip: on a team, rewards go to each player who claims them, so everyone builds their own purse.
3. **The Price Bands**: checkmark *(after: Where Tokens Come From)*
   > What: the shop has three price bands. Small (1 to 3 tokens): cheap stacks of things you'd otherwise spend an afternoon gathering. Medium and large are on the next pages.
   > How: 1 token: 32 torches, 16 bread, 8 bottles o' enchanting, 32 bone meal, 64 sand, 64 gravel or 32 clay balls.
   > How: 2 tokens: 16 iron ingots, 16 coke, 16 rubber sheets, 16 fire clay dust, 32 salt dust, 16 string, 16 leather or a sleeping bag.
   > How: 3 tokens: 8 osmium ingots, 2 backpack upgrade bases, 16 gunpowder, 16 slime balls, 32 redstone or 16 lapis.
   > Tip: sand and gravel are the best early value: concrete, glass and silicon all start there.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Medium band (4 to 8 tokens): raw ores (you still process them yourself) and drops you would otherwise farm.
   > How: 4 tokens: a Warp Stone, 32 raw copper, 16 raw tin, 16 raw lead, 16 bauxite dust, 32 quartz or 32 glowstone dust.
   > How: 5: 16 raw nickel, 8 ender pearls, 4 phantom membranes, 16 amethyst. 6: 8 blaze rods, 4 ghast tears, 16 certus quartz, 8 source gems.
   > How: 7: 8 raw titanium or 2 name tags. 8: 8 raw tungsten or 32 prismarine shards.
   > Tip: raw ore bought here is worth up to 5x once your Mekanism line is running. Buy late, process well.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Large band (Greater Tokens): the big trades cost Greater Demigod Tokens, not regular ones.
   > How: 1 Greater: 4 golden apples, 4 diamonds, 16 emeralds or a saddle. 2: 2 shulker shells, a heart of the sea or a netherite scrap.
   > How: 3 Greater: a totem of undying or 4 echo shards. 4 Greater: an enchanted golden apple.
   > Tip: shulker shells mean shulker boxes. Many players find that the best trade in the shop.
4. **The Exchange**: `kubejs:greater_demigod_token` *(after: The Price Bands)*
   > What: a Greater Demigod Token is worth 9 Demigod Tokens, and the trade works both ways.
   > How: 9 tokens in a crafting grid make 1 Greater Token. 1 Greater Token alone in the grid gives the 9 back.
   > Tip: late-tier milestones and boss loot sometimes pay Greater Tokens directly.
5. **Market Day: Early**: 10x `kubejs:demigod_token` *(after: The Price Bands, Iron)*
   > What: a reward for saving. Hold 10 Demigod Tokens at once and choose one comfort: a sleeping bag, a Warp Stone, backpack upgrade bases or a saddle.
   > How: the tokens are only checked, not taken. Spend them afterwards if you like.
   > Tip: the Warp Stone is the pick if you explore a lot.
6. **Market Day: Industrial**: 30x `kubejs:demigod_token` *(after: Market Day: Early, Analog Circuit)*
   > What: hold 30 tokens and choose a stack of raw feedstock: tin, lead, nickel, bauxite or salt.
   > How: tokens are checked, not taken.
   > Tip: bauxite is the slow one to find, and aluminium is the gate to MV.
7. **Market Day: Divine**: 64x `kubejs:demigod_token` *(after: Market Day: Industrial, EV: Processing Units)*
   > You remember when worshippers brought you treasures. Now you just keep a full stack.
   > What: hold a full stack of 64 tokens and choose a treasure: a totem, shulker shells, a heart of the sea, an enchanted golden apple or 3 Greater Tokens.
   > How: tokens are checked, not taken. Exchange Greater Tokens back if you need 64 loose ones.
   > Tip: picking the Greater Tokens is the same as taking 27 regular tokens home.
8. **A Dragon's Hoard**: 9x `kubejs:greater_demigod_token` *(after: The Exchange)*
   > What: hold nine Greater Demigod Tokens at once. That's 81 tokens you chose not to spend.
   > Tip: the demigod approves of patience. The demigod also notes that totems exist.
9. **The Machine Shop**: checkmark *(after: The Market)*
   > You remember forges that worked while you slept. Once you know how a thing is made, its copies come cheap.
   > What: repeatable shop quests that sell copies of machines, boilers, tanks, hulls and cables.
   > How: a machine goes on sale only after you finish the quest where you build it yourself. Until then its entry is invisible.
   > How: hold the price and click Submit: the tokens are taken and the machine is yours. Buy again whenever you like.
   > Tip: counters run Steam, LV, MV, HV, EV. From MV up, prices are in Greater Demigod Tokens (9 tokens each). Multiblock controllers are never sold.

   > How: click to open it. Each machine in this row appears once you finish the quest where you build it yourself.
   > Tip: prices at this counter are 3 to 6 tokens.

### Market: Blocks, Food and Wild Goods

*Buy more of the blocks, food and wild goods you've already gathered.*

1. **The World Stall**: checkmark *(after: Demigod Tokens)*
   > You remember the harvest festivals held in your name. The world still sends its gifts.
   > What: this stall sells building blocks, food, crops, saplings, mob drops and the stone and plants of other worlds.
   > How: an item appears here only after the quest where you first got it. Hand in the tokens and claim the bundle; the entry resets so you can buy again.
   > Tip: tokens save gathering, never exploring. Each world's goods only appear once you've been there.
   > Tip: the space stall costs Greater Demigod Tokens (1 Greater = 9 tokens; craft them in a grid).
2. **Overworld Stall**: checkmark *(after: Steam Power)*
   > What: the Steam-age stall: Overworld blocks, crops, saplings and common mob drops.
   > How: entries show up one by one as you finish the quests where you first gathered them.

## Basics

### Gear and Comfort

*Better tools from better materials, and a soft place to land.*

1. **Repair Kits**: `silentgear:crude_repair_kit` *(after: Tools from Parts)*
   > You remember tools that never wore out. These will, but you can mend them.
   > What: Silent Gear tools don't break for good; at zero durability they just stop working until repaired.
   > How: craft a Crude Repair Kit, load it with matching material, then combine it with the tool in a crafting grid.
   > Tip: a better kit (Sturdy, then Crimson and Azure) holds more material and repairs more per use.
2. **Blaze Gold**: 4x `silentgear:blaze_gold_ingot` *(after: Repair Kits, Into the Fire)*
   > What: Silent Gear's first magic alloy. It's a key ingredient of the Material Grader and the Starlight Charger.
   > Chemistry: gold (Au) is a noble metal: it barely reacts with anything, which is why it's found as native nuggets. Blaze gold is fictional; the blaze powder does the work.
   > How: gold ingot + 2 blaze powder in the Alloy Forge, or check JEI for the early crafting route.
   > Tip: keep a stack spare. Blaze gold blocks also go into the Starlight Charger.
3. **Material Grader**: `silentgear:material_grader` *(after: Blaze Gold)*
   > What: grades Silent Gear materials. A higher grade adds a stat bonus to every part made from that material.
   > How: quartz, iron, blaze gold and an Advanced Upgrade Base (check JEI). Feed it materials plus a catalyst (check JEI for which items count).
   > Tip: grade only the materials you'll use for heads and main parts; rods and bindings matter less.
4. **Salvager**: `silentgear:salvager` *(after: Material Grader)*
   > What: breaks old Silent Gear tools back into parts, so upgrading doesn't waste materials.
   > How: place it and drop in the old tool. Some material is lost on each salvage.
   > Tip: salvage before you throw anything in lava; the parts often have most of their value left.
5. **Crimson Iron**: 8x `silentgear:crimson_iron_ingot` *(after: Repair Kits, Into the Fire)*
   > What: crimson iron ore generates in Nether biomes. It's the base of crimson steel and the Alloy Forge.
   > How: mine crimson iron ore in the Nether (Jade shows the name), then smelt the raw ore.
   > Tip: run a few through the Alchemistry Dissolver and see which real elements it gives back.
6. **Crimson Steel**: 4x `silentgear:crimson_steel_ingot` *(after: Crimson Iron)*
   > What: a tough, heat-loving alloy for tool heads and the Alloy Forge frame.
   > Chemistry: real steel is iron with a little carbon (under about 2%); the carbon atoms jam the iron lattice so it can't slip. Crimson steel is the fictional cousin.
   > How: the first ingots are a shaped craft (crimson iron, blaze rods, magma cream); check JEI.
7. **The Alloy Forge**: `silentgear:alloy_forge` *(after: Crimson Steel)*
   > What: mixes metals into Silent Gear alloys: blaze gold, crimson steel (3 per batch), azure electrum and tyrian steel.
   > How: crimson steel ingots, blackstone and an iron block (check JEI). Fuel it like a furnace.
   > Tip: alloying in the forge gives more ingots per batch than the crafting-table route.
8. **Azure Electrum**: 4x `silentgear:azure_electrum_ingot` *(after: The Alloy Forge, The End)*
   > What: azure silver ore generates in the End. Alloyed with gold it becomes azure electrum, a fast, enchantable metal.
   > Chemistry: real electrum is a natural gold–silver alloy (Au–Ag); the ancient Lydians struck the first coins from it.
   > How: azure silver ore needs a netherite-tier pickaxe (netherite, refined obsidian, crimson steel or better; see the Harvest Tiers chapter). Then Alloy Forge: an azure silver block, 2 gold ingots and an ender pearl.
9. **Tyrian Steel**: 4x `silentgear:tyrian_steel_ingot` *(after: Azure Electrum)*
   > What: the top Silent Gear alloy: crimson steel, azure electrum, crushed shulker shell and netherite scrap.
   > Chemistry: Tyrian purple was a real dye made from sea snails, once worth its weight in silver. The steel just borrowed the colour.
   > How: Alloy Forge (check JEI). Crush shulker shells first.
10. **Osmium Paxel**: `mekanismtools:osmium_paxel` *(after: Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser)*
   > What: Mekanism's signature metal as a paxel: more durability and speed than bronze, iron tier for mining.
   > Chemistry: osmium (Os) is the densest natural element at about 22.6 g/cm³, twice as dense as lead.
   > How: osmium ore generates in the Overworld; smelt or process it, then craft the pickaxe, axe and shovel and combine them with a stick (check JEI).
   > Tip: your steel paxel from T1 already mines at diamond tier. This one is about durability and speed.
11. **The Ultimate Paxel**: `mekanismtools:refined_obsidian_paxel` *(after: Osmium Paxel)*
   > You remember a hammer that could split mountains. This is a start.
   > What: refined obsidian is Mekanism's toughest material, and its paxel is the best of the line (netherite tier).
   > How: infuse obsidian dust with diamond in the Metallurgic Infuser, then press the refined obsidian dust in the Osmium Compressor (check JEI).
   > Tip: the same ingots make the Atomic Disassembler and much of Mekanism's late gear.
12. **Atomic Disassembler**: `mekanism:atomic_disassembler` *(after: The Ultimate Paxel)*
   > What: an electric tool that mines, chops and digs, with vein and area modes. It runs on FE instead of durability.
   > How: refined obsidian, atomic alloy, infused alloy and an Energy Tablet (check JEI). Charge it in an energy cube.
   > Tip: sneak + right-click to switch modes.
13. **Bottled Oxygen**: `mekanism:scuba_mask`; `mekanism:scuba_tank` *(after: Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser)*
   > What: the Scuba Mask and Tank let you breathe underwater for as long as the tank has oxygen.
   > Chemistry: the Electrolytic Separator splits water: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂. The O₂ fills the tank; the H₂ is fuel.
   > How: steel, a control circuit and a chemical tank (check JEI). Fill the tank from a Chemical Tank or the separator's oxygen output.
   > Tip: great for ocean monuments and underwater prospecting.
14. **Free Runners**: `mekanism:free_runners` *(after: Bottled Oxygen)*
   > What: electric boots: auto step-up and no fall damage while charged.
   > How: infused alloy, a basic control circuit and an Energy Tablet (check JEI).
   > Tip: the armoured version adds protection; upgrade once you have more alloy.
15. **MekaSuit**: `mekanism:mekasuit_helmet`; `mekanism:mekasuit_bodyarmor` *(after: Free Runners, EV: Processing Units)*
   > You remember armour that was never armour, only certainty. This is the closest a mortal gets.
   > What: Mekanism's modular power armour. Add modules for flight, night vision, magnet, radiation shielding and more.
   > Chemistry: it needs HDPE sheets (polyethylene: long C₂H₄ chains) and polonium pellets. Real ²¹⁰Po is made by hitting bismuth-209 with neutrons; Mekanism makes it from nuclear waste in the Solar Neutron Activator.
   > How: netherite armour, HDPE sheets, ultimate control circuits, polonium pellets and induction cells (check JEI). Install modules in the Modification Station.
16. **Hazmat Gear**: `mekanism:hazmat_mask` *(after: Bottled Oxygen)*
   > What: the full hazmat suit stops Mekanism radiation from building up in you. Cheap and worth having before fission.
   > Chemistry: lead (Pb) is dense and has many electrons, so it absorbs gamma rays well.
   > How: lead ingots and orange dye for each piece (check JEI).
17. **Hydrogen Jetpack**: `mekanism:jetpack` *(after: Bottled Oxygen)*
   > What: Mekanism's jetpack burns hydrogen gas. Short hops, not true flight.
   > Chemistry: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. Burning hydrogen gives only water and a lot of energy.
   > How: steel, tin, a basic control circuit and a chemical tank. Fill it with H₂ from the Electrolytic Separator.
18. **Jetpacks**: `ironjetpacks:basic_coil`; `ironjetpacks:jetpack` *(after: Analog Circuit)*
   > What: Iron Jetpacks run on FE. Every tier needs a coil, and in this pack the coils need MI circuits.
   > How: Basic coil = analog circuit (LV). Craft the coil, then cells, thrusters, strap and the jetpack for your metal (check JEI).
   > Tip: better metals fly faster and hold more FE. Charge it in any energy cube.
19. **Advanced Coil**: `ironjetpacks:advanced_coil` *(after: Jetpacks, MV: Aluminum)*
   > What: unlocks the middle jetpack tiers.
   > How: needs an MI electronic circuit (MV, aluminum chemistry). Check JEI for which jetpacks use it.
   > Tip: JEI shows which jetpacks use this coil.
20. **Elite Coil**: `ironjetpacks:elite_coil` *(after: Advanced Coil, HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > What: faster, longer flights.
   > How: needs an MI digital circuit (HV, polyethylene).
   > Tip: the digital circuit is your polyethylene line paying off; make a few extra.
21. **Ultimate Coil**: `ironjetpacks:ultimate_coil` *(after: Elite Coil, EV: Processing Units)*
   > What: the top jetpack tier.
   > How: needs an MI processing unit (EV, PVC chemistry).
   > Tip: by now the Angel Ring may suit you better; the jetpack still has the best speed.
22. **The Angel Ring**: `angelring:diamond_ring`; `angelring:angel_ring` *(after: Jetpacks, HV: Digital Circuits, The End)*
   > You remember the sky being yours. Now it is again.
   > What: portable creative flight, no fuel, from a Curios ring slot.
   > Chemistry: its MI digital circuit needs polyethylene: n C₂H₄ → (C₂H₄)ₙ, ethylene from your distillation tower.
   > How: Elytra, ghast tears, diamond blocks and Nether Stars plus the digital circuit. Craft the Diamond Ring first, then the Angel Ring.
23. **Hammock**: `comforts:hammock_white` *(after: Rest Anywhere)*
   > What: skips the day the way a sleeping bag skips the night, without moving your spawn.
   > How: white wool, string and sticks. Hang it between two Rope and Nails placed on facing walls (check JEI).
   > Tip: useful when you want night-only mobs, like the ones a Deep Learner needs.
24. **Mining Gadget**: `mininggadgets:mininggadget_simple` *(after: LV Machine Hull)*
   > What: a mining laser that breaks blocks at range. Upgrades add 3x3 (and bigger) size, efficiency, magnet and void filters.
   > How: iron, gold, diamond and redstone (check JEI). Charge it with FE.
   > Tip: a void filter for stone and dirt keeps your inventory clean on long ore runs.
25. **Bindings and Grips**: `silentgear:binding`; `silentgear:grip` *(after: Tools from Parts)*
   > What: bindings and grips are optional Silent Gear parts. Each adds its material's traits and stats to the tool.
   > How: make the Binding and Grip blueprints, then craft the parts from string, vines, leather or wool (check JEI). Add them to a tool in a crafting grid.
   > Tip: the Material Book (or JEI) shows every material's traits. Hover a part to see what it adds.
26. **Coatings**: `silentgear:coating_smithing_template` *(after: Bindings and Grips, Material Grader)*
   > What: a coating covers a finished tool's main part in another material, like diamond or netherite, changing its stats and colour.
   > Chemistry: real tools are coated too: drill bits get a thin layer of titanium nitride (TiN) or diamond to stay sharp much longer.
   > How: craft the coating smithing template (check JEI), then apply the coating material at a smithing table.
27. **Silent Jewellery**: 1x any of `or(item(silentgear:ring)item(silentgear:bracelet)item(silentgear:necklace))` *(after: Bindings and Grips)*
   > What: Silent Gear jewellery carries material traits as curios: a ring of a lucky or magnetic material gives you that trait while worn.
   > How: a ring shank, bracelet band or necklace chain plus a gem setting, made with the matching blueprint (check JEI).
   > Tip: try different metals and gems. The traits list on each material shows what jewellery will do.
28. **Armour from Parts**: 4x any of `or(item(silentgear:helmet)item(silentgear:chestplate)item(silentgear:leggings)item(silentgear:boots))` *(after: Bindings and Grips, Crimson Steel)*
   > What: Silent Gear armour is built from plates of any material, so your best alloy becomes your best armour.
   > How: helmet, chestplate, legging and boot plates from their blueprints, then assemble each piece (check JEI). Any four pieces.
   > Tip: crimson steel and azure electrum plates have strong traits; check the Material Book before choosing.
29. **Primordial Goo**: `justdirethings:gooblock_tier1` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: Just Dire Things goo converts the blocks it touches. Tier 1 goo turns an iron block into raw ferricore ore.
   > How: clay, sugar, rotten flesh and dirt (check JEI). The full goo line, from ferricore to eclipse alloy, is in the Just Dire Things chapter.
   > Tip: JEI's goo tab shows every conversion and which goo tier it needs.
30. **Pocket Generator**: `justdirethings:pocket_generator` *(after: Raw Ferricore)*
   > What: the Pocket Generator burns fuel in your inventory and charges your FE items.
   > How: ferricore, a furnace, coal and a redstone block (check JEI).
   > Chemistry: burning coal is oxidation: C + O₂ → CO₂ releases about 394 kJ per mole of carbon as heat.
31. **Thinking with Portals**: `justdirethings:portalgun` *(after: VoidShimmer and Celestigem)*
   > You remember stepping between places without walking. You'd forgotten how much fun it was.
   > What: the Portal Gun shoots two linked portals onto walls. Walk in one, come out the other.
   > Tip: there is an upgraded Portal Gun too; JEI has its recipe.
32. **Grading Catalysts**: 4x `silentgear:glowing_dust`; 4x `silentgear:blazing_dust` *(after: Material Grader, Hammered Dust)*
   > What: the Material Grader needs a catalyst for each try. Glowing dust is tier 1, blazing dust tier 2; a better catalyst allows a higher grade.
   > Chemistry: a real catalyst speeds a reaction without being used up. These are spent on every try, so 'reagent' would be the honest word.
   > How: glowing dust: a stick, 2 glowstone dust and a quartz (makes 4). Blazing dust: blaze gold dust and 2 glowstone dust (makes 4).
   > Tip: grade the material for a tool head, not the rod; the head carries most of the stats.
33. **Glittery Dust**: 8x `silentgear:glittery_dust` *(after: Grading Catalysts, The End)*
   > What: the best Grader catalyst, for the highest grades.
   > How: popped chorus fruit, emerald nuggets, glowstone dust and a nether banana make 8 (check JEI). Chorus grows in the End; nether bananas grow on netherwood trees.
   > Tip: popped chorus is just chorus fruit smelted in a furnace.
34. **Hammered Dust**: 2x `silentgear:blaze_gold_dust` *(after: Blaze Gold)*
   > What: Silent Gear turns its ingots into dust with a hammer: blaze gold, crimson iron, azure silver and more.
   > Chemistry: grinding a metal to powder hugely raises its surface area. That's why fine metal dusts burn or react so much faster than a solid bar.
   > How: a tool action with any hammer (the c:tools/hammer tag) on the ingot; JEI shows the steps and which block it needs.
   > Tip: blaze gold dust is the tier 1 Starlight Charger catalyst and the base of blazing dust.
35. **Starlight Charger**: `silentgear:starlight_charger` *(after: Hammered Dust)*
   > What: the Starlight Charger collects starlight at night and charges Silent Gear materials, giving them a 'charged' bonus.
   > How: quartz blocks, glass, polished blackstone and a blaze gold block (check JEI). Place it under open sky, add a catalyst (blaze gold dust is tier 1) and the item.
   > Tip: the catalyst tier sets how strong the charge can get; JEI's tag view lists each tier.
36. **Starmetal**: 2x `silentgear:azure_silver_dust`; 3x `silentgear:starmetal_dust` *(after: Azure Electrum, Hammered Dust, The Wither)*
   > What: starmetal dust is a late Silent Gear material made from azure metals and a Nether Star fragment.
   > Chemistry: every atom heavier than iron was forged in dying stars or neutron-star collisions. Real 'starmetal' is just... metal.
   > How: azure electrum dust, 2 azure silver dust, blaze gold dust and a nether star fragment make 3 (check JEI). Hammer the ingots into dust first.
   > Tip: one Nether Star crafts into 9 fragments, so a single Wither kill goes a long way.
37. **Recrystallizer**: `silentgear:recrystallizer` *(after: Azure Electrum)*
   > What: the Recrystallizer fuses gems and dusts into a hybrid gem material whose stats depend on what you put in.
   > Chemistry: real recrystallisation purifies a solid: dissolve it hot, cool slowly, and pure crystals grow while impurities stay in the liquid.
   > How: azure electrum ingots, an emerald, a diamond, purpur blocks and a gold block (check JEI).
   > Tip: the Material Book explains hybrid gems; experiment with cheap gems first.
38. **A Metallurgist's Shelf**: `silentgear:crimson_steel_block`; `silentgear:azure_electrum_block`; `silentgear:tyrian_steel_block` *(after: Tyrian Steel)*
   > Three alloys, three blocks, each one a recipe you wrote yourself. You remember a forge like this.
   > What: a storage block of crimson steel, azure electrum and tyrian steel: Silent Gear's three great alloys, side by side.
   > Chemistry: alloys aren't mixtures you can see: the atoms share one crystal lattice. Bronze, steel and electrum are all solid solutions or mixed phases at the atomic scale.
   > How: nine ingots of each make a block (check JEI).

### Tools, Armour and Harvest Tiers

*Which pickaxe mines what, and why harder is not the same as tougher.*

1. **The Hardness of Things**: checkmark *(after: Sticks and a Wooden Pick)*
   > Once you could split a mountain with a look. Now you need the right pick. You remember why: everything has a hardness.
   > What: every ore needs a pickaxe of a certain tier: wood, stone, iron, diamond, netherite. Too weak a pick breaks the block slowly and drops nothing.
   > Chemistry: hardness is resistance to scratching and denting; toughness is resistance to cracking. A good tool needs both, and they pull against each other.
   > How: look at a block: Jade shows the tool it needs and turns red when yours is too weak. This page walks up the tiers.
   > Tip: this pack raises some tiers: MI titanium, tungsten, platinum and iridium ores need iron, and the rocket metals climb from iron to netherite.
2. **Flint**: 4x `minecraft:flint` *(after: The Hardness of Things)*
   > What: flint drops from gravel. Silent Gear makes tool heads from it, and it lights the Nether portal.
   > Chemistry: flint and chert are microcrystalline quartz, SiO₂, about 7 on the Mohs scale: harder than steel. It breaks with a curved, shell-like (conchoidal) fracture that leaves a razor edge.
   > How: dig gravel with a shovel; each block has a small chance to drop flint instead.
   > Tip: a Silent Gear pickaxe with a flint head mines like stone, but you can repair and upgrade it.
3. **Stone Tier**: 8x `minecraft:raw_iron`; 8x `minecraft:raw_copper` *(after: The Hardness of Things, Stone Age)*
   > What: a stone pickaxe (or better) opens iron, copper and lapis, plus almost every Modern Industrialization and Mekanism ore: tin, lead, nickel, antimony, bauxite, salt, monazite, uranium, osmium and fluorite.
   > Chemistry: a stone pick is a rock hitting a rock. It works on iron ore because the iron minerals (haematite Fe₂O₃, magnetite Fe₃O₄) are softer than the granite-like stone of the head... roughly.
   > How: mine 8 raw iron and 8 raw copper with any stone-tier pick.
   > Tip: you can't mine gold, redstone or diamond yet. Mark where you saw them and come back with iron.
4. **Bronze Age**: 8x `modern_industrialization:raw_tin` *(after: Stone Tier, The First Alloy)*
   > What: bronze tools are iron tier (Mekanism bronze, Silent Gear bronze): more durable than stone, and they reach gold, redstone and diamond.
   > Chemistry: pure copper is soft, about Mohs 3. Add roughly 12% tin and the bigger tin atoms sit in the copper lattice and pin the defects (dislocations) that let metal bend. That is solid-solution strengthening, and it started an age.
   > How: mine 8 raw tin. Tin ore needs only a stone pick; its mineral, cassiterite (SnO₂), is actually harder than iron ore.
   > Tip: the bronze paxel (Bronze Age on the T0 page) is a pick, axe and shovel in one.
5. **Iron Tier**: 4x `minecraft:raw_gold`; 8x `minecraft:redstone`; `minecraft:diamond` *(after: Stone Tier, Iron Pickaxe)*
   > Iron rings against stone, and something in you rings back. You remember iron.
   > What: an iron-tier pick opens gold, redstone, diamond and emerald, Create zinc, AE2 sky stone, Silent Gear crimson iron, and in this pack the hard MI ores: titanium, tungsten, platinum and iridium.
   > Chemistry: pure iron is soft (about Mohs 4). Iron from a blast furnace (pig iron) carries about 4% carbon as brittle iron carbide, so it shatters. Useful iron sits between the two.
   > How: mine 4 raw gold, 8 redstone and a diamond with an iron pickaxe, iron paxel, bronze or osmium tools.
   > Tip: diamonds sit deep (near Y -58). Branch-mine in deepslate.
6. **Hard Ores**: 4x `modern_industrialization:raw_tungsten` *(after: Iron Tier)*
   > What: in this pack MI titanium, tungsten, platinum and iridium ores need an iron-tier pick. The metals inside still need the chemistry lines.
   > Chemistry: their real minerals are hard: wolframite ((Fe,Mn)WO₄) about 4-4.5, ilmenite (FeTiO₃) 5-6, sperrylite (PtAs₂) 6-7. Tungsten itself melts at 3422 °C, higher than any other metal.
   > How: mine 4 raw tungsten. Rich tungsten deposits sit at their own depth; check the ore pages in JEI.
   > Tip: a stone pick on these ores gets you nothing but a broken block. Bring iron.
7. **Diamond Tier, Without Diamonds**: 4x `minecraft:obsidian`; `minecraft:crying_obsidian` *(after: Iron Tier, Steel Paxel)*
   > You remember quenching a blade in a cold river, and the hiss of it.
   > What: Mekanism steel tools are diamond tier. Your steel paxel already mines obsidian, crying obsidian and ancient debris, long before you own a diamond pick.
   > Chemistry: steel is iron with 0.2-2% carbon. Heat it red hot and quench it in water and it becomes martensite: very hard, but brittle. Temper it (reheat to 200-600 °C) and it trades a little hardness for toughness.
   > How: mine 4 obsidian and a crying obsidian with the steel paxel (or any diamond-tier tool). Obsidian forms where water meets lava.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Chemistry: obsidian isn't actually hard: it's volcanic glass, mostly SiO₂ that cooled too fast to crystallise, about Mohs 5.5. It snaps to edges sharper than steel, which is why surgeons still sometimes use obsidian blades.
   > Tip: the game makes obsidian slow to mine for its blast resistance, not its hardness. Real obsidian shatters under a hammer.
8. **Netherite Tier**: 4x `minecraft:netherite_scrap`; `minecraft:netherite_upgrade_smithing_template` *(after: Diamond Tier, Without Diamonds, Into the Fire)*
   > What: a netherite-tier tool opens Silent Gear azure silver ore (the End), Mekanism Extras naquadah ore and, much later, Ad Astra calorite.
   > Chemistry: netherite is fiction. The real champion of hard tools is tungsten carbide (WC, Mohs about 9), cemented with a little cobalt so it doesn't shatter: a ceramic-metal composite, or cermet.
   > How: smelt ancient debris into scrap; four scrap and four gold make a netherite ingot. The upgrade template comes from bastion chests.
   > Tip: copy a template with 7 diamonds and a netherrack before you use your last one.
9. **Azure Silver**: 4x `silentgear:raw_azure_silver` *(after: Netherite Tier, The End)*
   > What: azure silver ore grows on End islands and needs a netherite-tier tool. It's the base of Silent Gear's azure electrum.
   > How: mine 4 raw azure silver in the End with a netherite, refined obsidian or eclipse alloy pick.
   > Tip: a diamond pick just bounces off it; check the Jade tooltip first.
10. **Refined Obsidian**: 2x `mekanism:ingot_refined_obsidian` *(after: Diamond Tier, Without Diamonds, Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser)*
   > What: refined obsidian tools are netherite tier, no Nether trip needed. They're also Mekanism Tools' strongest set.
   > Chemistry: infusing osmium into obsidian dust is invented, but the idea is real: cermets (ceramic grains in a metal binder) are what drill bits and cutting inserts are made of.
   > How: Metallurgic Infuser: obsidian dust + diamond infusion → refined obsidian dust, then the Osmium Compressor (check JEI).
   > Tip: the refined obsidian paxel is on the Tools page; the armour is on the Mekanism page.
11. **Beyond Netherite**: 16x `undergarden:dreadrock` *(after: Netherite Tier, The Undergarden, Forgotten Tools)*
   > Harder was never the whole answer. You remember a stone that only its own metal could cut.
   > What: dreadrock and its utherium and rogdorium ores need a Forgotten tool. Netherite fails here: dreadrock is on its 'can't mine' list.
   > Chemistry: 'harder' is not one number. A cutting edge has to out-scratch the mineral, survive the impact and not wear or react away. A diamond bit cuts granite but dissolves into hot steel, because carbon diffuses into iron.
   > How: mine 16 dreadrock at the bottom of the Undergarden with a Forgotten pickaxe.
   > Tip: warden and resonarium tools (Deeper and Darker) also mine it.
12. **Ores of Other Worlds**: checkmark *(after: Diamond Tier, Without Diamonds, One Small Step)*
   > What: in this pack the rocket metals climb the ladder: Moon desh needs an iron pick, Mars ostrum a diamond-tier pick, Venus calorite a netherite-tier pick.
   > Chemistry: the three are fiction, but real space mining would face the same problem: unknown minerals, unknown hardness. Geologists still carry a steel knife and a glass plate to test them.
   > How: bring a netherite-tier tool on every trip past the Moon. The desh, ostrum and calorite quests are on the T7 and Space pages.
   > Tip: a refined obsidian paxel covers all three and doesn't need the Nether.
13. **Every Block**: 1x any of `or(item(mekanism:atomic_disassembler)item(mekanism:meka_tool)item(deeperdarker:warden_pickaxe))` *(after: Refined Obsidian)*
   > No block refuses you now. You remember this: not strength, but understanding.
   > What: the Atomic Disassembler, the Meka-Tool and the warden pickaxe have no 'can't mine' list. They break every block in the pack, dreadrock included.
   > Chemistry: an energy tool doesn't scratch. It's closer to a laser or plasma cutter: put enough energy into a spot and the bonds break whatever the hardness.
   > How: the Atomic Disassembler is on the Tools page, the Meka-Tool on the Mekanism page, the warden pickaxe on the Deeper and Darker page. Any one of them counts.
   > Tip: energy tools need charging; keep a charger or an Energy Cube near your base.
14. **Lapis Tools**: 1x any of `or(item(mekanismtools:lapis_lazuli_pickaxe)item(mekanismtools:lapis_lazuli_paxel))` *(after: Stone Tier)*
   > What: Mekanism Tools makes a lapis pickaxe and paxel. They mine at stone tier but enchant very well.
   > Chemistry: lapis lazuli is a rock, not one mineral: mostly lazurite (a sodium aluminosilicate with sulfur) about Mohs 5-5.5. The blue comes from S₃⁻ radical ions trapped in the crystal.
   > How: lapis and sticks, shaped like any pick (check JEI).
   > Tip: ground lapis was ultramarine, once worth more than gold to painters.
15. **Iron-Tier Cousins**: 1x any of `or(item(justdirethings:ferricore_pickaxe)item(twilightforest:ironwood_pickaxe)item(undergarden:cloggrum_pickaxe)item(mekanismtools:bronze_pickaxe)item(mekanismtools:osmium_pickaxe)item(mekanismtools:osmium_paxel))` *(after: Iron Tier)*
   > What: each of these mines exactly what an iron pick does: ferricore (Just Dire Things), ironwood (Twilight), cloggrum (Undergarden), bronze and osmium (Mekanism Tools).
   > Chemistry: osmium is the densest element (22.6 g/cm³) and quite hard, but brittle: real osmium is almost never used for tools, only for tiny wear-proof tips like old pen nibs.
   > How: craft any one of them; their mods' pages show the recipes.
   > Tip: durability and speed differ a lot between them even at the same tier. Check the tooltip.
16. **Diamond Pickaxe**: `minecraft:diamond_pickaxe` *(after: Iron Tier)*
   > What: the vanilla road to diamond tier: obsidian, crying obsidian and ancient debris. Also the base for Mystical Agriculture tools.
   > Chemistry: diamond is carbon with every atom bonded to four neighbours in a 3D network (sp³). It's Mohs 10, the hardest natural material, but it cleaves along flat planes: a sharp knock in the right direction splits it.
   > How: three diamonds and two sticks.
   > Tip: a steel paxel (T1) is already diamond tier. Spend early diamonds on machines, not picks, if you're short.
17. **Diamond-Tier Cousins**: 1x any of `or(item(mekanismtools:steel_pickaxe)item(mekanismtools:refined_glowstone_pickaxe)item(mekanismtools:refined_glowstone_paxel)item(justdirethings:blazegold_pickaxe)item(justdirethings:celestigem_pickaxe)item(twilightforest:steeleaf_pickaxe)item(twilightforest:knightmetal_pickaxe)item(undergarden:utherium_pickaxe)item(modern_industrialization:steam_mining_drill))` *(after: Diamond Tier, Without Diamonds)*
   > What: all of these are diamond tier: Mekanism steel and refined glowstone, JDT blazegold and celestigem, Twilight steeleaf and knightmetal, Undergarden utherium, and MI's Steam Mining Drill.
   > Chemistry: the Steam Mining Drill is honest engineering: a hardened bit turned by a steam engine. Real drill bits use tungsten carbide or industrial diamond tips on a tough steel body.
   > How: craft any one of them; each mod page and JEI have the recipe.
   > Tip: the steam drill burns fuel instead of wearing out, and digs 3x3. Its tooltip lists the modes.
18. **Netherite Pickaxe**: `minecraft:netherite_pickaxe` *(after: Netherite Tier, Diamond Pickaxe)*
   > What: the vanilla netherite-tier pick. Upgrading keeps every enchantment on your diamond pick.
   > How: smithing table: netherite upgrade template + diamond pickaxe + netherite ingot.
   > Tip: netherite items float in lava and don't burn. Drop one in the Nether and it can be fished back out.
19. **Netherite-Tier Cousins**: 1x any of `or(item(mekanismtools:refined_obsidian_pickaxe)item(mekanismtools:refined_obsidian_paxel)item(mekanismtools:netherite_paxel)item(justdirethings:eclipsealloy_pickaxe)item(justdirethings:eclipsealloy_paxel)item(twilightforest:fiery_pickaxe)item(modern_industrialization:diesel_mining_drill))` *(after: Netherite Tier)*
   > What: all netherite tier: Mekanism refined obsidian and netherite paxel, JDT eclipse alloy, Twilight fiery, MI's Diesel Mining Drill. A Silent Gear pick with a crimson steel, azure electrum or tyrian steel head counts too (its tier comes from the head).
   > Chemistry: fiery metal is 'quenched' in fiery blood; real metallurgists do the same with oil, brine or polymer baths to control how fast the steel cools.
   > How: craft any one of the listed tools (check JEI).
   > Tip: the diesel drill is listed on the T5 page as part of Diesel Toys.
20. **A Grown Pickaxe**: 1x any of `or(item(mysticalagriculture:inferium_pickaxe)item(mysticalagriculture:prudentium_pickaxe)item(mysticalagriculture:tertium_pickaxe)item(mysticalagriculture:imperium_pickaxe)item(mysticalagriculture:supremium_pickaxe))` *(after: Diamond Pickaxe)*
   > What: Mystical Agriculture tools have no 'can't mine' list: even an inferium pick breaks azure silver, naquadah and dreadrock.
   > How: a diamond pickaxe with two inferium ingots and two inferium gemstones around it (check JEI). Higher essences make it faster, not 'higher tier'.
   > Tip: it still can't give you the metal: the ores need the same chemistry lines as ever.
21. **Fast and Useless**: `minecraft:golden_pickaxe` *(after: Stone Tier)*
   > What: a golden pick mines faster than any vanilla pick, but only at wood tier and with almost no durability.
   > Chemistry: gold is about Mohs 2.5-3: a fingernail nearly scratches it. Real gold is so soft it's alloyed with copper or silver for jewellery (18 carat is 75% gold).
   > How: three gold ingots and two sticks.
   > Tip: enchant it with Silk Touch and it's a quick glass and ice collector.
22. **Bronze Armour**: `mekanismtools:bronze_helmet`; `mekanismtools:bronze_chestplate`; `mekanismtools:bronze_leggings`; `mekanismtools:bronze_boots` *(after: Bronze Age)*
   > What: Mekanism Tools bronze armour is a touch better than iron, and it saves your iron for machines.
   > Chemistry: Bronze Age armour really was bronze, often hammered cold: working the metal (work hardening) piles up dislocations and makes it harder still.
   > How: 24 bronze ingots, shaped like any armour set. MI bronze counts (it's a c:ingots/bronze ingot).
23. **Steel Armour**: `mekanismtools:steel_helmet`; `mekanismtools:steel_chestplate`; `mekanismtools:steel_leggings`; `mekanismtools:steel_boots` *(after: Diamond Tier, Without Diamonds)*
   > What: Mekanism Tools steel armour: better than iron, from the steel you already make in MI.
   > Chemistry: real plate armour was hardened on the outside and left soft inside (case hardening): a hard face to stop blades, a tough core so it dents instead of cracking.
   > How: 24 steel ingots, shaped like any armour set (any c:ingots/steel counts).
24. **Diamond Armour**: `minecraft:diamond_helmet`; `minecraft:diamond_chestplate`; `minecraft:diamond_leggings`; `minecraft:diamond_boots` *(after: Iron Tier)*
   > What: the full vanilla diamond set: the step before netherite, and the base you'll upgrade.
   > Chemistry: real diamond armour would be a disaster: diamond is hard but brittle, and a solid plate would crack on the first heavy blow. Real body armour stacks hard ceramic plates (boron carbide, B₄C) on tough fibres.
   > How: 24 diamonds. If that hurts, make the steel set first and come back.
25. **Netherite Armour**: `minecraft:netherite_helmet`; `minecraft:netherite_chestplate`; `minecraft:netherite_leggings`; `minecraft:netherite_boots` *(after: Netherite Tier, Diamond Armour)*
   > Your skin is mortal now, so you wear the strongest shell the world allows. You remember not needing one.
   > What: the full vanilla netherite set: the best plain armour, with knockback resistance and immunity to burning up in lava as an item.
   > How: smithing table, one piece at a time: template + diamond piece + netherite ingot. Four templates, four ingots.
   > Tip: copy templates with diamonds and netherrack so you never run out.
26. **Bastion Remnant**: find structure `minecraft:bastion_remnant` *(after: Netherite Tier)*
   > What: every bastion has a netherite upgrade template in its chests, often gold blocks and ancient debris too.
   > How: find a bastion in the Nether (anywhere except basalt deltas) and step inside.
   > Tip: piglin brutes don't care about gold armour. Bring a shield and a bow.
27. **The Scratch Test**: `minecraft:calcite`; `chemlib:calcium_sulfate`; `mekanism:fluorite_gem`; `chemlib:hydroxylapatite`; `minecraft:quartz`; `chemlib:aluminum_oxide`; `minecraft:diamond` *(after: Iron Tier)*
   > What: in 1812 Friedrich Mohs ranked ten minerals by which scratches which. Seven of them exist here.
   > Chemistry: gypsum CaSO₄·2H₂O (2), calcite CaCO₃ (3), fluorite CaF₂ (4), apatite Ca₅(PO₄)₃(OH) (5), quartz SiO₂ (7), corundum Al₂O₃ (9), diamond C (10). Talc (1), orthoclase (6) and topaz (8) are missing.
   > How: calcite in dripstone caves and amethyst geodes; fluorite from Mekanism ore; nether quartz; diamond. Calcium sulfate, hydroxylapatite and aluminium oxide come from the Alchemistry machines (check JEI).
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Chemistry: the scale only ranks, it doesn't measure. Diamond (10) is about four times harder than corundum (9), while corundum is only a bit harder than topaz (8).
   > Tip: a fingernail is about 2.5, a copper coin 3.5, a steel knife 5.5, window glass 5.5. That's the field geologist's whole kit.
28. **Hard Rock, Soft Ore**: checkmark *(after: The Scratch Test)*
   > What: the ores you mine have real hardnesses, and they don't line up with the game's tiers at all.
   > Chemistry: galena (PbS, lead ore) 2.5; bauxite 1-3; fluorite 4; wolframite 4-4.5; uraninite (UO₂) 5-6; ilmenite 5-6; cassiterite (SnO₂) 6-7; sperrylite (PtAs₂) 6-7. Tin ore is harder than iron ore, yet the game puts it lower.
   > How: read it, then click the check.
   > Tip: real miners don't pick ore apart by hand: they blast the rock and crush it, then separate by density and froth flotation.
29. **Green Beryl**: 4x `minecraft:emerald` *(after: Iron Tier)*
   > What: emerald ore is iron tier; in the Overworld it only appears in mountain biomes.
   > Chemistry: emerald is beryl, Be₃Al₂Si₆O₁₈, Mohs 7.5-8, coloured green by a trace of chromium or vanadium. Pure beryl is colourless; iron makes it blue (aquamarine).
   > How: mine 4 emeralds with an iron pick, or trade with villagers.
   > Tip: beryllium from beryl makes copper-beryllium alloy: hard, and it doesn't spark, so it's used for tools near explosives.
30. **Tungsten Carbide**: 2x `modern_industrialization:tungsten_dust` *(after: Hard Ores)*
   > What: the real material that nearly every drill bit and cutting insert on Earth is made of.
   > Chemistry: heat tungsten powder with carbon at 1400-2000 °C: W + C → WC. Tungsten carbide is about Mohs 9 and keeps its hardness when red hot. Pressed with 6-12% cobalt as a binder it becomes 'cemented carbide', hard and tough at once.
   > How: macerate raw tungsten into 2 tungsten dust.
   > Tip: tungsten carbide is about twice as dense as steel. Pick up a carbide drill bit and it feels wrong.
31. **Wooden Tools**: `minecraft:wooden_sword`; `minecraft:wooden_axe`; `minecraft:wooden_shovel` *(after: The Hardness of Things)*
   > What: the full wooden set: weak, cheap, and a fine fuel once it wears out.
   > Chemistry: wood is a natural composite: long cellulose fibres, (C₆H₁₀O₅)ₙ chains of glucose, glued together by lignin. It's strong along the grain and splits easily across it.
   > How: planks and sticks, shaped like any tool.
   > Tip: a broken wooden tool burns in a furnace for as long as a plank. Nothing goes to waste.
32. **Soft Gold**: 8x `minecraft:gold_ingot`; `minecraft:golden_sword` *(after: Iron Tier)*
   > What: a golden sword hits about as hard as a wooden one and wears out faster. Piglins like it, though.
   > Chemistry: gold is the most malleable metal: one gram can be beaten into a leaf about a square metre wide and a few hundred atoms thick. Great for leaf, useless for an edge.
   > How: smelt 8 gold ingots from raw gold (needs an iron-tier pick), then craft the sword.
   > Tip: wearing one piece of gold armour keeps most piglins calm in the Nether.
33. **Diamond Sword and Shovel**: `minecraft:diamond_sword`; `minecraft:diamond_shovel` *(after: Diamond Pickaxe)*
   > What: the diamond sword is the vanilla weapon to beat until netherite; the shovel digs sand and gravel at speed.
   > Chemistry: real diamond blades exist: diamond scalpels cut with an edge only a few nanometres wide. They're kept for eye surgery because one sideways knock can chip them.
   > How: two diamonds and a stick for the sword, one diamond and two sticks for the shovel.
   > Tip: enchant before you upgrade to netherite: the enchantments carry over.
34. **Netherite Sword**: `minecraft:netherite_sword` *(after: Netherite Tier, Diamond Sword and Shovel)*
   > What: the strongest vanilla sword, and it can't burn up in lava.
   > How: smithing table: netherite upgrade template + diamond sword + netherite ingot.
   > Tip: copy a template with 7 diamonds and a netherrack first, so the sword doesn't cost your last one.
35. **Mekanism Blades**: 1x any of `or(item(mekanismtools:bronze_sword)item(mekanismtools:lapis_lazuli_sword)item(mekanismtools:osmium_sword)item(mekanismtools:steel_sword)item(mekanismtools:refined_glowstone_sword)item(mekanismtools:refined_obsidian_sword))` *(after: Bronze Age)*
   > What: Mekanism Tools makes a sword in every one of its metals: bronze, lapis, osmium, steel, refined glowstone and refined obsidian. Any one counts.
   > Chemistry: a good sword is a compromise. Hard steel keeps an edge; soft steel bends instead of snapping. Japanese smiths welded both into one blade and quenched it with clay on the spine.
   > How: two ingots (or gems) of the metal and a stick, like any sword (check JEI).
   > Tip: refined obsidian is the best of the set; steel is the cheapest one worth carrying.
36. **Lapis Armour**: `mekanismtools:lapis_lazuli_helmet`; `mekanismtools:lapis_lazuli_chestplate`; `mekanismtools:lapis_lazuli_leggings`; `mekanismtools:lapis_lazuli_boots` *(after: Lapis Tools)*
   > What: Mekanism Tools lapis armour protects about as well as chainmail but takes enchantments very well.
   > Chemistry: the blue of lapis is the S₃⁻ radical ion caged in lazurite. Grind it, wash out the grey minerals, and you have ultramarine pigment.
   > How: 24 lapis lazuli, shaped like any armour set (check JEI).
   > Tip: a cheap set to practise enchanting on while your diamonds go into machines.
37. **A Full Leather Set**: `minecraft:leather_helmet`; `minecraft:leather_leggings` *(after: Leather Armour)*
   > What: the helmet and leggings that finish the leather set from Getting Started. Leather can be dyed any colour.
   > Chemistry: leather is tanned hide: tannins (plant polyphenols) or chromium(III) salts cross-link the collagen protein chains, so the skin stops rotting and stays flexible.
   > How: 5 leather for the cap, 7 for the leggings. Craft a piece with dye to colour it; a water cauldron washes the dye out.
   > Tip: leather boots let you walk on powder snow without sinking.
38. **Armour for a Friend**: `minecraft:wolf_armor`; 2x `minecraft:armadillo_scute` *(after: A Full Leather Set)*
   > What: wolf armour soaks up damage for a tamed wolf. When it cracks, repair it with scutes.
   > Chemistry: scutes are keratin plates, the same protein as hair, horn and nails. Disulfide (S–S) bridges between the chains make keratin tough; that's also why burning hair smells of sulfur.
   > How: brush an armadillo (savanna and badlands) with a brush for scutes. 6 scutes make the armour; keep 2 for repairs.
   > Tip: right-click a tamed wolf with the armour to put it on. Dye it if you like.
39. **Barding**: 1x any of `or(item(minecraft:leather_horse_armor)item(minecraft:iron_horse_armor)item(minecraft:golden_horse_armor)item(minecraft:diamond_horse_armor))` *(after: A Full Leather Set)*
   > What: horse armour, any kind. Leather horse armour can be crafted and dyed; iron, gold and diamond only turn up in chests.
   > How: 7 leather for the leather one, or loot dungeons, temples, villages and Ancient Cities for the metal ones.
   > Tip: Farmer's Delight Horse Feed heals a horse and speeds it up (Farming page).

### Storage and Logistics

*A god needs somewhere to keep things.*

1. **Sophisticated Barrel**: `sophisticatedstorage:barrel` *(after: A Backpack)*
   > You remember vaults that held the stars. A barrel is humbler, but it's a start.
   > What: Sophisticated Storage chests and barrels take upgrades, just like your backpack. Sophisticated Storage Plus raises their limits.
   > How: craft a wooden barrel (check JEI). Tier upgrades improve it in place later.
   > Tip: barrels keep their contents when broken, so moving a full one is easy.
2. **Tier Upgrades**: `sophisticatedstorage:basic_to_iron_tier_upgrade` *(after: Sophisticated Barrel)*
   > What: tier upgrades turn a placed chest or barrel into the next tier (copper, iron, gold, diamond, netherite) without moving items.
   > How: craft the upgrade (check JEI) and right-click it on the placed container.
   > Tip: you can skip tiers with the direct upgrades, like basic → iron.
3. **Compacting**: `sophisticatedstorage:compacting_upgrade` *(after: Tier Upgrades)*
   > What: the Compacting Upgrade squeezes 9 nuggets into an ingot and 9 ingots into a block as items arrive.
   > Chemistry: a block holds the same metal atoms as 9 ingots; only the packing changes, so no mass is lost either way.
   > How: craft it (check JEI) and put it in an upgrade slot. Add a filter so it only compacts what you choose.
4. **Storage Controller**: `sophisticatedstorage:controller`; 2x `sophisticatedstorage:storage_link` *(after: Compacting)*
   > What: the Controller joins touching Sophisticated containers into one inventory; Storage Links extend its reach.
   > How: place it next to your chests and barrels. Pipes into the controller reach every connected container.
   > Tip: one pipe into the controller is a simple sorting system: items go where matching items already are.
5. **Drawers**: `functionalstorage:oak_1` *(after: Sophisticated Barrel)*
   > What: Functional Storage drawers hold lots of a single item and show it on the front.
   > How: craft an oak drawer (1, 2 or 4 slots; check JEI). Right-click to insert, left-click to take.
   > Tip: upgrades (copper, gold, diamond, netherite) multiply drawer capacity.
6. **Compacting Drawer**: `functionalstorage:compacting_drawer` *(after: Drawers)*
   > What: a compacting drawer stores nuggets, ingots and blocks of one metal as a single pool, and hands out whichever you ask for.
   > How: craft it (check JEI), then insert the item you want to track.
   > Tip: perfect for copper and tin near your bronze setup.
7. **Drawer Controller**: `functionalstorage:storage_controller` *(after: Compacting Drawer)*
   > What: the Storage Controller links nearby drawers into one inventory you (and pipes) can use.
   > How: place it among your drawers. Use the Linking Tool to add drawers further away.
   > Tip: a Controller Extension gives you a second access point.
8. **An Early Network**: `toms_storage:storage_terminal`; `toms_storage:inventory_connector` *(after: Drawers)*
   > What: Tom's Simple Storage connects your chests into one searchable terminal. It's your network until AE2.
   > How: place an Inventory Connector touching your chests (or link them with Inventory Cables), and a Storage Terminal on it.
   > Tip: point it at a drawer controller and every drawer shows up in the terminal.
9. **Crafting Terminal**: `toms_storage:crafting_terminal` *(after: An Early Network)*
   > What: a terminal with a crafting grid that pulls ingredients from the network. JEI's + button fills it for you.
   > How: upgrade a Storage Terminal (check JEI).
   > Tip: a Wireless Terminal (also in JEI) lets you use it from across the base.
10. **Faster Furnaces**: `ironfurnaces:iron_furnace` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: Iron Furnaces are faster furnaces in metal tiers. A generator augment turns one into a small FE source.
   > Chemistry: smelting iron ore is a reduction: carbon pulls the oxygen off, Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂.
   > How: ring a furnace with iron (check JEI). Upgrade kits move it up a tier without breaking it.
11. **Pipez**: 8x `pipez:item_pipe` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: simple pipes for moving items, fluids and energy between non-MI machines.
   > How: place a line from source to target, then set the end touching the source to extract (the pipe tooltip explains how).
   > Tip: MI machines have their own pipes; Pipez is best for everything else.
12. **LaserIO**: 2x `laserio:laser_node` *(after: Pipez, LV Machine Hull)*
   > What: Laser Nodes move items, fluids and energy between machines without cables.
   > How: place nodes on machines, link them with the Laser Wrench, and add cards to set what moves (check JEI).
   > Tip: one node can serve all six faces of a block, great for compact chemical setups.
13. **Entangled**: checkmark *(after: Iron, Sophisticated Barrel)*
   > What: an Entangled Block is a window into another inventory: bind it to a chest or machine, and anything put in the Entangled Block goes into the bound block, even across dimensions.
   > How: ender pearls, obsidian and a wooden chest (check JEI). Right-click the target with the Entangled Binder (pearls, obsidian and a diamond), then right-click the Entangled Block. Click the checkmark when one is working.
   > Tip: put one next to a remote ore processor and pipe the output straight home. Both chunks must be loaded.
14. **Storage in Motion**: `sophisticatedstorageinmotion:storage_minecart` *(after: Tier Upgrades)*
   > What: Sophisticated Storage in Motion puts upgradeable chests and barrels on minecarts, boats and rafts, upgrades and all.
   > How: combine a minecart with a Sophisticated chest or barrel (check JEI). Boats and rafts work the same way.
   > Tip: a hopper upgrade on a storage minecart makes a simple ore train between your mine and base.
15. **Stack Upgrades**: `sophisticatedstorage:stack_upgrade_tier_1` *(after: Tier Upgrades)*
   > What: stack upgrades multiply how many items fit in each slot of a chest or barrel. Higher tiers multiply more.
   > How: an upgrade base and storage blocks (check JEI). Insert it in an upgrade slot.
   > Tip: a barrel with a few stack upgrades holds a whole mine's worth of cobblestone or raw ore.
16. **Drawer Upgrades**: `functionalstorage:diamond_upgrade` *(after: Drawer Controller)*
   > What: storage upgrades multiply a drawer's capacity. Each tier (copper, gold, diamond, netherite) holds more.
   > How: craft the upgrades in order (check JEI) and right-click the drawer to open its upgrade slots.
   > Tip: the Iron Downgrade does the reverse, limiting a drawer to a single stack per slot.
17. **Pullers and Pushers**: `functionalstorage:puller_upgrade`; `functionalstorage:pusher_upgrade` *(after: Drawer Upgrades)*
   > What: utility upgrades: the Puller pulls items from the block it faces, the Pusher pushes items into it. No pipes needed.
   > How: check JEI. Put one in a drawer's utility slot and set its direction in the drawer's menu.
   > Tip: a drawer with a Puller behind a macerator collects all the dust without a single pipe.
18. **Fluid Drawers**: `functionalstorage:fluid_1` *(after: Drawer Upgrades)*
   > What: fluid drawers store a fluid instead of items, and show it on the front.
   > Chemistry: handy for small stocks of acids: one drawer of H₂SO₄, one of HCl, one of HNO₃. A real lab keeps acids in separate, labelled containers too.
   > How: check JEI. Pipes and MI fluid pipes can fill and drain them; the storage upgrades work on them too.
19. **Ender Drawer**: `functionalstorage:ender_drawer` *(after: Drawer Upgrades)*
   > What: every Ender Drawer with the same frequency shares one inventory, wherever it is.
   > How: check JEI. Link drawers with the Linking Tool to give them the same frequency.
   > Tip: put one at your mine and one at your smelters to send ore home.
20. **Inventory Cables**: 16x `toms_storage:inventory_cable`; `toms_storage:inventory_cable_connector` *(after: An Early Network)*
   > What: inventory cables carry the Inventory Connector's reach to chests that aren't touching it.
   > How: run cables from the connector and put a Cable Connector on each chest or drawer (check JEI).
   > Tip: framed cables can wear any block's texture, so they hide in walls.
21. **Wireless Terminal**: `toms_storage:adv_wireless_terminal` *(after: Crafting Terminal)*
   > What: the Advanced Wireless Terminal opens your Tom's network from a long way off.
   > How: check JEI, then right-click it on a Storage Terminal to bind it.
   > Tip: it's the cheapest remote storage access until AE2.
22. **Sophisticated Chests**: `sophisticatedstorage:chest` *(after: Sophisticated Barrel)*
   > What: Sophisticated chests take the same tier upgrades and upgrade cards as the barrels.
   > How: craft a wooden chest version (check JEI). Tier upgrades work on it in place.
   > Tip: the Decoration Table re-skins chests and barrels with any wood or block, so your storage room can match your base.
23. **Sophisticated Shulker Box**: `sophisticatedstorage:shulker_box` *(after: Sophisticated Chests, The End)*
   > What: a shulker box that takes tier upgrades and upgrade cards, and keeps everything inside when you pick it up.
   > How: a chest, two shulker shells and a lever (check JEI). Shulkers live in End cities.
   > Tip: a shulker box with a compacting upgrade is a portable ore bank for long mining trips.
24. **Netherite Storage**: 1x any of `or(item(sophisticatedstorage:netherite_barrel)item(sophisticatedstorage:netherite_chest))` *(after: Stack Upgrades, Ancient Debris)*
   > What: the netherite tier has the most slots and upgrade slots of any Sophisticated container.
   > How: a diamond-to-netherite tier upgrade on a placed diamond chest or barrel (check JEI).
   > Tip: upgrade the containers you use most first; a netherite barrel full of stack upgrades holds a staggering amount.
25. **Limited Barrels**: `sophisticatedstorage:limited_barrel_1`; `sophisticatedstorage:limited_barrel_4` *(after: Sophisticated Barrel)*
   > What: limited barrels have one to four big slots and show their items on the front, like drawers, but take Sophisticated upgrades.
   > How: check JEI for each size. They use the same tier upgrades as normal barrels.
   > Tip: a four-slot limited barrel per metal (ore, dust, ingot, block) makes a tidy wall.
26. **Hopper Upgrade**: `sophisticatedstorage:hopper_upgrade` *(after: Tier Upgrades)*
   > What: the Hopper Upgrade pulls items from one side and pushes them out another, with filters.
   > How: an upgrade base, a hopper, iron and redstone (check JEI). Set directions and filters in the container's upgrade tab.
   > Tip: a barrel with a hopper upgrade under a machine's output collects everything without pipes.
27. **Compression Upgrade**: `sophisticatedstorage:compression_upgrade` *(after: Compacting)*
   > What: the Compression Upgrade links a few slots so nuggets, ingots and blocks of one material count as a single stock.
   > How: an upgrade base, pistons, iron and redstone (check JEI). Choose which slots it uses in the upgrade tab.
   > Tip: take out exactly the form you need: blocks for storage, ingots for crafting, nuggets for small recipes.
28. **Storage Input and Output**: `sophisticatedstorage:storage_input`; `sophisticatedstorage:storage_output` *(after: Storage Controller)*
   > What: Storage Input only accepts items into the controller's containers; Storage Output only lets them out. Pipes and hoppers use them like any inventory.
   > How: a wooden storage block, gold, planks and a repeater (check JEI). Place them touching the controller's group.
   > Tip: put an Input at the end of your ore line and an Output by your crafting area, so the two never mix.
29. **Storage Tool**: `sophisticatedstorage:storage_tool` *(after: Storage Input and Output)*
   > What: the Storage Tool links containers to a controller without touching it and toggles settings like locks and displays.
   > How: an ender pearl, iron, sticks and a redstone torch (check JEI). Its tooltip lists each mode.
   > Tip: locked slots keep their item type even when empty, so a sorting system never fills them with junk.
30. **Gold Backpack**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:gold_backpack` *(after: Iron Backpack)*
   > What: the gold backpack adds inventory rows and upgrade slots over the iron one.
   > How: surround an iron backpack with eight gold ingots. Everything inside stays put.
   > Tip: this pack's upgrade base is also sold in the Demigod Token shop (search "Demigod Token" in JEI).
31. **Diamond Backpack**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:diamond_backpack` *(after: Gold Backpack)*
   > What: the diamond backpack is the tier before netherite: even more rows and upgrade slots.
   > How: surround a gold backpack with eight diamonds. Netherite comes after it (see Netherite Backpack on the QoL page).
   > Tip: spend the extra slots on stack upgrades first; they multiply every slot at once.
32. **Everlasting**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:everlasting_upgrade` *(after: Diamond Backpack, The Wither, The End)*
   > What: with the Everlasting Upgrade, a dropped backpack can't burn, explode or despawn.
   > How: an upgrade base, nether stars and end crystals (check JEI). That means beating the Wither and visiting the End.
   > Tip: worth it before reactor work or deep Nether trips, where a lost pack hurts most.
33. **Crafting Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:crafting_upgrade` *(after: Backpack Upgrades)*
   > What: adds a 3x3 crafting grid to the backpack screen that can use the backpack's own items.
   > How: an upgrade base, a crafting table, iron and a chest (check JEI).
   > Tip: JEI's + button fills the backpack grid straight from the backpack.
34. **Smelting on the Go**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:smelting_upgrade`; `sophisticatedbackpacks:auto_smelting_upgrade` *(after: Crafting Upgrade)*
   > What: the Smelting Upgrade is a furnace in the backpack screen. The Auto-Smelting Upgrade smelts matching items inside the backpack by itself, using fuel from the backpack.
   > Chemistry: smelting iron ore is a reduction: carbon monoxide strips the oxygen off the ore, Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂.
   > How: an upgrade base and a furnace for the first; the auto version adds a hopper, gold, redstone and a diamond (check JEI).
   > Tip: filter auto-smelting to raw ores only, or it will smelt your logs into charcoal too.
35. **Void Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:void_upgrade` *(after: Smelting on the Go)*
   > What: the Void Upgrade destroys chosen items as they enter the backpack: cobblestone, dirt, gravel, rotten flesh.
   > Chemistry: real matter can't vanish (mass is conserved in every chemical reaction). In Minecraft, it can.
   > How: an upgrade base, ender pearls, obsidian and redstone (check JEI). Set the filter carefully.
   > Tip: keep a stack of cobblestone out of the filter. You'll want it for building and for the Matter Condenser later.
36. **Deposit and Restock**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:deposit_upgrade`; `sophisticatedbackpacks:restock_upgrade` *(after: Void Upgrade)*
   > What: with a Deposit Upgrade, using the backpack on a chest puts matching items into it. A Restock Upgrade does the reverse, topping up the backpack from the chest.
   > How: an upgrade base, a chest, iron, redstone and a piston (sticky for restock). Check JEI.
   > Tip: deposit ores into your processing chest, restock torches and food from your supply chest, all in two clicks.
37. **Tank Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:tank_upgrade` *(after: Deposit and Restock)*
   > What: the Tank Upgrade stores fluid inside the backpack. Fill and empty it with buckets or tanks from its upgrade tab.
   > Chemistry: a real acid needs the right container: HF eats glass, so it's kept in PTFE; concentrated H₂SO₄ can sit in steel. A backpack tank isn't fussy.
   > How: an upgrade base surrounded by glass (check JEI).
   > Tip: a tank of water means you're never stuck in a lava cave without a way to cool it into obsidian.
38. **Speed and Fuel Augments**: `ironfurnaces:augment_speed`; `ironfurnaces:augment_fuel` *(after: Faster Furnaces)*
   > What: augments go in an Iron Furnace's augment slot. Speed cooks faster but burns more fuel; Fuel Efficiency does the opposite.
   > How: stone, redstone and paper around sugar (speed) or coal (fuel). Check JEI.
   > Tip: speed for ores you need now, fuel efficiency for slow bulk jobs like glass or charcoal.
39. **Furnace Generator**: `ironfurnaces:augment_generator` *(after: Speed and Fuel Augments)*
   > What: the Generator Augment turns an Iron Furnace into a small FE generator that burns furnace fuel.
   > Chemistry: burning carbon releases about 394 kJ per mole: C + O₂ → CO₂. Every generator, from a furnace to a power plant, turns that heat into work.
   > How: stone, redstone and paper around a repeater (check JEI). Put it in the augment slot and pull FE from the furnace.
   > Tip: a few generator furnaces on charcoal can run the Alchemistry Dissolver before MI's electric age.
40. **Factory and Blasting**: `ironfurnaces:augment_factory`; `ironfurnaces:augment_blasting` *(after: Furnace Generator)*
   > What: the Factory Augment gives a furnace several input slots that smelt side by side. The Blasting Augment makes it work like a blast furnace (the Smoking Augment like a smoker).
   > How: stone, redstone and paper around a piston (factory) or a blast furnace (blasting). Check JEI.
   > Tip: a factory furnace runs on FE, so put it next to your generator furnaces.
41. **Gold Furnace**: `ironfurnaces:gold_furnace` *(after: Faster Furnaces)*
   > What: each furnace tier cooks faster than the last: iron, gold, diamond, emerald, obsidian, netherite.
   > Chemistry: gold melts at 1064 °C, lower than iron (1538 °C). It's here for its glitter, not its heat resistance.
   > How: gold ingots and a gold block around an Iron Furnace (check JEI).
42. **Diamond Furnace**: `ironfurnaces:diamond_furnace` *(after: Gold Furnace)*
   > What: the diamond furnace is a big step up in speed.
   > Chemistry: diamond is pure carbon, and it burns: heated in air to about 900 °C it turns into CO₂, like coal does.
   > How: diamonds and glass around a Gold Furnace (check JEI).
43. **Emerald Furnace**: `ironfurnaces:emerald_furnace` *(after: Diamond Furnace)*
   > What: the emerald furnace is faster than diamond, and the base for the obsidian tier.
   > Chemistry: emerald is the mineral beryl, Be₃Al₂Si₆O₁₈, coloured green by a trace of chromium.
   > How: emeralds around a Diamond Furnace (check JEI). Villager trading is the easy source of emeralds.
44. **Obsidian Furnace**: `ironfurnaces:obsidian_furnace` *(after: Emerald Furnace, Blaze Rods)*
   > What: the obsidian furnace needs Nether blaze rods and is faster again.
   > Chemistry: obsidian is volcanic glass: lava, mostly SiO₂, cooled so fast that no crystals could form.
   > How: obsidian and blaze rods around an Emerald Furnace (check JEI).
45. **Netherite Furnace**: `ironfurnaces:netherite_furnace` *(after: Obsidian Furnace, Ancient Debris)*
   > You remember fire that answered to you. This one comes close.
   > What: the netherite furnace is the top of the normal Iron Furnaces line.
   > How: netherite ingots, magma cream and a soul fire block around an Obsidian Furnace (check JEI).
   > Tip: use upgrade kits on a placed furnace so you keep its augment and settings.
46. **Silver Furnace**: `ironfurnaces:silver_furnace` *(after: Faster Furnaces, Ore Byproducts)*
   > What: the silver furnace is a side tier between iron and gold, made with silver ingots.
   > Chemistry: silver (Ag) is the best conductor of heat and electricity of any element, better even than copper.
   > How: silver ingots and glass around an Iron Furnace (check JEI). Silver dust comes from ore byproducts in the MI Centrifuge.
47. **Upgrade Kits**: `ironfurnaces:upgrade_gold`; `ironfurnaces:upgrade_diamond` *(after: Gold Furnace)*
   > What: upgrade kits turn a placed furnace into the next tier and keep its contents, augment and settings.
   > How: each kit is the next tier's materials around a block (check JEI). Right-click the placed furnace with it.
   > Tip: kits are cheaper than crafting a new furnace when you have a whole row to upgrade.
48. **Barrels and Trapped Chests**: 2x `minecraft:barrel`; `minecraft:trapped_chest` *(after: Somewhere to Put Things)*
   > What: a barrel holds as much as a chest and opens even with a block on top. A trapped chest gives a redstone signal while someone has it open.
   > How: barrel: planks and slabs. Trapped chest: a chest and a tripwire hook (check JEI).
   > Tip: a trapped chest next to a door makes a cheap 'is anyone in my lab?' alarm.
49. **Ender Chest**: `minecraft:ender_chest` *(after: Barrels and Trapped Chests, A Door of Fire)*
   > What: every Ender Chest you open shows the same 27 slots, and only you can see yours.
   > How: 8 obsidian around an eye of ender.
   > Tip: keep spare tools and a water bucket in it; any Ender Chest becomes an emergency kit.
50. **Hoppers**: 2x `minecraft:hopper` *(after: Barrels and Trapped Chests, Iron)*
   > What: a hopper pulls items from the container above it and pushes them into the one it points at.
   > How: 5 iron ingots around a chest (Utilitarian also has a log recipe; check JEI).
   > Tip: a redstone signal locks a hopper, which makes simple item gates.
51. **On Rails**: 32x `minecraft:rail`; `minecraft:minecart`; `minecraft:chest_minecart`; `minecraft:hopper_minecart` *(after: Hoppers)*
   > What: minecarts move players and items along rails. A chest minecart carries cargo; a hopper minecart loads and unloads it.
   > Chemistry: steel rails on steel wheels have very low rolling resistance, which is why one locomotive can pull thousands of tonnes.
   > How: rails from iron and sticks; carts from 5 iron; combine a cart with a chest or a hopper (check JEI). Add powered rails to keep them moving.
   > Tip: a hopper under the track at your base empties every chest cart that rolls over it.
52. **Simple Compacting Drawer**: `functionalstorage:simple_compacting_drawer` *(after: Compacting Drawer)*
   > What: the simple version handles two forms of one item (ingot and block, say) instead of three.
   > How: check JEI. Insert the item you want it to track.
   > Tip: good for things with no nugget form, like coal and coal blocks.
53. **Drawer Tools**: `functionalstorage:configuration_tool`; `functionalstorage:linking_tool` *(after: Drawer Controller)*
   > What: the Configuration Tool locks drawers to their item and changes how the front displays. The Linking Tool adds far-away drawers to a controller.
   > How: check JEI for both. Sneak-use cycles the tool's mode; the mode shows on the item.
   > Tip: lock every drawer in a sorting wall, so an empty drawer still only accepts its own item.
54. **Controller Access Point**: `functionalstorage:controller_extension` *(after: Drawer Tools)*
   > What: an access point works like the controller itself: pipes and players can use the whole drawer network through it.
   > How: check JEI, then link it with the Linking Tool.
   > Tip: one access point by the smelters, one by the crafting bench.
55. **Copper and Gold Upgrades**: `functionalstorage:copper_upgrade`; `functionalstorage:gold_upgrade` *(after: Drawer Upgrades)*
   > What: the first two capacity upgrades, before diamond. Each one multiplies how much a drawer holds.
   > Chemistry: copper (8.96 g/cm³) and gold (19.3 g/cm³) are both soft and malleable, which is why they were the first metals people worked.
   > How: copper: copper ingots and blocks, chests and a drawer. Gold builds on copper (check JEI).
56. **Netherite Drawer Upgrade**: `functionalstorage:netherite_upgrade` *(after: Copper and Gold Upgrades, Ancient Debris)*
   > What: the top drawer upgrade. One drawer holds an absurd amount of a single item.
   > How: smithing table: netherite upgrade template + diamond upgrade + netherite ingot.
   > Tip: save it for cobblestone, raw ore or dust, the things you have tens of thousands of.
57. **Void and Downgrade**: `functionalstorage:void_upgrade`; `functionalstorage:iron_downgrade` *(after: Drawer Upgrades)*
   > What: the Void Upgrade destroys whatever doesn't fit, so a full drawer never backs up a pipe. The Iron Downgrade limits a drawer to one stack per slot.
   > How: both are drawer upgrades (check JEI).
   > Tip: a void-upgraded cobblestone drawer at the end of a quarry line keeps everything flowing.
58. **Upgrade Base**: 2x `sophisticatedstorage:upgrade_base` *(after: Sophisticated Barrel)*
   > What: every Sophisticated Storage upgrade card starts from an upgrade base.
   > How: planks and iron ingots in a checker pattern. The backpack mod has its own base; JEI shows both.
   > Tip: make a few at a time; you'll want stack, hopper and compacting upgrades soon.
59. **Copper Tier**: `sophisticatedstorage:basic_to_copper_tier_upgrade` *(after: Tier Upgrades)*
   > What: the copper tier sits between wood and iron: a few more slots for a little copper.
   > Chemistry: copper tarnishes green: over years it forms a patina of basic copper carbonate, Cu₂CO₃(OH)₂, which then protects the metal underneath.
   > How: right-click the placed container with the tier upgrade (check JEI).
60. **Gold and Diamond Tiers**: `sophisticatedstorage:iron_to_gold_tier_upgrade`; `sophisticatedstorage:gold_to_diamond_tier_upgrade` *(after: Tier Upgrades)*
