   > What: tier upgrades for an iron container to gold, then gold to diamond. More slots and more upgrade slots each time.
   > How: check JEI, then right-click the placed chest or barrel. Nothing inside moves.
   > Tip: upgrade the barrel your ore line feeds first; it fills fastest.
61. **The Netherite Tier Kit**: `sophisticatedstorage:diamond_to_netherite_tier_upgrade` *(after: Gold and Diamond Tiers, Ancient Debris)*
   > What: turns a placed diamond chest or barrel into netherite: the most slots any Sophisticated container gets.
   > How: a lever and a netherite ingot, shapeless.
   > Tip: upgrade in place and every item and upgrade card inside stays where it was.
62. **Copper Backpack**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:copper_backpack` *(after: A Backpack)*
   > What: the copper backpack sits between leather and iron: a few more slots and an extra upgrade slot.
   > How: surround your backpack with copper ingots (check JEI). Everything inside stays put.
   > Tip: copper is plentiful early, so this is the cheapest upgrade in the line.
63. **Bigger Stacks**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:stack_upgrade_tier_2`; 1x any of `or(item(sophisticatedbackpacks:stack_upgrade_tier_3)item(sophisticatedbackpacks:stack_upgrade_tier_4))` *(after: Stack Upgrade)*
   > What: each stack tier multiplies how many items fit in every backpack slot. Tier 2 and either tier 3 or 4.
   > How: each tier is built from the one before with better materials (check JEI).
   > Tip: a backpack full of stacked dust is the cheapest way to move a day's mining to your machines.
64. **Compacting and Filters**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:compacting_upgrade`; `sophisticatedbackpacks:filter_upgrade` *(after: Backpack Upgrades)*
   > What: the Compacting Upgrade squeezes 9 of something into its block as you pick it up. The Filter Upgrade decides what pipes and hoppers may put in or take out.
   > How: an upgrade base with pistons, iron and redstone (compacting), or with string and redstone (filter). Check JEI.
   > Tip: compact redstone, lapis and coal while mining; whole blocks take a ninth of the space.
65. **Advanced Pickup**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_pickup_upgrade`; `sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_magnet_upgrade`; `sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_filter_upgrade` *(after: Compacting and Filters, Gold Backpack)*
   > What: the advanced versions of pickup, magnet and filter: more filter slots, plus filters by tag, mod or durability.
   > How: each one is its basic upgrade with gold, diamonds and redstone (check JEI).
   > Tip: a tag filter for 'c:raw_materials' picks up every raw ore in the pack with one entry.
66. **Advanced Everything**: 2x any of `or(item(sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_feeding_upgrade)item(sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_refill_upgrade)item(sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_restock_upgrade)item(sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_deposit_upgrade)item(sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_void_upgrade)item(sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_tool_swapper_upgrade)item(sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_compacting_upgrade)item(sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_pump_upgrade))` *(after: Advanced Pickup)*
   > What: almost every upgrade has an advanced form with more slots and finer filters: feeding, refill, restock, deposit, void, tool swapper, compacting, pump. Any two.
   > How: the basic upgrade plus gold, diamonds and redstone (check JEI for each).
   > Tip: advanced feeding can be set to eat only when it won't waste food, so meals last longer.
67. **Smoker and Blast Furnace**: 1x any of `or(item(sophisticatedbackpacks:smoking_upgrade)item(sophisticatedbackpacks:blasting_upgrade))`; 1x any of `or(item(sophisticatedbackpacks:auto_smoking_upgrade)item(sophisticatedbackpacks:auto_blasting_upgrade))` *(after: Smelting on the Go)*
   > What: smoking upgrades cook food twice as fast; blasting upgrades smelt ores twice as fast. The auto versions work by themselves.
   > Chemistry: a blast furnace forces air through the fuel, so it burns hotter. Real ones blow hot air into the bottom of a coke-and-ore stack: C + O₂ → CO₂, then CO₂ + C → 2CO, and the CO reduces the ore.
   > How: an upgrade base with a smoker or a blast furnace, iron and redstone; the auto ones add hoppers, gold and diamonds (check JEI).
   > Tip: one of each, not both furnace upgrades: they share the backpack's fuel.
68. **Pumps**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:pump_upgrade`; `sophisticatedbackpacks:xp_pump_upgrade` *(after: Tank Upgrade)*
   > What: the Pump Upgrade fills and empties the backpack's tank from the world or from tanks. The XP Pump stores your experience and gives it back.
   > How: pump: an upgrade base with buckets, glass, a piston and a sticky piston. XP pump: an advanced pump upgrade with ender eyes, bottles o' enchanting and redstone (check JEI).
   > Tip: bank your levels in the XP pump before a risky fight; a grave keeps items, not levels.
69. **Battery Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:battery_upgrade` *(after: Crafting Upgrade, Forge Energy)*
   > What: stores Forge Energy in the backpack, which other upgrades and charging tools can use.
   > Chemistry: a battery stores energy as chemistry: two electrodes with different appetites for electrons, kept apart by an electrolyte.
   > How: an upgrade base with gold ingots and redstone blocks (check JEI).
   > Tip: charge it at home, then top up your jetpack or Mining Gadget in the field.
70. **Stonecutter Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:stonecutter_upgrade` *(after: Crafting Upgrade)*
   > What: the Stonecutter Upgrade adds a stonecutter to the backpack screen.
   > How: an upgrade base with a stonecutter, iron and redstone (check JEI).
   > Tip: perfect for Create Deco, Rechiseled and laboratory blocks on a building trip.
71. **Inception**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:inception_upgrade` *(after: Diamond Backpack, The Wither)*
   > What: with the Inception Upgrade, backpacks stored inside your backpack keep using their own upgrades, and you can open them from the outer one.
   > How: an upgrade base with ender eyes, diamonds and a Nether Star (check JEI).
   > Tip: a small 'mining' backpack inside your main one keeps its magnet and void settings separate.
72. **Mixtape**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:jukebox_upgrade` *(after: Crafting Upgrade)*
   > You remember a time when the spheres sang to you. A jukebox in a backpack will have to do.
   > What: the Jukebox Upgrade plays music discs from inside your backpack, wherever you walk.
   > Tip: it plays to everyone nearby. Choose your disc with care.
73. **Copper Furnace**: `ironfurnaces:copper_furnace` *(after: Fire)*
   > What: the copper furnace is a small step faster than vanilla, and the cheapest Iron Furnace.
   > Chemistry: copper conducts heat about five times better than iron, which is why good saucepans have copper bottoms.
   > How: 8 copper ingots around a furnace.
74. **Crystal Furnace**: `ironfurnaces:crystal_furnace` *(after: Diamond Furnace)*
   > What: a side tier from diamond: as fast as a diamond furnace, built of clear glass.
   > Chemistry: glass lets visible light through because its electrons need more energy than visible light carries to jump up, so the photons pass straight through.
   > How: clear glass and an eye of ender around a diamond furnace (check JEI).
75. **Every Kit**: 2x any of `or(item(ironfurnaces:upgrade_copper)item(ironfurnaces:upgrade_iron)item(ironfurnaces:upgrade_iron2)item(ironfurnaces:upgrade_gold2)item(ironfurnaces:upgrade_silver)item(ironfurnaces:upgrade_silver2)item(ironfurnaces:upgrade_emerald)item(ironfurnaces:upgrade_crystal)item(ironfurnaces:upgrade_obsidian)item(ironfurnaces:upgrade_obsidian2)item(ironfurnaces:upgrade_netherite))` *(after: Upgrade Kits)*
   > What: there's a kit for every step: vanilla to copper or iron, copper to iron, iron to gold or silver, diamond to emerald or crystal, up to netherite. Any two.
   > How: each is the next tier's material around a stone tool material or gem (check JEI).
   > Tip: kits keep the furnace's augment, so upgrade a generator furnace without losing its setup.
76. **Smoking Augment**: `ironfurnaces:augment_smoking` *(after: Factory and Blasting)*
   > What: turns an Iron Furnace into a smoker: food only, at double speed.
   > Chemistry: smoking preserves meat: phenols and other compounds in wood smoke kill microbes and slow the fats going rancid.
   > How: stone, redstone and paper around a smoker.
77. **Wireless Heat**: `ironfurnaces:heater`; `ironfurnaces:item_heater` *(after: Factory and Blasting)*
   > What: the Wireless Heat Transmitter takes FE; a Wireless Heat Receiver bound to it goes into a furnace's fuel slot and heats it with that energy. Iron tier and up.
   > How: the transmitter is stone, a comparator, a redstone block and a furnace; the receiver is stone, redstone and a comparator. Bind the receiver to the transmitter (check its tooltip).
   > Tip: one transmitter on your power line, receivers in a whole row of furnaces: no coal ever again.
78. **Settings Linker**: `ironfurnaces:item_copy` *(after: Faster Furnaces)*
   > What: the Furnace Settings Linker copies a furnace's side and redstone settings onto other furnaces.
   > How: paper around a furnace (check JEI). Use it on the configured furnace, then on the others.
   > Tip: set up one furnace's input and output sides, then copy it down the whole row.
79. **The Rainbow Furnace**: 8x `ironfurnaces:rainbow_plating`; `ironfurnaces:rainbow_core`; `ironfurnaces:million_furnace` *(after: Netherite Furnace, Crystal Furnace, Silver Furnace, Copper Furnace)*
   > Every colour of fire at once. You remember when a flame would do whatever you asked.
   > What: the Rainbow Furnace is the top of Iron Furnaces, built from one of every other furnace.
   > Chemistry: flame colours are real chemistry: copper burns green, sodium yellow, strontium red, potassium lilac. Each element's electrons emit their own wavelengths (that's how fireworks get their colours).
   > How: rainbow plating is iron, gold, diamond, emerald, obsidian, crystal, copper and silver furnaces, shapeless (makes 8). The core is a netherite furnace in rainbow glass. 8 plating around the core makes the furnace.

### Power

*Energy is chemistry too: combustion, gas burning, fission and fusion.*

1. **Choosing Your Power**: checkmark *(after: Forge Energy)*
   > You remember holding lightning. For now, the generator you built in T1 will do.
   > What: this page lists the pack's power options by row: combustion, storage, MI steam and EU, Powah, renewables and nuclear. Pick the lines that suit your base; most are optional.
   > Chemistry: every generator turns some stored energy into current: chemical bonds (C + O₂ → CO₂), sunlight, wind, heat, or the nucleus itself.
   > How: start from the Generator Galore generator you made for Forge Energy (FE), the power most mods share. Click the checkmark to open the page.
   > Tip: MI machines run on EU, Modern Industrialization's own electricity (the MI steam and EU row). Most other mods run on FE.
2. **A Faster Burn**: `generatorgalore:gold_generator` *(after: Choosing Your Power)*
   > What: the next Generator Galore tier: it burns fuel faster and makes more FE per tick.
   > How: upgrade from the iron generator (check JEI for the recipe).
   > Tip: a faster burn needs a steadier fuel supply. Pipe in charcoal from a tree farm.
3. **Generator Collector**: `generatorgalore:diamond_generator`; `generatorgalore:culinary_generator`; `generatorgalore:magmatic_generator`; `generatorgalore:halitosis_generator` *(after: A Faster Burn)*
   > What: a diamond-tier generator plus three that burn strange fuels.
   > How: each one's tooltip and JEI page show what it burns. The Halitosis Generator wants dragon's breath, so plan an End trip.
   > Tip: the Culinary Generator eats spare food. Hook it to a farm's overflow.
4. **Bio Fuel**: `mekanismgenerators:bio_generator` *(after: Heat Generator)*
   > What: Mekanism's Bio-Generator burns Bio Fuel.
   > Chemistry: plants store sunlight as sugars and cellulose. Burning them releases it, and the CO₂ is the same CO₂ the plant took in.
   > How: crush seeds and crops into Bio Fuel in a Mekanism Crusher.
5. **Burning Hydrogen**: `mekanismgenerators:gas_burning_generator` *(after: Choosing Your Power, Mekanism Gases)*
   > What: the Gas-Burning Generator turns flammable gas into FE.
   > Chemistry: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O + energy. The only exhaust is water.
   > How: pipe hydrogen from your Electrolytic Separator in with pressurized tubes.
   > Tip: electrolysis costs more energy than burning hydrogen returns. Use it to store spare power, not to make it.
6. **Diesel Generators**: `modern_industrialization:mv_diesel_generator` *(after: Choosing Your Power, Diesel Power)*
   > What: MI generators that burn the fuels from your distillation tower.
   > Chemistry: diesel is a mix of hydrocarbons around C₁₂ to C₂₀. Long chains pack lots of C-H bonds, and lots of energy.
   > How: pipe diesel into the generator and cable it to your machines.
7. **Large Diesel Generator**: `modern_industrialization:large_diesel_generator` *(after: Diesel Generators, HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > What: a multiblock diesel generator for real factories.
   > How: the 3D layout is in JEI and the MI guidebook. It needs fluid input and energy output hatches.
   > Tip: refined fuels (like boosted diesel) burn for more EU per bucket. Check JEI.
8. **Heat Generator**: `mekanismgenerators:heat_generator` *(after: Choosing Your Power, Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser)*
   > What: Mekanism's first generator. It burns fuel and turns heat into FE.
   > How: place lava next to it for a passive bonus, and feed it fuel for more.
   > Tip: lava from a pump makes this a decent passive generator early on.
9. **Store It**: `mekanism:basic_energy_cube` *(after: Heat Generator)*
   > What: energy cubes hold FE so short spikes don't stall your machines.
   > How: put one between your generators and machines. Configure its sides with the Configurator.
   > Tip: cubes upgrade in place: craft the next tier around the old one.
10. **Bigger Cubes**: `mekanism:advanced_energy_cube` *(after: Store It, MV: Aluminum)*
   > What: the Advanced Energy Cube holds and moves much more energy.
   > How: a basic cube with infused alloy, osmium ingots and energy tablets around it (check JEI). Upgrading in place keeps the stored energy.
   > Tip: Elite and Ultimate cubes follow the same pattern with reinforced and atomic alloys.
11. **Evaporation Ponds**: `mekanism:thermal_evaporation_controller`; `mekanism:brine_bucket` *(after: Bigger Cubes)*
   > What: the Thermal Evaporation Plant boils water down into brine, and brine down into liquid lithium.
   > Chemistry: real lithium comes from salt flats: brine sits in ponds until the water evaporates and the salts concentrate.
   > How: a multiblock tower of Thermal Evaporation Blocks, Valves and one Controller. See Just Enough Mekanism Multiblocks in JEI.
   > Tip: taller towers and more heat run faster. Feed it plain water.
12. **Lithium**: 8x `mekanism:dust_lithium` *(after: Evaporation Ponds)*
   > What: lithium dust, for induction cells (and later, tritium).
   > Chemistry: lithium is the lightest metal and gives up its electron easily, which is why lithium-ion batteries store so much energy for their weight.
   > How: run brine through the plant again for liquid lithium. Turn it into gas in a Rotary Condensentrator, then crystallise it in a Chemical Crystallizer.
   > Tip: check JEI with R on Lithium Dust to confirm each step.
13. **Induction Matrix**: 16x `mekanism:induction_casing`; `mekanism:induction_port`; `mekanism:basic_induction_cell`; `mekanism:basic_induction_provider` *(after: Lithium)*
   > Power stored, waiting, obedient. This feels familiar.
   > What: a hollow multiblock battery. Cells inside set how much it stores; providers set how fast it charges and discharges.
   > How: casings form the shell (Structural Glass works for the walls), ports move energy in and out. Layout: Just Enough Mekanism Multiblocks.
   > Tip: switch one port to output with the Configurator. Start small; you can rebuild it larger later.
14. **Wireless Grid**: `fluxnetworks:basic_flux_storage`; `fluxnetworks:flux_plug`; `fluxnetworks:flux_point` *(after: Induction Matrix, EV: Processing Units)*
   > What: Flux Networks sends power through the air: Plugs take it in, Points give it out, Storage buffers it.
   > How: the Flux Core needs an MI processing unit (EV) in this pack. Link all devices to one network in their GUI.
   > Tip: put a Flux Plug on your induction matrix's output port and every Point on the network draws from it.
15. **EU Storage**: `modern_industrialization:lv_storage_unit` *(after: Choosing Your Power, LV Machine Hull)*
   > What: MI's storage unit holds EU, Modern Industrialization's electricity.
   > How: built from redstone batteries, battery alloy plates and an LV hull. Put it between your turbine and your machines.
   > Tip: a buffer lets your steam turbine keep running while machines are idle.
16. **MV Steam Turbine**: `modern_industrialization:mv_steam_turbine` *(after: EU Storage, MV: Aluminum)*
   > What: a bigger steam turbine that outputs MV power.
   > Chemistry: a turbine converts the energy of hot, expanding steam into rotation, then a generator turns rotation into current.
   > How: assemble it from an MV hull, aluminum rotors and large motors (check JEI).
17. **Transformers**: `modern_industrialization:lv_mv_transformer` *(after: MV Steam Turbine)*
   > What: a transformer moves energy between two neighbouring voltage tiers (LV and MV here).
   > How: place it between an MV cable and your LV machines (or the other way round). Check which face is which in its tooltip.
   > Tip: real grids do the same: high voltage for transmission, low voltage at the socket.
18. **HV Steam Turbine**: `modern_industrialization:hv_steam_turbine` *(after: Transformers, HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > What: the HV steam turbine, for HV machine lines.
   > How: check JEI for the recipe. Feed it from a large boiler.
   > Tip: more steam than one turbine can eat? Add a second turbine on the same steam line.
19. **Large Steam Turbine**: `modern_industrialization:large_steam_turbine` *(after: HV Steam Turbine, EV: Processing Units)*
   > What: MI's multiblock steam turbine. It eats steam by the thousands of mB and makes serious EU.
   > How: the controller needs an HV steam turbine, a processing unit (EV) and a highly advanced hull. Layout: JEI or the MI guidebook.
   > Tip: pair it with a large boiler or a reactor's steam output.
20. **Energized Steel**: 8x `powah:steel_energized` *(after: Choosing Your Power, Uranium Dioxide)*
   > What: Powah's basic alloy, made by the Energizing Orb.
   > How: place Energizing Rods aimed at the orb and power them. Put 1 iron + 1 gold in the orb for 2 Energized Steel.
   > Tip: more rods (and better rods) charge faster.
21. **Powah Energy Cells**: `powah:energy_cell_basic` *(after: Energized Steel)*
   > What: Powah's energy storage block, with tiers from Starter to Nitro.
   > How: iron, a dielectric casing and Powah capacitors. Higher tiers use better capacitors and crystals (check JEI).
   > Tip: cells pass power through each other, so a wall of them makes one big buffer.
22. **Thermo Generator**: `powah:thermo_generator_starter` *(after: Powah Energy Cells)*
   > What: a generator that needs a hot block underneath and a coolant fed in.
   > Chemistry: thermoelectric plates make current from a temperature difference (the Seebeck effect). Hotter below and colder inside means more power.
   > How: place it on lava or magma and pipe water in.
23. **Powah Reactor**: 36x `powah:reactor_basic` *(after: Thermo Generator)*
   > What: a multiblock reactor fuelled by the uraninite you oxidised yourself.
   > Chemistry: uraninite is UO₂. Its uranium releases heat as it fissions; the reactor turns that heat into FE.
   > How: place the reactor blocks in a stack and they form one reactor (check JEI). Feed it uraninite.
   > Tip: fuel, temperature and coolant all show in its GUI. Watch the temperature as you scale up.
24. **Photovoltaics**: `mekanismgenerators:solar_generator`; `powah:solar_panel_starter` *(after: Choosing Your Power, MV: Aluminum)*
   > What: solar panels from Mekanism and Powah.
   > Chemistry: silicon solar cells use a p-n junction: a photon knocks an electron loose and the junction pushes it into a current.
   > How: place them under open sky. They stop at night and slow in rain.
   > Tip: pair solar with an energy cube to cover the night.
25. **Advanced Solar**: `mekanismgenerators:advanced_solar_generator` *(after: Photovoltaics)*
   > What: Mekanism's Advanced Solar Generator, a larger array with much more output.
   > How: check JEI for the recipe. Give it space: it's bigger than one block.
   > Tip: like the basic panel, it only works in daylight. Buffer it with a cube.
26. **Wind Power**: `mekanismgenerators:wind_generator` *(after: Photovoltaics)*
   > What: Mekanism's Wind Generator. It works day and night.
   > How: it makes more power the higher it's placed. Build it on a mountain or a tall tower.
   > Tip: it needs open space around it, so leave room.
27. **Reactor Safety**: 2x `mekanismgenerators:fission_reactor_logic_adapter` *(after: Choosing Your Power, Fission)*
   > What: Logic Adapters let redstone read the reactor and switch it off.
   > Chemistry: a fission reactor makes heat by splitting heavy nuclei. If heat can't escape fast enough, the reactor takes damage; at 100% it melts down.
   > How: set one adapter to emit a signal on damage or high temperature (pick the mode in its GUI) and wire it to another in Activation mode.
   > Tip: start at a low burn rate (0.1 mB/t), keep coolant flowing, and drain waste and heated coolant constantly.
28. **Industrial Turbine**: 16x `mekanismgenerators:turbine_casing` *(after: Reactor Safety)*
   > What: Mekanism's multiblock turbine. Feed it steam from fission or a boiler and it makes huge amounts of FE.
   > How: casings, valves, vents, rotors with blades, a rotational complex, a pressure disperser and electromagnetic coils. Layout: Just Enough Mekanism Multiblocks.
   > Tip: a Saturating Condenser turns spent steam back into water, closing the loop.
29. **D-T Fuel**: `mekanism:solar_neutron_activator`; `mekanismgenerators:hohlraum` *(after: Industrial Turbine, Lithium)*
   > What: fusion fuel: deuterium and tritium, the two heavy isotopes of hydrogen.
   > Chemistry: deuterium comes from heavy water (D₂O). Tritium is bred from lithium by neutrons: ⁶Li + n → ³H + ⁴He.
   > How: electrolyse heavy water for deuterium; put lithium in the Solar Neutron Activator for tritium. Combine them into D-T fuel in the Chemical Infuser, then fill a Hohlraum with it (a chemical tank's item slot works; see its tooltip).
   > Tip: heavy water comes from a Mekanism Electric Pump with a Filter Upgrade.
30. **Fusion**: `mekanismgenerators:fusion_reactor_controller` *(after: D-T Fuel, Transmutation by Neutron)*
   > The power of a star, in a box you built. This is what you were.
   > What: Mekanism's fusion reactor, the top of the power tree.
   > Chemistry: D + T → ⁴He + n + 17.6 MeV, millions of times more energy per kilogram than any chemical reaction.
   > How: a filled Hohlraum in the controller, then a burst from a Laser through a Laser Amplifier to ignite it. Layout: Just Enough Mekanism Multiblocks.
31. **Upgrade in Place**: `generatorgalore:iron_to_gold_upgrade` *(after: A Faster Burn)*
   > What: Generators Galore upgrade kits turn a placed generator into the next tier, keeping its fuel and connections.
   > How: gold ingots, an item frame and a redstone block for iron → gold (check JEI for the others). Right-click the placed generator.
   > Tip: the tree branches: gold leads to diamond or to the food-burning Culinary Generator.
32. **Eight Times the Burn**: `generatorgalore:iron_generator_8x` *(after: A Faster Burn, An Ancient City)*
   > What: 8x generators burn fuel eight times as fast and make eight times the FE in one block.
   > How: eight generators of a tier around an echo shard (check JEI). Echo shards come from Ancient City chests.
   > Tip: a 64x version exists too, for when space matters more than echo shards.
33. **Burning a Star**: `generatorgalore:netherstar_generator` *(after: Generator Collector)*
   > You remember lighting stars. Burning one feels like a waste, and also like coming home.
   > What: the Nether Star Generator burns Nether Stars for an enormous amount of FE.
   > Chemistry: real stars run on fusion: hydrogen nuclei fuse into helium (4 ¹H → ⁴He) and a little mass becomes a lot of energy, E = mc².
34. **Blazing Crystals**: 8x `powah:crystal_blazing`; `powah:energy_cell_blazing` *(after: Powah Reactor, Blaze Rods)*
   > What: every Powah tier is built from a crystal made in the Energizing Orb. Blazing crystals unlock the blazing tier of cells, generators and cables.
   > How: energize a blaze rod (or four blaze powder) with 120,000 FE. Then craft blazing-tier parts (check JEI).
   > Tip: feed the energizing rods from your biggest power source; crystals charge faster with more rods.
35. **Niotic Crystals**: 4x `powah:crystal_niotic`; `powah:energy_cell_niotic` *(after: Blazing Crystals)*
   > What: the niotic tier. Reactors and generators get much stronger.
   > Chemistry: diamond is pure carbon in a rigid lattice where every atom bonds to four others. Pumping energy into it is Powah's magic, but diamond really does conduct heat better than any metal.
   > How: energize a diamond with 300,000 FE (check JEI).
36. **Spirited Crystals**: 4x `powah:crystal_spirited`; `powah:energy_cell_spirited` *(after: Niotic Crystals)*
   > What: the spirited tier, one step below the top.
   > Chemistry: emerald is the mineral beryl, Be₃Al₂Si₆O₁₈. A trace of chromium (Cr³⁺) replacing some aluminum gives it its green colour.
   > How: energize an emerald with 1,000,000 FE (check JEI). A villager trading hall pays off here.
37. **Nitro Crystals**: 16x `powah:crystal_nitro` *(after: Spirited Crystals)*
   > What: nitro crystals build the strongest Powah reactors and cells.
   > How: energize a Nether Star, two redstone blocks and a blazing crystal block with 20,000,000 FE. One craft makes sixteen.
   > Tip: save your Nether Stars for this; the Wither is the only reliable source (check JEI for a Hostile Neural Networks wither model).
38. **Ender Power**: `powah:ender_cell_basic`; `powah:player_transmitter_basic` *(after: Powah Energy Cells)*
   > What: Ender Cells share one energy pool across your base; the Player Transmitter charges the items in your inventory.
   > How: both need an Ender Core (an eye of ender, dielectric casing and a tiny capacitor, energized). Check JEI, and link them with a Binding Card.
   > Tip: a player transmitter keeps jetpacks and the MekaSuit charged while you work.
39. **Herculean Storage**: `fluxnetworks:herculean_flux_storage` *(after: Wireless Grid)*
   > What: Herculean (and then Gargantuan) Flux Storage holds far more energy in one block, shared with the whole flux network.
   > How: Basic Flux Storage blocks around glass panes (check JEI). Gargantuan is the same with Herculean blocks.
   > Tip: flux storage keeps its energy when broken, so you can carry charged batteries to a new base.
40. **Flux Controller**: `fluxnetworks:flux_controller`; `fluxnetworks:flux_configurator` *(after: Wireless Grid)*
   > What: the Flux Controller sends network energy wirelessly into players' inventories. The Configurator copies settings between flux devices.
   > How: flux blocks, a Flux Core and flux dust (check JEI). The Flux Core needs an MI processing unit in this pack.
   > Tip: turn charging off for your armor slots if it fights with other chargers.
41. **Obsidian Generator**: `generatorgalore:obsidian_generator` *(after: Generator Collector, A Door of Fire)*
   > What: a stronger burner, and the base for the ender, enchantment and magmatic generators.
   > How: a diamond generator in obsidian with a redstone block (or use the diamond to obsidian upgrade kit on a placed one).
   > Tip: the upgrade kits keep fuel and connections; JEI shows the whole tree.
42. **Emerald and Netherite Generators**: `generatorgalore:emerald_generator`; `generatorgalore:netherite_generator` *(after: Generator Collector, Ancient Debris)*
   > What: the emerald and netherite generators burn ordinary fuel at a much higher rate for much more FE per tick.
   > How: emerald: a diamond generator in emeralds with a redstone block. Netherite: smithing table, template + diamond generator + netherite ingot.
   > Tip: feed them coal blocks or coke blocks; loose coal won't keep up.
43. **Ender and Enchantment Generators**: `generatorgalore:ender_generator`; `generatorgalore:enchantment_generator` *(after: Obsidian Generator)*
   > What: the ender generator burns ender pearls; the enchantment generator burns enchanted books. Junk books from fishing finally have a use.
   > How: an obsidian generator in ender pearls with a redstone block, or in enchanted books with an enchanting table (check JEI).
   > Tip: an enderman farm feeds the ender generator for ever.
44. **Honey and Potion Generators**: `generatorgalore:honey_generator`; `generatorgalore:potion_generator` *(after: Generator Collector)*
   > What: two branches from the Culinary Generator: one burns honey, the other burns potions.
   > Chemistry: honey is about 80% sugars (fructose and glucose). Sugar burns well: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O, the same reaction your cells run, only slower.
   > How: a culinary generator in honey blocks with buckets and a redstone block, or in pink dye with brewing stands (check JEI).
   > Tip: a few beehives with campfires underneath keep the honey generator running.
45. **Compressed Generators**: 1x any of `or(item(generatorgalore:copper_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:copper_generator_64x)item(generatorgalore:iron_generator_64x)item(generatorgalore:gold_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:gold_generator_64x)item(generatorgalore:diamond_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:diamond_generator_64x)item(generatorgalore:emerald_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:emerald_generator_64x)item(generatorgalore:obsidian_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:obsidian_generator_64x)item(generatorgalore:netherite_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:netherite_generator_64x)item(generatorgalore:magmatic_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:magmatic_generator_64x)item(generatorgalore:culinary_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:culinary_generator_64x)item(generatorgalore:honey_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:honey_generator_64x)item(generatorgalore:potion_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:potion_generator_64x)item(generatorgalore:ender_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:ender_generator_64x)item(generatorgalore:enchantment_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:enchantment_generator_64x)item(generatorgalore:halitosis_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:halitosis_generator_64x)item(generatorgalore:netherstar_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:netherstar_generator_64x))` *(after: Eight Times the Burn)*
   > What: any compressed generator other than the iron 8x: magmatic, star, gem, food, whatever you run most. 64x generators are eight 8x ones around a conduit.
   > How: 8x: eight generators around an echo shard. 64x: eight 8x generators around a conduit (check JEI).
   > Tip: a 64x generator eats fuel 64 times as fast. Make sure the fuel line can keep up first.
46. **Flux Dust**: 16x `fluxnetworks:flux_dust`; `fluxnetworks:flux_block` *(after: Choosing Your Power, Into the Fire)*
   > What: flux dust is the base of every Flux Networks device. Nine make a Flux Block.
   > Chemistry: real redstone doesn't exist, but pressure really does change minerals: graphite squeezed hard enough becomes diamond, and that's the idea here.
   > How: its tooltip says it: redstone compressed with bedrock and obsidian. JEI's Flux Networks page shows the setup. Bedrock is easy to reach at the Nether's floor or roof.
   > Tip: make a big batch now. The Flux Core still needs an MI processing unit (EV), but the dust doesn't.

### Powah!

*Powah: dielectric parts, the Energizing Orb, crystal tiers, generators, cells and wireless power. The starter tier is open early; the Orb needs an MI electronic circuit (MV).*

1. **Dielectric Paste**: 16x `powah:dielectric_paste` *(after: Forge Energy)*
   > Insulators and conductors. You remember that power is mostly about where it is not allowed to go.
   > What: the base of every Powah block: rods, casings, capacitors and cables.
   > Chemistry: a dielectric is an insulator that polarises in an electric field. Fired clay (aluminosilicates such as kaolinite, Al₂Si₂O₅(OH)₄) is the porcelain on real power-line insulators.
   > How: shapeless: 3 coal or charcoal + 2 clay balls + a lava bucket makes 24. Or 2 coal + 1 clay ball + 1 blaze powder for 16.
   > Tip: the lava recipe gives more per craft and keeps the bucket. Make a stack.
2. **Dielectric Rods**: 8x `powah:dielectric_rod`; 8x `powah:dielectric_rod_horizontal` *(after: Dielectric Paste)*
   > What: insulated rods, upright and horizontal. Both go into casings, the Orb, cables and cards.
   > How: 6 paste around 3 iron bars: a vertical line of bars for the upright rod, a horizontal line for the horizontal one. 8 per craft.
   > Tip: you'll need far more horizontal rods than upright ones; every cable craft eats six.
3. **Dielectric Casing**: 2x `powah:dielectric_casing` *(after: Dielectric Rods)*
   > What: the frame inside almost every Powah machine, cell and generator.
   > How: 4 iron ingots in the corners, horizontal rods top and bottom, upright rods in the middle row (check JEI).
4. **Capacitors**: 4x `powah:capacitor_basic`; 2x `powah:capacitor_basic_tiny` *(after: Dielectric Casing)*
   > What: capacitors set a block's tier. The tiny ones go into starter blocks, the basic ones into basic blocks.
   > Chemistry: a capacitor is two conductors separated by a dielectric. It stores E = ½CV², and a better dielectric raises the capacitance C.
   > How: iron ingots, paste and a redstone block make 4 basic capacitors. One basic capacitor splits into 2 tiny ones.
   > Tip: two basic capacitors combine into a large one, which the hardened tier needs later.
5. **Energy Cables**: 12x `powah:energy_cable_starter` *(after: Capacitors)*
   > What: Powah's cables. Each tier carries more FE per tick.
   > How: 6 horizontal rods, 2 iron nuggets and a tiny capacitor make 12 starter cables.
   > Tip: cables connect to any FE block, not just Powah ones. Use the Powah wrench to configure sides.
6. **Starter Energy Cell**: `powah:energy_cell_starter` *(after: Energy Cables)*
   > What: the smallest Powah cell. Enough to smooth out a furnator's output.
   > How: iron ingots in the corners, tiny capacitors on the sides, a dielectric casing in the middle.
   > Tip: the basic cell is the same recipe with basic capacitors. The bigger tiers come with energized steel and crystals.
7. **Powah Wrench**: `powah:wrench` *(after: Dielectric Paste)*
   > What: Powah's wrench. It has Rotate, Config and Link modes; the mode shows on the item.
   > How: iron ingots and dielectric paste (check JEI).
   > Tip: Config mode sets which sides of a cell or generator push or take power.
8. **Furnator**: `powah:furnator_starter` *(after: Capacitors)*
   > What: a Powah generator that burns furnace fuel for FE. It's an early way to run the Dissolver.
   > Chemistry: burning oxidises carbon. Coke burns cleaner and longer than coal because its volatile tars were already driven off.
   > How: paste, 2 tiny capacitors, a dielectric casing and a furnace.
   > Tip: feed it coke from your coke ovens for long runs.
9. **Magmator**: `powah:magmator_starter` *(after: Furnator)*
   > What: a generator that burns lava (and other hot fluids) instead of solid fuel.
   > Chemistry: lava is molten silicate rock at roughly 700 to 1,200 °C. The Magmator draws that stored heat off as FE.
   > How: like the Furnator, but with a bucket in place of the furnace. JEI's Magmatic Fluids list shows what it accepts.
   > Tip: a Nether lava lake and a pump give endless fuel.
10. **Basic Generators**: 1x any of `or(item(powah:furnator_basic)item(powah:magmator_basic)item(powah:thermo_generator_basic)item(powah:solar_panel_basic))` *(after: Furnator, Magmator)*
   > What: every Powah block upgrades by crafting the lower tier into the next one. Basic is the first step.
   > How: a starter generator in the bottom middle, iron ingots, 2 basic capacitors and a dielectric casing (check JEI).
   > Tip: upgrading keeps the old block's cost, so you never waste a starter.
11. **Player Aerial Pearl**: `powah:player_aerial_pearl` *(after: Dielectric Paste)*
   > What: the core of the Player Transmitter.
   > How: craft an Aerial Pearl (an ender pearl in iron bars and paste), then use it on a Zombie or a Husk.
   > Tip: trap a zombie near your base so you can make more later.
12. **Player Transmitter**: `powah:player_transmitter_starter`; `powah:binding_card` *(after: Player Aerial Pearl, Capacitors)*
   > What: a block that charges the FE items carried by the player bound to it.
   > How: Player Aerial Pearl on top, tiny capacitors and a casing in the middle, an upright rod below. The Binding Card is a blank card (2 horizontal rods) with redstone and rotten flesh; right-click to bind it to yourself.
   > Tip: power it from a cell and your jetpack never runs dry at home.
13. **Panes and Plates**: 3x `powah:photoelectric_pane`; 3x `powah:thermoelectric_plate` *(after: Capacitors)*
   > What: photoelectric panes go into Powah solar panels; thermo plates go into thermo generators (both in the Power chapter).
   > Chemistry: light can knock electrons out of a material: the photoelectric effect Einstein explained in 1905. Lapis gets its blue from trisulfur radical ions (S₃⁻) trapped in the mineral lazurite.
   > How: pane: a glass pane in lapis and paste. Plate: a tiny capacitor in redstone and blaze powder.
   > Tip: blaze powder means a trip to the Nether first.
14. **Hopper and Discharger**: `powah:energy_hopper_starter`; `powah:energy_discharger_starter` *(after: Starter Energy Cell)*
   > What: the Energy Hopper charges FE items in the container it faces; the Energy Discharger pulls FE back out of items put in it.
   > How: both are a dielectric casing, tiny capacitors and paste; the hopper also takes a vanilla hopper (check JEI).
   > Tip: a hopper on a chest of tools makes a charging station.
15. **Batteries**: `powah:battery_starter` *(after: Starter Energy Cell)*
   > What: Powah batteries are items that hold FE. Higher tiers hold more.
   > How: basic capacitors, a redstone block and paste. Check its tooltip for how it charges your gear.
   > Tip: fill it from an Energy Hopper, empty it in a Discharger.
16. **Dimensional Binding Card**: `powah:binding_card_dim` *(after: Player Transmitter)*
   > What: the dimensional version of the Binding Card, for transmitters and other Powah blocks that take a card.
   > How: use a Binding Card on an Enderman or an Endermite.
   > Tip: read its tooltip to see what it does differently from the plain card.
17. **The Energizing Orb**: `powah:energizing_orb`; 2x `powah:energizing_rod_starter` *(after: Starter Energy Cell, Electronic Circuit)*
   > A glass sphere that fills with light. You remember charging things just by holding them.
   > What: the Orb turns FE into new materials: energized steel, crystals, ender cores. Every Powah tier above basic needs it.
   > How: in this pack: glass on top and sides, an MI electronic circuit on each side of a dielectric casing in the middle, and 3 horizontal rods on the bottom. Rods: quartz, tiny capacitors, a casing and an upright rod.
   > How: place the orb, aim Energizing Rods at it from nearby, feed the rods FE and put the ingredients in the orb. JEI's Energizing tab shows each recipe and its FE cost.
   > Tip: the first job is uraninite and energized steel: see the Main Path and Power chapter links.
18. **Charged Snowball**: 4x `powah:charged_snowball` *(after: The Energizing Orb)*
   > What: a snowball charged with 500,000 FE. Throw it and lightning strikes where it lands.
   > Chemistry: a lightning channel heats air to around 30,000 K, hotter than the Sun's surface. It splits N₂ and O₂, and the nitrogen oxides it makes fertilise the soil.
   > How: one snowball in the Energizing Orb.
   > Tip: lightning turns a pig into a zombified piglin and a villager into a witch. Aim carefully.
19. **Better Rods**: 2x `powah:energizing_rod_basic` *(after: The Energizing Orb)*
   > What: higher-tier rods pour FE into the orb faster. Several rods stack.
   > Chemistry: quartz is crystalline SiO₂ and is piezoelectric: squeeze it and it makes a voltage. Every quartz watch keeps time with a vibrating crystal.
   > How: a block of quartz on top, basic capacitors and a casing in the middle, a starter rod below.
   > Tip: crystals cost hundreds of thousands of FE. More and better rods matter more than anything else here.
20. **Hardened Rods**: 2x `powah:energizing_rod_hardened` *(after: Better Rods, Hardened Capacitors)*
   > What: the hardened rod, another step in charging speed.
   > How: a block of quartz, hardened capacitors, a casing and a basic rod below.
   > Tip: every rod tier is built from the one before, so keep upgrading the same rods.
21. **Hardened Capacitors**: 2x `powah:capacitor_basic_large`; 2x `powah:capacitor_hardened` *(after: Energized Steel)*
   > What: hardened capacitors unlock the hardened tier of everything.
   > How: 2 basic capacitors make a large one. A large capacitor in energized steel and paste makes 2 hardened capacitors.
   > Tip: large capacitors go into every crystal capacitor too. Craft spares.
22. **Hardened Cables**: 6x `powah:energy_cable_basic`; 12x `powah:energy_cable_hardened` *(after: Hardened Capacitors)*
   > What: faster cables for your growing grid.
   > How: basic: 6 rods, 2 starter cables, a basic capacitor. Hardened: 6 rods, 2 energized steel, a hardened capacitor makes 12 (check JEI).
   > Tip: a cable is only as fast as its slowest segment. Upgrade the trunk line first.
23. **Hardened Energy Cell**: `powah:energy_cell_hardened` *(after: Hardened Capacitors, Powah Energy Cells)*
   > What: the next storage step after the basic cell.
   > How: 2 basic cells, energized steel, hardened capacitors and a dielectric casing.
   > Tip: the crystal cells in the Power chapter each start from the cell below them.
24. **Hardened Generators**: 1x any of `or(item(powah:furnator_hardened)item(powah:magmator_hardened)item(powah:thermo_generator_hardened)item(powah:solar_panel_hardened))` *(after: Hardened Capacitors, Basic Generators)*
   > What: a hardened Furnator, Magmator, Thermo Generator or Solar Panel. Any one counts.
   > How: the basic generator plus energized steel, hardened capacitors and a casing (check JEI).
   > Tip: a hardened thermo generator on lava with water fed in is quiet, fuel-free power.
25. **Blazing Generators**: 1x any of `or(item(powah:furnator_blazing)item(powah:magmator_blazing)item(powah:thermo_generator_blazing)item(powah:solar_panel_blazing))` *(after: Hardened Generators, Blazing Gear)*
   > What: any blazing-tier generator. Output takes a big jump here.
   > How: the hardened generator plus blazing crystals, blazing capacitors and a casing.
   > Tip: feed the orb's rods from these and the next crystal tier comes quicker.
26. **Niotic Generators**: 1x any of `or(item(powah:furnator_niotic)item(powah:magmator_niotic)item(powah:thermo_generator_niotic)item(powah:solar_panel_niotic))` *(after: Blazing Generators, Niotic Gear)*
   > What: any niotic-tier generator. Spirited and nitro follow the same pattern.
   > How: the blazing generator plus niotic crystals, niotic capacitors and a casing (check JEI).
27. **Blazing Gear**: 2x `powah:capacitor_blazing`; `powah:energizing_rod_blazing` *(after: Blazing Crystals, Hardened Rods)*
   > What: the blazing capacitor is the key part of every blazing block; the blazing rod charges the orb faster still.
   > How: capacitor: a large capacitor in blazing crystals and paste (makes 2). Rod: quartz block, blazing capacitors, a casing and a hardened rod.
   > Tip: a blaze farm (or a Hostile Neural Networks blaze model) keeps the crystals coming.
28. **Niotic Gear**: 2x `powah:capacitor_niotic`; `powah:energizing_rod_niotic` *(after: Niotic Crystals, Blazing Gear)*
   > What: niotic capacitors and the niotic rod.
   > Chemistry: diamond is an excellent electrical insulator but conducts heat better than copper, because its stiff carbon lattice carries vibrations so well.
   > How: capacitor: a large capacitor in niotic crystals and paste. Rod: quartz block, niotic capacitors, a casing and a blazing rod.
   > Tip: niotic cables (6 rods, 2 niotic crystals, a niotic capacitor) carry far more FE.
29. **Spirited Gear**: 2x `powah:capacitor_spirited`; `powah:energizing_rod_spirited` *(after: Spirited Crystals, Niotic Gear)*
   > What: spirited capacitors and the spirited rod, one step below the top.
   > How: capacitor: a large capacitor in spirited crystals and paste. Rod: quartz block, spirited capacitors, a casing and a niotic rod.
   > Tip: each spirited crystal costs 1,000,000 FE. Run several spirited rods before you try for nitro.
30. **Nitro**: `powah:energizing_rod_nitro`; `powah:energy_cell_nitro` *(after: Nitro Crystals, Spirited Gear)*
   > Twenty million FE poured into a star. You remember power like this; it used to be yours.
   > What: the nitro rod and nitro energy cell, the strongest Powah blocks.
   > How: nitro capacitor: a large capacitor in nitro crystals and paste. Rod: quartz block, nitro capacitors, a casing and a spirited rod. Cell: nitro crystals, nitro capacitors, 2 spirited cells and a casing.
   > Tip: the nitro crystal recipe needs a block of 9 blazing crystals, so save some blazing crystals for it.
31. **Ender Core**: 2x `powah:ender_core` *(after: The Energizing Orb)*
   > What: the heart of Ender Cells and Ender Gates.
   > How: Energizing Orb: an eye of ender, a dielectric casing and a tiny capacitor, 50,000 FE.
   > Tip: one core per ender block, at every tier.
32. **Ender Gates**: 4x `powah:ender_gate_starter` *(after: Ender Core)*
   > What: ender gates connect to the same ender energy network as your Ender Cells, without storing much themselves.
   > How: obsidian, 2 starter cables and an ender core make 4. Set the channel in the GUI to match your cells.
   > Tip: put a gate next to each remote machine and one Ender Cell at your main bank.
33. **Dry Ice**: 4x `powah:dry_ice` *(after: Powah Reactor)*
   > What: a strong solid coolant for the Powah reactor. Cooler reactors waste less fuel.
   > Chemistry: real dry ice is solid CO₂, which sublimes straight to gas at -78.5 °C. Powah's is made from energized blue ice, which is H₂O, so take the name loosely.
   > How: Energizing Orb: 2 blue ice, 10,000 FE. JEI's Coolants and Solid Coolants tabs list every option and its strength.
   > Tip: the reactor also takes carbon and redstone to boost it. Check its GUI slots.
34. **Hardened Reactor**: 36x `powah:reactor_hardened` *(after: Dry Ice, Hardened Capacitors)*
   > What: a hardened reactor, much stronger than the basic one.
   > Chemistry: uraninite (UO₂) holds U-235, which splits when it absorbs a neutron and releases more neutrons and heat.
   > How: 4 basic reactor blocks, 4 hardened capacitors and 1 uraninite make 4 hardened blocks. Every block in the stack must be the same tier.
   > Tip: blazing, niotic, spirited and nitro reactors follow the same recipe with that tier's capacitor.
35. **Powah's Manual**: `powah:book` *(after: Dielectric Paste)*
   > What: Powah's in-game book, with a page and a picture for every block on this chapter.
   > How: a book and a dielectric paste, shapeless.
   > Tip: add it to your Akashic Tome (Quality of Life page) so it doesn't take a slot.
36. **Starter Reactor Blocks**: 8x `powah:reactor_starter` *(after: Starter Energy Cell, Uranium Dioxide)*
   > What: starter reactor blocks. A stack of them forms a small reactor, and every basic reactor block is crafted from them.
   > Chemistry: uranium dioxide is a ceramic: it melts near 2,865 °C, which is why real fuel pellets are UO₂ and not uranium metal.
   > How: 4 uraninite, 4 tiny capacitors and a dielectric casing make 4. Basic blocks: 4 starter blocks, 4 large capacitors and a uraninite make 4.
   > Tip: build the basic reactor (Power chapter) straight from these; starter reactors are weak.
37. **Bigger Batteries**: 1x any of `or(item(powah:battery_basic)item(powah:battery_hardened)item(powah:battery_blazing)item(powah:battery_niotic)item(powah:battery_spirited)item(powah:battery_nitro))` *(after: Batteries)*
   > What: each battery tier holds and moves more FE. Any one above starter counts.
   > Chemistry: real batteries climb tiers too: lead-acid, then nickel-metal hydride, then lithium-ion, each storing more energy per kilogram.
   > How: the lower battery, that tier's capacitors, a redstone block and paste (hardened and up add energized steel or crystals; check JEI).
38. **Faster Chargers**: 1x any of `or(item(powah:energy_hopper_basic)item(powah:energy_hopper_hardened)item(powah:energy_hopper_blazing)item(powah:energy_hopper_niotic)item(powah:energy_hopper_spirited)item(powah:energy_hopper_nitro)item(powah:energy_discharger_basic)item(powah:energy_discharger_hardened)item(powah:energy_discharger_blazing)item(powah:energy_discharger_niotic)item(powah:energy_discharger_spirited)item(powah:energy_discharger_nitro))` *(after: Hopper and Discharger)*
   > What: higher-tier Energy Hoppers and Dischargers move FE into and out of items faster. Any one counts.
   > How: the lower block in a ring of paste, with that tier's capacitors and a casing (check JEI).
   > Tip: a niotic hopper fills a MekaSuit in moments.
39. **Crystal Cables**: 6x any of `or(item(powah:energy_cable_blazing)item(powah:energy_cable_niotic)item(powah:energy_cable_spirited)item(powah:energy_cable_nitro))` *(after: Hardened Cables, Blazing Gear)*
   > What: blazing, niotic, spirited and nitro cables: each carries far more FE per tick. Any six.
   > How: 6 horizontal rods, 2 cables of the tier below and that tier's capacitor make 6.
   > Tip: only the trunk from your reactor needs top-tier cable; branches can stay hardened.
40. **Starter Ender Cell**: `powah:ender_cell_starter` *(after: Ender Core)*
   > What: an Ender Cell shares one energy pool with every other ender block on the same channel, wherever it is.
   > How: an ender core, 4 obsidian and 4 iron nuggets.
   > Tip: the channel is set in its screen; all your cells on channel 1 are one big battery.
41. **A Wider Ender Network**: 1x any of `or(item(powah:ender_cell_hardened)item(powah:ender_cell_blazing)item(powah:ender_cell_niotic)item(powah:ender_cell_spirited)item(powah:ender_cell_nitro))`; 1x any of `or(item(powah:ender_gate_basic)item(powah:ender_gate_hardened)item(powah:ender_gate_blazing)item(powah:ender_gate_niotic)item(powah:ender_gate_spirited)item(powah:ender_gate_nitro))` *(after: Starter Ender Cell, Ender Gates, Hardened Capacitors)*
   > What: any ender cell above starter and any ender gate above starter. Higher tiers move more FE through the network.
   > How: an ender core in obsidian with energized steel or crystals for cells, or that tier's cables for gates (check JEI).
   > Tip: gates are cheap taps on the network; keep the big cells at home.
42. **Stronger Transmitters**: 1x any of `or(item(powah:player_transmitter_hardened)item(powah:player_transmitter_blazing)item(powah:player_transmitter_niotic)item(powah:player_transmitter_spirited)item(powah:player_transmitter_nitro))` *(after: Player Transmitter, Hardened Capacitors)*
   > What: higher-tier Player Transmitters push more FE into your inventory per tick. Any one above basic.
   > How: the lower transmitter on top, that tier's capacitors and a casing in the middle, a rod below.
   > Tip: one good transmitter beats three weak ones; it charges every item at once.
43. **Crystal Reactor**: 36x any of `or(item(powah:reactor_blazing)item(powah:reactor_niotic)item(powah:reactor_spirited)item(powah:reactor_nitro))` *(after: Hardened Reactor, Blazing Gear)*
   > What: 36 reactor blocks of one crystal tier (blazing, niotic, spirited or nitro), enough for a full reactor.
   > Chemistry: a real reactor's power is limited by how fast heat can be carried away, not by the fuel. Better coolant and better heat transfer mean more power from the same uranium.
   > How: 4 blocks of the tier below, 4 of this tier's capacitors and a uraninite make 4.
   > Tip: all 36 must be the same tier, or they won't form one reactor.
44. **Spirited Generators**: 1x any of `or(item(powah:furnator_spirited)item(powah:furnator_nitro)item(powah:magmator_spirited)item(powah:magmator_nitro)item(powah:thermo_generator_spirited)item(powah:thermo_generator_nitro)item(powah:solar_panel_spirited)item(powah:solar_panel_nitro))` *(after: Niotic Generators, Spirited Gear)*
   > What: any spirited or nitro Furnator, Magmator, Thermo Generator or Solar Panel.
   > How: the niotic generator with spirited crystals, spirited capacitors and a casing (nitro the same, one tier up).
   > Tip: a row of nitro solar panels is silent, fuel-free and enough for most bases.
45. **A Block of Nitro**: `powah:nitro_crystal_block` *(after: Nitro)*
   > Nine crystals, each a star's worth of charge, pressed into one block. You remember holding that much. You used to call it Tuesday.
   > What: a storage block of nitro crystals. It does nothing; it's just very, very expensive.
   > Tip: you can always break it back into crystals.

### Farming and Food

*Grow what you need, cook it well, feed it back to the soil.*

1. **Knife and Board**: `farmersdelight:flint_knife`; `farmersdelight:cutting_board` *(after: Something to Eat)*
   > You remember feasts that lasted a week. Start with something smaller.
   > What: Farmer's Delight adds crops, meals and kitchen blocks. The knife harvests straw and cuts ingredients.
   > How: craft a Flint Knife and a Cutting Board. Place items on the board and use the knife on them.
   > Tip: a knife on tall grass gives straw; wild crops (tomatoes, onions, cabbage, rice) grow in the wild.
2. **Cooking Pot**: `farmersdelight:cooking_pot` *(after: Knife and Board)*
   > What: the Cooking Pot turns several ingredients into one meal. It needs heat underneath.
   > Chemistry: browning meat is the Maillard reaction: amino acids and sugars react above about 140 °C, making hundreds of flavour compounds.
   > How: iron, bricks, a wooden shovel and a water bucket (check JEI). Place it over a fire, campfire or Stove.
3. **A Proper Meal**: 2x `farmersdelight:vegetable_soup` *(after: Cooking Pot)*
   > What: Farmer's Delight meals restore a lot of hunger and give long effects like Nourishment (hunger stops dropping) and Comfort.
   > How: cook vegetable soup in the Cooking Pot (check JEI), then bowl it.
   > Tip: a Feeding Upgrade in your backpack eats these for you.
4. **Pasta with Meatballs**: 2x `farmersdelight:pasta_with_meatballs` *(after: A Proper Meal, The New Crops)*
   > What: a hearty meal that chains every kitchen tool: knife (minced beef), board (raw pasta from dough) and pot (tomato sauce).
   > Chemistry: dough is starch and gluten proteins; water lets gluten chains cross-link into the stretchy network that holds pasta together.
   > How: follow the tree in JEI: wheat dough → raw pasta, beef → minced beef, tomatoes → tomato sauce, then the pot.
   > Tip: press U on any ingredient in JEI to see every meal that uses it.
5. **A Varied Diet**: 6x any of `item_tag(farmersdelight:meals)` *(after: Pasta with Meatballs)*
   > What: collect six bowls or plates of any Farmer's Delight meal: stews, soups, rice dishes, ratatouille, you choose.
   > How: anything in the 'meals' tag counts. Mix and match, they don't have to be different.
   > Tip: meals stack to 16; keep a stack in the backpack for long mining trips.
6. **Rich Soil**: `farmersdelight:organic_compost`; 4x `farmersdelight:rich_soil` *(after: Knife and Board)*
   > What: organic compost slowly turns into Rich Soil, which grows crops faster and mushrooms into colonies.
   > Chemistry: composting is microbes breaking down organic matter with oxygen. They release CO₂ and heat, and leave humus rich in nitrogen.
   > How: craft compost from dirt, straw and bone meal plus rotten flesh or tree bark (check JEI), place it and wait.
   > Tip: till Rich Soil with a hoe to get rich farmland for crops.
7. **The Stove**: `farmersdelight:stove` *(after: Cooking Pot)*
   > What: the Stove heats a Cooking Pot or Skillet on top and can grill up to six items on its own surface.
   > How: iron ingots, bricks and a campfire (check JEI). Light it with flint and steel.
   > Tip: unlike a campfire it doesn't need logs, and it looks right in a kitchen.
8. **A Feast**: `farmersdelight:honey_glazed_ham_block` *(after: A Proper Meal)*
   > What: feasts are placed as blocks and served with a bowl, several portions each.
   > How: cook a Honey Glazed Ham (check JEI). Place it on a table and right-click with bowls.
   > Tip: a feast is the easiest way to feed a whole team before a boss fight.
9. **Banquet**: `farmersdelight:roast_chicken_block`; `farmersdelight:shepherds_pie_block` *(after: A Feast)*
   > What: two more feasts for the table: a whole Roast Chicken and a Shepherd's Pie.
   > How: both come from the Cooking Pot (check JEI). Each needs a container, often a bowl, to serve.
   > Tip: place feasts where everyone passes, like next to the team's waystone.
10. **Mushroom Colonies**: 2x any of `item_tag(farmersdelight:mushroom_colonies)` *(after: Rich Soil)*
   > What: a mushroom on Rich Soil grows into a colony that you can harvest again and again.
   > Chemistry: fungi don't photosynthesise. They digest organic matter with enzymes, which is why rich, dark soil suits them.
   > How: plant a brown or red mushroom on Rich Soil in low light, wait, then harvest it with shears; the colony stays and regrows.
   > Tip: mushroom colonies are the steady source of mushrooms for stews and rice dishes.
11. **Skillet**: `farmersdelight:skillet` *(after: The Stove)*
   > What: a frying pan that cooks one item at a time over heat, and doubles as a surprisingly good weapon.
   > How: iron ingots and a brick (check JEI). Place it on the Stove or a campfire, or check its tooltip for cooking in hand.
   > Tip: Fire Aspect on a skillet sounds silly; it works.
12. **Breakfast**: 4x `farmersdelight:fried_egg`; 4x `farmersdelight:cooked_bacon` *(after: Skillet)*
   > What: the start of most Farmer's Delight breakfasts: fried eggs and cooked bacon.
   > Chemistry: egg white turns opaque as heat unfolds its proteins (denaturation) and they tangle together; it can't go back.
   > How: cut raw porkchop into bacon on the Cutting Board, then fry it and the eggs on the Skillet or Stove.
   > Tip: combine them into Bacon and Eggs in the Cooking Pot (check JEI).
13. **The New Crops**: 4x `farmersdelight:tomato`; 4x `farmersdelight:onion`; 4x `farmersdelight:cabbage`; 4x `farmersdelight:rice` *(after: Knife and Board)*
   > What: Farmer's Delight crops are the base of nearly every meal.
   > How: find wild tomatoes, onions, cabbages and rice in the world (rice grows in shallow water). Break them for seeds and replant.
   > Tip: rice must be planted in water one block deep, like in a real paddy.
14. **Tomatoes on a Rope**: 16x `farmersdelight:rope` *(after: The New Crops)*
   > What: tomato vines climb rope, so a single plant grows several blocks tall and fruits all the way up.
   > How: craft rope from straw (check JEI), hang it above a tomato plant, and let the vine climb.
   > Tip: rope also lets you climb down mineshafts; right-click a placed rope to extend it downward.
15. **Harvest Festival**: 128x any of `item_tag(c:crops)` *(after: The New Crops)*
   > What: a full harvest: any 128 items from the shared crops tag (wheat, carrots, potatoes, tomatoes, rice and more).
   > How: a large field, Hopper Botany Pots, or an MI Farmer all count. Carry them in one go.
   > Tip: crop storage blocks (crates and bags) pack 9 crops each; you need the loose crops here.
16. **Hopper Botany Pots**: `botanypots:terracotta_hopper_botany_pot` *(after: Knife and Board)*
   > What: Hopper Botany Pots grow crops and push the harvest into the container below.
   > How: place one on a chest, add soil (dirt) and a seed.
   > Tip: Rich Soil or farmland grows faster than dirt, and Mystical Agriculture seeds work in pots too.
17. **Animal Husbandry**: 2x `minecraft:lead`; 16x `minecraft:wheat` *(after: Knife and Board)*
   > What: cows, sheep, pigs and chickens give food, leather, wool and eggs. Two adults fed their favourite food make a baby.
   > How: lead two animals into a pen and feed them. Just Enough Breeding adds a JEI page per animal: look up any mob egg or food to see what it eats and what it drops.
   > Tip: babies take about 20 minutes to grow; feeding them their breeding food speeds that up.
18. **Pet Food**: `farmersdelight:horse_feed`; `farmersdelight:dog_food` *(after: Animal Husbandry, Knife and Board)*
   > What: Horse Feed heals and speeds up horses; Dog Food heals tamed wolves and gives them buffs.
   > How: both are Farmer's Delight crafting recipes (check JEI).
   > Tip: a well-fed wolf is a decent bodyguard in the early Twilight Forest.
19. **N, P and K**: `chemlib:urea`; `chemlib:diammonium_phosphate`; `chemlib:potassium_nitrate` *(after: The Combiner)*
   > What: plants need nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P) and potassium (K) more than anything else from the soil. These three compounds deliver them.
   > Chemistry: urea CO(NH₂)₂ is 46% nitrogen; diammonium phosphate (NH₄)₂HPO₄ carries N and P; potassium nitrate KNO₃ carries K and N.
   > How: make all three in the Alchemistry Combiner (check JEI for the element recipe of each).
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Deep dive: why nitrogen is the hard one.
   > Air is 78% nitrogen, but N₂ has a triple bond that plants can't break. Only some soil bacteria (and lightning) can 'fix' it.
   > In 1909 Fritz Haber found how to force N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃ with a metal catalyst, high pressure and heat; Carl Bosch scaled it up.
   > Today about half the nitrogen in your body passed through a Haber-Bosch plant. Ammonia is turned into urea, ammonium nitrate and phosphates.
   > You'll build that same reaction in the main quests (Haber-Bosch, HV tier). Phosphorus comes from mined phosphate rock, and potassium from potash salts like KCl.
20. **NPK Fertilizer**: `extended_industrialization:npk_fertilizer_bucket` *(after: N, P and K, The Chemical Reactor, Sulfuric Acid)*
   > What: Extended Industrialization's NPK Fertilizer is a fluid the MI Farmer can spread to grow crops faster.
   > Chemistry: bone meal is calcium phosphate; sulfuric acid frees phosphoric acid, H₃PO₄, just like the real 'wet process' for phosphate rock.
   > How: Chemical Reactor, three steps (check JEI): bone meal + H₂SO₄ → phosphoric acid; potato/carrot/beetroot + water + HCl → potassium chloride, then KCl + H₂ + O₂ → potassium hydroxide; finally nitrogen + phosphoric acid + KOH → NPK Fertilizer.
   > Tip: real NPK plants start from ammonia, not raw nitrogen. Here the recipe takes the shortcut.
21. **The Steam Farmer**: `extended_industrialization:steam_farmer` *(after: Analog Circuit, Electric Motor)*
   > What: Extended Industrialization's Farmer is a multiblock that tills, plants, harvests and (with fertiliser) speeds up a whole field.
   > How: analog circuits, a motor, bronze plated bricks, a steel combine and a bronze pipe casing (check JEI). Its layout is in JEI and the MI guidebook.
   > Tip: the Electric Farmer is the upgrade. JEI has a fertiliser page that shows which fluids speed up a Farmer.
22. **Food Fight**: 8x `farmersdelight:rotten_tomato` *(after: The New Crops)*
   > What: you found a use for spoiled tomatoes: rotten tomatoes can be thrown.
   > Chemistry: rotting is bacteria and fungi breaking sugars into acids, alcohols and gases. Don't eat it.
   > Tip: they're also good compost material. Probably better than throwing them at the team.
23. **Kitchen Garden**: 16x `minecraft:wheat_seeds`; 8x `minecraft:potato`; 8x `minecraft:carrot`; 8x `minecraft:melon_slice`; 8x `minecraft:sweet_berries` *(after: A First Field)*
   > What: the vanilla crops beyond wheat: potatoes and carrots from village farms, melons from jungles, sweet berries from taiga.
   > Chemistry: a potato is mostly starch, long chains of glucose packed into grains. Cooking swells and bursts the grains (gelatinisation), which is why a baked potato is soft.
   > How: break grass for seeds, raid a village farm for potatoes and carrots, and replant everything.
   > Tip: sweet berry bushes hurt to walk through. Plant a row as a mob fence.
24. **Barnyard Goods**: 16x any of `or(item(minecraft:beef)item(minecraft:porkchop)item(minecraft:mutton)item(minecraft:chicken)item(minecraft:rabbit))`; 4x `minecraft:leather`; 4x `minecraft:feather`; 4x `minecraft:egg` *(after: Animal Husbandry)*
   > What: 16 raw meat of any kind, plus leather, feathers and eggs: the steady output of a few animal pens.
   > Chemistry: an eggshell is about 95% calcium carbonate, CaCO₃: the same compound as chalk and limestone. Drop one in vinegar and it fizzes away as CO₂.
   > How: breed cows, pigs, sheep, chickens or rabbits and harvest the adults. Chickens lay eggs on their own.
   > Tip: cook meat before eating; raw chicken can give you Hunger.
25. **Milk**: `minecraft:milk_bucket` *(after: Animal Husbandry, Water)*
   > What: drinking milk clears every potion effect, good and bad. It's also a baking ingredient.
   > Chemistry: milk is an emulsion: fat droplets held in water by proteins (casein). Add acid and the casein clumps into curds, which is the first step of every cheese.
   > How: use an empty bucket on a cow (or a goat).
   > Tip: carry one into the Deep Dark or the Wither fight to wipe Darkness or Wither in one gulp.
26. **Sugar**: 16x `minecraft:sugar` *(after: Sugar Cane)*
   > What: sugar goes into cakes, pies, fermented spider eyes and speed potions.
   > Chemistry: table sugar is sucrose, C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁: a glucose and a fructose joined together. Heat it past about 160 °C and it breaks down into hundreds of brown, bitter-sweet compounds: caramel.
   > How: one sugar cane makes one sugar. A row of cane on Snad (Quality of Life page) grows fast.
   > Tip: the Alchemistry Dissolver splits sucrose into carbon, hydrogen and oxygen if you need the elements.
27. **Bake Sale**: `minecraft:cake`; 2x `minecraft:pumpkin_pie` *(after: Sugar, Milk, Barnyard Goods)*
   > What: a cake (placed and eaten a slice at a time) and pumpkin pie, the best vanilla snack per bite.
   > Chemistry: baking is chemistry you can eat: egg proteins set the structure, sugar caramelises, and the Maillard reaction between sugars and proteins browns the crust.
   > How: cake: 3 milk buckets, 2 sugar, an egg and 3 wheat (you keep the buckets). Pie: a pumpkin, sugar and an egg.
   > Tip: a cake on the table in your base means nobody ever starves between trips.
28. **Honey and Wax**: 6x `minecraft:honeycomb`; 4x `minecraft:honey_bottle` *(after: Campfire)*
   > What: shears on a full bee nest give honeycomb; a glass bottle gives honey. Honeycomb waxes copper so it never tarnishes.
   > Chemistry: beeswax is mostly long esters (fatty acids joined to long alcohols). Wax on copper keeps out the air and water that would turn it green.
   > How: put a campfire under the nest first: the smoke keeps the bees calm. Then shear it or bottle it when it's dripping.
   > Tip: honey bottles cure poison and can be crafted into sugar.
29. **An Apiary**: `minecraft:beehive`; 2x `minecraft:honey_block`; 2x `minecraft:honeycomb_block` *(after: Honey and Wax)*
   > What: a beehive you can place where you like, plus the two honey blocks: sticky honey blocks and decorative honeycomb blocks.
   > Chemistry: honey is a supersaturated sugar solution, about 80% sugar in 17% water. That's why it slowly crystallises, and why bacteria can't live in it: the sugar pulls the water out of them.
   > How: a beehive is planks and honeycomb. A honey block is 4 honey bottles; a honeycomb block is 4 honeycomb. Lead bees home with flowers.
   > Tip: honey blocks slow anything on them and stop pistons pulling other blocks; great for flying machines.
30. **Wildflowers**: 16x any of `or(item(minecraft:dandelion)item(minecraft:poppy)item(minecraft:cornflower)item(minecraft:blue_orchid)item(minecraft:allium)item(minecraft:azure_bluet)item(minecraft:oxeye_daisy)item(minecraft:lily_of_the_valley)item(minecraft:red_tulip)item(minecraft:orange_tulip)item(minecraft:white_tulip)item(minecraft:pink_tulip)item(minecraft:torchflower))` *(after: Knife and Board)*
   > What: flowers make dyes, feed bees and decorate. Any 16 count.
   > Chemistry: many flower colours are anthocyanins, pigments that change colour with pH: the same molecule is red in acid and blue in alkali, like red cabbage indicator.
   > How: pick them in meadows and flower forests, or bone meal grass to grow more.
   > Tip: cornflower gives blue dye without lapis.
31. **Bone Meal**: 32x `minecraft:bone_meal` *(after: Rich Soil)*
   > What: bone meal makes crops, saplings and flowers grow instantly.
   > Chemistry: bone is mostly hydroxyapatite, Ca₅(PO₄)₃(OH). Ground bone was one of the first phosphate fertilisers, before mined phosphate rock took over.
   > How: one bone makes 3 bone meal; a composter also turns plant scraps into it.
   > Tip: the NPK quests further along this page start from bone meal.
32. **Hay Bales**: 4x `minecraft:hay_block` *(after: Animal Husbandry)*
   > What: a hay bale is 9 wheat. Horses and llamas eat it, and landing on one cuts fall damage by 80%.
   > How: 9 wheat in the crafting grid.
   > Tip: a hay bale under a campfire makes the smoke rise much higher: a signal for friends.
33. **Crates and Bags**: 4x any of `or(item(farmersdelight:cabbage_crate)item(farmersdelight:onion_crate)item(farmersdelight:tomato_crate)item(farmersdelight:carrot_crate)item(farmersdelight:potato_crate)item(farmersdelight:beetroot_crate)item(farmersdelight:rice_bag))` *(after: The New Crops)*
   > What: Farmer's Delight crates and bags hold 9 crops each and look good in a pantry. Any four.
   > How: 9 of the crop in the crafting grid (check JEI). Break one back into crops any time.
   > Tip: a wall of crates is a kitchen store that doubles as decoration.
34. **From the Sea**: 16x `minecraft:kelp`; 16x `minecraft:dried_kelp`; `minecraft:tropical_fish` *(after: Gone Fishing)*
   > What: kelp grows fast underwater; dried, it's a snack and (as a block) a good furnace fuel. Tropical fish come from fishing or warm oceans.
   > Chemistry: burnt kelp ash was the world's first source of iodine: Bernard Courtois found it in 1811 when sulfuric acid on seaweed ash gave off violet I₂ vapour. The ash was also a source of soda for glass.
   > How: harvest kelp, smelt it into dried kelp, and catch or bucket a tropical fish.
   > Tip: 9 dried kelp make a block that burns for 20 items in a furnace.
35. **Nether Fungi**: 4x `minecraft:crimson_fungus`; 4x `minecraft:warped_fungus` *(after: Into the Fire, Bone Meal)*
   > What: crimson and warped fungi grow into huge Nether trees when bone-mealed on matching nylium. Warped fungus on a stick steers a strider.
   > Chemistry: real fungi aren't plants: their cell walls are chitin, the same polymer as insect shells, not cellulose.
   > How: pick them in the crimson and warped forests. Bone meal on nylium grows more.
   > Tip: hoglins run from warped fungus. Plant some around your Nether base.
36. **Chorus Orchard**: 16x `minecraft:chorus_fruit`; 8x `minecraft:popped_chorus_fruit` *(after: The End)*
   > What: chorus fruit teleports you a short way when eaten. Smelted, it becomes popped chorus fruit for purpur blocks, end rods and Silent Gear's glittery dust.
   > How: break chorus plants on the outer End islands, or plant a chorus flower on end stone and grow your own.
   > Tip: in this pack the Potion of Flying uses hydrogen, not chorus, so this crop is for building and Silent Gear.
37. **Flax**: 4x `silentgear:flax_seeds`; 8x `silentgear:flax_string` *(after: The New Crops)*
   > What: Silent Gear's flax gives fibre for string, so bows and bindings don't depend on spider hunts.
   > Chemistry: flax fibre is nearly pure cellulose. Linen, made from it, is one of the oldest textiles, woven for over 30,000 years.
   > How: find flax seeds (check JEI for where they drop), grow them, and craft 2 flax fibre into a flax string.
   > Tip: flax flowers make blue dye too.
38. **Overqualified**: `minecraft:netherite_hoe` *(after: Netherite Tier)*
   > You remember making forests grow with a word. Now you're upgrading a hoe with netherite. Priorities.
   > What: a netherite hoe. It tills, it harvests leaves and sculk fast, and it cost you a netherite ingot.
   > Tip: hoes are the fastest tool for leaves, hay, moss and sculk. So it isn't entirely a joke.

### Quality of Life

*Small things that make a big difference.*

1. **Comfort First**: checkmark *(after: Planks and a Workbench)*
   > You remember never wasting a motion. These small things feel familiar.
   > What: this page collects the mods that save time and clicks: guidebooks, backpacks, waystones, maps, keybinds and the Utilitarian shortcuts.
   > How: each row is one topic. Nearly everything here is optional, so pick what helps you. Click the checkmark to open the page.
   > Tip: none of this is needed for the main path, but most of it pays for itself within an hour.
2. **One Book to Rule Them All**: `akashictome:tome` *(after: Comfort First)*
   > What: the Akashic Tome merges every mod's guidebook into one item.
   > How: craft it, then right-click it with other guidebooks to add them.
   > Tip: right-click the tome to choose which book to open.
3. **Find Anything**: `naturescompass:naturescompass`; `explorerscompass:explorerscompass` *(after: Comfort First, Iron)*
   > What: Nature's Compass finds biomes; Explorer's Compass finds structures (Nether Fortresses, Ancient Cities, villages).
   > How: craft both (check JEI), right-click to pick a target, then follow the needle.
   > Tip: the Explorer's Compass is the fastest way to find an Ancient City for the Deeper and Darker quests.
4. **No More Mob Spawns**: `torchmaster:megatorch` *(after: Comfort First, Iron)*
   > What: the Mega Torch stops hostile mobs spawning naturally in a huge radius.
   > How: check JEI for the recipe and place it near the middle of your base.
   > Tip: it blocks natural spawns only. Spawners and Simulation Chambers still work.
5. **Graves**: checkmark *(after: Comfort First, Iron)*
   > What: if you die, Corail Tombstone keeps your items in a grave where you fell.
   > How: walk back and open the grave to recover everything. Click the checkmark once you've read this.
   > Tip: JourneyMap drops a waypoint where you died, so the grave is easy to find.
6. **Backups**: checkmark *(after: Comfort First)*
   > What: Simple Backups saves your world automatically.
   > How: on a server, backups live in the server's backups folder. In single player, look in your instance folder.
   > Tip: copy a backup somewhere else before trying risky reactor builds.
7. **Dread Lamp**: `torchmaster:dreadlamp` *(after: No More Mob Spawns, Into the Fire)*
   > What: the Dread Lamp blocks Nether mob spawns in a large radius, the way the Mega Torch does for Overworld mobs.
   > How: check JEI. Place it at your Nether base or portal hub.
   > Tip: place it before building in the Nether so your base stays quiet.
8. **Crafting on a Stick**: `crafting_on_a_stick:crafting_table` *(after: Comfort First)*
   > What: a crafting table you carry around. Right-click it to open a 3x3 grid anywhere: in a mine, out exploring, mid-build.
   > How: craft it from a crafting table and a stick (check JEI). The same mod makes pocket versions of the stonecutter, smithing table, anvil, grindstone, loom and cartography table.
   > Tip: it saves a hotbar slot over placing and breaking tables. The pocket stonecutter is great for building with Create Deco and Rechiseled blocks.
9. **A Whole Workshop**: `crafting_on_a_stick:stonecutter`; `crafting_on_a_stick:smithing_table` *(after: Crafting on a Stick)*
   > What: optional: the pocket stonecutter and smithing table.
   > How: each one is its block plus a stick (check JEI).
   > Tip: the smithing table is how netherite and Apotheosis upgrades are applied, so it's handy to carry.
10. **Backpack Upgrades**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:pickup_upgrade`; `sophisticatedbackpacks:magnet_upgrade` *(after: Comfort First, A Backpack)*
   > What: pickup and magnet upgrades pull items straight into your backpack.
   > How: craft an Upgrade Base, then the upgrades (check JEI). Put them in the backpack's upgrade slots.
   > Tip: set a filter on the pickup upgrade so it only grabs ores and drops you actually want.
11. **Iron Backpack**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:iron_backpack` *(after: Comfort First, A Backpack)*
   > What: each backpack tier adds inventory rows and upgrade slots: iron, gold, diamond, netherite.
   > How: surround your backpack with iron ingots (check JEI). It keeps everything inside.
   > Tip: stack upgrades multiply how many items fit in each slot.
12. **Feeding Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:feeding_upgrade` *(after: Backpack Upgrades)*
   > What: eats food from the backpack automatically when you're hungry.
   > How: check JEI. Farmer's Delight meals restore a lot per bite.
   > Tip: set a filter so it doesn't eat your golden apples.
13. **Netherite Backpack**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:netherite_backpack` *(after: Iron Backpack)*
   > What: the top tier: the most inventory slots and upgrade space.
   > How: ring the backpack with gold, then diamonds, then smith in a netherite ingot with a netherite upgrade template.
   > Tip: a netherite backpack has room for several stack upgrades at once.
14. **Waystones**: `waystones:waystone` *(after: Comfort First, Iron)*
   > What: waystones are teleport points. Activate one by right-clicking it, then warp between any you've activated.
   > How: found in villages, or craft one (check JEI). Place them at your base, mines and portals.
   > Tip: warping costs a little XP depending on distance; check the config if it seems steep.
15. **Warp Scrolls**: 4x `waystones:warp_scroll` *(after: Waystones)*
   > What: a single-use warp to any activated waystone, handy before you can afford a Warp Stone.
   > How: paper, an ender pearl, gold nuggets and an ink sac (check JEI).
   > Tip: keep one in your backpack for emergencies.
16. **Maps**: checkmark *(after: Comfort First)*
   > What: JourneyMap draws a minimap and a full world map as you explore, with waypoints.
   > How: press J for the full JourneyMap. FTB Chunks has its own map for claims (check Controls for its key). Click the checkmark when you've tried them.
   > Tip: drop a waypoint at every rich ore deposit you find. Deposits are rare, so note the depth too.
17. **Inventory Tricks**: checkmark *(after: Comfort First)*
   > What: small mods that save hours: Mouse Tweaks (drag and scroll to move stacks), Inventory Tweaks (sorting) and TrashSlot (a trash can in your inventory).
   > How: try a scroll-wheel drag over stacks, the sort button, and the trash slot by your hotbar. Click the checkmark when done.
   > Tip: Polymorph shows a button when two recipes share a grid; click it to pick the one you want.
18. **Feral Flare Lantern**: `torchmaster:feral_flare_lantern` *(after: No More Mob Spawns, Into the Fire)*
   > What: the lantern places invisible light sources in the dark spots around it, so a cave or a big hall lights up without a single torch.
