   > How: gold ingots, glass and glowstone dust (check JEI). Place it in the middle of the room.
   > Tip: great for a clean-looking factory floor. It still lets mobs spawn in spots it can't reach.
19. **Grave Tricks**: checkmark *(after: Graves)*
   > What: Corail Tombstone does more than store your items: it adds scrolls, tablets and the Ankh of Prayer, plus a book that makes items soulbound.
   > How: search 'tombstone' in JEI to browse them. Click the checkmark when you've had a look.
   > Tip: by default only you can open your grave, so a death on a server doesn't mean losing your gear to someone else.
20. **Loot for Everyone**: checkmark *(after: Comfort First, Iron)*
   > What: with Lootr, structure chests (dungeons, temples, villages, mineshafts) hold separate loot for each player.
   > How: open any generated chest. You get your own roll; your friends still get theirs. Click the checkmark when you've seen one.
   > Tip: on a server, nobody has to race to a dungeon first.
21. **Stack Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:stack_upgrade_tier_1` *(after: Iron Backpack)*
   > What: a stack upgrade multiplies how many items each backpack slot holds. Higher tiers multiply more.
   > How: check JEI; each tier is built from the one before it.
   > Tip: stack upgrades make a backpack the best place to carry dust and ingots between machines.
22. **Tool Swapper**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:tool_swapper_upgrade` *(after: Stack Upgrade)*
   > What: swaps the tool in your hand for the best one in your backpack when you start mining a block or hitting a mob.
   > How: check JEI, then put it in an upgrade slot and fill the backpack with tools.
   > Tip: pairs well with a paxel; it switches to shears or a sword only when needed.
23. **Refill Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:refill_upgrade` *(after: Stack Upgrade)*
   > What: keeps chosen hotbar items topped up from the backpack: torches, blocks, food.
   > How: check JEI. Set the items to refill in the upgrade's tab.
   > Tip: refill building blocks while bridging and you'll never stop to open your inventory.
24. **Pocket Anvil**: `crafting_on_a_stick:anvil`; `crafting_on_a_stick:grindstone` *(after: A Whole Workshop)*
   > What: pocket versions of the anvil and grindstone, opened with right-click.
   > How: each one is its block plus a stick (check JEI).
   > Tip: the pocket anvil wears down like a placed one, so carry a spare for long trips.
25. **FTB Ultimine**: checkmark *(after: Comfort First, Stone Age)*
   > What: Ultimine breaks every connected matching block at once: a full ore vein, a tree, a strip of stone.
   > How: hold the Ultimine key (default `, the key left of 1) and break a block. Arrow keys up and down change the shape. Click the checkmark when you've tried it.
   > Tip: it can cost extra hunger, so eat first. Shapes include tunnels and flat planes for clearing space.
26. **Form a Team**: checkmark *(after: Comfort First)*
   > What: FTB Teams groups players into a party. Teammates share quest progress and claimed chunks.
   > How: open the Teams screen from the button on your inventory screen (or use /ftbteams) and create a party, then invite friends. Click the checkmark when done.
   > Tip: playing alone? A solo party still lets you set chunk permissions for visitors.
27. **Homes and /back**: checkmark *(after: Form a Team)*
   > What: FTB Essentials adds /sethome and /home (one home by default), /back to return to where you died or last teleported, /spawn, and /tpa to ask to teleport to a friend.
   > How: stand at your base and type /sethome, then try /home from somewhere else. Click the checkmark when done.
   > Tip: each command has a short cooldown. /back after a death walks you straight to your grave.
28. **Just Zoom**: checkmark *(after: Comfort First)*
   > What: Just Zoom lets you zoom in on the distance with a key, no item needed.
   > How: find its key under Options → Controls, and hold it to zoom (its options are in the Mods menu). Click the checkmark when you've tried it.
   > Tip: handy for spotting structures, meteorites and villages from a hilltop.
29. **Ping Wheel**: checkmark *(after: Form a Team)*
   > What: Ping Wheel puts a marker on the spot you look at, visible to the other players nearby.
   > How: find its keys under Options → Controls. Look at something and ping it. Click the checkmark when done.
   > Tip: ping an ore deposit or a dangerous mob instead of typing coordinates.
30. **Chat Heads**: checkmark *(after: Form a Team)*
   > What: Chat Heads shows each player's face next to their messages in chat.
   > How: nothing to set up; it works as soon as someone talks. Click the checkmark when you've seen it.
   > Tip: its options are in the Mods menu if you want to change how heads are shown.
31. **Trade Cycling**: 16x `minecraft:emerald` *(after: Comfort First, Iron)*
   > What: Trade Cycling adds a button to the villager trade screen that rerolls the offers of a villager nobody has traded with yet.
   > How: give a villager a job block, open its trades and press the cycle button until the offer you want appears. Earn 16 emeralds by trading.
   > Tip: once you trade, the offers lock. Cycle a librarian until it sells the enchanted book you need.
32. **Merchant Prince**: 4x `minecraft:emerald_block` *(after: Trade Cycling)*
   > What: four emerald blocks: 36 emeralds. The villagers have noticed you.
   > Chemistry: emerald is beryl, Be₃Al₂Si₆O₁₈, coloured green by traces of chromium.
   > Tip: every Warp Stone needs an emerald, so a good trading hall pays for your travel network.
33. **Tool Belt**: `toolbelt:belt` *(after: Comfort First, Iron)*
   > What: the Tool Belt holds tools outside your hotbar and opens as a radial menu so you can swap fast.
   > How: leather and string (check JEI). Keep it in your inventory; find its key under Options → Controls.
   > Tip: put the wrench, the config card and your paxel on the belt.
34. **Belt Pouches**: 2x `toolbelt:pouch` *(after: Tool Belt)*
   > What: each pouch adds a slot to your tool belt.
   > How: craft pouches, then craft them together with the belt (check JEI).
   > Tip: a full belt keeps your hotbar free for blocks and food.
35. **A Waystone Network**: 4x any of `or(item(waystones:waystone)item(waystones:mossy_waystone)item(waystones:sandy_waystone)item(waystones:deepslate_waystone)item(waystones:blackstone_waystone)item(waystones:end_stone_waystone))` *(after: Waystones)*
   > What: one waystone is a landmark; four make a network. Base, mine, Nether portal and a far-off biome.
   > How: any four waystones of any style (check JEI for the variants), or bring back ones found in villages.
   > Tip: name each one clearly ('Bauxite Mine -40') so the list stays readable.
36. **Warp Stone**: `waystones:warp_stone` *(after: A Waystone Network)*
   > What: a reusable item that opens the waystone menu wherever you stand. It recharges after each use.
   > How: amethyst shards, ender pearls and an emerald (check JEI). It's also in the Demigod Token shop.
   > Tip: with a Warp Stone, warp scrolls become backup only.
37. **Waypoints**: checkmark *(after: Maps)*
   > What: JourneyMap waypoints mark places on the minimap and in the world, with distance shown on screen.
   > How: open the full map (J) and right-click a spot to add a waypoint, or use JourneyMap's waypoint key (see Controls). Click the checkmark when you've made one.
   > Tip: JourneyMap makes a death waypoint for you; share waypoints with teammates in chat.
38. **Utilitarian Shortcuts**: checkmark *(after: Comfort First)*
   > What: the Utilitarian mod adds bulk recipes that skip the planks step (two logs in a column make 16 sticks), plus small handy blocks: tiny coal, the Trowel, the Angel Block, Snad and more. This row is its catalogue.
   > How: press U on any log in JEI to see every log shortcut. Click the checkmark when you've had a look.
   > Tip: the bulk recipes give the same items as the vanilla ones, just with fewer clicks and no waste.
39. **Chests and Ladders**: 4x `minecraft:chest`; 24x `minecraft:ladder` *(after: Utilitarian Shortcuts)*
   > What: logs in a chest ring make 4 chests at once. Seven logs in a ladder shape make 24 ladders.
   > How: the same shapes as the plank recipes, but with logs (check JEI).
   > Tip: three logs in a V make 12 bowls, and logs between iron make a hopper without a chest.
40. **Slabs and Stairs**: 24x any of `item_tag(minecraft:wooden_slabs)`; 16x any of `item_tag(minecraft:wooden_stairs)` *(after: Utilitarian Shortcuts)*
   > What: three logs in a row make 24 slabs; six logs in a stair shape make 16 stairs.
   > How: use logs of one wood type in the usual slab or stair shape (check JEI).
   > Tip: two slabs placed diagonally in the grid turn back into a plank, so leftover slabs are never wasted.
41. **Doors and Trapdoors**: 12x any of `item_tag(minecraft:wooden_doors)`; 12x any of `item_tag(minecraft:wooden_trapdoors)` *(after: Slabs and Stairs)*
   > What: six logs in a door shape make 12 doors; six logs in a trapdoor shape make 12 trapdoors.
   > How: one wood type per craft (check JEI). Two logs side by side also make 4 pressure plates.
   > Tip: doors placed side by side open together, so a double door needs only one click.
42. **Re-Dyeing**: 8x any of `item_tag(c:concretes)` *(after: Doors and Trapdoors)*
   > What: Utilitarian lets you re-dye concrete, concrete powder, terracotta, stained glass, glass panes and candles that already have a colour.
   > Chemistry: real pigments are chemicals too: concrete's colours come from metal oxides, like iron oxide (Fe₂O₃) for red and brown.
   > How: eight coloured blocks around one dye re-colours all eight, or one block plus one dye does a single block (check JEI).
   > Tip: it also mixes blue and yellow dye into green, so cactus isn't the only green.
43. **Tiny Coal**: 8x `utilitarian:tiny_coal`; 8x `utilitarian:tiny_charcoal` *(after: Utilitarian Shortcuts, Coal)*
   > What: one coal or charcoal makes 8 tiny pieces. Each burns for 10 seconds, so you don't waste a whole coal on one item.
   > Chemistry: charcoal is wood heated without air (pyrolysis): water and volatile compounds are driven off, leaving mostly carbon.
   > How: put one coal or charcoal in the crafting grid. Eight tiny pieces craft back into one.
   > Tip: this pack's furnaces cook faster than vanilla, so one tiny coal covers more than one item.
44. **The Trowel**: `utilitarian:trowel` *(after: Utilitarian Shortcuts, Iron)*
   > What: the Trowel places a random block from your hotbar each time you use it. Great for natural-looking walls and paths.
   > How: two iron ingots and a stick (check JEI). Sneak-use it to switch between hotbar only and your whole inventory.
   > Tip: fill the hotbar with stone, cobblestone, andesite and tuff, and a plain wall looks weathered in seconds.
45. **Angel Block**: 4x `utilitarian:angel_block` *(after: Utilitarian Shortcuts, Iron)*
   > What: the Angel Block can be placed in empty air, with nothing next to it. It's the start of any sky bridge or floating build.
   > How: two feathers, two gold ingots and obsidian (check JEI). Use it while looking at empty air.
   > Tip: it's a building block, not flight. Flying in this pack is a chemistry milestone (see the Nether chapter).
46. **Snad**: 4x `utilitarian:snad` *(after: Tiny Coal)*
   > What: cactus, sugar cane, kelp and bamboo grow taller and faster on Snad. Soul Snad does the same for nether wart.
   > Chemistry: sand is mostly quartz grains, SiO₂, the same compound as the Nether quartz and certus you'll meet later.
   > How: two sand make one Snad (red sand makes Red Snad, soul sand makes Soul Snad).
   > Tip: a column of sugar cane on Snad is the fastest paper source for Sophisticated upgrades and Iron Furnace augments.
47. **Block Magnet**: `utilitarian:magnet` *(after: The Trowel)*
   > What: with a redstone signal, the Block Magnet pulls iron blocks, steel blocks and anvils below it up towards it.
   > Chemistry: iron is ferromagnetic: its atoms' tiny magnetic moments line up in domains. The recipe is an electromagnet, an iron core with copper on each side.
   > How: copper ingot, iron block, copper ingot in a row. Place it, put an iron block somewhere below, and power the magnet.
   > Tip: a magnet and a lever make a simple lift for iron blocks: power it to pull them up, cut the power to let them fall.
48. **Fluid Hopper**: `utilitarian:fluid_hopper` *(after: The Trowel, Water)*
   > What: the Fluid Hopper moves fluids the way a hopper moves items: it collects fluid from above and passes it on, the way a hopper does with items (check its JEI page).
   > How: iron ingots around a bucket, with white dye on top (check JEI).
   > Tip: under an infinite water source it fills a tank for your first steam boiler without any pump.
49. **Well Behaved Dropper**: `utilitarian:well_behaved_dropper` *(after: The Trowel)*
   > What: a dropper that drops items neatly in front of itself instead of flinging them in random directions.
   > How: a dropper with a gold nugget on each side (check JEI).
   > Tip: drop items onto a pressure plate or into water streams and they land exactly where you planned.
50. **Redstone Clock**: `utilitarian:redstone_clock` *(after: Snad)*
   > What: the Redstone Clock pulses a redstone signal on its own, with no repeater loop.
   > How: chiseled stone bricks with redstone on four sides (check JEI). Right-click it with an empty hand to change the speed; sneak to change it faster.
   > Tip: a slow clock on a dispenser or a Well Behaved Dropper makes a simple timed feeder.
51. **TPS Meter**: `utilitarian:tps_meter` *(after: Redstone Clock)*
   > What: the TPS Meter gives a redstone signal based on the dimension's ticks per second. A healthy server runs at 20.
   > How: four comparators around obsidian (check JEI).
   > Tip: wire it to a lamp in your factory: if it dims, something you built is lagging the server.
52. **Sound Muffler**: `utilitarian:sound_muffler` *(after: Redstone Clock)*
   > What: the Sound Muffler mutes sounds in a radius around it. Your crushers, pumps and boilers go quiet.
   > Chemistry: real soundproofing works the same way: soft, porous fibres like wool turn sound energy into a tiny amount of heat.
   > How: any wool plus a note block, shapeless.
   > Tip: one in the middle of a machine row is usually enough. Its tooltip shows the radius.
53. **Trader Carpet**: 1x any of `or(item(utilitarian:white_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:orange_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:magenta_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:light_blue_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:yellow_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:lime_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:pink_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:gray_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:light_gray_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:cyan_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:purple_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:blue_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:brown_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:green_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:red_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:black_soliciting_carpet))` *(after: Redstone Clock)*
   > What: a wandering trader arriving nearby appears on a Trader Carpet instead of right in your face.
   > How: any carpet plus a small flower, shapeless. Each colour has its own carpet.
   > Tip: put it in a little market stall by your base. JEI also shows a trapped version, if you're feeling unkind.
54. **No Soliciting**: `utilitarian:no_soliciting_banner` *(after: Trader Carpet)*
   > What: the No Soliciting Banner stops wandering traders from spawning in the chunks around it.
   > How: wool, a lead and a stick, in a banner shape (check JEI).
   > Tip: use either the carpet or the banner: carpet if you like the trader's goods, banner if you don't.
55. **Outpost Claim**: `utilitarian:no_raider_block` *(after: No Soliciting)*
   > What: place the Raider Outpost Claim Block inside a pillager outpost and raiders stop coming back to it.
   > How: the recipe uses an ominous (illager) banner, which a pillager captain drops (check JEI).
   > Tip: claim the outpost before building there; it makes a fine tower base.
56. **Un-Name Tag**: `utilitarian:unname_tag` *(after: No Soliciting)*
   > What: the Un-Name Tag removes a mob's custom name.
   > How: a name tag plus white dye, shapeless. Use it on the named mob.
   > Tip: useful when a pet name typo has been bothering you for weeks.
57. **Slime in a Bucket**: `utilitarian:slime_bucket` *(after: Un-Name Tag)*
   > You remember finding hidden things by feel. The slime remembers too.
   > What: you scooped a small slime into a bucket. It gets visibly excited when you carry it into a slime chunk.
   > How: use an empty bucket on a small slime. Place it again by using the bucket on the ground.
   > Tip: slime chunks spawn slimes underground at any light level, which makes them the best spot for a slime farm.
58. **The Enchanting Table**: `minecraft:enchanting_table`; 15x `minecraft:bookshelf`; 3x `minecraft:book` *(after: Comfort First, Iron Pickaxe)*
   > What: the enchanting table, with the 15 bookshelves it needs for level 30 enchantments. Apotheosis makes it much deeper (Magic group).
   > Chemistry: paper is pressed cellulose fibre; old books yellow because acids left in the paper slowly break those chains (and lignin oxidises).
   > How: table: a book, 2 diamonds and 4 obsidian. Bookshelf: 6 planks and 3 books. Book: 3 paper and a leather.
   > Tip: leave one block of air between the table and the shelves, or they don't count.
59. **Anvil**: `minecraft:anvil` *(after: Comfort First, Iron)*
   > What: the anvil joins enchanted books to tools, repairs gear with its own material, and renames items.
   > Chemistry: a real anvil is a block of hardened steel on a softer body: the hard face doesn't dent, the soft body doesn't crack.
   > How: 3 iron blocks and 4 iron ingots: 31 iron in all.
   > Tip: every repair raises the 'too expensive' cost. Combine books first, then put them on the tool in one go.
60. **Map, Compass and Clock**: `minecraft:map`; `minecraft:compass`; `minecraft:clock` *(after: Comfort First, Iron)*
   > What: a map draws the land as you walk; a compass points to world spawn (or a lodestone); a clock shows the time of day, even underground.
   > Chemistry: a real compass needle is magnetised iron. The first ones (China, about 1,000 years ago) used lodestone, naturally magnetic magnetite, Fe₃O₄.
   > How: map: paper around a compass. Compass: 4 iron around redstone. Clock: 4 gold around redstone.
   > Tip: JourneyMap does the mapping for you; a framed map on the wall is still a nice trophy.
61. **Redstone Basics**: `minecraft:lever`; 4x `minecraft:redstone_torch`; 2x `minecraft:repeater` *(after: Comfort First, Iron Pickaxe)*
   > What: the three parts of most redstone builds: a lever (a switch), a redstone torch (a NOT gate) and a repeater (a delay and a booster).
   > Chemistry: redstone is fiction, but the logic is real: a torch is an inverter, exactly like a transistor wired as a NOT gate in every chip you own.
   > How: lever: a stick on cobblestone. Torch: redstone on a stick. Repeater: 2 torches and redstone on stone.
   > Tip: MI and Mekanism machines can be switched off with redstone; a lever by your machines saves power at night.
62. **Daylight Detector**: `minecraft:daylight_detector` *(after: Redstone Basics, Nether Quartz)*
   > What: it outputs a signal that follows the sun. Right-click it to invert, so it fires at night instead.
   > Chemistry: a real light sensor is a photodiode: light knocks electrons loose in a semiconductor and a current flows. Same physics as a solar panel, just smaller.
   > How: glass, Nether quartz and wooden slabs (check JEI).
   > Tip: inverted, it switches on street lamps at dusk.
63. **Conduit Power**: `minecraft:conduit` *(after: Comfort First, Buried Treasure)*
   > What: an activated conduit gives Conduit Power to players in the water nearby: no drowning, night vision underwater and faster mining. A bigger frame also attacks hostile mobs.
   > Chemistry: nautilus shells are aragonite, a form of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) with a different crystal packing from calcite. The pearly sheen is layers of it thinner than a wavelength of light.
   > How: a heart of the sea (buried treasure) in 8 nautilus shells (drowned and fishing). Place it in water inside a frame of prismarine (check the wiki shape in JEI's info tab).
   > Tip: perfect for an underwater base, or for clearing an ocean monument.
64. **Harvester Pylon**: `pylons:harvester_pylon` *(after: Wings of a God, Animal Husbandry)*
   > What: harvests crops in a square around it (3x3 up to 9x9) and puts them in a chest above it. It wears a hoe down by 1 durability per harvest.
   > How: quartz slabs, iron bars and polished blackstone around a hay bale. Put it in the farm's water block (or level with the crops), a hoe inside, a chest on top.
   > Tip: an Unbreaking hoe lasts far longer; a Mending one never runs out.
65. **Interdiction Pylon**: `pylons:interdiction_pylon`; 1x any of `or(item(pylons:mob_filter)item(pylons:lifeless_filter))` *(after: Wings of a God, Ancient Debris)*
   > What: stops chosen mobs spawning in up to 5x5 chunks. A Mob Filter names the mob; the Lifeless Filter blocks all natural spawns over a much larger area.
   > How: the pylon frame around a netherite block. Filters: cyan terracotta, green dye and glass around netherite (mob) or a Nether Star (lifeless). Use a mob filter on the mob to set it.
   > Tip: a phantom filter over your base means sleepless nights are only a figure of speech.
66. **Guard Pylons**: `pylons:protection_pylon`; `pylons:expulsion_pylon`; 1x any of `or(item(pylons:player_filter)item(pylons:block_filter))` *(after: Wings of a God, Form a Team)*
   > What: the Protection Pylon stops you breaking chosen blocks or hurting chosen mobs in its range (so a pet or a showpiece is safe from your own sword). The Expulsion Pylon sends other players out of your chunks; whitelist friends with a Player Filter.
   > How: the pylon frame around a honeycomb block (protection) or a diamond block (expulsion). Filters: cyan terracotta, green dye and glass around honeycomb (block) or a diamond (player).
   > Tip: with FTB Teams, your team is whitelisted automatically.

### Building and Decoration

*A god's house should look like one.*

1. **Building Basics**: checkmark *(after: Planks and a Workbench)*
   > You remember raising cities with a gesture. For now, a few clever tools will do.
   > What: this page is a catalogue: building tools, gadgets, framed blocks, furniture, Macaw's blocks, Supplementaries, Create decor and a proper chemistry lab, one row each.
   > How: everything here is optional and cheap; pick what you like. Click the checkmark to open the page.
   > Tip: the lab row at the bottom opens once you have Nether quartz.
2. **Effortless Building**: `effortlessbuilding:randomizer_tool` *(after: Building Basics)*
   > What: Effortless Building adds mirror, array and line modes for big builds.
   > How: open its menu (check Controls) and pick a mode. The randomizer places a random mix of the blocks you load into it.
   > Tip: the randomizer with stone, andesite and cobblestone makes natural-looking walls.
3. **Construction Stick**: `constructionstick:wooden_stick` *(after: Building Basics)*
   > What: a Construction Stick places a whole row or face of blocks matching the one you click, using blocks from your inventory.
   > How: three sticks in a column (check JEI). Right-click the face of a wall to grow it by one layer.
   > Tip: the tooltip lists its modes, such as only extending in a straight line.
4. **Diamond Stick**: `constructionstick:diamond_stick` *(after: Construction Stick)*
   > What: better sticks place more blocks per click and last longer: copper, iron, diamond, then netherite.
   > Chemistry: diamond is pure carbon (C) in a tight 3D lattice, which makes it the hardest natural material.
   > How: a diamond on two sticks (check JEI). Templates applied at a smithing table add tricks like placing in mid-air.
5. **Rechiseled**: checkmark *(after: Building Basics, Iron)*
   > What: Rechiseled adds a chisel that turns stone, planks, metal blocks and more into decorative patterns: bricks, tiles, pillars, gears.
   > How: craft the chisel from an iron ingot on a stick, right-click to open it, put blocks in and pick a pattern. Click the checkmark when you've chiseled something.
   > Tip: many patterns connect to each other when placed side by side. Try the iron and copper block patterns for a machine room.
6. **Building Gadgets**: `buildinggadgets2:gadget_building` *(after: Building Basics, LV Machine Hull)*
   > What: FE-powered gadgets that place, swap, copy and remove blocks in bulk.
   > How: iron, redstone, lapis and a diamond (check JEI). Charge it in an energy cube.
   > Tip: link the gadget to a chest or backpack so it pulls blocks from storage.
7. **Copy and Paste**: `buildinggadgets2:gadget_copy_paste`; `buildinggadgets2:template_manager` *(after: Building Gadgets)*
   > What: copy an area and paste it elsewhere; the Template Manager saves copies to share.
   > How: check JEI. Great for repeating a chemical reactor cell or a row of machines.
   > Tip: templates can be shared with friends on the server.
8. **Exchanging Gadget**: `buildinggadgets2:gadget_exchanging` *(after: Building Gadgets)*
   > What: replaces blocks in an area with another block, keeping the shape.
   > How: check JEI. Perfect for turning a cobble shell into something pretty.
   > Tip: it uses the blocks in your inventory, so carry enough.
9. **Destruction Gadget**: `buildinggadgets2:gadget_destruction` *(after: Building Gadgets)*
   > What: removes a box of blocks in front of you, sized however you like. It can undo its last action.
   > How: check JEI. Set the depth, width and height in its menu.
   > Tip: perfect for hollowing out a hillside for a new factory floor.
10. **Framed Blocks**: 8x `framedblocks:framed_cube`; `framedblocks:framed_hammer` *(after: Building Basics)*
   > What: FramedBlocks are wooden frames that take the look of any block you right-click into them, in dozens of shapes.
   > How: framed cubes are planks and sticks (check JEI). Right-click a framed block with any full block to apply it as camouflage. The Framed Hammer takes it back off.
   > Tip: camouflage with glass, ores or even machine casings: the block keeps its shape and takes the texture.
11. **Slopes and Panels**: 6x any of `or(item(framedblocks:framed_slope)item(framedblocks:framed_corner_slope)item(framedblocks:framed_stairs)item(framedblocks:framed_slab)item(framedblocks:framed_panel)item(framedblocks:framed_pillar)item(framedblocks:framed_prism))` *(after: Framed Blocks)*
   > What: any six framed slopes, corner slopes, stairs, slabs, panels, pillars or prisms.
   > How: each shape is made from framed cubes (check JEI). Most come several at a time.
   > Tip: framed slopes camouflaged as stone make roofs and ramps that look hand-carved.
12. **Secret Storage**: `framedblocks:framed_secret_storage` *(after: Slopes and Panels)*
   > What: a full-block chest that wears any block's texture, so it disappears into a wall.
   > How: a framed chest surrounded by framed cubes (check JEI), then camouflage it.
   > Tip: hide your rarest elements in one. Nobody suspects the third stone brick from the left.
13. **Somewhere to Sit**: 2x any of `or(item(handcrafted:oak_chair)item(handcrafted:spruce_chair)item(handcrafted:birch_chair)item(handcrafted:jungle_chair)item(handcrafted:acacia_chair)item(handcrafted:dark_oak_chair)item(handcrafted:mangrove_chair)item(handcrafted:cherry_chair)item(handcrafted:bamboo_chair)item(handcrafted:crimson_chair)item(handcrafted:warped_chair))`; 1x any of `or(item(handcrafted:oak_table)item(handcrafted:spruce_table)item(handcrafted:birch_table)item(handcrafted:jungle_table)item(handcrafted:acacia_table)item(handcrafted:dark_oak_table)item(handcrafted:mangrove_table)item(handcrafted:cherry_table)item(handcrafted:bamboo_table)item(handcrafted:crimson_table)item(handcrafted:warped_table))` *(after: Building Basics)*
   > What: Handcrafted adds furniture you can actually sit on: chairs, couches, benches, tables, desks.
   > How: any wood works (check JEI). Right-click a chair to sit.
   > Tip: the Handcrafted Hammer changes the shape of trims and some other pieces (check its tooltip).
14. **A Proper Study**: 2x any of `or(item(handcrafted:oak_couch)item(handcrafted:spruce_couch)item(handcrafted:birch_couch)item(handcrafted:jungle_couch)item(handcrafted:acacia_couch)item(handcrafted:dark_oak_couch)item(handcrafted:mangrove_couch)item(handcrafted:cherry_couch)item(handcrafted:bamboo_couch)item(handcrafted:crimson_couch)item(handcrafted:warped_couch))`; 1x any of `or(item(handcrafted:oak_desk)item(handcrafted:spruce_desk)item(handcrafted:birch_desk)item(handcrafted:jungle_desk)item(handcrafted:acacia_desk)item(handcrafted:dark_oak_desk)item(handcrafted:mangrove_desk)item(handcrafted:cherry_desk)item(handcrafted:bamboo_desk)item(handcrafted:crimson_desk)item(handcrafted:warped_desk))` *(after: Somewhere to Sit)*
   > What: couches connect into long sofas; desks connect into long workbenches.
   > How: any wood (check JEI). Cushions and sheets add colour.
   > Tip: a desk by your Alchemistry machines makes a fine place to read the quest book.
15. **Macaw's Furniture**: 2x any of `or(item(mcwfurnitures:oak_wardrobe)item(mcwfurnitures:spruce_wardrobe)item(mcwfurnitures:birch_wardrobe)item(mcwfurnitures:jungle_wardrobe)item(mcwfurnitures:acacia_wardrobe)item(mcwfurnitures:dark_oak_wardrobe)item(mcwfurnitures:mangrove_wardrobe)item(mcwfurnitures:cherry_wardrobe)item(mcwfurnitures:crimson_wardrobe)item(mcwfurnitures:warped_wardrobe)item(mcwfurnitures:oak_drawer)item(mcwfurnitures:spruce_drawer)item(mcwfurnitures:birch_drawer)item(mcwfurnitures:jungle_drawer)item(mcwfurnitures:acacia_drawer)item(mcwfurnitures:dark_oak_drawer)item(mcwfurnitures:mangrove_drawer)item(mcwfurnitures:cherry_drawer)item(mcwfurnitures:crimson_drawer)item(mcwfurnitures:warped_drawer)item(mcwfurnitures:oak_kitchen_cabinet)item(mcwfurnitures:spruce_kitchen_cabinet)item(mcwfurnitures:birch_kitchen_cabinet)item(mcwfurnitures:jungle_kitchen_cabinet)item(mcwfurnitures:acacia_kitchen_cabinet)item(mcwfurnitures:dark_oak_kitchen_cabinet)item(mcwfurnitures:mangrove_kitchen_cabinet)item(mcwfurnitures:cherry_kitchen_cabinet)item(mcwfurnitures:crimson_kitchen_cabinet)item(mcwfurnitures:warped_kitchen_cabinet))` *(after: Somewhere to Sit)*
   > What: Macaw's Furniture adds kitchens, wardrobes, drawers, bookshelves and more. Many of them store items.

   > What: a lava lamp for your desk. This one really has lava in it.

38. **Know Your Rocks**: 64x any of `or(item(minecraft:stone)item(minecraft:deepslate)item(minecraft:andesite)item(minecraft:diorite)item(minecraft:granite)item(minecraft:tuff)item(minecraft:calcite))` *(after: Building Basics, Stone Age)*
   > What: stone, deepslate, andesite, diorite, granite, tuff or calcite, mixed as you like. Each has a polished and brick form for building.
   > Chemistry: granite cooled slowly deep underground, so its quartz and feldspar crystals grew big; andesite and diorite are its iron- and calcium-richer cousins. Tuff is welded volcanic ash, and calcite is CaCO₃.
   > How: mine them with Silk Touch for smooth stone, or smelt cobblestone back into stone.
   > Tip: the Trowel (Quality of Life page) mixes them into a natural-looking wall.
39. **Rocks of Other Biomes**: 16x `regions_unexplored:chalk`; 16x `regions_unexplored:argillite`; 8x `regions_unexplored:mossy_stone` *(after: Know Your Rocks)*
   > What: three building stones from Regions Unexplored biomes: white chalk, dark red argillite and mossy stone.
   > Chemistry: chalk is CaCO₃ made of the tiny plates (coccoliths) of ancient sea algae: the white cliffs of Dover are trillions of them. Argillite is clay squeezed into hard rock.
   > How: find the biomes with Nature's Compass (Quality of Life page) and mine the stone.
   > Tip: chalk is soft and white; it lights a room almost like the lab blocks.
40. **Dripstone**: 8x `minecraft:pointed_dripstone`; 8x `minecraft:dripstone_block` *(after: Know Your Rocks)*
   > What: pointed dripstone grows down from the ceiling and up from the floor in dripstone caves. Hanging under a water source, it slowly fills cauldrons below.
   > Chemistry: water carrying calcium bicarbonate drips, loses CO₂ and leaves calcite behind: Ca(HCO₃)₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O + CO₂. A real stalactite grows about a centimetre a century.
   > How: mine both in a dripstone cave (Nature's Compass finds one).
   > Tip: falling pointed dripstone hurts like an arrow. Mind your head.
41. **Masonry**: 16x `minecraft:clay_ball`; 16x `minecraft:brick`; 4x `minecraft:chiseled_stone_bricks`; 8x `minecraft:cobblestone_wall` *(after: Building Basics, Fire)*
   > What: clay fires into bricks; stone bricks chisel into patterns; walls make fences that mobs can't jump.
   > Chemistry: clay is mostly kaolinite, Al₂Si₂O₅(OH)₄. Fired above about 900 °C it loses its water and the particles sinter together into hard, waterproof ceramic.
   > How: dig clay from riverbeds and lush caves and smelt it into bricks. Chiseled stone bricks come from the stonecutter; walls from cobblestone.
   > Tip: a stonecutter makes walls, stairs and slabs with no waste.
42. **Terracotta and Concrete**: 16x `minecraft:terracotta`; 16x any of `or(item(minecraft:white_concrete_powder)item(minecraft:orange_concrete_powder)item(minecraft:magenta_concrete_powder)item(minecraft:light_blue_concrete_powder)item(minecraft:yellow_concrete_powder)item(minecraft:lime_concrete_powder)item(minecraft:pink_concrete_powder)item(minecraft:gray_concrete_powder)item(minecraft:light_gray_concrete_powder)item(minecraft:cyan_concrete_powder)item(minecraft:purple_concrete_powder)item(minecraft:blue_concrete_powder)item(minecraft:brown_concrete_powder)item(minecraft:green_concrete_powder)item(minecraft:red_concrete_powder)item(minecraft:black_concrete_powder))` *(after: Masonry)*
   > What: terracotta is fired clay; concrete powder is sand, gravel and dye that sets into concrete when it touches water.
   > Chemistry: real concrete doesn't dry, it reacts: calcium silicates in cement take up water (hydration) and grow interlocking crystals. It even sets underwater.
   > How: smelt clay blocks into terracotta; 4 sand, 4 gravel and a dye make 8 concrete powder of any colour.
   > Tip: place powder in front of a water flow, or run it through Create's bulk washing, to harden a whole stack.
43. **Lighting Without Torches**: 16x `minecraft:glowstone_dust`; 4x `minecraft:glowstone`; 4x `minecraft:redstone_lamp`; 2x `minecraft:soul_lantern` *(after: Building Basics, Into the Fire)*
   > What: glowstone gives the brightest block light; redstone lamps switch on and off; soul lanterns burn blue and dim.
   > Chemistry: a flame is incandescence (hot soot glowing). Cold light, from LEDs to glow-sticks, is luminescence: electrons drop between energy levels and give off exactly one colour.
   > How: glowstone from the Nether ceiling (4 dust per block); lamp: glowstone in redstone; soul lantern: a soul torch in iron nuggets.
   > Tip: a lamp on a daylight detector lights itself at dusk.
44. **Froglights**: `minecraft:ochre_froglight`; `minecraft:verdant_froglight`; `minecraft:pearlescent_froglight` *(after: Lighting Without Torches, Animal Husbandry)*
   > What: a frog that eats a small magma cube leaves a froglight. Its colour depends on the frog: temperate, warm or cold.
   > Chemistry: real frogs' skin colour comes from pigment cells stacked in layers: yellow pigment over a layer that scatters blue light makes green, the same trick as a blue sky.
   > How: scoop tadpoles from a swamp in a bucket, raise them in a temperate, a warm and a cold biome, and bring the three frogs to the Nether's magma cubes.
   > Tip: a lead is the easiest way to walk frogs through a portal.
45. **Mineral Blocks**: 4x `minecraft:copper_block`; 2x `minecraft:lapis_block`; 8x `minecraft:quartz_block` *(after: Building Basics, Nether Quartz)*
   > What: copper blocks weather from orange to green; lapis and quartz blocks are the classic blue and white trims.
   > Chemistry: copper turns green as it reacts with air, water and CO₂ into basic copper carbonate (the Statue of Liberty's patina). Honeycomb wax stops it, an axe scrapes it back.
   > How: 9 copper ingots or 9 lapis per block; 4 Nether quartz per quartz block. Cut copper and quartz pillars come from the stonecutter.
   > Tip: copper blocks in Create Deco and Rechiseled take the same patina.
46. **Amethyst**: 8x `minecraft:amethyst_shard`; 2x `minecraft:amethyst_block` *(after: Building Basics, Iron Pickaxe)*
   > What: amethyst clusters grow on budding amethyst inside underground geodes. Shards make spyglasses, tinted glass and amethyst blocks that chime.
   > Chemistry: amethyst is quartz, SiO₂, coloured violet by traces of iron that natural radiation has nudged into Fe⁴⁺ colour centres. Heat it and it turns yellow (citrine).
   > How: break fully grown clusters in a geode (calcite and smooth basalt shells), and craft 4 shards into a block.
   > Tip: never break the budding amethyst: it can't be moved and it's the only thing that grows more.
47. **Building with Ice**: 8x `minecraft:snow_block`; 8x `minecraft:packed_ice`; 2x `minecraft:blue_ice` *(after: Building Basics)*
   > What: snow blocks, packed ice (doesn't melt) and blue ice, the slipperiest block in the game: boats on blue ice outrun horses.
   > Chemistry: ice floats because hydrogen bonds lock water into an open hexagonal lattice, about 9% less dense than liquid water. That's why lakes freeze from the top.
   > How: 4 snowballs make a snow block; 9 ice make packed ice, 9 packed ice make blue ice. Ice needs Silk Touch; icebergs have packed and blue ice.
   > Tip: a blue-ice boat road in the Nether makes long trips fast.
48. **Nether Masonry**: 16x `minecraft:polished_blackstone`; `minecraft:gilded_blackstone`; 4x `minecraft:chain` *(after: Building Basics, Blackstone)*
   > What: polished blackstone and its bricks make dark, gothic builds; gilded blackstone sparkles with gold; chains hang lanterns.
   > Chemistry: gold in veins inside dark rock is how real gold is often found: hot water carries dissolved gold through cracks and drops it as it cools.
   > How: polish blackstone in a stonecutter. Gilded blackstone is found in bastions. Chain: an iron ingot between two iron nuggets.
   > Tip: gilded blackstone sometimes drops gold nuggets when mined without Silk Touch.
49. **End Stone**: 16x `minecraft:end_stone`; 8x `minecraft:end_stone_bricks` *(after: Building Basics, The End)*
   > What: end stone and its bricks: pale yellow and very blast-resistant. Chorus plants grow only on it.
   > How: mine end stone on any End island; 4 end stone make 4 end stone bricks.
   > Tip: end stone resists explosions far better than cobblestone, so wall in anything that might blow.
50. **Finishing Touches**: 2x `minecraft:painting`; `minecraft:carved_pumpkin`; `minecraft:cauldron`; 8x any of `or(item(minecraft:stripped_oak_log)item(minecraft:stripped_spruce_log)item(minecraft:stripped_birch_log)item(minecraft:stripped_jungle_log)item(minecraft:stripped_acacia_log)item(minecraft:stripped_dark_oak_log)item(minecraft:stripped_mangrove_log)item(minecraft:stripped_cherry_log))` *(after: Building Basics, Iron)*
   > What: the small things that make a base feel lived in: paintings, a carved pumpkin, a cauldron and stripped-log beams.
   > Chemistry: stripping a log takes off the bark, which is full of tannins: the same polyphenols that tan leather.
   > How: painting: sticks around wool. Carve a pumpkin with shears. Cauldron: 7 iron. Use an axe on any log to strip it.
   > Tip: a cauldron under pointed dripstone fills with water by itself.
51. **Showing Off**: `minecraft:diamond_block` *(after: Mineral Blocks, Iron Tier)*
   > You remember a throne cut from a single gem. A block of diamond on the mantelpiece is a start.
   > What: a block of diamond, placed only to be looked at.
   > Chemistry: a diamond block's worth of real diamond would be about 3.5 tonnes of pure carbon. Burn it and you'd get about 13 tonnes of CO₂.
52. **Tool Extras**: `framedblocks:framing_saw`; `mcwwindows:hammer`; `constructionstick:template_angel` *(after: Framed Blocks, Windows, Diamond Stick)*
   > What: the Framing Saw crafts any framed shape from plain framed cubes; the Window Hammer reshapes a placed Macaw's window; the Angel template lets a Construction Stick place blocks in mid-air.
   > How: check JEI for each. Apply the template to a stick at a smithing table.
   > Tip: the angel template is a building aid, not flight. Flight in this pack is a chemistry milestone.
53. **Bamboo Spikes**: 4x `supplementaries:bamboo_spikes` *(after: Jars)*
   > What: Supplementaries bamboo spikes hurt mobs that walk on them; coated with a lingering potion they poison them too.
   > How: 4 bamboo over 3 wooden slabs (check JEI). Use a lingering potion on placed spikes to coat them.
   > Tip: a ring of spikes around a farm keeps zombies off the crops.

## Chemistry Lab

### The Periodic Table

*Rebuild the table, group by group. Each column shares a chemistry, because each shares an outer-electron arrangement.*

1. **Reading the Table**: checkmark *(after: First Entries in the Periodic Table)*
   > You remember this chart. You used to know every box by heart.
   > What: the periodic table orders the elements by proton number. Rows are periods; columns are groups.
   > Chemistry: elements in the same group have the same number of outer (valence) electrons, so they react alike.
   > How: press U on any element in JEI to see which blocks the Dissolver turns into it.
   > Tip: this chapter is a side path. Nothing in the main story waits on it, but it pays well.
2. **Alkali Metals**: 8x `chemlib:lithium`; 8x `chemlib:sodium`; 8x `chemlib:potassium` *(after: Reading the Table)*
   > What: lithium, sodium and potassium, the softest and most reactive metals.
   > Chemistry: one valence electron, easily lost. Sodium fizzes on water (2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂); potassium burns lilac.
   > How: end stone gives lithium; lapis lazuli gives sodium (the mineral lazurite is a sodium aluminosilicate). Plants give potassium.
   > Tip: check JEI with U on each element. Many common blocks hide small amounts.
3. **Alkaline Earth Metals**: 4x `chemlib:beryllium`; 8x `chemlib:magnesium`; 8x `chemlib:calcium` *(after: Alkali Metals)*
   > What: beryllium, magnesium and calcium: lighter structural metals and the stuff of bones and limestone.
   > Chemistry: two valence electrons, so they form 2+ ions. Calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) is limestone; magnesium burns blinding white.
   > How: andesite and bone give calcium (bone via hydroxylapatite, the mineral in teeth). Beryllium and magnesium come out of their compounds: check JEI.
4. **Transition Metals**: 16x `chemlib:iron`; 16x `chemlib:copper`; 8x `chemlib:nickel`; 8x `chemlib:zinc`; 4x `chemlib:gold` *(after: Alkaline Earth Metals)*
   > What: the hard, conductive metals behind every machine you've built.
   > Chemistry: their d-orbitals fill across the row. That's why they form coloured compounds and make good catalysts.
   > How: dissolve ingots, nuggets or dusts of each metal.
   > Tip: ore you already process gives nuggets and dust. Dissolve the spares, not your ingots.
5. **Post-Transition Metals**: 8x `chemlib:aluminum`; 8x `chemlib:tin`; 8x `chemlib:lead`; 4x `chemlib:indium` *(after: Transition Metals)*
   > What: aluminum, tin, lead and indium: softer, lower-melting metals just right of the transition block.
   > Chemistry: indium tin oxide is the clear conductor in every touchscreen. Lead is dense enough to stop X-rays.
   > How: diorite dissolves into tin and indium. Aluminum and lead come from their ingots, dusts and minerals (check JEI).
   > Perk: hold one of each of these four elements and your body remembers them: +2 armor toughness, permanently. Soft metals bend instead of breaking.
   > Tip: type /warbucks elements to see which Periodic Table perks you've unlocked and what's still missing.
6. **Liquid Metals**: 4x `chemlib:mercury`; 4x `chemlib:gallium` *(after: Transition Metals)*
   > What: mercury and gallium, the two metals you can pour (almost) at room temperature.
   > Chemistry: mercury melts at −38.8 °C; gallium at 29.8 °C, below body temperature.
   > How: ender pearls and end stone dissolve into mercury. Cobblestone gives a little gallium.
7. **Challenge: The First Twenty**: `chemlib:hydrogen`; `chemlib:helium`; `chemlib:lithium`; `chemlib:beryllium`; `chemlib:boron`; `chemlib:carbon`; `chemlib:nitrogen`; `chemlib:oxygen`; `chemlib:fluorine`; `chemlib:neon`; `chemlib:sodium`; `chemlib:magnesium`; `chemlib:aluminum`; `chemlib:silicon`; `chemlib:phosphorus`; `chemlib:sulfur`; `chemlib:chlorine`; `chemlib:argon`; `chemlib:potassium`; `chemlib:calcium` *(after: Noble Gases)*
   > What: one of each of elements 1 to 20, the four shortest rows of the table.
   > Chemistry: these twenty make up almost all of your body, the oceans and the air.
   > How: most come from the groups in this chapter. Boron and the noble gases need the Fusion Chamber (boron is 5: try H + Be).
   > Tip: an optional collection. Keep one of each in a chest as you go.
8. **The Coinage Metals**: 8x `chemlib:copper`; 8x `chemlib:silver`; 8x `chemlib:gold` *(after: Transition Metals)*
   > What: the three metals humans have minted into money for thousands of years.
   > Chemistry: they're unreactive enough to keep their shine. Silver is the best electrical conductor of any element.
   > How: deepslate dissolves into a little silver. Check JEI for richer sources.
9. **Metalloids**: 4x `chemlib:germanium`; 16x `chemlib:silicon`; 4x `chemlib:arsenic` *(after: Reading the Table)*
   > What: germanium, silicon and arsenic sit on the staircase between metals and non-metals.
   > Chemistry: silicon conducts a little, and a trace of arsenic (doping) controls how much. The first transistor (1947) was germanium.
   > How: sand dissolves into silicon dioxide, which dissolves again into silicon and oxygen. Blaze powder and Nether bricks give germanium.
   > Tip: you'll need a lot of silicon later, for circuits and AE2.
10. **Non-Metals**: 16x `chemlib:nitrogen`; 8x `chemlib:phosphorus`; 16x `chemlib:sulfur` *(after: Metalloids)*
   > What: nitrogen, phosphorus and sulfur. Life and industry both run on them.
   > Chemistry: nitrogen and phosphorus feed every crop; sulfur becomes sulfuric acid, the most-made chemical on Earth.
   > How: check JEI with U. Nether blocks are a good place to look for sulfur.
11. **Chalcogens**: 16x `chemlib:oxygen`; 16x `chemlib:sulfur`; 4x `chemlib:selenium` *(after: Non-Metals)*
   > What: oxygen, sulfur and selenium. 'Chalcogen' means 'ore-former'.
   > Chemistry: two electrons short of a full shell, so they grab metals: most ores are oxides or sulfides (Fe₂O₃, ZnS, PbS).
   > How: fish and crimson fungus dissolve into selenium. Oxygen comes from nearly everything.
   > Tip: selenium is a trace nutrient: you need a little, and too much is poisonous.
12. **Halogens**: 4x `chemlib:fluorine`; 8x `chemlib:chlorine`; 4x `chemlib:bromine`; 4x `chemlib:iodine` *(after: Chalcogens)*
   > What: fluorine, chlorine, bromine and iodine, the most reactive non-metals.
   > Chemistry: one electron short of full. 'Halogen' means 'salt-maker': Na + Cl → NaCl, table salt.
   > How: magma blocks give fluorine and bromine. Horn coral gives iodine (via lead iodide). Chlorine comes out of salts: check JEI.
13. **Noble Gases**: 8x `chemlib:helium`; 8x `chemlib:neon`; 8x `chemlib:argon` *(after: Halogens, Post-Transition Metals, EV: Processing Units)*
   > Two halves of the table, joined. More of the old knowledge settles into place.
   > What: helium, neon and argon, the gases that refuse to react.
   > Chemistry: a full outer shell means nothing to gain or lose. Argon shields welds from air; neon glows red in a discharge tube.
   > How: nothing dissolves into them, so build them: the Alchemistry Fusion Chamber (EV) adds proton numbers, so H + H → He. Check JEI for neon and argon.
   > Tip: real stars fuse hydrogen into helium too, though it takes them four protons, not two.
14. **Heavy Noble Gases**: 2x `chemlib:xenon`; 2x `chemlib:radon` *(after: Noble Gases)*
   > What: xenon and radon, the heaviest natural noble gases.
   > Chemistry: in 1962 xenon was made to react (with platinum hexafluoride), ending the idea that noble gases never react. Radon is radioactive.
   > How: dragon's breath dissolves into both. That means a trip to the End.
15. **Rare Earths**: 4x `chemlib:lanthanum`; 4x `chemlib:cerium`; 4x `chemlib:neodymium` *(after: Noble Gases)*
   > What: the lanthanides: lanthanum, cerium, neodymium and their near-identical neighbours.
   > Chemistry: they differ only in an inner (4f) shell, so their chemistry is almost the same. Neodymium makes the strongest permanent magnets.
   > How: check JEI for sources. The Alchemistry Fusion Chamber can also build them from lighter elements.
16. **Actinides**: 4x `chemlib:thorium`; 8x `chemlib:uranium`; 4x `chemlib:plutonium` *(after: Noble Gases, Transmutation by Neutron)*
   > What: thorium, uranium and plutonium, the fuels of the nuclear age.
   > Chemistry: every actinide is radioactive. Plutonium barely exists in nature: you made it by firing neutrons at uranium.
   > How: dissolve uranium and thorium materials. Plutonium comes from your fission reactor's waste.
17. **Isotopes: Heavy Water**: `mekanism:electric_pump`; `mekanism:upgrade_filter`; `mekanism:heavy_water_bucket` *(after: Alkali Metals, Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser)*
   > What: heavy water, D₂O: water made with deuterium, hydrogen with an extra neutron.
   > Chemistry: isotopes have the same protons (so the same chemistry) but different neutrons. About 1 in 6,400 hydrogen atoms is deuterium.
   > How: put a Filter Upgrade in a Mekanism Electric Pump and pump from water. It pulls out heavy water instead.
   > Tip: deuterium is half of fusion fuel. You'll want this again in the Power chapter.
18. **Superheavy Elements**: `chemlib:tennessine` *(after: Rare Earths, Actinides)*
   > What: tennessine, element 117. Nothing in the world dissolves into it; you have to build it.
   > Chemistry: real labs make superheavy elements by smashing nuclei together; only a handful of atoms have ever existed.
   > How: the Alchemistry Fusion Chamber joins two elements, adding their proton numbers. Check JEI for the pairs that reach 117.
   > Tip: one more step after this: add hydrogen (1) to tennessine (117) and you get 118.
19. **Element 118**: `chemlib:oganesson` *(after: Superheavy Elements, The Complete Periodic Table)*
   > The last box on the table. You remember now: you once named these.
   > What: oganesson, the heaviest element ever made.
   > Chemistry: in reality it lasts under a millisecond. Here it sits in your inventory, which is the kind of thing demigods can do.
   > How: fuse tennessine with hydrogen (or any pair adding to 118) in the Fusion Chamber.
20. **Covalent Bonds: CO₂**: 4x `chemlib:carbon_dioxide` *(after: Non-Metals)*
   > What: carbon dioxide, your first compound in this chapter.
   > Chemistry: C + O₂ → CO₂. Non-metals don't hand electrons over; they share them in covalent bonds (O=C=O).
   > How: in the Combiner, pick Carbon Dioxide and supply 1 carbon + 2 oxygen.
   > Tip: the Combiner GUI shows each recipe once you select its output.
21. **Hydrocarbons**: 4x `chemlib:methane`; 4x `chemlib:ethylene` *(after: Covalent Bonds: CO₂)*
   > What: methane (natural gas) and ethylene (the building block of polyethylene).
   > Chemistry: CH₄ has four single bonds. C₂H₄ has a C=C double bond, which is what lets it link into plastic chains.
   > How: Combiner: methane = 1 C + 4 H; ethylene = 2 C + 4 H.
22. **Ammonia**: 4x `chemlib:ammonia` *(after: Hydrocarbons)*
   > What: ammonia, NH₃, the base of nearly all fertiliser.
   > Chemistry: N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃. Breaking nitrogen's triple bond is hard; the Haber-Bosch process needs heat, pressure and an iron catalyst.
   > How: Combiner: 1 nitrogen + 3 hydrogen. Later you'll run real Haber-Bosch in an MI machine.
23. **Ionic Bonds: Salt**: 8x `chemlib:sodium_chloride` *(after: Ammonia)*
   > What: sodium chloride, NaCl: table salt.
   > Chemistry: sodium gives its one electron to chlorine. Na⁺ and Cl⁻ then hold together in a cubic crystal: an ionic bond.
   > How: Combiner: 1 sodium + 1 chlorine.
   > Tip: a reactive metal plus a poisonous gas makes something you sprinkle on food. Chemistry is strange.
24. **Strong Acids**: 4x `chemlib:hydrochloric_acid`; 4x `chemlib:nitric_acid` *(after: Ionic Bonds: Salt)*
   > What: hydrochloric acid (HCl) and nitric acid (HNO₃).
   > Chemistry: acids give up H⁺ ions in water. Mixed 3:1, HCl and HNO₃ make aqua regia, which dissolves gold and platinum.
   > How: Combiner: HCl = 1 H + 1 Cl; HNO₃ = 1 H + 1 N + 3 O.
25. **King of Chemicals**: 8x `chemlib:sulfuric_acid` *(after: Strong Acids)*
   > Built atom by atom. The old craft is coming back faster now.
   > What: sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄, built straight from elements.
   > Chemistry: industry makes it by the contact process: S → SO₂ → SO₃ → H₂SO₄. Here you skip the plant and place the atoms yourself.
   > How: Combiner: 2 hydrogen + 1 sulfur + 4 oxygen.
26. **Sugar and Wood**: 2x `chemlib:sucrose`; 2x `chemlib:cellulose` *(after: Covalent Bonds: CO₂)*
   > What: sucrose (table sugar) and cellulose (what wood and paper are made of).
   > Chemistry: plants make both from CO₂ and water using sunlight. Cellulose is a chain of glucose rings: C₆H₁₀O₅ per unit.
   > How: Combiner: sucrose = 12 C + 22 H + 11 O; cellulose = 6 C + 10 H + 5 O.
   > Tip: that's a lot of atoms. Stock up on carbon, hydrogen and oxygen first.
27. **Alcohol**: 4x `chemlib:hydroxide`; 2x `chemlib:ethanol` *(after: Hydrocarbons)*
   > What: ethanol, C₂H₅OH, made by attaching a hydroxide (OH) group to a two-carbon chain.
   > Chemistry: the -OH group is what makes it an alcohol and lets it mix with water.
   > How: Combiner: hydroxide = 1 O + 1 H, then ethanol = 2 C + 5 H + 1 hydroxide.
28. **Lye**: 4x `chemlib:sodium_hydroxide` *(after: Ionic Bonds: Salt)*
   > What: sodium hydroxide, NaOH: lye, a strong base.
   > Chemistry: industry makes it by electrolysing salt water: 2NaCl + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + Cl₂ + H₂. Acid + base → salt + water.
   > How: Combiner: 1 sodium + 1 hydroxide (make hydroxide from 1 O + 1 H).
29. **Rust**: 4x `chemlib:iron_oxide` *(after: Strong Acids)*
   > What: iron(III) oxide, Fe₂O₃: rust, and also hematite, the most common iron ore.
   > Chemistry: 4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃. A blast furnace runs this backwards, using carbon to pull the oxygen off.
   > How: Combiner: 2 iron + 3 oxygen.
30. **Group 1, Complete**: `chemlib:lithium`; `chemlib:sodium`; `chemlib:potassium`; `chemlib:rubidium`; `chemlib:cesium`; `chemlib:francium` *(after: Noble Gases)*
   > What: all six alkali metals: Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs and Fr.
   > Chemistry: reactivity climbs down the group: the outer electron sits further from the nucleus and is lost more easily. Caesium explodes in water.
   > How: press U on rubidium and caesium in JEI for Dissolver sources. Francium is rare in both reality and here; the Fusion Chamber can build it.
   > Tip: real francium has a half-life of about 22 minutes. Yours keeps.
31. **Group 2, Complete**: `chemlib:beryllium`; `chemlib:magnesium`; `chemlib:calcium`; `chemlib:strontium`; `chemlib:barium`; `chemlib:radium` *(after: Group 1, Complete)*
   > What: all six alkaline earth metals: Be, Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba and Ra.
   > Chemistry: strontium salts burn red and barium salts green: that's how fireworks get their colours. Radium glows from its own radioactivity.
   > How: JEI (U) shows Dissolver sources for strontium, barium and radium; the Fusion Chamber fills any gaps.
32. **The Boron Group**: `chemlib:boron`; `chemlib:aluminum`; `chemlib:gallium`; `chemlib:indium`; `chemlib:thallium` *(after: Group 2, Complete)*
   > What: boron, aluminum, gallium, indium and thallium.
   > Chemistry: boron is a metalloid; the rest are metals. Borosilicate glass (with B₂O₃) survives sudden heat, which is why lab glassware uses it.
   > How: boron needs the Fusion Chamber (5 = 1 + 4: hydrogen + beryllium). Check JEI for thallium.
   > Tip: thallium is very toxic in reality. In a chest it's harmless.
33. **The Carbon Group**: `chemlib:carbon`; `chemlib:silicon`; `chemlib:germanium`; `chemlib:tin`; `chemlib:lead` *(after: Post-Transition Metals)*
   > What: carbon, silicon, germanium, tin and lead, all with four valence electrons.
   > Chemistry: the group runs from a non-metal (carbon) through metalloids (Si, Ge) to metals (Sn, Pb). Same outer shell, very different behaviour.
   > How: all five come from the Dissolver: coal or graphite, sand, Nether bricks, diorite and lead ingots (check JEI).
34. **The Pnictogens**: `chemlib:nitrogen`; `chemlib:phosphorus`; `chemlib:arsenic`; `chemlib:antimony`; `chemlib:bismuth` *(after: Non-Metals)*
   > What: nitrogen, phosphorus, arsenic, antimony and bismuth.
   > Chemistry: five valence electrons, so they often form three bonds (NH₃, PH₃). Bismuth crystals grow in stepped 'hopper' shapes with a rainbow oxide film.
   > How: JEI (U) shows Dissolver sources for antimony and bismuth.
35. **Group 17, Complete**: `chemlib:fluorine`; `chemlib:chlorine`; `chemlib:bromine`; `chemlib:iodine`; `chemlib:astatine` *(after: The Boron Group)*
   > What: the four common halogens plus astatine, one of the rarest natural elements on Earth.
   > Chemistry: down the group the halogens go from gas (F₂, Cl₂) to liquid (Br₂) to solid (I₂): bigger molecules attract each other more strongly.
   > How: astatine has a few Dissolver sources (press U in JEI), or build it in the Fusion Chamber.
36. **Group 18, Complete**: `chemlib:helium`; `chemlib:neon`; `chemlib:argon`; `chemlib:krypton`; `chemlib:xenon`; `chemlib:radon` *(after: Heavy Noble Gases)*
   > What: helium through radon, the whole right-hand column.
   > Chemistry: from 1960 to 1983 the metre was defined by the orange light of krypton-86. Xenon lights car headlamps and drives ion engines in spacecraft.
   > How: nothing dissolves into the light ones: fuse them in the Fusion Chamber (krypton is 36: try neon + iron). Xenon and radon come from dragon's breath.
37. **All Fifteen Lanthanides**: `chemlib:lanthanum`; `chemlib:cerium`; `chemlib:praseodymium`; `chemlib:neodymium`; `chemlib:promethium`; `chemlib:samarium`; `chemlib:europium`; `chemlib:gadolinium`; `chemlib:terbium`; `chemlib:dysprosium`; `chemlib:holmium`; `chemlib:erbium`; `chemlib:thulium`; `chemlib:ytterbium`; `chemlib:lutetium` *(after: Rare Earths)*
   > What: the full lanthanide row, the first line of the f-block.
   > Chemistry: europium makes the red in old TV screens and the anti-forgery glow in euro notes. Promethium has no stable isotope at all.
   > How: a few have Dissolver sources (press U); the Fusion Chamber builds the rest by adding proton numbers.
   > Tip: a challenge, not a requirement. Work through them as spare elements pile up.
38. **All Fifteen Actinides**: `chemlib:actinium`; `chemlib:thorium`; `chemlib:protactinium`; `chemlib:uranium`; `chemlib:neptunium`; `chemlib:plutonium`; `chemlib:americium`; `chemlib:curium`; `chemlib:berkelium`; `chemlib:californium`; `chemlib:einsteinium`; `chemlib:fermium`; `chemlib:mendelevium`; `chemlib:nobelium`; `chemlib:lawrencium` *(after: Actinides)*
   > What: the full actinide row. Everything past uranium is man-made.
   > Chemistry: einsteinium and fermium were first found in the debris of the first hydrogen bomb test in 1952. Americium sits in household smoke detectors.
   > How: the Fusion Chamber: gold (79) plus a light element reaches actinium and beyond (check JEI for the pairs).
39. **Limestone**: 4x `chemlib:calcium_carbonate` *(after: Covalent Bonds: CO₂)*
   > What: calcium carbonate, the mineral in limestone, chalk, marble and seashells.
   > Chemistry: heat it and it splits: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. That quicklime is the start of cement and mortar.
   > How: Combiner: first carbonate (1 carbon + 3 oxygen), then 1 calcium + 1 carbonate.
40. **Saltpeter**: 4x `chemlib:potassium_nitrate` *(after: Ammonia)*
   > What: potassium nitrate, the oxidiser in gunpowder and a classic fertiliser.
   > Chemistry: black powder is roughly 75% KNO₃, 15% charcoal and 10% sulfur. The nitrate brings its own oxygen, so it burns without air.
   > How: Combiner: nitrate (1 nitrogen + 3 oxygen), then 1 potassium + 1 nitrate.
   > Tip: the Combiner also turns potassium nitrate, sulfur and graphite into gunpowder (check JEI).
41. **Aspirin**: 2x `chemlib:acetylsalicylic_acid` *(after: Alcohol)*
   > What: acetylsalicylic acid, the world's best-known painkiller.
   > Chemistry: willow bark contains salicin, used against pain for thousands of years. Adding an acetyl group (1897) made it gentler on the stomach.
   > How: Combiner: 9 carbon + 8 hydrogen + 4 oxygen.
42. **Permanganate**: 2x `chemlib:potassium_permanganate` *(after: Lye)*
   > What: potassium permanganate, deep purple crystals and a strong oxidiser.
   > Chemistry: manganese here is in its +7 oxidation state and eager to take electrons back. The purple fades as it reacts, so chemists use it as its own indicator.
   > How: Combiner: 1 potassium + 1 manganese + 4 oxygen.
43. **Morning Coffee**: `chemlib:caffeine` *(after: Ammonia)*
   > Even a demigod likes a cup in the morning. You remember that much without trying.
   > What: caffeine, built atom by atom: 8 carbon, 10 hydrogen, 4 nitrogen, 2 oxygen.
   > Chemistry: it blocks adenosine receptors in the brain, the signal that tells you you're tired.
   > Tip: plants make caffeine as an insecticide. You drink it on purpose.
44. **Han Purple**: `chemlib:han_purple` *(after: Ionic Bonds: Salt)*
   > What: han purple, BaCuSi₂O₆, a barium copper silicate.
   > Chemistry: Chinese artisans made it more than 2,000 years ago by firing barium, copper and silica minerals together. It colours figures in the Terracotta Army.
   > How: Combiner: 1 barium + 1 copper + 2 silicon + 6 oxygen.
   > Tip: one of the first synthetic pigments in history. You just repeated an ancient experiment.

### Mekanism

*Osmium, infusion and gases: Mekanism's machines, factories, circuits and logistics. Reactors and add-ons are on the next page.*

1. **The Mekanism Way**: checkmark *(after: Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser)*
   > Osmium hums in your hand. You remember metals that drank other substances and grew stronger.
   > What: Mekanism is a machine mod built on infusion and gases: soak a metal in carbon, redstone, diamond or refined obsidian and it becomes an alloy; pipe gases between machines and they become chemistry.
   > How: every machine comes in tiers (basic, advanced, elite, ultimate). In this pack each tier's control circuit needs the matching MI circuit.
   > Tip: this page is a side path. The main-path Mekanism quests are linked on the left; click one to jump there. Reactors, More Machine and Mekanism Extras are on the next page, Power and Beyond.
2. **Configurator**: `mekanism:configurator` *(after: The Mekanism Way)*
   > What: the Configurator sets which side of a Mekanism block takes input and gives output, ejects contents, and rotates blocks.
   > How: iron, an osmium ingot and steel. Sneak + right-click to change its mode; the side colours match the machine's GUI.
   > Tip: most "my machine won't take gas" problems are a side set to the wrong colour.
3. **Energy Tablet**: `mekanism:energy_tablet` *(after: The Mekanism Way, Infused Alloy)*
   > What: a portable FE store. It is also a crafting part in the Robit, the Wind Generator, lasers, Free Runners and the Portable Teleporter.
   > How: gold ingots, redstone and Infused Alloy (check JEI).
   > Tip: make a few at once; you'll keep needing them.
4. **Reinforced Alloy**: 4x `mekanism:alloy_reinforced` *(after: The Mekanism Way, Infused Alloy)*
   > What: the second Mekanism alloy, used in elite circuits, lasers and the Solar Neutron Activator.
   > Chemistry: real alloys work the same way: a few percent of a second element (carbon in steel, chromium in stainless) changes the metal's properties.
   > How: Metallurgic Infuser: Infused Alloy + diamond infusion (from diamonds or diamond dust; check JEI).
5. **Atomic Alloy**: 4x `mekanism:alloy_atomic` *(after: Reinforced Alloy)*
   > What: the top Mekanism alloy, needed for ultimate circuits, teleportation cores and the Robit.
   > How: first infuse obsidian dust with diamond to get refined obsidian dust, then infuse Reinforced Alloy with refined obsidian.
   > Tip: crush obsidian in the Crusher or an MI macerator for obsidian dust.
6. **Refined Obsidian**: `mekanism:osmium_compressor`; 4x `mekanism:ingot_refined_obsidian` *(after: Atomic Alloy)*
   > What: refined obsidian ingots: very hard, blast-proof metal for teleporters, the Robit and endgame tools.
   > How: the Osmium Compressor presses refined obsidian dust with liquid osmium into ingots. It needs an Advanced Control Circuit (MV).
   > Tip: refined glowstone ingots come from the same machine: glowstone dust plus osmium.
7. **Advanced Control Circuit**: 2x `mekanism:advanced_control_circuit` *(after: The Mekanism Way, MV: Aluminum)*
   > What: the circuit for every advanced-tier Mekanism block: factories, cubes, tanks, the Purification Chamber, and in this pack the whole 4x/5x ore line (injection, dissolution, washer, crystallizer).
   > How: an MI electronic circuit above two Infused Alloys and a Basic Control Circuit (check JEI).
   > Tip: the old infuser shortcut for circuits is removed in this pack. Circuits follow MI's voltage tiers.
8. **Elite Control Circuit**: 2x `mekanism:elite_control_circuit` *(after: Advanced Control Circuit, HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > What: the circuit for elite-tier blocks, the Combiner, the Security Desk and the Solar Neutron Activator.
   > How: an MI digital circuit above two Reinforced Alloys and an Advanced Control Circuit (check JEI).
   > Tip: HV comes with polyethylene on the main path. Make a stack of these before upgrading factories.
9. **Ultimate Control Circuit**: 2x `mekanism:ultimate_control_circuit` *(after: Elite Control Circuit, EV: Processing Units)*
   > What: the circuit behind Mekanism's best blocks: the Isotopic Centrifuge, QIO, the Quantum Entangloporter, the Dimensional Stabilizer, the MekaSuit and the Meka-Tool.
   > How: an MI processing unit above two Atomic Alloys and an Elite Control Circuit (check JEI).
   > Tip: this unlocks the rest of the page: ultimate factories, QIO, More Machine's big machines and Mekanism Extras.
10. **Teleportation Core**: 2x `mekanism:teleportation_core` *(after: Refined Obsidian)*
   > What: the part inside teleporters, the Digital Miner, QIO drive arrays and the Quantum Entangloporter.
   > How: Atomic Alloy, gold ingots, a diamond and ender pearls (check JEI).
   > Tip: you'll need at least four of these for this page alone. Automate Atomic Alloy early.
11. **Teleporter**: `mekanism:teleporter`; 9x `mekanism:teleporter_frame` *(after: Teleportation Core)*
   > What: a frame-and-controller portal that links to other teleporters, even across dimensions.
   > How: the controller is a Teleportation Core in steel casings with basic circuits. Frames are refined obsidian around refined glowstone. Build a 3x4 frame with the controller in it (check JEI).
   > Tip: set both ends to the same frequency, and give the sending end plenty of power.
12. **Portable Teleporter**: `mekanism:portable_teleporter` *(after: Teleportation Core)*
   > What: a hand-held teleporter that jumps you to any teleporter frequency you own.
   > How: a Teleportation Core between two Energy Tablets and two basic circuits (check JEI). Charge it first.
   > Tip: the further the jump, the more energy it costs.
13. **Dimensional Stabilizer**: `mekanism:dimensional_stabilizer` *(after: Refined Obsidian, EV: Processing Units)*
   > What: Mekanism's chunk loader. It keeps chunks around it running while you're away, so your factories never pause.
   > How: refined obsidian, Atomic Alloy, Ultimate Control Circuits (EV) and a diamond block (check JEI). Pick the chunks in its GUI.
   > Tip: load only what you need. Every loaded chunk costs server time.
14. **Quantum Entangloporter**: 2x `mekanism:quantum_entangloporter` *(after: Teleportation Core, EV: Processing Units)*
   > What: two Entangloporters on the same frequency act as one block: energy, items, fluids, chemicals and heat go in one and out the other, across any distance or dimension.
   > Chemistry: real quantum entanglement can't carry information or matter faster than light (the no-communication theorem). Mekanism takes a little artistic licence.
   > How: refined obsidian, Atomic Alloy, Ultimate Control Circuits (EV) and a Teleportation Core (check JEI).
   > Tip: a pair is the easiest way to pipe uranium hexafluoride or D-T fuel from a remote plant to your base.
15. **Robit**: `mekanism:robit` *(after: Refined Obsidian)*
   > What: the Robit follows you, picks up items, smelts and crafts. It is also a crafting part for the Digital Miner and several More Machine blocks.
   > How: Atomic Alloy, refined obsidian, steel, an Energy Tablet and a personal chest (check JEI). Place it on a Chargepad to recharge.
   > Tip: rename it with a name tag. It won't mind.
16. **Digital Miner**: `mekanism:digital_miner` *(after: Robit, Teleportation Core)*
   > What: a machine that mines out a large radius below it, taking only the blocks you filter for.
   > How: Atomic Alloy, a Logistical Sorter, a Robit, a Teleportation Core and a steel casing (check JEI). Set filters (tags like c:ores work), radius and height, then start it.
   > Tip: it uses a lot of power. Speed upgrades help, but bring Energy upgrades too. Rich deposits sit at metal-specific depths: set its height range to match.
17. **QIO**: `mekanism:qio_drive_array`; `mekanism:qio_dashboard`; `mekanism:qio_drive_base` *(after: Ultimate Control Circuit)*
   > What: Quantum Item Orchestration: drives in a drive array hold items, and dashboards, importers and exporters reach them wirelessly through a frequency.
   > How: the drive array needs a Teleportation Core and Ultimate Control Circuits (EV); the base drive needs an ultimate circuit too. Give every QIO block the same frequency.
   > Tip: AE2 is the pack's main storage. QIO is a good wireless add-on for a remote outpost.
18. **QIO In and Out**: `mekanism:qio_importer`; `mekanism:qio_exporter`; `mekanism:portable_qio_dashboard` *(after: QIO, Polonium)*
   > What: importers pull items from the inventory they face into QIO; exporters push chosen items out. The Portable Dashboard opens your QIO from anywhere.
   > How: importer and exporter: lead, ender pearls, a Teleportation Core, an ultimate circuit and a (sticky) piston. The portable dashboard wraps a dashboard and a core in seven polonium pellets (check JEI).
   > Tip: an exporter with a filter on a machine's input is a tiny autocrafting line.
19. **Challenge: Denser Drives**: `mekanism:qio_drive_hyper_dense` *(after: QIO In and Out)*
   > What: the Hyper-Dense QIO Drive holds far more than a base drive. Time-Dilating and Supermassive drives go further still.
   > How: each tier wraps the one below with a Teleportation Core and rarer materials (check JEI for each).
   > Tip: drive count matters as much as size: an array holds 12 drives.
20. **Energized Smelter**: `mekanism:energized_smelter` *(after: The Mekanism Way, Mekanism Circuits)*
   > What: Mekanism's electric furnace. It smelts anything a furnace can, takes upgrades, and is the base of the smelting factory.
   > Chemistry: electric heating is Joule heating: current through a resistance makes heat (P = I²R). No fuel, no smoke.
   > How: Basic Alloy, glass, a Basic Control Circuit and a steel casing (check JEI).
21. **Basic Factory**: 1x any of `or(item(mekanism:basic_smelting_factory)item(mekanism:basic_enriching_factory)item(mekanism:basic_crushing_factory)item(mekanism:basic_compressing_factory)item(mekanism:basic_combining_factory)item(mekanism:basic_purifying_factory)item(mekanism:basic_injecting_factory)item(mekanism:basic_infusing_factory)item(mekanism:basic_sawing_factory))` *(after: Energized Smelter)*
   > What: a factory is a machine with several slots that work in parallel. A basic factory runs 3 operations at once.
   > How: craft any single machine (Energized Smelter, Enrichment Chamber, Crusher...) with Basic Control Circuits and Basic Alloy. Any factory type counts.
   > Tip: factories sort their own inputs with auto-sort in the GUI, so one input pipe is enough.
22. **Advanced Factory**: 1x any of `or(item(mekanism:advanced_smelting_factory)item(mekanism:advanced_enriching_factory)item(mekanism:advanced_crushing_factory)item(mekanism:advanced_compressing_factory)item(mekanism:advanced_combining_factory)item(mekanism:advanced_purifying_factory)item(mekanism:advanced_injecting_factory)item(mekanism:advanced_infusing_factory)item(mekanism:advanced_sawing_factory))` *(after: Basic Factory)*
   > What: 5 parallel slots, and faster with upgrades.
   > How: upgrade a basic factory in the crafting grid with Advanced Control Circuits, Infused Alloy and osmium, or use a Tier Installer on a placed one.
   > Tip: upgrading keeps the factory's type, so plan which machines you want at five slots.
23. **Elite Factory**: 1x any of `or(item(mekanism:elite_smelting_factory)item(mekanism:elite_enriching_factory)item(mekanism:elite_crushing_factory)item(mekanism:elite_compressing_factory)item(mekanism:elite_combining_factory)item(mekanism:elite_purifying_factory)item(mekanism:elite_injecting_factory)item(mekanism:elite_infusing_factory)item(mekanism:elite_sawing_factory))` *(after: Advanced Factory)*
   > What: 7 parallel slots. Pair an Elite Purifying or Injecting Factory with your ore line and the bottleneck moves elsewhere.
   > How: upgrade an advanced factory with Elite Control Circuits and Reinforced Alloy (check JEI).
   > Tip: the factory GUI shows each slot's progress; idle slots mean the input line is too slow.
24. **Ultimate Factory**: 1x any of `or(item(mekanism:ultimate_smelting_factory)item(mekanism:ultimate_enriching_factory)item(mekanism:ultimate_crushing_factory)item(mekanism:ultimate_compressing_factory)item(mekanism:ultimate_combining_factory)item(mekanism:ultimate_purifying_factory)item(mekanism:ultimate_injecting_factory)item(mekanism:ultimate_infusing_factory)item(mekanism:ultimate_sawing_factory))` *(after: Elite Factory)*
   > Nine tasks in one box, all at once. You remember doing many things at once without effort.
   > What: 9 parallel slots, the top of base Mekanism. Mekanism Extras goes further (see the bottom band).
   > How: upgrade an elite factory with Ultimate Control Circuits and Atomic Alloy (check JEI).
   > Tip: add Speed and Energy upgrades: speed raises power use, energy upgrades bring it back down.
25. **Tier Installers**: `mekanism:basic_tier_installer`; `mekanism:advanced_tier_installer` *(after: Basic Factory)*
   > What: right-click a placed machine with a Tier Installer to turn it into the next tier, keeping its contents and settings.
   > How: the basic installer needs a Basic Control Circuit; the advanced one needs an Advanced Control Circuit (MV).
   > Tip: a plain machine plus a basic installer becomes a basic factory.
26. **Precision Sawmill**: `mekanism:precision_sawmill` *(after: Energized Smelter)*
   > What: cuts logs into more planks than hand crafting, often with a bonus of sawdust, and breaks wooden items back down.
   > Chemistry: wood is about 40-50% cellulose (chains of glucose), with hemicellulose and lignin gluing the fibres together. Sawdust is the same polymers, finely divided.
   > How: iron, Infused Alloy, a Basic Control Circuit and a steel casing (check JEI).
   > Tip: sawdust feeds wood gasification in the PRC and the Cardboard Box.
27. **Factories for the Ore Line**: 1x any of `or(item(mekanism:basic_purifying_factory)item(mekanism:basic_injecting_factory)item(mekanism:advanced_purifying_factory)item(mekanism:advanced_injecting_factory)item(mekanism:elite_purifying_factory)item(mekanism:elite_injecting_factory)item(mekanism:ultimate_purifying_factory)item(mekanism:ultimate_injecting_factory))` *(after: Advanced Factory, 4x Ore: Hydrogen Chloride)*
   > What: a Purifying (O₂, 3x) or Injecting (HCl, 4x) Factory runs several ores at once. Ore processing is where factories pay off most.
   > Chemistry: the gas is consumed per operation: oxygen oxidises the ore surface into clumps, hydrogen chloride attacks it into shards. More slots means more gas, so size the separator to match.
   > How: build the factory from a Purification Chamber or Chemical Injection Chamber (both MV in this pack). Any tier and either type counts.
   > Tip: feed the gas into the factory's gas side with pressurized tubes, the same as the single machine.
28. **Combiner**: `mekanism:combiner` *(after: Energized Smelter, HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > What: the Combiner presses a main input together with a second block, for example flint + cobblestone into gravel, or 4 obsidian dust + cobbled deepslate back into obsidian.
   > Chemistry: pressing powders into a solid below their melting point is sintering; it's how ceramics and many metal parts are made.
   > How: Reinforced Alloy, Elite Control Circuits (HV) and a steel casing (check JEI). Press U on it in JEI for every recipe.
29. **Speed and Energy Upgrades**: 2x `mekanism:upgrade_speed`; 2x `mekanism:upgrade_energy` *(after: Basic Factory)*
   > What: slot them into any Mekanism machine. Speed upgrades make it work faster; energy upgrades cut its power use and enlarge its buffer.
   > How: Infused Alloy and glass around osmium dust (speed) or gold dust (energy). A machine takes up to 8 of each.
   > Tip: speed upgrades raise power use faster than they raise speed. Balance every speed upgrade with an energy upgrade.
30. **The Other Upgrades**: `mekanism:upgrade_filter`; `mekanism:upgrade_chemical`; `mekanism:upgrade_muffling`; `mekanism:upgrade_anchor`; `mekanism:upgrade_stone_generator` *(after: Speed and Energy Upgrades)*
   > What: the Filter upgrade lets the Electric Pump pick heavy water; Chemical cuts gas use in gas-fed machines; Muffling quiets machines; Anchor keeps a machine's chunk loaded.
   > Chemistry: the Stone Generator upgrade does what a cobble generator does: lava cooled by water solidifies into stone.
   > How: Infused Alloy and glass around tin dust, iron dust or diamond dust; wool for muffling; water and lava buckets for stone (check JEI).
   > Tip: a machine's tooltip lists which upgrades it accepts.
31. **Moving Day**: `mekanism:cardboard_box` *(after: Precision Sawmill)*
   > What: a Cardboard Box made from sawdust. Right-click almost any block (even a full chest or a spawner) to pack it up and carry it.
   > Chemistry: cardboard is pressed cellulose fibre, the same polymer that makes up most of the sawdust.
   > Tip: boxes can't pick up everything; blocks on the mod's blacklist won't pack.
32. **Challenge: Every Stage of Iron**: `mekanism:crystal_iron`; `mekanism:shard_iron`; `mekanism:clump_iron`; `mekanism:dirty_dust_iron` *(after: Factories for the Ore Line, 5x Ore: Dissolution)*
   > What: the full 5x chain, one stage of each: crystal (5x) → shard (4x) → clump (3x) → dirty dust → dust.
   > Chemistry: sulfuric acid dissolves the iron oxide into iron sulfate (Fe₂O₃ + 3H₂SO₄ → Fe₂(SO₄)₃ + 3H₂O). Washing rinses out insoluble rock, and crystallising pulls pure salt back out of solution.
