   > How: dissolve, wash and crystallise, then inject crystals with HCl, purify shards with O₂, crush clumps. Dirty dust goes to the MI Centrifuge for byproducts.
   > Tip: each stage can also be fed raw ore directly, so a half-built line still gives 3x or 4x.
33. **Heating the Plant**: `mekanism:resistive_heater`; `mekanism:fuelwood_heater`; 8x `mekanism:basic_thermodynamic_conductor` *(after: The Mekanism Way, Evaporation Ponds)*
   > What: the Resistive Heater turns FE into heat; the Fuelwood Heater burns furnace fuel. Thermodynamic Conductors carry the heat to where it's needed, such as a Thermal Evaporation Plant.
   > Chemistry: evaporation speeds up with temperature because more water molecules have enough energy to escape the surface. The conductors are copper in steel: copper conducts heat about 8 times better than steel.
   > How: heaters need a steel casing and a circuit or Energy Tablet; conductors are steel and copper (check JEI). Watch the plant's temperature in its GUI.
   > Tip: a hot plant in a desert biome runs much faster than a cold one in the snow.
34. **Salt and Sodium**: 16x `mekanism:salt` *(after: Heating the Plant, Mekanism Gases)*
   > What: brine from the evaporation plant crystallises into salt, and splits into sodium and chlorine in the Electrolytic Separator.
   > Chemistry: real sodium is made by electrolysing molten NaCl (2NaCl → 2Na + Cl₂, the Downs cell). Salt is also a classic HCl source: NaCl + H₂SO₄ → NaHSO₄ + HCl.
   > How: Chemical Crystallizer: 15 mB brine → 1 salt. Electrolytic Separator: brine → sodium + chlorine. Salt also counts as a hydrogen chloride source in an HCl machine's chemical item slot (press U on Salt in JEI).
   > Tip: sodium is the coolant for the best fission setups (see Sodium Coolant on the Power and Beyond page).
35. **Dynamic Tank**: 16x `mekanism:dynamic_tank`; 2x `mekanism:dynamic_valve`; 4x `mekanism:structural_glass` *(after: The Mekanism Way, Mekanism Circuits)*
   > What: a hollow multiblock tank of any size from 3x3x3 up, for huge amounts of a fluid or a chemical.
   > How: dynamic tank blocks (steel and a bucket) for the frame, structural glass for walls, and valves to pipe in and out. The layout is in Just Enough Mekanism Multiblocks in JEI.
   > Tip: one dynamic tank block is also a part in the PRC and the Chemical Oxidizer.
36. **Pressurized Reaction Chamber**: `mekanism:pressurized_reaction_chamber` *(after: Mekanism Gases, Dynamic Tank)*
   > What: the PRC reacts an item, a fluid and a gas together under pressure. It makes substrate, HDPE, plutonium and polonium pellets, and gasifies coal and wood.
   > Chemistry: pressure pushes gas molecules closer together so they collide with the other reactants more often. Le Chatelier: a reaction that shrinks gas volume is favoured by high pressure.
   > How: Basic Control Circuits, Infused Alloy, steel, an Enrichment Chamber, a Dynamic Tank and chemical tanks (check JEI). Press U on it in JEI for every recipe.
   > Tip: it often makes two products at once (an item and a gas). Give each output side its own pipe.
37. **Substrate**: 16x `mekanism:substrate` *(after: Pressurized Reaction Chamber)*
   > What: substrate is Mekanism's polymer seed: a little of it, with ethene and oxygen, becomes HDPE.
   > Chemistry: plant matter can become ethylene: real bio-ethylene is made by dehydrating bioethanol (C₂H₅OH → C₂H₄ + H₂O). Polyethylene is then thousands of C₂H₄ units joined on a catalyst.
   > How: PRC: 2 bio fuel + water + hydrogen → substrate + ethene. Then substrate + water + ethene → 8 substrate (plus a little O₂). Check JEI for amounts.
   > Tip: MI ethylene is tagged as ethene in this pack, so your distillation tower can feed this line too.
38. **HDPE Parts**: 8x `mekanism:hdpe_sheet`; 2x `mekanism:hdpe_rod`; 4x `mekanism:hdpe_stick` *(after: Substrate, HDPE)*
   > What: HDPE pellets shaped into sheets, rods and sticks: parts for the Solar Neutron Activator, module bases, the MekaSuit and the Meka-Tool.
   > Chemistry: high-density polyethylene has straight chains with few branches, so they pack tightly. That makes it stiffer and stronger than the bendy LDPE in plastic bags.
   > How: PRC: substrate + ethene + oxygen → HDPE pellet (or use your MI line from the main path). Then shape pellets in the crafting grid (check JEI).
   > Tip: the MekaSuit alone eats dozens of sheets. Automate the pellets.
39. **Modules**: 4x `mekanism:module_base`; `mekanism:modification_station` *(after: HDPE Parts, Polonium)*
   > What: module bases are the blank every MekaSuit and Meka-Tool module is built on. The Modification Station installs modules into your gear.
   > How: module base: an HDPE sheet in tin ingots and bronze nuggets (makes 2). Station: HDPE sheets, a chest, Ultimate Control Circuits (EV), a steel casing and a polonium pellet (check JEI).
   > Tip: press U on a Module Base in JEI to see every module and what each one needs.
40. **Meka-Tool**: `mekanism:meka_tool` *(after: Modules)*
   > What: the Atomic Disassembler grown up: one FE-powered tool that mines, digs, chops and fights, and takes modules for range, speed, silk touch, veinmining and more.
   > How: an Atomic Disassembler, a Configurator, HDPE sheets, Ultimate Control Circuits, polonium pellets and a Basic Induction Cell (check JEI).
   > Tip: it drinks power fast with big modules. Carry a charged energy cube or wear the MekaSuit.
41. **The Full MekaSuit**: `mekanism:mekasuit_pants`; `mekanism:mekasuit_boots` *(after: Modules, MekaSuit)*
   > Four pieces, one will. You remember standing in fire and feeling only warmth.
   > What: the MekaSuit legs and boots, completing the armour started on the Tools page. Legs take movement and locomotion modules; boots take jump and fall protection.
   > How: netherite leggings / boots in HDPE sheets, Ultimate Control Circuits, polonium pellets and a Basic Induction Cell (check JEI).
   > Tip: the full suit shares one energy pool through its modules. Charge it on a Chargepad or with a charging module.
42. **Pigments**: `mekanism:pigment_extractor`; `mekanism:painting_machine` *(after: Pressurized Reaction Chamber, MV: Aluminum)*
   > What: the Pigment Extractor pulls coloured pigment out of dyes; the Painting Machine applies it to blocks and items.
   > Chemistry: a pigment's colour comes from the light its molecules absorb: indigo absorbs orange-red light, so it looks blue.
   > How: the extractor needs Basic Circuits; the Painting Machine needs an Advanced Control Circuit (MV).
43. **Coal Gasification**: 16x `mekanism:dust_sulfur` *(after: Pressurized Reaction Chamber)*
   > What: the PRC can gasify coal: coal + water + oxygen → hydrogen gas, with the coal's sulfur left behind as sulfur dust.
   > Chemistry: the real water-gas reaction is C + H₂O → CO + H₂ at about 1,000 °C; a little oxygen burns part of the coal to keep it hot. Coal holds 0.5-5% sulfur, which refineries recover as elemental sulfur.
   > How: PRC with any coal or coal dust, water and O₂ (check JEI). Logs and sawdust gasify the same way into charcoal dust.
   > Tip: a handy extra sulfur source for the contact process.
44. **Challenge: The Full Chemical Plant**: `mekanism:chemical_infuser`; `mekanism:chemical_oxidizer`; `mekanism:electrolytic_separator`; `mekanism:pressurized_reaction_chamber`; `mekanism:chemical_washer`; `mekanism:chemical_crystallizer`; `mekanism:chemical_dissolution_chamber`; `mekanism:isotopic_centrifuge`; `mekanism:solar_neutron_activator`; `mekanism:sps_port` *(after: Pressurized Reaction Chamber, Supercritical Phase Shifter)*
   > What: one of each of Mekanism's ten chemical machines, from the Chemical Infuser to an SPS port.
   > Chemistry: together they cover the unit operations of a real chemical plant: reaction, oxidation, electrolysis, washing, crystallisation, dissolution and isotope separation.
   > How: most are on the main path (see the links on the left). The washer, crystallizer and dissolution chamber are MV in this pack; the centrifuge needs Ultimate Control Circuits (EV).
   > Tip: an optional collection. Keep spares in a chest as you build each one.
45. **Cables and Pipes**: 8x `mekanism:basic_universal_cable`; 8x `mekanism:basic_mechanical_pipe` *(after: The Mekanism Way, Mekanism Circuits)*
   > What: Universal Cable carries FE, Mechanical Pipe carries fluids. With pressurized tubes (gases) and conductors (heat) they make Mekanism's four transmitter types.
   > How: steel with redstone (cable) or a bucket (pipe), 8 per craft. Higher tiers wrap 8 of the lower tier around an alloy.
   > Tip: transmitters of the same type join into one network. Colour them with a Configurator or paint to keep two networks apart.
46. **Logistical Transporters**: 16x `mekanism:basic_logistical_transporter` *(after: Cables and Pipes)*
   > What: item pipes that carry stacks to the nearest inventory that will take them, and show the items moving.
   > How: steel around a Basic Control Circuit, 8 per craft.
   > Tip: a transporter's colour (set with the Configurator) only delivers into sides of the same colour.
47. **Logistical Sorter**: `mekanism:logistical_sorter` *(after: Logistical Transporters)*
   > What: pulls items out of the inventory behind it and sends them down transporters by filter: item, tag, mod or material.
   > How: iron, a piston and a Basic Control Circuit. It is also a part of the Digital Miner.
   > Tip: give each filter a colour, and the items arrive only at inventories with that colour.
48. **Diversion and Restriction**: 2x `mekanism:diversion_transporter`; 2x `mekanism:restrictive_transporter` *(after: Logistical Transporters)*
   > What: a Diversion Transporter opens or closes with redstone; a Restrictive Transporter is only used when no other path works.
   > How: steel and iron bars, plus redstone for the diversion type (check JEI).
   > Tip: a restrictive segment in front of an overflow chest makes it fill last.
49. **Faster Transporters**: 8x `mekanism:elite_logistical_transporter`; 8x `mekanism:ultimate_logistical_transporter` *(after: Logistical Transporters)*
   > What: higher tiers move bigger stacks, faster.
   > How: 8 transporters of the tier below around Reinforced Alloy (elite) or Atomic Alloy (ultimate).
   > Tip: the line only needs to be as fast as its slowest machine. Upgrade the trunk, not every branch.
50. **Seismic Survey**: `mekanism:seismic_vibrator`; `mekanism:seismic_reader` *(after: Cables and Pipes)*
   > What: the Seismic Vibrator shakes the ground beneath it; the Seismic Reader then shows every block straight down to bedrock.
   > Chemistry: real prospectors use reflection seismology: sound waves bounce off layers of different density, and the echo times map oil and ore bodies.
   > How: vibrator: tin, lapis, Basic Control Circuits and a steel casing; reader: steel, lapis and an Energy Tablet (check JEI).
   > Tip: rich ore deposits sit at metal-specific depths. Survey before you dig.
51. **Formulaic Assemblicator**: `mekanism:formulaic_assemblicator` *(after: Logistical Transporters)*
   > What: saves a crafting recipe on a Crafting Formula and crafts it whenever ingredients arrive.
   > How: steel, a crafter, a chest, Basic Control Circuits and a steel casing (check JEI). Encode the recipe on a formula in its GUI.
   > Tip: handy for alloy blocks or circuits until your AE2 autocrafting is up.
52. **Nutritional Paste**: `mekanism:nutritional_liquifier`; `mekanism:canteen` *(after: Cables and Pipes)*
   > What: the Nutritional Liquifier turns food into nutritional paste; a Canteen carries it and feeds you when you drink.
   > Chemistry: food energy is chemical energy in carbohydrates, fats and proteins. Mashing food changes its form, not its calories.
   > How: liquifier: redstone, bowls, Basic Control Circuits and a steel casing. Canteen: tin and a bowl (check JEI). The MekaSuit has a module that drinks paste for you.
53. **Mine, Not Yours**: `mekanism:personal_chest`; `mekanism:security_desk` *(after: Logistical Transporters)*
   > What: a Personal Chest only opens for its owner. The Security Desk sets who may use your Mekanism blocks: you, a trusted list, or everyone.
   > How: personal chest: steel, glass, chests and a Basic Control Circuit. Security desk: steel, glass, a Network Reader and Elite Control Circuits (HV) (check JEI).
   > Tip: on a shared server, lock your reactor controls.
54. **Enriched Infusion**: 8x `mekanism:enriched_carbon`; 8x `mekanism:enriched_redstone`; 8x `mekanism:dust_charcoal` *(after: The Mekanism Way, Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser)*
   > What: the Enrichment Chamber turns coal, charcoal and redstone into enriched forms. One enriched item gives the Metallurgic Infuser far more infuse than the raw material.
   > Chemistry: charcoal is nearly pure carbon left after heating wood without air (pyrolysis). Enriching it is like refining coal into coke: less ash, more carbon per gram.
   > How: crush charcoal into Charcoal Dust in the Crusher, then put coal, charcoal or redstone through the Enrichment Chamber (check JEI).
   > Tip: feed enriched items into the infuser's left slot: one stack lasts a long time.
55. **Obsidian Dusts**: 8x `mekanism:dust_obsidian`; 4x `mekanism:dust_refined_obsidian` *(after: Reinforced Alloy)*
   > What: obsidian dust, and refined obsidian dust made by infusing it with diamond. Refined obsidian dust becomes Atomic Alloy and refined obsidian ingots.
   > Chemistry: obsidian is volcanic glass, mostly SiO₂ (about 70%) with aluminium, iron and alkali oxides, frozen before it could crystallise.
   > How: crush obsidian in the Crusher, then Metallurgic Infuser: obsidian dust + diamond infusion → refined obsidian dust (check JEI).
   > Tip: a Combiner can turn spare obsidian dust back into obsidian later.
56. **Bio Fuel**: 32x `mekanism:bio_fuel` *(after: The Mekanism Way, Mekanism Circuits)*
   > What: bio fuel is crushed plant matter. It burns in the Bio-Generator and is the start of the substrate line in the PRC.
   > Chemistry: plants store sunlight as sugars and cellulose: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂. Burning or digesting them gives that energy back.
   > How: put seeds, saplings, crops or other plant items into the Crusher (press U on Bio Fuel in JEI to see what counts).
   > Tip: a Mystical Agriculture or Farmer's Delight farm feeding a Crusher makes it renewable.
57. **Dictionary and Gauge Dropper**: `mekanism:dictionary`; `mekanism:gauge_dropper` *(after: The Mekanism Way, Mekanism Circuits)*
   > What: the Dictionary shows the tags of any item or block you click. The Gauge Dropper sucks a little fluid or gas out of a tank, or dumps a tank you don't want.
   > How: Dictionary: a book under a Basic Control Circuit. Gauge Dropper: osmium over glass panes (check JEI).
   > Tip: the Dictionary is the fastest way to find out which tag a filter needs (c:dusts/iron, c:ores and so on).
58. **Chargepad**: `mekanism:chargepad` *(after: Energy Tablet)*
   > What: the Chargepad charges the FE items in your inventory (and a Robit) while you stand on it.
   > How: polished blackstone pressure plates over steel and an Energy Tablet (check JEI). Feed it power from below.
   > Tip: put one in front of your storage. Every visit tops up your tools.
59. **Portable Fluid Tanks**: `mekanism:basic_fluid_tank`; `mekanism:advanced_fluid_tank` *(after: The Mekanism Way, Infused Alloy)*
   > What: Mekanism fluid tanks keep their fluid when broken, so you can carry a tank of acid to another machine. Each tier holds more and moves it faster.
   > How: basic: iron and Basic Alloy. Advanced: a basic tank ringed with iron and Infused Alloy (check JEI). They stack on top of each other and pass fluid down.
   > Tip: right-click a tank with a bucket to fill or empty it; tanks also fill buckets placed in their GUI.
60. **Elite Tanks**: `mekanism:elite_fluid_tank`; `mekanism:elite_chemical_tank` *(after: Portable Fluid Tanks)*
   > What: elite tanks hold far more than basic ones. The chemical tank is the gas version, for H₂, O₂, Cl₂ or SO₂.
   > How: the advanced tank ringed with Reinforced Alloy and iron (fluid) or osmium (chemical). Check JEI.
   > Tip: a chemical tank under an Electrolytic Separator smooths out its output while the rest of the line catches up.
61. **Liquefied Gases**: `mekanism:hydrogen_bucket`; `mekanism:oxygen_bucket` *(after: Water Vapor, Portable Fluid Tanks)*
   > What: the Rotary Condensentrator turns gases into liquids and back. Liquid hydrogen and oxygen fit in buckets and ordinary fluid tanks.
   > Chemistry: hydrogen boils at -253 °C and oxygen at -183 °C. Liquid oxygen is pale blue and is attracted to a magnet, because O₂ has two unpaired electrons.
   > How: set the condensentrator to condensing, feed it H₂ or O₂ from a separator, and pipe the liquid into a fluid tank. Fill buckets from the tank.
   > Tip: rockets in this pack burn fuel and oxygen; liquids are how big amounts travel.
62. **Acids by the Bucket**: `mekanism:hydrogen_chloride_bucket`; `mekanism:sulfuric_acid_bucket` *(after: Liquefied Gases, Contact Process 3: H₂SO₄, Hydrogen Chloride)*
   > What: the same machine liquefies hydrogen chloride and sulfuric acid, so other mods' machines (and the Undergarden catalyst) can use Mekanism's acids.
   > Chemistry: hydrogen chloride dissolved in water is hydrochloric acid; sulfuric acid is already a liquid at room temperature and boils at 337 °C.
   > How: Rotary Condensentrator on condensing mode, fed from your contact process or HCl line (check JEI).
   > Tip: one bucket is 1,000 mB, the same as 1,000 mB of the gas form.
63. **Advanced Transmitters**: 8x `mekanism:advanced_universal_cable`; 8x `mekanism:advanced_mechanical_pipe`; 8x `mekanism:advanced_pressurized_tube`; 8x `mekanism:advanced_logistical_transporter`; 8x `mekanism:advanced_thermodynamic_conductor` *(after: Logistical Transporters, Infused Alloy)*
   > What: every Mekanism transmitter has four tiers. Advanced ones carry several times more energy, fluid, gas, items or heat than basic.
   > How: eight basic transmitters around Infused Alloy make eight advanced ones (check JEI).
   > Chemistry: gas flow through a pipe rises with its cross-section and the pressure difference; Mekanism just lets you buy the bigger pipe.
   > Tip: upgrade the trunk line from the separator first; the branches can stay basic.
64. **Ultimate Universal Cable**: 8x `mekanism:ultimate_universal_cable` *(after: Advanced Transmitters)*
   > What: the top tier of power cable: tens of thousands of times what a basic cable carries.
   > How: elite cables around Atomic Alloy (elite cables use Reinforced Alloy). Check JEI.
   > Chemistry: real cables lose power as heat (P = I²R); fusion plants send power at high voltage so the current, and the loss, stays low.
65. **Electric Bow**: `mekanism:electric_bow` *(after: Energy Tablet)*
   > What: an FE-powered bow. Its fire mode sets arrows alight.
   > How: string, Infused Alloy and an Energy Tablet (check JEI). Charge it on a Chargepad.
   > Tip: it has no durability, only charge.
66. **Flamethrower**: `mekanism:flamethrower` *(after: Advanced Control Circuit, Mekanism Gases)*
   > What: a hand-held flamethrower that burns hydrogen gas. One mode smelts the blocks it hits.
   > Chemistry: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, about 286 kJ per mole of hydrogen. The flame is nearly invisible in daylight and leaves only water vapour.
   > How: tin, bronze, a basic chemical tank, flint and steel and an Advanced Control Circuit (MV). Fill it with H₂ from the separator's output or a chemical tank.
   > Tip: never point it at your storage.
67. **Pigment Mixer**: `mekanism:pigment_mixer` *(after: Pigments)*
   > What: mixes two pigments into a new one, for colours no single dye gives.
   > Chemistry: pigments mix subtractively: each absorbs part of the spectrum, so yellow + cyan leaves only green to reflect.
   > How: Reinforced Alloy, HDPE rods, a steel casing and Elite Control Circuits (HV). Check JEI.
68. **Osmium Armour**: `mekanismtools:osmium_helmet`; `mekanismtools:osmium_chestplate`; `mekanismtools:osmium_leggings`; `mekanismtools:osmium_boots` *(after: The Mekanism Way)*
   > What: Mekanism Tools adds a full armour set for each of its metals. Osmium is the first, and tougher than iron.
   > Chemistry: osmium is the densest natural element (22.6 g/cm³). Real osmium is brittle and its oxide, OsO₄, is volatile and very toxic, so nobody actually wears it.
   > How: osmium ingots in the usual armour shapes (check JEI).
   > Tip: bronze, steel and lapis sets exist too; see JEI for their stats.
69. **Refined Obsidian Armour**: `mekanismtools:refined_obsidian_helmet`; `mekanismtools:refined_obsidian_chestplate`; `mekanismtools:refined_obsidian_leggings`; `mekanismtools:refined_obsidian_boots` *(after: Osmium Armour, The Ultimate Paxel)*
   > What: the strongest Mekanism Tools armour: high protection and toughness, good until the MekaSuit.
   > Chemistry: obsidian is volcanic glass: lava cooled too fast for crystals to form. Infusing it with diamond and pressing it with osmium makes Mekanism's refined form.
   > How: refined obsidian ingots from the Osmium Compressor, in armour shapes (check JEI).
70. **Refined Glowstone Armour**: `mekanismtools:refined_glowstone_helmet`; `mekanismtools:refined_glowstone_chestplate`; `mekanismtools:refined_glowstone_leggings`; `mekanismtools:refined_glowstone_boots` *(after: Refined Obsidian Armour)*
   > What: the other Osmium Compressor metal as an armour set. Check JEI for how it compares with refined obsidian.
   > Chemistry: real glow-in-the-dark materials store energy in their crystal and release it as light (phosphorescence); glowstone is Minecraft's version.
   > How: Osmium Compressor: glowstone dust + osmium → refined glowstone ingots, then armour shapes.

### Mekanism: Power and Beyond

*Boilers, turbines and fusion; Mekanism: More Machine; and Mekanism Extras' four tiers beyond ultimate.*

1. **Power and Beyond**: checkmark *(after: The Mekanism Way)*
   > The machines obey you now. You remember wanting more: more heat, more power, more than the last tier allowed.
   > What: the second Mekanism page. It covers the big power multiblocks (boiler, turbine, fusion), Mekanism: More Machine and Mekanism Extras.
   > How: each row opens when its main-path quest is done: fission for the boiler, the turbine casing, D-T fuel for fusion, yellowcake for Extras. Those quests are linked on the left.
   > Tip: the machines, factories, circuits and logistics are on the first Mekanism page.
2. **Thermoelectric Boiler**: 16x `mekanism:boiler_casing`; 2x `mekanism:boiler_valve`; 4x `mekanism:superheating_element`; `mekanism:pressure_disperser` *(after: Power and Beyond, Fission)*
   > What: a multiblock boiler that turns water into steam, heated by Superheating Elements (power) or by hot coolant from a fission reactor.
   > Chemistry: boiling water takes 2,260 J per gram, far more than heating it. That latent heat is what the turbine later turns back into work.
   > How: the layout is in Just Enough Mekanism Multiblocks in JEI: casing walls, valves, a layer of pressure dispersers, and elements on the bottom.
   > Tip: a sodium-cooled fission reactor sends heated sodium here instead of boiling water itself.
3. **Sodium Coolant**: checkmark *(after: Thermoelectric Boiler, Salt and Sodium)*
   > What: cool your fission reactor with sodium instead of water. It returns as superheated sodium, which the Thermoelectric Boiler uses to make steam before sending the sodium back.
   > Chemistry: sodium melts at 98 °C and boils at 883 °C, so it stays liquid at reactor temperatures without high pressure. Real fast reactors use it, and keep it away from water, which it reacts with violently.
   > How: sodium comes from brine in the Electrolytic Separator (see Salt and Sodium). Pipe it into the reactor, superheated sodium out to a boiler valve, and the cooled sodium back. Click to confirm once it runs.
   > Tip: one sodium loop feeds a much bigger boiler and turbine than water cooling does.
4. **Turbine Valves and Vents**: 2x `mekanismgenerators:turbine_valve`; 8x `mekanismgenerators:turbine_vent` *(after: Power and Beyond, Industrial Turbine)*
   > What: valves feed steam in and take power out; vents let the spent steam leave through the walls above the rotor.
   > Chemistry: a turbine extracts work as steam expands and cools. The more vent area, the more steam can pass per tick.
   > How: valve: turbine casings around an Advanced Control Circuit (MV). Vent: casings around iron bars (check JEI).
   > Tip: the turbine GUI shows whether vent flow or blade count is your limit.
5. **Turbine Internals**: 4x `mekanismgenerators:turbine_rotor`; 8x `mekanismgenerators:turbine_blade`; `mekanismgenerators:rotational_complex`; 2x `mekanismgenerators:electromagnetic_coil`; 4x `mekanismgenerators:saturating_condenser` *(after: Turbine Valves and Vents)*
   > What: the moving parts inside an Industrial Turbine. More blades and coils mean more power from the same steam.
   > Chemistry: condensers turn spent steam back into water, so the loop reuses the same water over and over.
   > How: stack rotors with two blades each on the centre column, a Rotational Complex on top, then coils and condensers above. See Just Enough Mekanism Multiblocks.
   > Tip: the turbine's GUI shows whether steam flow or blade count is the limit.
6. **Building the Fusion Reactor**: 16x `mekanismgenerators:fusion_reactor_frame`; 4x `mekanismgenerators:reactor_glass`; 2x `mekanismgenerators:fusion_reactor_port`; `mekanismgenerators:laser_focus_matrix` *(after: Turbine Internals, D-T Fuel)*
   > What: the shell of the Fusion Reactor: frames, reactor glass, ports for fuel and output, and a Laser Focus Matrix to let the ignition laser in.
   > How: the 3D layout is in Just Enough Mekanism Multiblocks in JEI. The controller sits on top in the middle.
   > Tip: ports switch between input and output with a Configurator.
7. **Ignition**: 3x `mekanism:laser`; `mekanism:laser_amplifier` *(after: Building the Fusion Reactor)*
   > What: lasers charge a Laser Amplifier, which fires a single huge pulse into the reactor to ignite it.
   > Chemistry: deuterium and tritium only fuse above about 100 million °C, when the nuclei move fast enough to beat their electric repulsion.
   > How: put a filled Hohlraum in the controller, aim the amplifier at the Laser Focus Matrix and fire it with a redstone signal. Then go to the Fusion quest.
   > Tip: once lit, the reactor sustains itself as long as fuel keeps coming.
8. **Challenge: Every Generator**: `mekanismgenerators:heat_generator`; `mekanismgenerators:solar_generator`; `mekanismgenerators:advanced_solar_generator`; `mekanismgenerators:wind_generator`; `mekanismgenerators:gas_burning_generator`; `mekanismgenerators:bio_generator` *(after: Power and Beyond)*
   > What: one of each Mekanism generator: heat, solar, advanced solar, wind, gas-burning and bio.
   > Chemistry: between them: combustion, the photovoltaic effect, kinetic energy of air, and the energy stored in plant sugars by photosynthesis.
   > How: each one has its own quest on the Power page. The wind generator needs an Energy Tablet; the advanced solar is built from four basic solar generators.
   > Tip: none of these beats fission or fusion, but they never need fuel deliveries.
9. **Radioactive Waste Barrel**: 2x `mekanism:radioactive_waste_barrel` *(after: Power and Beyond, Fission)*
   > What: a barrel that stores spent nuclear waste and other radioactive chemicals, and lets them slowly decay.
   > Chemistry: radioactive decay can't be sped up by chemistry; you can only wait out the half-life. Real spent fuel spends years in cooling ponds, then decades in dry casks.
   > How: check JEI for the recipe. Pipe waste into it with pressurized tubes; never vent it or break a full tube.
   > Tip: reprocessing waste into plutonium and polonium (the T6 page) is better than storing it.
10. **Fusion Logic Adapter**: `mekanismgenerators:fusion_reactor_logic_adapter` *(after: Ignition)*
   > What: a reactor block that outputs redstone for things like ignition state, plasma temperature or low fuel.
   > How: a fusion reactor frame surrounded by redstone; swap one frame of the shell for it and pick the mode in its GUI.
   > Tip: wire "ready for ignition" to your laser amplifier to relight the reactor automatically.
11. **Advanced Induction**: `mekanism:advanced_induction_cell`; `mekanism:advanced_induction_provider` *(after: Power and Beyond, Induction Matrix, Advanced Control Circuit)*
   > What: cells set how much an Induction Matrix stores; providers set how fast power goes in and out. Swap basic ones for advanced and the same shell does far more.
   > Chemistry: the basic cells are lithium: Li has the lowest density of any metal and gives up its electron easily, which is why real batteries use it.
   > How: cell: four basic cells around an Advanced Energy Cube, with Energy Tablets in the corners. Provider: four basic providers around an Advanced Energy Cube, with Advanced Control Circuits (MV). Check JEI.
   > Tip: cells and providers go inside the matrix, not in its walls.
12. **Elite Induction**: `mekanism:elite_induction_cell`; `mekanism:elite_induction_provider` *(after: Advanced Induction, Elite Control Circuit)*
   > What: elite cells and providers, each again several times bigger than the advanced ones.
   > How: the same pattern one tier up: advanced cells around an Elite Energy Cube; advanced providers with Elite Control Circuits (HV). Check JEI.
   > Tip: a fission or fusion plant needs a big buffer for when the turbine spins down. Size the providers to your turbine's output.
13. **Ultimate Energy Cube**: `mekanism:ultimate_energy_cube` *(after: Power and Beyond, Atomic Alloy)*
   > What: the top Energy Cube: a lot of storage in one block you can pick up and carry, contents and all.
   > How: an Elite Energy Cube (Reinforced Alloy, gold) upgraded again with Atomic Alloy, Energy Tablets and diamonds (check JEI).
   > Tip: it's also the core of the ultimate induction cell and provider.
14. **Challenge: Ultimate Induction**: `mekanism:ultimate_induction_cell`; `mekanism:ultimate_induction_provider` *(after: Elite Induction, Ultimate Energy Cube, Ultimate Control Circuit)*
   > You remember holding the energy of a sun and not noticing the weight. This is close.
   > What: the top Induction Matrix parts. A matrix full of these stores more than any other block in base Mekanism.
   > How: elite cells or providers around an Ultimate Energy Cube, with Ultimate Control Circuits for the provider (check JEI).
   > Tip: a full matrix lets a fusion reactor keep your base running while you refuel or rebuild it.
15. **CNC Machines**: 1x any of `or(item(mekmm:cnc_stamper)item(mekmm:cnc_lathe)item(mekmm:cnc_rolling_mill))` *(after: Power and Beyond, Mekanism Circuits)*
   > What: Mekanism: More Machine adds CNC machines: the Stamper presses plates, the Lathe turns rods, the Rolling Mill rolls wire.
   > How: the CNC Stamper needs Basic Control Circuits, Basic Alloy, pistons and a steel casing. The Lathe also needs a Robit (check JEI). Any one counts.
   > Tip: MI's machines make most plates already. Use CNC machines for the mod recipes that list them in JEI (the stamper also prints AE2 processors).
16. **Recycler**: `mekmm:recycler`; 8x `mekmm:scrap` *(after: CNC Machines, MV: Aluminum)*
   > What: the Recycler grinds cheap blocks (stone, dirt, substrate) and sometimes leaves Scrap.
   > How: a Crusher, Advanced Control Circuits (MV), Infused Alloy and osmium (check JEI). About 1 stone in 6 gives a scrap.
   > Tip: 64 scrap compress into a Scrap Box, the first step towards UU-Matter. Start stockpiling early.
17. **Large Machines**: 1x any of `or(item(mekmm:large_heat_generator)item(mekmm:large_gas_burning_generator)item(mekmm:large_wind_generator)item(mekmm:large_chemical_infuser)item(mekmm:large_electrolytic_separator)item(mekmm:large_rotary_condensentrator)item(mekmm:large_solar_neutron_activator)item(mekmm:large_pigment_mixer))` *(after: CNC Machines, EV: Processing Units)*
   > What: More Machine's large machines do the work of many normal ones, such as the Large Electrolytic Separator or Large Chemical Infuser.
   > How: most need a Robit, steel blocks and ultimate-tier tanks or circuits (EV). Any one counts; check JEI for each.
   > Tip: the Large Solar Neutron Activator is a big help for polonium and tritium.
18. **UU-Matter**: `mekmm:replicator`; `mekmm:uu_matter` *(after: Recycler, Antimatter)*
   > Scrap, crystal, antimatter, and then anything. You remember when making matter was just a thought.
   > What: UU-Matter is More Machine's universal matter. The Replicator turns it back into items.
   > How: scrap boxes become Empty Crystals in the PRC (with fusion fuel and a special gas, check JEI). 64 crystals + antimatter in the Antiprotonic Nucleosynthesizer (an optional t7 quest) make one UU-Matter.
   > Tip: the Replicator needs Ultimate Control Circuits and Atomic Alloy. Check JEI for what it can copy.
19. **Presser**: `mekmm:presser` *(after: CNC Machines, HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > What: the Presser builds on the CNC Stamper and makes processors and other pressed parts (check JEI for its recipes).
   > How: a CNC Stamper with Elite Control Circuits (HV), Reinforced Alloy and pistons.
   > Tip: press U on the Presser in JEI to see what it makes.
20. **Planting Station**: `mekmm:planting_station` *(after: Recycler, HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > What: a machine that grows seeds and saplings indoors and outputs the harvest.
   > Chemistry: photosynthesis: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂, here powered by electricity instead of sunlight.
   > How: Elite Control Circuits (HV), Reinforced Alloy, bio fuel and a steel casing (check JEI).
21. **A Small Tribute**: `mekmm:author_doll` *(after: UU-Matter)*
   > What: a decorative doll of More Machine's author, compressed out of 64 UU-Matter and a breath of antimatter in the Osmium Compressor.
   > Tip: the mod's modeller has a doll too, made from UU-Matter gas instead. Thank you, modders.
22. **Ambient Gas Collector**: `mekmm:ambient_gas_collector` *(after: Recycler, EV: Processing Units)*
   > What: a machine that collects gas from its surroundings (check JEI and its GUI for what it gathers).
   > Chemistry: real air is 78% N₂, 21% O₂ and 1% argon; industry separates it by cooling it into a liquid and distilling it.
   > How: Atomic Alloy, an osmium block, an ultimate chemical tank and ultimate tubes (EV).
23. **Radiance**: 4x `mekanism_extras:dust_radiance`; 2x `mekanism_extras:alloy_radiance` *(after: Power and Beyond, Yellowcake)*
   > What: Mekanism Extras adds four tiers beyond ultimate: absolute, supreme, cosmic and infinite. Each needs a new alloy, starting with Radiance.
   > How: Osmium Compressor: glowstone dust + uranium oxide gas → Radiance Dust. Enrich it, then infuse Atomic Alloy with radiance (check JEI).
   > Tip: uranium oxide comes from oxidising yellowcake in the Chemical Oxidizer.
24. **Absolute Control Circuit**: 2x `mekanism_extras:absolute_control_circuit` *(after: Radiance)*
   > What: the first Extras circuit: an Ultimate Control Circuit between two Radiance Alloys.
   > How: craft it, or infuse an ultimate circuit with radiance in the Metallurgic Infuser.
   > Tip: absolute factories, cubes and tanks all start here.
25. **Supreme Control Circuit**: 2x `mekanism_extras:alloy_thermonuclear`; `mekanism_extras:supreme_control_circuit` *(after: Absolute Control Circuit)*
   > What: tier six. Its alloy is Thermonuclear: Radiance Alloy infused with thermonuclear material.
   > How: enriched radiance reacts with lava and molten thermonuclear in the PRC (check JEI for the full chain).
   > Tip: the circuit is an Absolute Control Circuit between two Thermonuclear Alloys.
26. **Cosmic Control Circuit**: 2x `mekanism_extras:alloy_shining`; `mekanism_extras:cosmic_control_circuit` *(after: Supreme Control Circuit, Antimatter)*
   > What: tier seven. Its alloy, Shining, needs enriched thermonuclear transmuted with antimatter.
   > How: Antiprotonic Nucleosynthesizer: enriched thermonuclear + antimatter → enriched shining. Then infuse Thermonuclear Alloy with it (check JEI).
   > Tip: the Nucleosynthesizer is slow; run it on fusion power.
27. **Infinite Control Circuit**: 2x `mekanism_extras:alloy_spectrum`; `mekanism_extras:infinite_control_circuit` *(after: Cosmic Control Circuit)*
   > Infinite, the circuit says. You remember when that word described you.
   > What: tier eight, the top of Mekanism Extras. Its alloy is Spectrum.
   > How: Osmium Compressor: enriched shining + antimatter → enriched spectrum; infuse Shining Alloy with it, then craft the circuit (check JEI).
28. **Absolute Factory**: 1x any of `or(item(mekanism_extras:absolute_smelting_factory)item(mekanism_extras:absolute_enriching_factory)item(mekanism_extras:absolute_crushing_factory)item(mekanism_extras:absolute_compressing_factory)item(mekanism_extras:absolute_combining_factory)item(mekanism_extras:absolute_purifying_factory)item(mekanism_extras:absolute_injecting_factory)item(mekanism_extras:absolute_infusing_factory)item(mekanism_extras:absolute_sawing_factory)item(mekanism_extras:absolute_oxidizing_factory)item(mekanism_extras:absolute_dissolving_factory)item(mekanism_extras:absolute_washing_factory)item(mekanism_extras:absolute_crystallizing_factory)item(mekanism_extras:absolute_centrifuging_factory))` *(after: Absolute Control Circuit)*
   > What: Extras factories have more slots than ultimate ones, and Extras adds factory types base Mekanism lacks (oxidizing, washing, crystallizing, centrifuging...).
   > How: upgrade an ultimate factory with Absolute Control Circuits and Radiance Alloy, or use an Absolute Tier Installer. Any absolute factory counts.
   > Tip: the extra factory types are the big win: a washing or crystallizing factory speeds up the whole 5x line.
29. **Naquadah**: 8x `mekanism_extras:raw_naquadah` *(after: Supreme Control Circuit)*
   > What: Naquadah ore, added by Mekanism Extras. It is the fuel for the Naquadah Reactor.
   > Chemistry: naquadah is not real; it comes from the Stargate films. Every other material on this page is real chemistry.
   > How: Naquadah ore generates underground and in the End. Jade shows the block name when you look at it.
   > Tip: it processes like other Mekanism ores: dissolve, wash and crystallise for the best yield.
30. **Naquadah Reactor**: `mekanism_extras:naquadah_reactor_controller`; 16x `mekanism_extras:naquadah_reactor_casing` *(after: Cosmic Control Circuit, Naquadah)*
   > What: a fusion-style power multiblock from Mekanism Extras that runs on naquadah-based fuel.
   > How: casings are lead blocks transmuted with antimatter in the Nucleosynthesizer; the controller needs Cosmic Control Circuits. Layout: Just Enough Mekanism Multiblocks.
   > Tip: the fuel chain starts with fluorinated naquadah-uranium fuel. Check JEI for each step.

## Industry and Automation

### Mob Data and Big Crafting

*Monifactory-inspired machinery: simulate mobs, craft on giant tables, and fold whole factories into a block.*

1. **Deep Learning**: `hostilenetworks:deep_learner`; `hostilenetworks:blank_data_model` *(after: Iron)*
   > You remember knowing every creature by name. You can learn them again, one fight at a time.
   > What: Hostile Neural Networks records mobs into data models. Trained models later make mob drops without the mob.
   > How: craft the Deep Learner and a Blank Data Model (check JEI). Put models in the Deep Learner and keep it in your inventory while you fight.
   > Tip: start with a mob whose drops you'll need in bulk, like blazes, slimes or endermen.
2. **Your First Model**: `hostilenetworks:data_model` *(after: Deep Learning)*
   > What: a data model attuned to one mob type. It starts at Faulty and levels up as you kill that mob.
   > How: right-click a mob with a Blank Data Model, or craft a specific model (check JEI). Then hunt with the Deep Learner.
   > Tip: tiers go Faulty, Basic, Advanced, Superior, Self Aware. Higher tiers are more accurate, so fewer simulations fail.
3. **Simulation**: `hostilenetworks:sim_chamber`; 4x `hostilenetworks:prediction_matrix` *(after: Your First Model, MV: Aluminum)*
   > What: the Simulation Chamber runs a trained model on FE and prediction matrices to make predictions and mob drops.
   > How: it needs an MV electronic circuit (aluminum chemistry). Insert a model of Basic tier or better, matrices and power.
   > Tip: pipe matrices in and drops out; one chamber per model keeps things simple.
4. **Loot Fabricator**: `hostilenetworks:loot_fabricator` *(after: Simulation)*
   > You remember making things appear from nothing. This is the mortal version: data, power and patience.
   > What: turns predictions into the specific drop you pick (blaze rods, ender pearls, slime balls and more).
   > How: also needs an MV electronic circuit. Feed it predictions from the chamber and select the output in its GUI.
   > Tip: simulated blazes are a cheap blaze-rod source for Silent Gear alloys and brewing.
5. **Self Aware**: checkmark *(after: Simulation)*
   > What: train one data model all the way to Self Aware, the top tier.
   > How: keep killing that mob with the model in your Deep Learner, or let the Simulation Chamber train it. Click the checkmark when you've done it.
   > Tip: a Self Aware model almost never fails a simulation.
6. **Twilight Predictions**: 4x `hostilenetworks:twilight_prediction` *(after: Simulation, The Twilight Forest)*
   > What: Twilight Forest mobs give their own prediction type.
   > How: train a model on a Twilight mob and run it in the Simulation Chamber.
   > Tip: the Loot Fabricator shows which drops each prediction can become.
7. **Black Iron Parts**: `extendedcrafting:black_iron_slate`; `extendedcrafting:basic_component`; `extendedcrafting:basic_catalyst` *(after: Steel)*
   > What: Extended Crafting tables are built from black iron slates plus a component and a catalyst of matching tier.
   > How: black iron ingot = iron ingot + black dye (shapeless). Two ingots make a slate. A component takes a slate, luminessence (glowstone, redstone, gunpowder) and iron; four components ring a black iron ingot for the catalyst.
   > Tip: make extra black iron; every table tier and the Crafting Core need more.
8. **Extended Crafting**: 8x `extendedcrafting:black_iron_ingot`; `extendedcrafting:basic_table` *(after: Black Iron Parts)*
   > What: the Basic Table is a 3x3 table for Extended Crafting recipes, and the base of every bigger table.
   > How: black iron slate, basic component and catalyst, an iron block and a crafting table.
   > Tip: each bigger table is crafted from the one before it, so don't use this one up as decoration.
9. **5x5: Advanced Table**: `extendedcrafting:advanced_table` *(after: Extended Crafting, MV: Aluminum)*
   > What: a 5x5 crafting grid for mid-game recipes.
   > Chemistry: its MI electronic circuit rests on aluminum, won by electrolysis of alumina: 2Al₂O₃ → 4Al + 3O₂.
   > How: the Basic Table, gold blocks, advanced component and catalyst, plus the electronic circuit (check JEI).
10. **7x7: Elite Table**: `extendedcrafting:elite_table` *(after: 5x5: Advanced Table, HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > What: a 7x7 grid. Crystaltine and many late parts are crafted here.
   > Chemistry: the MI digital circuit needs polyethylene, chains of ethylene (C₂H₄) from cracking oil.
   > How: the Advanced Table, diamond blocks, elite component and catalyst, plus the digital circuit.
11. **9x9: Ultimate Table**: `extendedcrafting:ultimate_table` *(after: 7x7: Elite Table, EV: Processing Units)*
   > You remember building worlds on a table far bigger than this. Nine by nine will do for now.
   > What: the endgame's biggest crafts happen here, including the Seed of a New World.
   > Chemistry: the MI processing unit needs PVC: polyvinyl chloride, (C₂H₃Cl)ₙ, made from ethylene and chlorine.
   > How: the Elite Table, emerald blocks, ultimate component and catalyst, plus the processing unit.
12. **Packaged Automation**: `packagedauto:packager`; `packagedauto:unpackager` *(after: The God's Archive, 5x5: Advanced Table)*
   > What: Packaged Auto lets AE2 autocraft with Extended Crafting tables, through the PackagedExCrafting addon.
   > How: encode recipes in the Encoder, then set up a Packager, a PackagedExCrafting crafter and an Unpackager by your ME network (tooltips and JEI explain each block).
   > Tip: one setup per table size handles every recipe of that size.
13. **Ender Crafting**: `extendedcrafting:ender_crafter`; 2x `extendedcrafting:ender_alternator` *(after: Black Iron Parts, Into the Fire)*
   > What: the Ender Crafter finishes its recipes over time, faster with more Ender Alternators nearby.
   > How: ender ingots (iron + ender pearl), eyes of ender and a crafting table (check JEI).
   > Tip: a ring of alternators around the crafter speeds it up a lot.
14. **Combination Crafting**: `extendedcrafting:crafting_core`; 4x `extendedcrafting:pedestal` *(after: 7x7: Elite Table)*
   > What: put the main item on the Crafting Core and the extras on Pedestals around it. The core uses FE to fuse them.
   > How: elite components and catalysts, a frame and black iron (check JEI). JEI shows every combination recipe.
   > Tip: pipe FE into the core; it won't start without power.
15. **Crystaltine**: 4x `extendedcrafting:crystaltine_ingot` *(after: 7x7: Elite Table)*
   > What: a late crafting metal made on the Elite Table.
   > Chemistry: lapis lazuli's blue comes from lazurite, a sodium aluminosilicate with trapped sulfur ions (S₃⁻).
   > How: diamonds, lapis, iron, gold and a Nether Star in a 7x4 pattern (check JEI).
16. **Compact Machines**: `compactmachines:personal_shrinking_device` *(after: LV Machine Hull)*
   > What: fold an entire factory into a single block. The Personal Shrinking Device lets you walk inside it.
   > How: shrinking and enlarging modules, an eye of ender, copper, iron and glass panes (check JEI).
   > Tip: it also shows you which machine room you're in and takes you back out.
17. **Machine Walls**: 16x `compactmachines:wall` *(after: Compact Machines)*
   > What: Compact Machine Walls frame every machine block.
   > How: crafted from polished deepslate (check JEI).
   > Tip: inside a room the walls are unbreakable; these crafted ones aren't.
18. **Atom Modules**: 2x `compactmachines:shrinking_module`; 2x `compactmachines:enlarging_module` *(after: Machine Walls)*
   > What: every Compact Machine needs one Atom Shrinking Module and one Atom Enlarging Module.
   > How: an eye of ender, a light pressure plate, a stone button and a piston (sticky for shrinking).
   > Tip: make spares; each new machine eats a pair.
19. **Step Inside**: visit `compactmachines:compact_world` *(after: Atom Modules)*
   > You remember holding a world in your palm. This one is smaller, but it's yours.
   > What: craft a Compact Machine, place it, and right-click it with the Personal Shrinking Device to enter its room.
   > How: walls + both modules + a metal sets the size: copper = tiny, iron = small, gold = normal, obsidian = giant, netherite = colossal (check JEI for the rest).
   > Tip: tunnels carry items, fluids and power through the walls; perfect for a compact chemical line.
20. **Hide the Cables**: `cable_facades:facade_wrench` *(after: LV Machine Hull)*
   > What: Cable Facades disguise cables and pipes as any block. Tidy factories, same throughput.
   > How: craft the Facade Wrench, then apply blocks to cables (check JEI).
   > Tip: facades on MI pipes make chemical lines much easier to look at.
21. **Teleporting Cake**: `telepastries:overworld_cake` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: TelePastries cakes teleport you to their dimension when you eat a slice.
   > How: the Overworld Cake brings you home. Refill it with saplings; the Nether Cake takes obsidian.
   > Tip: place the Overworld Cake in your Nether hub for a quick ride home.
22. **Cake at the End**: `telepastries:end_cake` *(after: Teleporting Cake, The End)*
   > What: a cake that sends you to the End.
   > How: a cake surrounded by eyes of ender. Refill it with eyes of ender.
   > Tip: leave it in your base so the End is one bite away.
23. **Training Data: Blazes**: kill 30x `minecraft:blaze` *(after: Your First Model, Into the Fire)*
   > What: every kill with a matching model in your Deep Learner adds data. Blaze models are worth it: blaze rods feed brewing, Powah and Create's Blaze Burners.
   > How: put a blaze data model in the Deep Learner, keep it in your inventory, and hunt blazes at a Nether Fortress.
   > Tip: a blaze model at a high tier turns the Simulation Chamber into an endless rod farm.
24. **Training Data: Endermen**: kill 30x `minecraft:enderman` *(after: Your First Model)*
   > What: ender pearls go into Entangled blocks, AE2 seeds, Powah ender cells and teleporting. An enderman model makes them renewable.
   > How: load an enderman data model and hunt them at night, in warped forests, or in the End.
   > Tip: wear a carved pumpkin, or look at their feet, so they don't attack you first.
25. **Three Worlds of Data**: 4x `hostilenetworks:overworld_prediction`; 4x `hostilenetworks:nether_prediction`; 4x `hostilenetworks:end_prediction` *(after: Simulation, The End)*
   > What: each simulation gives a prediction for the mob's home dimension as well as the drop. Overworld, Nether and End predictions are used in recipes and Fabrication Directives.
   > How: run simulations of one mob from each dimension, such as a zombie, a blaze and an enderman.
   > Tip: predictions stack up fast; send them to storage with a pipe.
26. **The Data Center**: `hostilenetworks:data_center`; `hostilenetworks:data_center_io_port` *(after: Loot Fabricator)*
   > You remember watching a million lives at once. This is a pale copy, but a useful one.
   > What: the Data Center runs up to 25 Self Aware data models at the same time, each making one drop per cycle.
   > How: a Sim Chamber, a Loot Fabricator, a Nether Star, echo shards and obsidian. Build a 7x7x7 hollow shell: obsidian floor, black stained glass walls and ceiling, with the controller in a bottom wall facing out (JEI shows the rules).
   > Tip: IO ports in the shell let pipes feed inputs and pull the drops. A Fabrication Directive picks which drop each slot makes.
27. **Flux Crafting**: `extendedcrafting:flux_crafter`; 2x `extendedcrafting:flux_alternator` *(after: Extended Crafting)*
   > What: the Flux Crafter runs special recipes using FE delivered by nearby Flux Alternators, like the Flux Star.
   > How: gold and redstone ingots (check JEI). Place alternators around the crafter and power them.
   > Tip: JEI's Flux Crafter tab lists every recipe and the FE each one needs.
28. **Auto Tables**: `extendedcrafting:basic_auto_table` *(after: Crystaltine)*
   > What: Auto Tables remember a recipe and craft it with FE whenever the ingredients are inside. Each table size has its own.
   > How: a crafting table of the same size plus crystaltine components (check JEI).
   > Tip: the Ultimate Auto Table is also the heart of Packaged ExCrafting's Ultimate Crafter (see the Applied Energistics page).
29. **A Room for Every Line**: 4x `compactmachines:machine` *(after: Step Inside)*
   > What: one compact machine per chemical line keeps your base tidy: a sulfuric acid room, a chlorine room, a petrochemical room.
   > How: craft more machines (check JEI for the sizes) and enter each with the Personal Shrinking Device.
   > Tip: a room only runs while the chunk with its machine block is loaded, so claim and force-load your factory.
30. **Multiblock Builder**: `industrialization_overdrive:terminal` *(after: MV: Aluminum, Electric Blast Furnace)*
   > What: Industrialization Overdrive's Multiblock Builder places every missing block of an MI multiblock from your inventory (or a linked ME network). Other modes copy and paste a formed one, or tear it down.
   > How: steel plates, glass panes and an MI electronic circuit (MV). Look at the controller and press the key combination its tooltip shows; another key cycles the modes.
   > Tip: carry the casings, hatches and coils first: it only places what you have.

### Automation and Logic

*Make the factory run itself.*

1. **A Computer**: `computercraft:computer_normal` *(after: LV Machine Hull)*
   > You never did your own chores. You remember having things that did them for you.
   > What: CC: Tweaked computers run Lua programs: monitor tanks, balance chemical lines, build a base dashboard.
   > How: place it and right-click. Type help, or edit startup to write a program that runs on boot.
   > Tip: Mekanism machines can be read by computers directly. Put a computer next to one and try peripheral.getNames().
2. **Monitors**: 4x `computercraft:monitor_advanced` *(after: A Computer)*
   > What: monitors show program output on a wall. Placed together, they join into one big screen.
   > How: put monitors next to the computer and run monitor <side> <program> to send output to them.
   > Tip: advanced monitors show colour and accept clicks, so you can make touch buttons.
3. **Wired Networks**: 2x `computercraft:wired_modem`; 16x `computercraft:cable` *(after: Monitors)*
   > What: wired modems and networking cable connect a computer to machines that aren't touching it.
   > How: put a modem on the machine, run cable back to a modem on the computer, and right-click the machine's modem to attach it.
   > Tip: each attached peripheral gets a name. List them with peripheral.getNames().
4. **Ender Modem**: `computercraft:wireless_modem_advanced`; `computercraft:pocket_computer_advanced` *(after: Wired Networks)*
   > What: the Ender Modem sends messages with no range limit, even between dimensions. A pocket computer carries a terminal with you.
   > How: use rednet on both ends: one computer broadcasts tank levels, your pocket computer reads them.
   > Tip: a remote alarm for your reactor is a very good idea.
5. **Turtles**: `computercraft:turtle_normal` *(after: A Computer)*
   > What: turtles are programmable robots that mine, build and farm.
   > How: craft one with a tool (a pickaxe makes a mining turtle) and fuel it with coal.
   > Tip: try the built-in excavate and tunnel programs first.
6. **Advanced Peripherals**: `advancedperipherals:energy_detector`; `advancedperipherals:me_bridge` *(after: Wired Networks, The God's Archive)*
   > What: extra peripherals: the Energy Detector measures power flow; the ME Bridge reads (and requests crafts from) your whole AE2 network.
   > How: place them on your wired network like any other peripheral.
   > Tip: an ME Bridge program can keep your stock of every intermediate topped up.
7. **Base Dashboard**: `advancedperipherals:fluid_detector`; 8x `computercraft:monitor_advanced` *(after: Advanced Peripherals)*
   > What: a wall screen that shows your chemical stocks, power and flow rates at a glance.
   > How: the Fluid Detector measures flow through a pipe. Combine it with tank readings and the energy detector in one program.
   > Tip: colour lines red when a tank drops below 20%. You'll spot problems from across the room.
8. **Buses**: `ae2:import_bus`; `ae2:export_bus`; `ae2:storage_bus` *(after: The God's Archive)*
   > What: an import bus pulls items out of a machine, an export bus pushes them in, and a storage bus lets ME see inside a chest or tank.
   > How: place them on cable facing the machine. Set filters in each bus's GUI.
   > Tip: Applied Mekanistics is in the pack, so buses and storage also handle Mekanism gases like hydrogen and SO₂.
9. **Crafting CPU**: 2x `ae2:crafting_unit`; `ae2:1k_crafting_storage` *(after: Buses)*
   > What: a crafting CPU is a multiblock that works out and tracks autocrafting jobs.
   > How: build a solid box of crafting units with at least one crafting storage, and connect it to your network.
   > Tip: more storage lets it plan bigger jobs; co-processing units run more steps at once.
10. **Encoding Patterns**: `ae2:pattern_encoding_terminal`; 8x `ae2:blank_pattern` *(after: Crafting CPU)*
   > What: a pattern is a recipe card: these inputs make that output.
   > How: in the Pattern Encoding Terminal, switch to Processing mode for machine recipes and fill in the inputs and outputs.
   > Tip: processing patterns work for any machine: MI, Mekanism or the Combiner.
11. **Autocraft a Chemical Line**: `ae2:pattern_provider`; `ae2:molecular_assembler` *(after: Encoding Patterns)*
   > What: pattern providers push ingredients into machines; molecular assemblers do crafting-table recipes.
   > How: put a provider against an MI or Mekanism machine, load a processing pattern, and send the output back into the network.
   > Tip: chain patterns (sulfur → SO₂ → SO₃ → H₂SO₄) and one request runs the whole line.
12. **Level Emitters**: `ae2:level_emitter` *(after: Base Dashboard, Buses)*
   > What: a level emitter gives a redstone signal when the network holds more (or less) than a number you set.
   > How: set the item and the amount, then wire the signal to a machine's redstone control.
   > Tip: stop the Electrolytic Separator when hydrogen hits your target and you never waste power on a full tank.
13. **Fully Automated Sulfuric Acid**: 16x `modern_industrialization:sulfuric_acid_bucket`; checkmark *(after: Autocraft a Chemical Line, Level Emitters)*
   > The factory hums without you. You remember this kind of quiet.
   > What: a line that makes sulfuric acid on its own and stops when the tanks are full.
   > Chemistry: 2SO₂ + O₂ → 2SO₃ (industry uses a vanadium oxide catalyst), then SO₃ + H₂O → H₂SO₄.
   > How: Separator (O₂) → Oxidizer (S → SO₂) → Infuser (SO₃) → Rotary Condensentrator (water vapour) → Infuser (H₂SO₄). Feed sulfur with a bus or LaserIO and gate it with a level emitter.
   > Tip: when it runs a full day with no help, fill 16 buckets and click the checkmark.
14. **Menril Resin**: 16x `integrateddynamics:crystalized_menril_chunk` *(after: LV Machine Hull)*
   > What: Integrated Dynamics builds everything from crystallised Menril, a resin from Menril trees.
   > Chemistry: drying resin is just evaporation: the liquid loses its solvent and hardens, like tree sap turning into amber.
   > How: squeeze Menril logs in a Squeezer for resin, then dry the resin in a Drying Basin.
   > Tip: Menril trees grow wild in the Overworld. Plant the saplings once you find one.
15. **Integrated Dynamics**: 8x `integrateddynamics:cable`; `integrateddynamics:logic_programmer`; 4x `integrateddynamics:variable` *(after: Menril Resin)*
   > What: read a value (tank level, item count), apply logic, and act on it, all with blocks and cards.
   > How: a Reader part (e.g. Fluid Reader) on a tank exposes values. Write one onto a Variable Card in the Logic Programmer.
   > Tip: a Redstone Writer can then turn that value into a signal: perfect for stopping a separator when its tank is full.
16. **Variable Store**: `integrateddynamics:variablestore`; `integrateddynamics:labeller` *(after: Integrated Dynamics)*
   > What: the Variable Store holds variable cards so the whole network can use them; the Labeller names them.
   > How: put cards in the store and reference them from any writer or display panel on the network.
   > Tip: name cards after what they measure ('H2 tank %'). You'll thank yourself later.
17. **Challenge: The Self-Stopping Separator**: checkmark *(after: Variable Store)*
   > What: make a Mekanism Electrolytic Separator turn itself off when its hydrogen tank is 90% full, and back on below 50%.
   > How: a Reader on the tank → a comparison in the Logic Programmer → a Redstone Writer on the separator (set it to redstone control in its GUI).
   > Tip: the gap between 50% and 90% (hysteresis) stops it flickering on and off.
   > Click the checkmark once it works.
18. **Super Factory Manager**: `sfm:manager`; 8x `sfm:cable`; `sfm:disk` *(after: Integrated Dynamics)*
   > What: one Manager block runs a short program that moves items, fluids and energy between everything on its cables.
   > How: put the disk in the Manager and write a program, e.g. EVERY 20 TICKS DO INPUT FROM a OUTPUT TO b END.
   > Tip: the in-game editor has examples. Start with one input and one output.
19. **Labels**: `sfm:labelgun`; `sfm:network_tool` *(after: Super Factory Manager)*
   > What: the Label Gun tags inventories with names (like a and b above) for your programs.
   > How: set a label in the gun, then right-click each machine. The Network Tool shows what's connected.
   > Tip: label by job ('sulfur_in', 'acid_out'), not by machine type.
20. **Logistics Network**: 2x `logisticsnetworks:logistics_node` *(after: Labels)*
   > What: Logistics Network nodes sit on machines and chests and move items, fluids and energy between every node in the same named network, with no cables.
   > How: obsidian, a redstone block, hoppers, an eye of ender and a redstone torch for a node (check JEI). Open a node to create or join a network, then set what it imports and exports.
   > Tip: the Wrench has a copy-paste mode: set up one node, then paste its settings onto the rest.
21. **Logistics Filters**: `logisticsnetworks:tag_filter`; `logisticsnetworks:amount_filter` *(after: Logistics Network)*
   > What: filters narrow what a node moves: by tag, by amount and more.
   > How: put a filter in a node's slot and set it up in its GUI (check JEI for all the filter types).
   > Tip: a tag filter for 'c:dusts' sends every dust to one chest.
22. **Node Upgrades**: `logisticsnetworks:iron_upgrade`; `logisticsnetworks:gold_upgrade` *(after: Logistics Network)*
   > What: upgrades raise how much a node moves per batch and how often. Iron, gold, diamond and netherite tiers each do more.
   > How: the tier's metal, hoppers, chests and smooth stone (check JEI). Put them in the node's upgrade slots.
   > Tip: the upgrade's tooltip lists its exact items, fluid and energy per batch.
23. **Moving Chemicals**: `logisticsnetworks:mekanism_chemical_upgrade` *(after: Node Upgrades, Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser)*
   > What: the Mekanism Chemical Upgrade lets nodes move Mekanism chemicals: H₂, O₂, Cl₂, SO₂ and the rest.
   > Chemistry: the contact process needs SO₂ and O₂ in the same place: 2SO₂ + O₂ → 2SO₃. Nodes can bring both to one Chemical Infuser.
   > How: basic chemical tanks, infused alloy, chests and an Iron Upgrade (check JEI).
   > Tip: one network for gases and another for items keeps the settings easy to read.
24. **Network Manager**: `logisticsnetworks:computer` *(after: Logistics Network)*
   > What: the Computer opens a Network Manager that lists your networks, their nodes and how much each channel moves.
   > How: iron, glass and a comparator (check JEI).
   > Tip: when a line stops, look here first: a channel with no flow shows where the jam is.
25. **LaserIO Cards**: 2x `laserio:card_item` *(after: LaserIO)*
   > What: cards tell each LaserIO node what to move and in which direction.
   > How: put a card in a node's side slot. Set it to Extract on the source and Insert on the destination.
   > Tip: right-click with a card in your hand to open its settings.
26. **Fluids and Gases by Laser**: 2x `laserio:card_fluid`; 2x `laserio:card_chemical` *(after: LaserIO Cards)*
   > What: fluid cards move liquids; chemical cards move Mekanism gases, like hydrogen and SO₂.
   > How: same as item cards: Extract on the tank, Insert on the machine.
   > Tip: one node can run several cards on one side. Hydrogen and oxygen out of one separator, two cards.
27. **LaserIO Filters**: `laserio:filter_basic`; `laserio:filter_tag`; `laserio:filter_count` *(after: Fluids and Gases by Laser)*
   > What: filters go inside cards. Basic matches a list, Tag matches a tag, Count keeps a set number in stock.
   > How: put the filter in a card's filter slot and set it up.
   > Tip: a count filter on an insert card keeps exactly 64 sulfur in the oxidizer and no more.
28. **Overclocking**: 2x `laserio:overclocker_card`; 2x `laserio:overclocker_node` *(after: LaserIO Filters)*
   > What: overclockers make LaserIO move more, faster.
   > How: overclocker cards go in a card's upgrade slot; overclocker nodes go in the node.
   > Tip: most lines don't need it. Add it when a machine starves.
29. **Printers and Disks**: `computercraft:printer`; `computercraft:disk_drive` *(after: A Computer)*
   > What: a Disk Drive lets you save programs on floppy disks and carry them between computers. A Printer prints text onto paper.
   > How: check JEI. Put a disk in the drive and it appears as disk/ in the computer's files.
   > Tip: print a list of your reactions and their inputs and bind the pages into a book: a real lab notebook.
30. **Advanced Turtle**: `computercraft:turtle_advanced` *(after: Turtles)*
   > What: advanced turtles have colour screens and can be clicked, which makes menus easy.
   > How: an advanced computer with gold instead of iron around it (check JEI). Give it a pickaxe to make a Mining Turtle.
   > Tip: run excavate 16 on a mining turtle and it digs a 16x16 hole down to bedrock, bringing everything back.
31. **Geo Scanner**: `advancedperipherals:geo_scanner` *(after: Advanced Peripherals)*
   > What: the Geo Scanner lists every block around it within a radius, including ores, for your computer to read.
   > Chemistry: real geologists find ore bodies by measuring gravity, magnetism and how rocks conduct electricity, rather than digging blind.
   > How: check JEI. Put it next to a computer (or in a pocket computer) and call scan(8).
   > Tip: write a program that counts ore blocks by type: it's a quick way to check a deposit before setting up a mine.
32. **Chat Box and Player Detector**: `advancedperipherals:chat_box`; `advancedperipherals:player_detector` *(after: Advanced Peripherals)*
   > What: the Chat Box lets a computer send chat messages; the Player Detector tells it who is nearby.
   > How: check JEI. Place them next to a computer.
   > Tip: have the base warn everyone in chat when a tank of hydrogen is nearly full or an induction matrix is running low.
33. **Inventory Manager**: `advancedperipherals:inventory_manager`; `advancedperipherals:memory_card` *(after: Advanced Peripherals)*
   > What: the Inventory Manager lets a computer move items into and out of your own inventory, once you bind it with a Memory Card.
   > How: right-click the Memory Card to bind it to yourself, then put it in the manager (check JEI).
   > Tip: a button that refills your hotbar with torches and food from storage is a classic first program.
34. **Integrated Tunnels**: checkmark *(after: Variable Store)*
   > What: Integrated Tunnels adds importer, exporter and interface parts for Integrated Dynamics cables: items, fluids and energy move along the network, controlled by variables.
   > How: craft an Item Importer and an Item Exporter (check JEI), put them on cables at a chest and a machine, and give the exporter a variable card that says what to move. Click the checkmark when it works.
   > Tip: a fluid exporter with a boolean variable from a tank reader only fills the reactor when it's below half.
35. **Integrated Terminals**: `integratedterminals:terminal_storage_portable` *(after: Integrated Tunnels)*
   > What: Integrated Terminals adds a Storage Terminal part that shows everything connected to an Integrated Dynamics network, plus a portable version.
   > How: a Storage Terminal part between two crystalized menril chunks makes the portable terminal (check JEI).
   > Tip: the Crafting Job Terminal shows what Integrated Crafting is working on.
36. **Integrated Crafting**: checkmark *(after: Integrated Tunnels)*
   > What: Integrated Crafting adds a Crafting Interface: give it recipe variables and it crafts on demand through the ID network, much like AE2 patterns.
   > How: craft a Crafting Interface (check JEI), write recipes into variable cards with the Logic Programmer, and put them in the interface. Click the checkmark when one craft works.
   > Tip: it's a cheaper autocrafter than AE2 for small chains, like rubber sheets or redstone batteries.
37. **Your First SFM Program**: checkmark *(after: Super Factory Manager)*
   > What: Super Factory Manager runs small text programs written on a disk. Labels name the blocks it talks to.
   > How: label a chest a and a furnace b with the Label Gun, then write this program on the disk and put it in the manager. Click the checkmark when items start moving.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Program:
   > EVERY 20 TICKS DO
   >     INPUT FROM a
   >     OUTPUT TO b
   > END
   > Tip: add a side, like OUTPUT TO b TOP SIDE, to choose which face of the block is used. The manager's built-in examples cover fluids and energy too.
38. **Menril Trees**: 8x `integrateddynamics:menril_log`; 8x `integrateddynamics:menril_planks`; 4x `integrateddynamics:menril_berries` *(after: LV Machine Hull)*
   > What: Menril trees are where Integrated Dynamics starts: logs for resin, planks for building, and berries from the leaves.
   > Chemistry: real tree resins are mixtures of terpenes, small hydrocarbons that plants make from units of isoprene (C₅H₈). Amber is resin that hardened over millions of years.
   > How: find a Menril tree in the Overworld (Jade names it) and plant its saplings near your base.
   > Tip: read the berries' tooltip before you eat a stack.
39. **Squeezer and Drying Basin**: `integrateddynamics:squeezer`; `integrateddynamics:drying_basin`; `integrateddynamics:bucket_menril_resin` *(after: Menril Trees)*
   > What: the Squeezer presses Menril logs into liquid resin; the Drying Basin dries resin into crystalized Menril chunks.
   > Chemistry: drying is evaporation: the solvent leaves and the dissolved resin is left as a solid, the same way salt is left behind when brine dries.
   > How: Squeezer: an iron block, iron, planks and sticks. Drying Basin: logs, iron and black dye (check JEI). Put a Menril log in the Squeezer and jump on it a few times; pipe or bucket the resin into the basin and wait.
   > Tip: place the Squeezer on top of the basin and the resin flows straight in.
40. **Mechanical Squeezer and Basin**: `integrateddynamics:mechanical_squeezer`; `integrateddynamics:mechanical_drying_basin` *(after: Squeezer and Drying Basin, Generator and Energy Battery)*
   > What: powered versions of the Squeezer and Drying Basin: faster, pipe-friendly and no jumping.
   > How: the hand-powered block with Energy Batteries, a diamond and obsidian (check JEI). Feed them FE.
   > Tip: they also squeeze and dry other things; press U on each in JEI.
41. **Generator and Energy Battery**: `integrateddynamics:coal_generator`; `integrateddynamics:energy_battery` *(after: Menril Resin)*
   > What: Integrated Dynamics' own Generator burns furnace fuel for FE; the Energy Battery stores it and can feed a network through its cables.
   > How: the battery is crystalized Menril chunks and blocks around a redstone block; the Generator is a battery plus a furnace (check JEI).
   > Tip: any FE source works. Link a cable to your main grid instead if you have one.
42. **The Manual and the Wrench**: `integrateddynamics:on_the_dynamics_of_integration`; `integrateddynamics:wrench` *(after: Menril Resin)*
   > What: On the Dynamics of Integration is the mod's own guide, with worked examples. The Menril wrench rotates and removes ID blocks and parts.
   > How: the book is a book and two crystalized Menril chunks; the wrench is Menril chunks and redstone (check JEI).
   > Tip: the manual's tutorials give rewards too. Do them once.
43. **Variable Transformers**: 2x `integrateddynamics:variable_transformer_input`; 2x `integrateddynamics:variable_transformer_output`; `integrateddynamics:portable_logic_programmer` *(after: Variable Store)*
   > What: input and output variable transformers are the crafting parts of readers, writers and interfaces. The Portable Logic Programmer is the programmer in your pocket.
   > How: variable cards, Menril chunks and a sticky piston make four transformers (check JEI). Craft extra before a big build.
   > Tip: carry the portable programmer while wiring up a factory, so you can fix a card on the spot.
44. **LaserIO Toolkit**: `laserio:laser_wrench`; 4x `laserio:logic_chip`; `laserio:laser_connector` *(after: LaserIO Cards)*
   > What: the Laser Wrench links nodes (click one, then the other). Logic chips go into every node and card. A Laser Connector relays lasers between nodes without holding cards.
   > How: raw logic chips are a quartz block, clay, gold nuggets and redstone (4 at a time); smelt them. The connector is glass, redstone, iron and a logic chip; the wrench is iron and a logic chip.
   > Tip: nodes link up to a set range; connectors let you go round corners and through walls.
45. **Energy and Redstone Cards**: 2x `laserio:card_energy`; 2x `laserio:card_redstone` *(after: Fluids and Gases by Laser)*
   > What: Energy Cards move FE between nodes; Redstone Cards read and send redstone signals along the laser network.
   > How: a logic chip with quartz, gold nuggets and redstone (a redstone block for the energy card). Set Extract and Insert like any card.
   > Tip: a Redstone Card can switch a separator on only while the sulfur chest has stock.
46. **Card Holder, Cloner and Mod Filter**: `laserio:card_holder`; `laserio:card_cloner`; `laserio:filter_mod` *(after: LaserIO Filters)*
   > What: the Card Holder carries spare cards and fills nodes from your inventory; the Card Cloner copies one card's settings onto others; the Mod Filter matches everything from one mod.
   > How: holder and cloner are a logic chip in iron with chests or paper; the Mod Filter is a basic filter plus a book (check JEI).
   > Tip: clone one tuned acid card to every reactor in the line.
47. **Pipez for Everything**: 8x `pipez:fluid_pipe`; 8x `pipez:energy_pipe`; 8x `pipez:gas_pipe` *(after: Pipez)*
   > What: Pipez has a pipe for each thing that moves: fluids, FE, and Mekanism chemicals (the gas pipe).
   > Chemistry: one gas pipe network carries one chemical at a time well. Keep H₂ and Cl₂ apart: mixed, they react explosively in light (H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl).
   > How: iron and redstone with buckets (fluid), redstone blocks (energy) or Infused Alloy (gas), 16 at a time. Sneak-click where a pipe meets a machine to make that end extract.
   > Tip: Pipez pipes pull only from ends you set to extract, so connecting a machine doesn't drain it.
48. **Universal Pipe**: 8x `pipez:universal_pipe` *(after: Pipez for Everything)*
   > What: the Universal Pipe carries several kinds of thing at once in one line (its tooltip lists which).
   > How: item, fluid and energy pipes with iron and a redstone block make six (check JEI).
   > Tip: set each side's mode per type in its GUI, so one pipe can feed a machine items and power together.
49. **Pipe Upgrades and Tools**: `pipez:wrench`; `pipez:filter_destination_tool`; `pipez:advanced_upgrade` *(after: Pipez for Everything)*
   > What: the Pipe Wrench disconnects and reconnects pipe sides. The Filter Destination Tool aims a filter at one inventory. Upgrades (basic to infinity) raise speed and unlock filters and redstone modes.
   > How: each upgrade tier is the one before plus better materials (advanced: an improved upgrade, diamonds and redstone blocks). The wrench is flint and rods; the tool is iron, glass and a button. Put upgrades in the extracting pipe end.
   > Tip: an advanced upgrade's round-robin mode spreads ore evenly across a row of machines.

### The Mechanical Age

*Create: rotation, presses and mixers. An early mechanical age that runs alongside steam and feeds into Modern Industrialization.*

1. **Andesite Alloy**: 16x `create:andesite_alloy` *(after: Iron)*
   > Gears and shafts. You remember a world that ran on clockwork, and you liked it.
   > What: andesite alloy, Create's first building material.
   > How: craft andesite with iron nuggets (zinc nuggets work too). Later a Mechanical Mixer makes it in bulk.
   > Tip: hold W over almost any Create block to watch its Ponder tutorial.
2. **Andesite Casing**: 8x `create:andesite_casing` *(after: Andesite Alloy)*
   > What: casing blocks are the shell for gearboxes, deployers and more.
   > How: right-click a stripped log or stripped wood with andesite alloy. That's 'item application', and Create uses it a lot.
   > Tip: strip logs with an axe first. Any wood type works.
3. **Rotational Power**: 8x `create:shaft`; 8x `create:cogwheel`; `create:water_wheel` *(after: Andesite Casing)*
   > What: Create runs on rotation, not electricity. A water wheel on flowing water turns shafts and cogs.
   > How: water must flow across the wheel's blades. Shafts carry rotation straight; cogwheels pass it sideways.
   > Tip: every machine costs stress units (SU). If the network is over capacity, everything stops.
4. **Gear Ratios**: 4x `create:large_cogwheel` *(after: Rotational Power)*
   > What: a large cogwheel meshed with a small one doubles the speed (or halves it the other way).
   > Chemistry: physics, really: power is torque times speed. Gearing trades one for the other, and Create shows the trade as stress: a machine's SU cost grows with its speed.
   > How: a shaft and two planks make a large cogwheel. Place it diagonally next to a small one so the teeth mesh.
   > Tip: run slow machines (like mixers you don't need fast) at low speed to save stress.
5. **Windmills**: `create:windmill_bearing`; 8x `create:white_sail` *(after: Gear Ratios)*
   > What: a windmill bearing with sails attached spins without water.
   > How: place the bearing, build at least 8 sails onto the front of it (the Ponder shows how), and right-click the bearing.
   > Tip: more sails means more stress capacity but slower speed. Check the numbers with your goggles.
6. **Gearboxes and Belts**: 2x `create:gearbox`; 4x `create:belt_connector` *(after: Windmills)*
   > What: gearboxes turn rotation through corners; belts carry both rotation and items between two shafts.
   > How: belts are made from dried kelp. Click one shaft with a belt, then the other, to link them.
   > Tip: belts make great machine feeders: items ride past presses and fans on their own.
7. **Pressing and Mixing**: `create:mechanical_press`; `create:basin` *(after: Gearboxes and Belts)*
   > What: the Mechanical Press flattens ingots into plates and compacts items in a basin.
   > How: put the press over a depot, a belt or a basin, and power it.
   > Tip: plates are shared with MI in this pack, so pressed plates work in MI recipes too.
8. **Heated Mixing**: `create:mechanical_mixer`; `create:blaze_burner` *(after: Pressing and Mixing, Blaze Rods)*
   > What: a mixer over a basin, heated by a Blaze Burner, makes alloys and fluids.
   > Chemistry: heat speeds up reactions and melts metals so they can mix into alloys.
   > How: catch a blaze in an Empty Blaze Burner (iron plates around netherrack), put it under the basin, feed it fuel, and put the mixer above.
   > Tip: feed the burner with a deployer or a mechanical arm so it never goes cold.
9. **Brass**: 8x `create:zinc_ingot`; 8x `create:brass_ingot` *(after: Heated Mixing)*
   > A golden metal, mixed in a basin. The old skill comes back to your hands.
   > What: brass, the key metal of Create's second age.
   > Chemistry: brass is a copper-zinc alloy, usually about two-thirds copper. Zinc makes it harder and gives the gold colour.
   > How: 1 copper + 1 zinc in a heated mixer gives 2 brass. Zinc ore generates in the world.
10. **Brass Casing**: 8x `create:brass_casing` *(after: Brass)*
   > What: brass casing, for mechanical crafters, arms and brass tunnels.
   > How: right-click a stripped log or stripped wood with a brass ingot.
   > Tip: a deployer holding brass ingots can apply it automatically.
11. **Precision**: `create:precision_mechanism`; 4x `create:mechanical_crafter` *(after: Deployers)*
   > Each step in its place, every time. You used to build worlds this way.
