   > What: the precision mechanism, made by sequenced assembly: one item passes the same stations several times. Mechanical Crafters join into a big grid for recipes too large for a crafting table.
   > How: start with a gold plate, then deploy a cogwheel, a large cogwheel and an iron nugget onto it, 5 loops. JEI shows the sequence. Crafters are an electron tube, brass casing and crafting table.
   > Tip: some outputs are scrap. Sort them off the end of the belt and recycle them.
12. **Hand Crank**: `create:hand_crank` *(after: Andesite Casing)*
   > What: the simplest power source: you turn it yourself.
   > How: three planks over an andesite alloy. Hold right-click on it to spin whatever it's attached to.
   > Tip: handy for testing a contraption before you build a real generator for it.
13. **Goggles and Wrench**: `create:goggles`; `create:wrench` *(after: Rotational Power)*
   > What: Engineer's Goggles show speed and stress when you look at a machine; the wrench rotates and picks up Create blocks.
   > How: wear the goggles in your helmet slot and look at a shaft or generator.
   > Tip: sneak-right-click with the wrench to pick a block up instantly.
14. **Gauges**: `create:speedometer`; `create:stressometer` *(after: Gear Ratios)*
   > What: the Speedometer reads RPM; the Stressometer shows how much of your network's capacity is in use.
   > How: a compass on an andesite casing makes the speedometer (check JEI for the stressometer). Put them inline on a shaft.
   > Tip: both give a comparator signal, so a nearly full network can switch things off by redstone.
15. **Clutch and Gearshift**: `create:clutch`; `create:gearshift` *(after: Gear Ratios)*
   > What: a powered Clutch cuts the rotation passing through it; a powered Gearshift reverses it.
   > How: andesite casing + redstone, with a shaft (clutch) or a cogwheel (gearshift).
   > Tip: a gearshift on a timer makes a piston or gantry go back and forth by itself.
16. **Chain Drives**: 2x `create:encased_chain_drive` *(after: Clutch and Gearshift)*
   > What: encased chain drives pass rotation between each other in a line, in any direction, like a bike chain.
   > How: an andesite casing and three iron nuggets. The Adjustable Chain Gearshift version changes speed with a redstone signal (check JEI).
   > Tip: a neat way to bring power up a wall without shafts sticking out.
17. **Create Deco**: 8x `createdeco:brass_catwalk`; 8x `createdeco:andesite_sheet_metal` *(after: Andesite Casing)*
   > What: catwalks, sheet metal, cage lamps and other industrial building blocks.
   > How: check JEI for Create Deco recipes. Many use a press or the stonecutter.
   > Tip: catwalks over your machine lines make maintenance much easier.
18. **Create: Connected**: `create_connected:brass_gearbox`; `create_connected:kinetic_bridge` *(after: Windmills)*
   > What: Create: Connected adds small conveniences: compact gearboxes, a kinetic bridge that carries rotation across gaps, and more.
   > How: check JEI for everything the mod adds.
   > Tip: the kinetic bridge saves long runs of shafts.
19. **Kinetic Battery**: `create_connected:kinetic_battery` *(after: Create: Connected)*
   > What: the Kinetic Battery charges from rotation and gives it back later, so a windmill's power isn't wasted when nothing is running.
   > How: check JEI and its Ponder scene (hold W over it). Put it on a shaft line to charge it.
   > Tip: a charged battery can be picked up and moved, like a wind-up spring.
20. **Mechanical Bearing**: `create:mechanical_bearing` *(after: Rotational Power)*
   > What: a bearing turns the blocks attached to its face into a moving 'contraption': doors, rotors, fans, ferris wheels.
   > How: a wooden slab, an andesite casing and a shaft. Build onto its face, power it, and right-click to start.
   > Tip: moving blocks keep working: a spinning contraption can carry drills, harvesters and seats.
21. **Clockwork Bearing**: `create:clockwork_bearing` *(after: Mechanical Bearing)*
   > What: the Clockwork Bearing points its contraption at the current in-game time, like the hands of a clock.
   > How: a wooden slab, a brass casing and an electron tube. Build an hour hand on it, and a second layer for the minute hand.
   > Tip: a giant clock tower is a classic Create build.
22. **Glue and Chassis**: `create:super_glue`; 4x `create:linear_chassis` *(after: Mechanical Bearing)*
   > What: Super Glue sticks blocks together so they move as one; chassis blocks grab whole rows and layers at once.
   > How: super glue is slime, an iron plate and an iron nugget; drag it across a region to glue it. Linear chassis is alloy and logs.
   > Tip: a slimeball on a chassis face makes it sticky. Check the Ponder for range settings.
23. **Rope Pulley**: `create:rope_pulley` *(after: Glue and Chassis)*
   > What: the Rope Pulley lowers and raises a contraption on a rope, which makes a simple lift.
   > How: an andesite casing, wool and an iron plate. Glue a platform under it and power it.
   > Tip: the brass Elevator Pulley (check JEI) adds floor buttons and stops at contacts.
24. **Mechanical Piston**: `create:mechanical_piston`; 8x `create:piston_extension_pole` *(after: Glue and Chassis)*
   > What: a mechanical piston pushes and pulls glued blocks along a straight line, as far as its poles reach.
   > How: a wooden slab, an andesite casing and an extension pole. Put poles behind the piston head; each pole adds one block of travel.
   > Tip: rotation direction decides push or pull, so a gearshift reverses it.
25. **Drills and Harvesters**: `create:mechanical_drill`; `create:mechanical_harvester` *(after: Mechanical Piston)*
   > What: a moving Drill breaks blocks in front of it; a Harvester picks crops and leaves the plant to regrow.
   > How: both use andesite casing and alloy, with iron (drill) or iron plates (harvester). Mount them on a piston, bearing or gantry.
   > Tip: a slow bearing with harvesters sweeping a round field is a cheap automatic farm.
26. **Gantries**: `create:gantry_carriage`; 8x `create:gantry_shaft` *(after: Mechanical Piston)*
   > What: a Gantry Carriage runs along a powered gantry shaft, carrying its contraption with it, with no length limit.
   > How: gantry shafts are alloy and redstone; the carriage is a slab, a casing and a cogwheel. Power the shaft and the carriage moves.
   > Tip: gantries can carry other gantries, which makes an X-Y frame for a big drill or quarry.
27. **Minecart Contraptions**: 2x `create:cart_assembler` *(after: Glue and Chassis)*
   > What: a Cart Assembler on a rail turns a passing minecart and the blocks glued to it into a moving contraption.
   > How: andesite alloy, redstone and logs. Place it as a rail, build on top, then send a minecart through with the assembler powered.
   > Tip: a minecart contraption with a drill digs its own tunnel along the track.
28. **Millstone**: `create:millstone` *(after: Gearboxes and Belts)*
   > What: the Millstone grinds cobblestone to gravel, wheat to flour, flowers to dye, bones to bone meal and more.
   > Chemistry: grinding raises surface area: a powder reacts, dissolves and mixes much faster than a lump.
   > How: a cogwheel, an andesite casing and stone. Power it from the side or below and drop items in on top.
   > Tip: it doesn't take ores here. Ore crushing needs Crushing Wheels later.
29. **Mechanical Saw**: `create:mechanical_saw` *(after: Millstone)*
   > What: a still saw over a belt cuts logs into planks and acts as a stonecutter; on a contraption it fells whole trees.
   > How: iron plates, an iron ingot and an andesite casing. Set its target recipe with a filter if it has several.
   > Tip: a row of saws on a bearing makes a tree farm that never misses a log.
30. **Copper Casing**: 8x `create:copper_casing` *(after: Pressing and Mixing)*
   > What: copper casing is the base for spouts, item drains and hose pulleys.
   > How: right-click a stripped log or stripped wood with a copper ingot.
   > Tip: press a stack of copper sheets while you're at it. Pipes need them next.
31. **Pipes and Pumps**: 16x `create:fluid_pipe`; `create:mechanical_pump` *(after: Copper Casing)*
   > What: fluid pipes carry liquids, but only while a Mechanical Pump pushes them along.
   > Chemistry: a pump makes a pressure difference, and fluid always flows from high pressure to low.
   > How: copper sheets around a copper ingot make 4 pipes; a pipe and a cogwheel make a pump. The arrow on the pump shows the flow direction.
   > Tip: reverse the pump's rotation to reverse the flow.
32. **Hose Pulley**: `create:hose_pulley` *(after: Pipes and Pumps)*
   > What: the Hose Pulley lowers a hose into a pool and sucks the fluid up, or fills an area from your pipes.
   > How: a copper casing, a dried kelp block and a copper plate. Power it and pipe its output away with a pump.
   > Tip: a big enough body of water or lava counts as endless (check the Ponder), so it's a free fluid source.
33. **Bioethanol**: `createaddition:seed_oil_bucket`; `createaddition:bioethanol_bucket` *(after: Pipes and Pumps)*
   > What: Crafts & Additions makes liquid fuel from plants: seed oil, then biomass, then bioethanol, which burns in a Liquid Blaze Burner.
   > Chemistry: real bioethanol comes from yeast fermenting sugar: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2 C₂H₅OH + 2 CO₂. Plant oils are triglycerides, long carbon chains that store a lot of energy.
   > How: compact seeds in a press and basin for seed oil; mix crops with seed oil over heat for biomass; mix biomass, sugar and cinder flour for bioethanol (check JEI).
   > Tip: it's a renewable fuel for Create steam engines that never touches your oil wells.
34. **Spout**: `create:spout` *(after: Pipes and Pumps)*
   > What: the Spout pours fluid into items below it on a depot or belt: water bottles, buckets, honey, lava cakes and more.
   > How: a copper casing over dried kelp. Pipe fluid into it and put a depot underneath.
   > Tip: spouts are a station in many sequenced assembly recipes, so you'll use them again.
35. **Item Drain**: `create:item_drain` *(after: Spout)*
   > What: the Item Drain empties fluid containers that roll over it and holds the fluid for your pipes.
   > How: iron bars over a copper casing. Put it in a belt line and pull the fluid out with a pump.
   > Tip: it's the easy way to turn buckets from another mod into piped fluid.
36. **Steam Engines**: 2x `create:steam_engine`; 4x `create:fluid_tank` *(after: Spout)*
   > What: Create's boiler: a fluid tank full of water, heated by Blaze Burners, drives steam engines on its sides.
   > Chemistry: water expands about 1,600 times when it boils. That pressure pushes the pistons.
   > How: pump water into the tank, put fuelled Blaze Burners underneath, and place engines on its sides with a shaft in front. Check the Ponder.
   > Tip: a bigger tank and more burners raise the boiler level. Goggles show what's limiting it.
37. **Blaze Cake**: 2x `create:blaze_cake` *(after: Spout)*
   > What: feeding a Blaze Cake to a burner makes it superheated for a while, hotter than any normal fuel.
   > How: compact an egg, sugar and cinder flour into a cake base, then spout 250 mB of lava into it.
   > Tip: some recipes need superheat (New Age's blank circuits, for one). Check the heat icon in JEI.
38. **Encased Fan**: 2x `create:encased_fan` *(after: Pressing and Mixing)*
   > What: an Encased Fan blows items along and processes them depending on what the air passes through.
   > How: a shaft, an andesite casing and a propeller (iron plates around alloy). Water in front washes, fire smokes, lava blasts, soul fire haunts.
   > Tip: items on a belt or depot in the air stream are processed; loose items on the ground are too.
39. **Smoking and Blasting**: `minecraft:campfire`; `minecraft:lava_bucket` *(after: Encased Fan)*
   > What: a fan blowing through fire or a campfire cooks food (smoking); through lava it smelts like a blast furnace (blasting).
   > Chemistry: hot air carries heat by convection, which is why a fan oven cooks faster than a still one.
   > How: put a lit campfire or a lava source block a block or two in front of the fan and send items through the stream.
   > Tip: one lava block never runs out, so bulk blasting costs nothing but rotation.
40. **Haunting**: `minecraft:soul_campfire`; 16x `minecraft:soul_sand` *(after: Smoking and Blasting)*
   > What: air blown through soul fire 'haunts' items: sand becomes soul sand, stone bricks infested, fungi swap Nether types.
   > How: a soul campfire or soul fire in front of a fan. Pass sand through it for soul sand. JEI lists every haunting recipe.
   > Tip: it's a renewable source of soul sand and soul soil, handy for Nether wart and soul torches.
41. **Fan Catalysts**: `create_connected:empty_fan_catalyst` *(after: Haunting)*
   > What: Create: Connected's fan catalysts hold the 'fire' or 'water' for a fan in one tidy block.
   > How: brass and iron bars make the empty catalyst; fill it to pick its processing type (check JEI).
   > Tip: no more flowing water flooding your belt line.
42. **Depots**: 2x `create:depot` *(after: Gearboxes and Belts)*
   > What: a Depot holds one stack of items for a press, fan, spout or deployer to work on.
   > How: andesite alloy and an andesite casing. Right-click to put items on it.
   > Tip: a depot under a press is the cheapest plate maker in the game.
43. **Funnels and Tunnels**: 4x `create:andesite_funnel`; 2x `create:andesite_tunnel` *(after: Depots)*
   > What: funnels pull items out of chests and machines onto belts, or insert items from a belt; tunnels split a belt line evenly.
   > How: andesite alloy over dried kelp makes 2 funnels. Place them on a chest face or at the end of a belt (check JEI for tunnels).
   > Tip: a redstone signal shuts a funnel off, which is an easy on/off switch.
44. **Weighted Ejector**: `create:weighted_ejector` *(after: Funnels and Tunnels)*
   > What: the Weighted Ejector flings items (or you) to a target block in an arc.
   > How: a gold plate, a depot and a cogwheel. Hold it and click the target before you place it.
   > Tip: stand on it for a free launch pad. The landing is your problem.
45. **Chutes**: 4x `create:chute` *(after: Funnels and Tunnels)*
   > What: chutes drop items straight down between machines and chests; a fan under or over one blows items upward.
   > How: iron plates and an iron ingot make 4 chutes.
   > Tip: a chute into a crushing wheel or basin is the simplest feeder there is.
46. **Item Vaults**: 4x `create:item_vault` *(after: Chutes)*
   > What: Item Vaults merge into one big storage block when placed together.
   > How: iron plates around a barrel. Place several side by side; funnels and pipes reach the whole vault.
   > Tip: vaults also go into frogports, so make a few extra.
47. **Smart Logistics**: 2x `create:brass_funnel`; 2x `create:brass_tunnel`; `create:smart_chute` *(after: Chutes)*
   > What: brass funnels, tunnels and smart chutes take a filter, so you choose exactly which items pass and how many.
   > How: each uses an electron tube and brass (check JEI). Put an item or a Create Filter in the slot on the block.
   > Tip: a brass tunnel set to 'synchronise' only lets items through when every lane has one: perfect for 1:1 recipes.
48. **Cardboard**: 8x `create:cardboard` *(after: Heated Mixing)*
   > What: cardboard, for Create's package logistics.
   > Chemistry: paper and card are mats of cellulose fibres; water lets the fibres bond as it dries, which is why pulp holds together.
   > How: mix 4 pulpable items (like sticks or sugar cane; check JEI) with 250 mB of water for pulp, then press the pulp into cardboard.
49. **Packagers**: 2x `create:packager` *(after: Cardboard)*
   > What: a Packager boxes items from the inventory behind it into a package with an address, or unpacks packages addressed to it.
   > How: a cardboard block, iron ingots and redstone. Put a sign or name on it for its address (see the Ponder).
   > Tip: packages ride belts, chutes and chain conveyors like any other item.
50. **Frogports and Chains**: 2x `create:package_frogport`; 2x `create:chain_conveyor` *(after: Packagers)*
   > What: chain conveyors carry packages through the air; a Package Frogport tongues them off the chain at the right stop.
   > How: a frogport is a slimeball, an item vault and andesite alloy; a chain conveyor is a large cogwheel in andesite casings. Link chains with iron chains.
   > Tip: a chain network with frogports at each base is a whole-base mail system.
51. **Stock Keeping**: `create:stock_link`; `create:stock_ticker` *(after: Frogports and Chains)*
   > What: a Stock Link reports what a packager can reach; a Stock Ticker lets you browse that stock and order items to be packed and sent.
   > How: a transmitter (lightning rod, copper plates, redstone) on an item vault makes the link; add glass and gold for the ticker.
   > Tip: put the ticker by your workbench and order ingredients without walking to storage.
52. **Factory Gauges**: 2x `create:factory_gauge` *(after: Stock Keeping)*
   > What: Factory Gauges watch your stock and request ingredients for a recipe whenever a target amount runs low.
   > How: a stock link and a precision mechanism make 2. Place them on a packager and link them in their panel (see the Ponder).
   > Tip: chain gauges together and one order can run a whole production line.
53. **Rose Quartz**: 4x `create:rose_quartz`; 4x `create:polished_rose_quartz` *(after: Heated Mixing)*
   > What: rose quartz, for electron tubes.
   > How: craft 1 Nether quartz with 8 redstone, then polish it: hold sandpaper with the rose quartz in your off-hand and use it (a deployer can do this too).
   > Tip: washing crushed iron makes redstone as a byproduct, so a later ore line can feed this.
54. **Electron Tubes**: 4x `create:electron_tube` *(after: Rose Quartz)*
   > What: electron tubes go into deployers, mechanical crafters and other smart machines.
   > How: polished rose quartz on top of an iron plate.
   > Tip: make a stack. You'll need more than you think.
55. **Deployers**: `create:brass_hand`; 2x `create:deployer` *(after: Brass Casing, Electron Tubes)*
   > What: a deployer acts like a player's hand: it places, uses and applies items.
   > How: an andesite casing, an electron tube and a brass hand (pressed brass sheets).
   > Tip: deployers over a belt are how Create builds things in steps: that's sequenced assembly.
56. **Mechanical Arm**: `create:mechanical_arm` *(after: Precision)*
   > What: the mechanical arm moves items between depots, belts, basins and machines in its reach.
   > How: hold the arm and click inputs and outputs before you place it. Check the Ponder.
   > Tip: one arm can feed a whole ring of depots around it.
57. **Speed Controller**: `create:rotation_speed_controller` *(after: Precision)*
   > What: the Rotation Speed Controller sets the speed of the cogwheel on top of it to any RPM you choose.
   > How: a precision mechanism over a brass casing. Power it from below and set the speed on its face.
   > Tip: faster costs more stress, so only speed up what needs it.
58. **Crushing Wheels**: `create:millstone`; 2x `create:crushing_wheel` *(after: Precision)*
   > What: two Crushing Wheels spinning toward each other grind ore blocks into crushed ore, obsidian into powder, and stone into gravel and sand.
   > How: each wheel is a mechanical crafting recipe (check JEI). Place them side by side, spin them inward, and drop items in from above.
   > How: yields: an ore block gives 1 crushed ore plus a 75% chance of a second; deepslate and modded ores are capped at 2 in this pack. Raw ore gives just 1 crushed ore (no gain), plus an XP nugget chance.
   > Tip: crush ore blocks (silk touch), not raw ore. Even so it's the same 2x ceiling as every route before acids; Mekanism's acid chain is where 3x and up begins.
59. **Bulk Washing**: `create:encased_fan`; 8x `create:crushed_raw_iron` *(after: Crushing Wheels)*
   > What: an encased fan blowing through water washes crushed ore into nuggets plus a byproduct.
   > How: put flowing water in front of the fan and pass items through the air stream (a belt works).
   > Tip: washed crushed iron gives 9 nuggets (one ingot's worth) and a 75% chance of redstone. The byproduct is the bonus, not extra iron.
60. **Sturdy Sheets**: 4x `create:powdered_obsidian`; 4x `create:sturdy_sheet` *(after: Crushing Wheels)*
   > What: sturdy sheets, the armour plate for train casings and schedules.
   > Chemistry: obsidian is volcanic glass: lava cooled so fast that its silica never formed crystals.
   > How: crush obsidian into powder, then a sequenced assembly: spout 500 mB of lava onto it, press, press. JEI shows the loop.
   > Tip: the crushing wheels give the obsidian back 75% of the time, so feed it in until it's all powder.
61. **Train Casing**: 8x `create:railway_casing` *(after: Sturdy Sheets)*
   > What: train casing is the base block for stations, controls, signals and bogeys.
   > How: right-click a brass casing with a sturdy sheet.
   > Tip: right-clicking a track with train casing places a bogey: the wheels your train sits on.
62. **Train Track**: 32x `create:track` *(after: Train Casing)*
   > What: Create's train track, which can curve, slope and cross.
   > How: sequenced assembly on stone slabs (the 'sleepers'): deploy an iron or zinc nugget, deploy another, then press. Check JEI.
   > Tip: click one track end, then another, to lay a curve or slope between them.
63. **Stations and Controls**: 2x `create:track_station`; `create:controls` *(after: Train Track)*
   > What: a Train Station assembles a train from the casing, bogeys and blocks on the track beside it; Train Controls let you drive it.
   > How: a station is train casing and a compass; controls are a lever, train casing and a precision mechanism.
   > Tip: stand at the station's GUI and press assemble once the controls face the way you want to go.
64. **Your First Train**: 2x `create:schedule` *(after: Stations and Controls)*
   > A machine that carries itself across the world. You used to move whole mountains like this.
   > What: a Train Schedule tells a train where to stop and when to leave, so it runs by itself.
   > How: a sturdy sheet and paper make 4. Write stops in it and give it to the conductor (a mob in a seat behind the controls).
   > Tip: a train with portable storage interfaces at each station moves ore and goods on its own.
65. **Signals**: 4x `create:track_signal` *(after: Stations and Controls)*
   > What: signals split a line into sections so two trains never share one. Real railways use the same 'block' idea.
   > How: train casing and an electron tube make 4. Place them on the track at each junction.
   > Tip: check the Ponder for chain signals at crossings.
66. **Rotation to Electricity**: `createaddition:alternator` *(after: Precision, Analog Circuit)*
   > What: Crafts and Additions' Alternator turns rotation into FE.
   > Chemistry: a coil turning in a magnetic field pushes electrons along the wire: electromagnetic induction.
   > How: in this pack its core is an MI analog circuit (LV), so electricity from rotation waits for the LV age. Feed it fast rotation.
67. **Electricity to Rotation**: `createaddition:electric_motor` *(after: Rotation to Electricity)*
   > What: the Electric Motor turns FE back into rotation, with a speed you set.
   > How: give it FE from your MI or Mekanism grid and set the speed in its GUI.
   > Tip: motors free you from water wheels and windmills. Put a Create line anywhere.
68. **Wires and Connectors**: `createaddition:rolling_mill`; 4x `createaddition:connector`; `createaddition:copper_spool` *(after: Rotation to Electricity)*
   > What: the Rolling Mill turns ingots into rods and plates into wire. Spools of wire link connectors into power lines.
   > How: roll copper plates into wire, wind it onto a spool, then click two connectors with the spool to string a wire.
   > Tip: connectors carry power over long gaps without cables on the ground.
69. **Accumulators**: 2x `createaddition:capacitor`; `createaddition:modular_accumulator` *(after: Wires and Connectors)*
   > What: the Modular Accumulator stores FE, and several placed together merge into one bigger battery.
   > Chemistry: the capacitor here is zinc over copper, the same pair Volta used in the first battery in 1800.
   > How: needs brass casing, capacitors, copper rods and electrum wire. Electrum is gold + silver mixed hot.
   > Tip: put it between your alternators and your machines to smooth out spikes.
70. **Tesla Coil**: `createaddition:tesla_coil` *(after: Accumulators)*
   > What: the Tesla Coil charges FE items on belts or depots below it, and zaps anything that walks under it.
   > How: a mechanical crafting recipe with brass, a capacitor, electron tubes and a copper spool (check JEI). Power it with FE.
   > Tip: put a belt of jetpacks or gadgets under it for an automatic charging station.
71. **Create: New Age**: `create_new_age:generator_coil`; `create_new_age:basic_energiser` *(after: Rotation to Electricity)*
   > What: magnet-and-coil generators, and Energisers that charge items with electricity.
   > How: the Generator Coil's core is an MI analog circuit (LV) in this pack. Spin it among magnets; the Ponder shows the layout.
   > Tip: the Basic Energiser is just an andesite casing and a lightning rod.
72. **New Age Motors**: `create_new_age:basic_motor`; `create_new_age:carbon_brushes` *(after: Create: New Age)*
   > What: New Age's Basic Motor runs on FE and spins a shaft; carbon brushes and motor extensions tune it.
   > Chemistry: a motor is a generator run backwards: current in a coil inside a magnetic field feels a force and turns.
   > How: an andesite casing, a magnetite block, a shaft and iron nuggets (check JEI for magnetite). Brushes are alloy, coal and a shaft.
73. **Heat Engines**: `create_new_age:stirling_engine`; `create_new_age:basic_solar_heating_plate` *(after: Create: New Age)*
   > What: New Age moves heat through heat pipes. Solar heating plates collect it from sunlight; a Stirling Engine turns it into slow rotation, and a Boiler Heater uses it in place of a blaze burner.
   > Chemistry: a real Stirling engine heats and cools a sealed gas. Hot gas expands and pushes a piston; cooled gas contracts and pulls it back. No fuel burns inside it.
   > How: heat pipes, iron and glass for the plate; a copper block, heat pipes and a shaft for the engine (check JEI and the Ponder scenes).
74. **Charging Metal**: 4x `create_new_age:overcharged_iron` *(after: Create: New Age)*
   > What: overcharged iron, made by charging an iron ingot in an Energiser.
   > How: power the Energiser with FE and put iron underneath it (on a depot or belt). Each ingot takes 1,000 FE.
   > Tip: overcharged metals make better wire and magnets.
75. **New Age Circuits**: 4x `create_new_age:blank_circuit`; `create_new_age:copper_circuit` *(after: Charging Metal)*
   > What: New Age's own circuit boards, used in its better machines (check JEI for uses).
   > Chemistry: real boards are an insulating base with copper traces; here quartz, stone, iron and redstone fuse into the base.
   > How: compact stone, redstone, iron and quartz over a superheated burner (blaze cake) for 4 blanks, then deploy copper wire onto one.
76. **Layered Magnets**: 4x `create_new_age:layered_magnet` *(after: Charging Metal)*
   > What: stronger magnets for New Age generators.
   > How: overcharged iron and overcharged gold in layers (check JEI).
   > Tip: a stronger field induces more current in the same coil.
77. **Thorium Reactor**: 8x `create_new_age:thorium`; `create_new_age:reactor_rod` *(after: Charging Metal, EV: Processing Units)*
   > What: New Age's nuclear reactor, fuelled by thorium.
   > Chemistry: thorium-232 isn't fissile itself; it absorbs a neutron and becomes uranium-233, which is.
   > How: the rods need MI processing units (EV) in this pack, so it arrives alongside Mekanism fission. Check JEI and the Ponder for the build.
   > Tip: treat it like any reactor: cooling first, then power.
78. **Liquid Experience**: `create_enchantment_industry:mechanical_grindstone`; `create_enchantment_industry:experience_bucket` *(after: Precision)*
   > What: Enchantment Industry turns experience into a fluid you can store and pipe.
   > How: the Mechanical Grindstone strips enchantments off items; a Grindstone Drain collects the XP as fluid. Check JEI.
   > Tip: feed it the enchanted junk from your mob farm.
79. **Automated Enchanting**: `create_enchantment_industry:blaze_enchanter` *(after: Liquid Experience)*
   > What: the Blaze Enchanter spends liquid XP to enchant items automatically.
   > How: it's a smithing upgrade of a Blaze Burner with an enchanting table (check JEI). Give it an enchanting template and XP.
   > Tip: put it beside a belt and a deployer for a hands-free enchanting line.
80. **The Printer**: `create_enchantment_industry:printer` *(after: Automated Enchanting)*
   > What: the Printer copies written and enchanted books, paid for in liquid XP.
   > How: check JEI and the Ponder for the setup.
   > Tip: find a good enchanted book once, then print it as often as your XP lasts.
81. **Experience Lantern**: `create_enchantment_industry:experience_lantern` *(after: Liquid Experience)*
   > What: the Experience Lantern pulls nearby experience orbs in and stores them as liquid XP.
   > How: check JEI for the recipe. Hang it over a mob farm's kill zone and pipe its XP away.
   > Tip: pair it with the Blaze Enchanter and your farm pays for its own enchanting.
82. **Large Water Wheel**: `create:large_water_wheel` *(after: Rotational Power)*
   > What: a 3x3 water wheel. It turns at half the speed of the small one but gives more stress capacity in total (check with goggles).
   > Chemistry: physics again: a bigger wheel catches the flow further from its axle, so the same water gives more torque.
   > How: a water wheel ringed with planks. Give it flowing water across the whole face.
   > Tip: follow it with a large cogwheel to get the speed back.
83. **Fine Rotation Control**: `create:vertical_gearbox`; `create:adjustable_chain_gearshift`; `create:sequenced_gearshift` *(after: Chain Drives, Electron Tubes)*
   > What: the Vertical Gearbox passes rotation up and down; the Adjustable Chain Gearshift changes its speed ratio with the strength of a redstone signal; the Sequenced Gearshift runs a programmed list of turns, waits and reversals.
   > How: vertical gearbox: a gearbox in the crafting grid. The other two add an electron tube to a chain drive or to brass casing and a cogwheel (check JEI).
   > Tip: a sequenced gearshift on a piston makes a door that opens, waits and closes on one pulse.
84. **Spare Burners**: 2x `create:empty_blaze_burner`; `create:blaze_cake_base` *(after: Heated Mixing)*
   > What: empty Blaze Burners to catch more blazes, and a Blaze Cake base ready to fill with lava.
   > Chemistry: a superheated burner runs hotter because the cake gives it richer fuel; as a rule of thumb, many reactions run about twice as fast for every 10 °C hotter.
   > How: burners are iron plates around netherrack; right-click a blaze with one, or use it on a monster spawner. The cake base is compacted egg, sugar and cinder flour (check JEI).
   > Tip: a big steam boiler wants nine or more burners. Catch them early.
85. **Valves and Smart Pipes**: `create:fluid_valve`; `create:copper_valve_handle`; `create:smart_fluid_pipe` *(after: Pipes and Pumps, Electron Tubes)*
   > What: a Fluid Valve opens or closes a pipe when rotation turns it (a valve handle turns it by hand); a Smart Fluid Pipe lets only the fluid you set pass.
   > Chemistry: chemical plants are mostly valves: the right reagent, in the right amount, at the right moment.
   > How: valve: an iron plate and a pipe. Handle: copper plates on andesite alloy. Smart pipe: a pipe with a brass plate and an electron tube (check JEI).
   > Tip: a smart pipe after a mixer stops the wrong fluid backing up the line.
86. **Nozzle**: `create:nozzle` *(after: Encased Fan)*
   > What: a Nozzle on the front of an Encased Fan spreads its air all around instead of in a line, and pushes or pulls mobs in range.
   > How: andesite alloy and wool (check JEI).
   > Tip: a fan, a nozzle and a fire behind it make a warm room. A water source behind it, a mob wash.
87. **Plough and Radial Chassis**: `create:mechanical_plough`; 3x `create:radial_chassis` *(after: Glue and Chassis)*
   > What: the Mechanical Plough tills dirt and breaks small blocks as a contraption moves; Radial Chassis grabs blocks around it in a ring, for bearing contraptions.
   > How: plough: iron plates, andesite alloy and a casing. Radial chassis: logs and andesite alloy, three at a time (check JEI).
   > Tip: a plough leading a row of harvesters and seed deployers is a field that farms itself.
88. **Portable Interfaces**: 2x `create:portable_storage_interface`; 2x `create:portable_fluid_interface` *(after: Minecart Contraptions, Copper Casing, Chutes)*
   > What: a pair of Portable Storage (or Fluid) Interfaces, one on the contraption and one on the ground, swap items or fluids whenever they line up.
   > How: an andesite casing (items) or copper casing (fluids) with a chute (check JEI).
   > Tip: a train with fluid interfaces can haul acid from a remote plant without a single pipe.
89. **Take a Seat**: 1x any of `item_tag(create:seats)` *(after: Andesite Casing)*
   > What: Create seats. You can sit on them, mobs sit on them, and a seated mob (or you) is what drives a train or moving contraption.
   > How: a wooden slab and wool of any colour. Dye one seat to recolour it.
   > Tip: a villager in a seat behind train controls becomes your conductor.
90. **Display Links and Nixie Tubes**: `create:display_link`; 4x `create:nixie_tube` *(after: Stock Keeping, Electron Tubes)*
   > What: a Display Link reads a block (a stockpile, a tank, a station, a speedometer) and writes it onto Nixie Tubes, signs or display boards.
   > How: a transmitter on brass casing makes the link; two electron tubes make four nixie tubes (check JEI).
   > Tip: link a tank of seed oil to a nixie row and you'll see the level from across the room.
91. **Re-Packager**: `create:repackager` *(after: Packagers)*
   > What: a Re-Packager opens incoming packages and repacks their contents, so a recipe's ingredients arrive at a machine in one box.
   > How: a Packager converted in the crafting grid (check JEI).
   > Tip: use it in front of a mechanical crafter that needs many different items at once.
92. **Train Fittings**: 2x `create:train_door`; 2x `create:train_trapdoor`; `create:track_observer` *(after: Stations and Controls)*
   > What: Train Doors and Trapdoors open only when the train is stopped at a station. A Train Observer gives a redstone signal when a train passes over it.
   > How: a wooden door or trapdoor with train casing; the observer is train casing and a pressure plate (check JEI).
   > Tip: a train observer before a station can open a loading gate in time.

### Just Dire Things

*Living goo that rewrites the blocks it touches: new metals, denser coal, refined fuels, upgradeable tools and small automation machines.*

1. **Feeding the Goo**: `justdirethings:gooblock_tier1`; 2x `minecraft:iron_block` *(after: Iron)*
   > You remember making things change just by touching them. The goo still can; you'll borrow the trick.
   > What: goo blocks slowly convert the blocks touching them. Tier 1 (Primogel) turns iron blocks into raw ferricore ore.
   > How: place the goo, put iron blocks against its sides and wait. JEI's Goo Spreading tab lists every conversion, its tier and its time.
   > Tip: after a conversion the goo can die (a 10% chance in this pack's config). Right-click exhausted Primogel with sugar or rotten flesh to wake it.
2. **Raw Ferricore**: 8x `justdirethings:raw_ferricore` *(after: Feeding the Goo)*
   > What: raw ferricore ore drops raw ferricore. Smelt or blast it into ferricore ingots, the base of everything on this page.
   > How: mine the converted block with a pickaxe. Silk Touch gives you the ore block itself instead.
   > Tip: one iron block (9 ingots) becomes one raw ferricore, so let a Create or MI line feed the goo once you need a lot.
3. **Upgrade Blanks**: 2x `justdirethings:upgrade_blank` *(after: Ferricore Tools)*
   > What: every Just Dire Things upgrade and smithing template starts from a blank.
   > How: four ferricore ingots in a diamond shape (check JEI).
   > Tip: keep a stack around; most upgrades are a blank plus a few vanilla items.
4. **Blazebloom and Blazegold**: `justdirethings:gooblock_tier2`; 4x `justdirethings:raw_blazegold` *(after: Raw Ferricore, Into the Fire)*
   > What: Blazebloom goo (tier 2) converts gold blocks into raw blazegold ore. Blazegold opens the second tier of tools and machines.
   > How: tier 1 goo ringed with blaze powder, redstone and Nether wart (check JEI). Smelt the raw blazegold.
   > Chemistry: real gold is famously unreactive: it doesn't tarnish in air because Au has a very high reduction potential (+1.50 V).
   > Tip: feed exhausted Blazebloom Nether wart or blaze powder.
5. **VoidShimmer and Celestigem**: `justdirethings:gooblock_tier3`; 4x `justdirethings:celestigem` *(after: Blazebloom and Blazegold, The Dragon's Breath)*
   > What: VoidShimmer goo (tier 3) turns diamond blocks into celestigem ore, which drops celestigem directly. Advanced machines and the third tool tier use it.
   > How: tier 2 goo ringed with ender pearls, end stone and dragon's breath (check JEI). A diamond conversion takes twice as long as iron or gold.
   > Chemistry: diamond is pure carbon: every atom bonds to four neighbours in a tetrahedral (sp³) lattice, which is why it's so hard.
   > Tip: VoidShimmer revives with chorus fruit or an ender pearl.
6. **Shadowpulse and Eclipse Alloy**: `justdirethings:gooblock_tier4`; 2x `justdirethings:raw_eclipsealloy` *(after: VoidShimmer and Celestigem, An Ancient City)*
   > The goo has learned to eat the hardest thing you own. You remember being that hungry.
   > What: Shadowpulse goo (tier 4) turns netherite blocks into raw eclipse alloy ore, Just Dire Things' top material.
   > How: tier 3 goo ringed with sculk, sculk shriekers and echo shards from an Ancient City (check JEI). Smelt the raw eclipse alloy.
   > Tip: one netherite block is a big price. Plan which eclipse alloy item you want first; Shadowpulse revives with sculk or a sculk catalyst.
7. **Primal Coal**: 8x `justdirethings:coal_t1` *(after: Feeding the Goo)*
   > What: tier 1 goo turns a coal block (or a charcoal block) into Primal Coal ore. Primal Coal burns for 4,800 ticks, three times a piece of coal.
   > Chemistry: real coal ranks up with heat and pressure: lignite (~65% carbon) → bituminous (~80%) → anthracite (>90%). More carbon, more energy per kilogram.
   > How: place coal or charcoal blocks against tier 1 goo and mine the ore (it drops several pieces).
   > Tip: nine Primal Coal make a block, and that block is the input for the next tier.
8. **Blaze Ember**: 8x `justdirethings:coal_t2` *(after: Primal Coal, Blazebloom and Blazegold)*
   > What: tier 2 goo turns a Primal Coal block into Blaze Ember ore. Blaze Ember burns 14,400 ticks: nine coal's worth.
   > How: craft a Primal Coal block, put it against Blazebloom goo and mine the ore for 3 to 4 embers.
   > Tip: each coal tier burns three times longer than the one before, so the climb pays off quickly.
9. **Voidflame Coal**: 8x `justdirethings:coal_t3` *(after: Blaze Ember)*
   > What: tier 3 goo turns a Blaze Ember block into Voidflame Coal ore: 43,200 ticks of burn per piece.
   > How: a block of Blaze Ember against VoidShimmer goo (check JEI for counts).
   > Tip: Voidflame Coal is also the catalyst for the tier 3 fluid fuel.
10. **Eclipse Ember**: 4x `justdirethings:coal_t4` *(after: Voidflame Coal)*
   > What: tier 4 goo turns a Voidflame Coal block into Eclipse Ember ore. One ember burns 129,600 ticks, as long as 81 pieces of coal.
   > How: a block of Voidflame Coal against Shadowpulse goo.
   > Chemistry: burning carbon, C + O₂ → CO₂, gives about 394 kJ per mole. Denser fuel just packs more carbon into the same slot.
11. **Charcoal Blocks**: 4x `justdirethings:charcoal` *(after: Feeding the Goo)*
   > What: Just Dire Things adds a charcoal block (nine charcoal). It burns for 16,000 ticks and tier 1 goo accepts it like a coal block.
   > Chemistry: charcoal is wood heated without air (pyrolysis): water and volatiles leave, mostly carbon stays.
   > Tip: a tree farm plus a furnace array makes the coal ladder fully renewable.
12. **Simple Coal Generator**: `justdirethings:generatort1` *(after: Primal Coal)*
   > What: burns solid fuel for Forge Energy: up to 1,000 FE/t into a 1,000,000 FE buffer.
   > How: ferricore, redstone, coal and a blast furnace (check JEI).
   > Tip: it burns fuel four times faster than a furnace, so the long-burning coal tiers are what make it worth having.
13. **Fuel Canister**: `justdirethings:fuel_canister` *(after: Primal Coal)*
   > What: a canister that soaks up furnace fuel and stores it as burn time. Its tooltip shows how much it holds.
   > How: ferricore around a piece of coal (check JEI).
   > Tip: pair it with the Pocket Generator from the Tools page so your FE tools recharge on long trips.
14. **Polymorphic Fluid**: 4x `justdirethings:polymorphic_catalyst`; `justdirethings:polymorphic_fluid_bucket` *(after: Blazebloom and Blazegold)*
   > What: Polymorphic Fluid is the base for every Just Dire Things fluid: fuels, portal fluid and time fluid.
   > How: blazegold + Nether wart makes four catalysts. Throw one into a water source block and it becomes Polymorphic Fluid. Bucket it up.
   > Chemistry: a real catalyst speeds a reaction and comes out unchanged. This one is used up, so chemists would call it a reagent.
   > Tip: JEI shows these 'fluid drop' recipes; each catalyst converts one source block.
15. **Blaze Ember Fuel**: `justdirethings:refined_t2_fluid_bucket` *(after: Polymorphic Fluid, Blaze Ember)*
   > What: liquid fuel for the Simple Fuel Generator. It comes from Polymorphic Fluid in two steps.
   > How: drop a Blaze Ember into a Polymorphic Fluid source to get Unrefined Blaze Ember Fuel, then let tier 2 goo touch that source to refine it.
   > Chemistry: real refineries separate crude oil by boiling point in a fractionating column; here the goo does the cleanup.
   > Tip: tier 3 and 4 fuels follow the same pattern: drop the next coal into the refined fuel below it, then refine with the next goo.
16. **Simple Fuel Generator**: `justdirethings:generatorfluidt1` *(after: Blaze Ember Fuel)*
   > What: burns refined fuel for up to 5,000 FE/t. Blaze Ember Fuel gives 450 FE per mB, Voidflame 1,300 and Eclipse Ember 4,000.
   > How: blazegold, redstone, buckets and a blast furnace (check JEI). Pipe or bucket refined fuel in.
   > Tip: one bucket of Eclipse Ember Fuel is 4,000,000 FE, nearly the generator's whole 5,000,000 FE buffer.
17. **Voidflame and Eclipse Fuels**: `justdirethings:refined_t3_fluid_bucket`; `justdirethings:refined_t4_fluid_bucket` *(after: Simple Fuel Generator)*
   > What: the tier 3 and tier 4 liquid fuels, roughly 3x and 9x the energy of Blaze Ember Fuel per mB.
   > How: Voidflame Coal into refined Blaze Ember Fuel, then VoidShimmer goo; Eclipse Ember into refined Voidflame Fuel, then Shadowpulse goo.
   > Tip: one bucket of each. The refined fuel is consumed by the next step, so keep a source block of each tier going.
18. **Energy Transmitter**: 2x `justdirethings:energytransmitter` *(after: Simple Coal Generator)*
   > What: Energy Transmitters move FE without cables, up to 1,000 FE/t, losing a little for every block of distance (check the GUI).
   > How: celestigem, redstone, an ender pearl and blazegold (check JEI).
   > Chemistry: real power lines lose energy as heat, P = I²R, which is why grids use high voltage and low current.
19. **Time Crystals**: 4x `justdirethings:time_crystal` *(after: Shadowpulse and Eclipse Alloy)*
   > What: tier 4 goo turns budding amethyst into a Budding Time Crystal block, which grows time crystal clusters.
   > How: budding amethyst can't be moved, so take Shadowpulse goo to a geode and place it touching a budding block. The budding block has to mature in stages first; check JEI and its tooltip for what it needs.
   > Chemistry: amethyst is quartz, SiO₂, coloured purple by iron (Fe³⁺) impurities and natural radiation.
   > Tip: a Time Crystal Block converts back into a budding block, so one success is enough.
20. **The Time Wand**: `justdirethings:time_wand`; `justdirethings:time_fluid_bucket` *(after: Time Crystals)*
   > What: the Time Wand makes a block tick faster (up to 256x), paid for in FE and Time Fluid.
   > How: Time Fluid: drop a time crystal into a Polymorphic Fluid source. The wand is blazegold, ferricore and a time crystal (check JEI).
   > Tip: try it on a slow crop, a furnace or a budding block.
21. **Paradox Machine**: `justdirethings:paradoxmachine` *(after: The Time Wand)*
   > What: the Paradox Machine reverts blocks and entities in an area to an earlier state, paying FE and Time Fluid per block or entity.
   > How: eclipse alloy, time crystals, a time crystal block and a bucket of Time Fluid (check JEI).
   > Tip: it's powerful and expensive. Read its GUI before you aim it at your base.

   > What: Just Dire Things tools work like iron ones but accept ability upgrades. Each tier can hold more abilities and break more blocks at once.
   > How: the usual tool shapes with ferricore ingots and sticks.
   > Tip: vein-style abilities are capped per tier: 64 blocks for ferricore, 128 blazegold, 192 celestigem, 256 eclipse alloy.

   > What: Ore Miner harvests every connected ore when you break one.

   > Tip: every ability goes on the same way. JEI shows which tools accept which upgrade.

   > How: a blazegold template is a blank ringed with blazegold. Smith it with a ferricore pickaxe and a blazegold ingot.

### Applied Energistics

*The archive of a god: every item as data, every recipe on demand.*

1. **Certus Quartz**: 16x `ae2:certus_quartz_crystal`; 8x `ae2:certus_quartz_dust` *(after: Fallen Stars)*
   > You remember crystals that sang when you touched them. These still hum, faintly.
   > What: certus quartz goes into almost every AE2 recipe: processors, glass, cells and cards.
   > Chemistry: certus is fictional, but it behaves like real quartz (SiO₂), which is piezoelectric: squeeze it and it makes a small voltage.
   > How: mine certus from meteorite craters and budding certus. Grind crystals into dust in the Inscriber with no press (or any crusher JEI lists).
   > Tip: charged certus plus certus dust dropped in water makes two new crystals. Grow it once you have a little.
2. **Sky Stone**: 16x `ae2:sky_stone_block`; 4x `ae2:smooth_sky_stone_block` *(after: Fallen Stars)*
   > What: sky stone is the rock of AE2 meteorites. The ME Controller in this pack needs smooth sky stone.
   > Chemistry: real stony meteorites are mostly silicate minerals like olivine and pyroxene; iron meteorites are an iron-nickel alloy.
   > How: mine the crater shell (it needs an iron pickaxe or better), then smelt sky stone into smooth sky stone.
   > Tip: the Inscriber grinds sky stone into sky dust, which ExtendedAE and AdvancedAE recipes ask for.
3. **All Four Presses**: `ae2:logic_processor_press`; `ae2:calculation_processor_press` *(after: Fallen Stars)*
   > What: the Inscriber has four presses: silicon, logic, calculation and engineering. You need all four for AE2's processors.
   > How: each meteorite's mysterious cube holds one press. Keep finding meteorites with the Meteorite Compass until you have the set.
   > Tip: never use your only copy in a long automation line. Make a spare in the Inscriber with an iron block first (check JEI).
4. **Printed Silicon**: 8x `modern_industrialization:silicon_ingot`; 4x `ae2:printed_silicon` *(after: All Four Presses)*
   > What: printed silicon is the base layer of every AE2 processor.
   > Chemistry: industry makes silicon by heating quartz with carbon to about 2000 °C: SiO₂ + 2C → Si + 2CO. Chips need it purer than 99.9999999%.
   > How: press MI silicon ingots in the Inscriber with the Silicon Press. They come from the Electric Blast Furnace (quartz dust + coke dust).
   > Tip: in this pack certus and sand don't smelt into silicon: carbothermic reduction is the only way, as in the real world.
5. **Logic Processors**: 4x `ae2:printed_logic_processor`; 4x `ae2:logic_processor` *(after: Printed Silicon)*
   > What: logic processors go into cell components, cores, interfaces and much more. You'll want hundreds.
   > Chemistry: gold (Au) barely reacts with air or water, so it never corrodes. Real chips use gold for contacts and bond wires.
   > How: press a gold ingot with the Logic Press, then put printed logic on top, redstone in the middle and printed silicon at the bottom.
   > Tip: one Inscriber per processor type, each fed by pipes, keeps all three in stock.
6. **Calculation Processors**: 4x `ae2:printed_calculation_processor`; 4x `ae2:calculation_processor` *(after: Logic Processors)*
   > What: calculation processors go into crafting units, cards, bigger cell components and wireless parts.
   > Chemistry: a real quartz crystal vibrates at a precise frequency when a voltage drives it. Watches count 32,768 vibrations of quartz a second to keep time.
   > How: press a certus crystal with the Calculation Press, then combine it with redstone and printed silicon like a logic processor.
   > Tip: engineering processors use a diamond the same way. Diamond spreads heat better than any metal, which is why it's used to cool chips.
7. **Quartz Glass and Fiber**: 8x `ae2:quartz_glass`; 3x `ae2:quartz_fiber` *(after: Certus Quartz)*
   > What: quartz glass goes into cell housings and patterns. Quartz Fiber shares power between networks without sharing channels.
   > Chemistry: glass made from pure SiO₂ (fused silica) barely expands when heated. Optical fibre is the same glass, so pure that light travels kilometres inside it.
   > How: quartz dust and glass make quartz glass; glass and quartz dust make fibre (check JEI).
8. **Cell Housings**: 2x `ae2:item_cell_housing`; 2x `ae2:fluid_cell_housing` *(after: Quartz Glass and Fiber)*
   > What: a storage cell is a housing plus a component. Item housings take iron and copper; fluid housings take copper.
   > How: quartz glass, redstone and metal in a crafting table (check JEI). Combine a housing with any component to make the cell.
   > Tip: sneak-use an empty cell in the air to split it back into housing and component, for upgrading to a bigger one.
9. **Annihilation and Formation**: 2x `ae2:annihilation_core`; 2x `ae2:formation_core` *(after: Logic Processors)*
   > What: annihilation cores take things into the network; formation cores put things out. Interfaces, pattern providers, planes and the Molecular Assembler all need both.
   > How: nether quartz (annihilation) or certus (formation), plus fluix dust and a logic processor, two at a time. Grind fluix crystals in the Inscriber for the dust.
   > Tip: make a stack of each. Autocrafting eats them fast.
10. **Upgrade Cards**: 2x `ae2:basic_card`; 2x `ae2:advanced_card`; `ae2:speed_card`; `ae2:capacity_card` *(after: Calculation Processors)*
   > What: Acceleration Cards speed up buses, Inscribers and Molecular Assemblers. Capacity Cards add filter slots. Fuzzy, Inverter, Crafting and Redstone cards change what a part does.
   > How: basic cards from gold, iron, redstone and a calculation processor; advanced cards use a diamond instead. Add fluix for speed or certus for capacity (check JEI).
   > Tip: a Crafting Card on an export bus makes it order missing items from your autocrafting.
11. **Memory Card and Network Tool**: `ae2:memory_card`; `ae2:network_tool` *(after: Calculation Processors)*
   > What: the Memory Card copies a part's settings and filters to another; the Network Tool shows channels and holds spare upgrade cards.
   > How: both use a calculation processor (check JEI). Sneak-use the Memory Card on the source, then use it on the target.
   > Tip: the Memory Card is also how you link P2P tunnels.
12. **Cell Workbench**: `ae2:cell_workbench` *(after: Upgrade Cards)*
   > What: the Cell Workbench sets which items a cell accepts (partitioning) and adds cards to cells.
   > How: wool, iron, a chest and a calculation processor (check JEI).
   > Tip: a cell partitioned to one dust, with a Void Card, keeps its stock without overflowing into your other cells.
13. **Dense Energy Cell**: `ae2:dense_energy_cell` *(after: Feeding the Network)*
   > What: a Dense Energy Cell stores eight times more AE than a normal cell.
   > How: eight Energy Cells around a calculation processor (check JEI). Put it anywhere on the network.
   > Tip: when a network starts flickering during autocrafting, more buffer is usually the cure, not more power input.
14. **Tunnels for Everything**: 2x `ae2:fe_p2p_tunnel`; 2x `ae2:fluid_p2p_tunnel` *(after: P2P Tunnels)*
   > What: P2P tunnels can carry FE, fluids, items, light or redstone instead of channels.
   > How: right-click an ME P2P tunnel with what it should carry, like a bucket or an FE item (check JEI for the full list).
   > Tip: FE tunnels move power through one dense cable instead of a bundle of power lines.
15. **Feeding the Network**: `ae2:energy_acceptor`; `ae2:energy_cell` *(after: AE2 Storage)*
   > What: the ME network turns FE into its own AE energy. The Energy Acceptor converts it; Energy Cells buffer it.
   > How: connect an Energy Acceptor to any FE source (an energy cube, a Powah cell, a Flux Point) and to your cables. Add an Energy Cell next to the controller (check JEI).
   > Tip: a big autocraft can drain the network fast. A Dense Energy Cell keeps it from browning out mid-job.
16. **Growing Certus**: 2x `ae2:growth_accelerator` *(after: Certus Quartz)*
   > What: Growth Accelerators speed up certus quartz buds growing on budding certus blocks.
   > Chemistry: real quartz (SiO₂) crystals grow from silica-rich water over thousands of years. Certus is fictional, but the idea of a seed crystal pulling dissolved material out of solution is real.
   > How: iron, fluix glass cable, quartz glass and a fluix block (check JEI). Place them touching budding certus and power them.
   > Tip: flawless budding certus never decays. Find it in meteorites and never break it with a normal pickaxe.
17. **P2P Tunnels**: 2x `ae2:me_p2p_tunnel` *(after: Cables and Channels)*
   > What: a pair of P2P tunnels carries 32 channels (or items, fluids, FE and redstone) through a single dense cable.
   > How: place both tunnels, then copy the input's settings to the output with a Memory Card (check JEI).
   > Tip: right-click a P2P tunnel with a bucket, a redstone dust or an FE item to change what it carries.
18. **The Matter Condenser**: `ae2:condenser`; `ae2:singularity` *(after: Feeding the Network)*
   > What: the Matter Condenser destroys items. With a 64k component inside, it squeezes them into Matter Balls or a Singularity.
   > How: craft it (check JEI), put a storage component in it, set it to Singularity and feed it cobblestone from a pipe. It takes a lot of items.
   > Tip: singularities unlock MEGA Cells' accumulation processor and every AdvancedAE machine, so start a cobblestone generator early.
19. **Quantum Bridge**: 8x `ae2:quantum_ring`; `ae2:quantum_link` *(after: P2P Tunnels)*
   > What: two Quantum Network Bridges joined by entangled singularities act like one cable, even across dimensions.
   > How: build a 3x3 ring of 8 Quantum Rings around a Quantum Link Chamber at each end, then put one of a pair of entangled singularities in each chamber.
   > Tip: both ends must be chunk-loaded. Use FTB Chunks to force-load them.
20. **Spooky Action**: 2x `ae2:quantum_entangled_singularity` *(after: The Matter Condenser)*
   > You remember being in two places at once. It felt exactly like this.
   > What: you made a pair of Quantum Entangled Singularities by blowing up a singularity with ender pearl dust.
   > Chemistry: real entangled particles share one quantum state: measure one and you know the other, however far apart. Sadly it can't send messages faster than light; AE2 is kinder.
21. **AE2 Storage**: `ae2:drive`; `ae2:terminal` *(after: The God's Archive)*
   > You remember a mind that held every name of every thing. The archive is waking.
   > What: ME Drives hold storage cells; terminals let you see and search everything.
   > How: connect the drive and a terminal to your ME Controller with cables (check JEI).
   > Tip: keep power stable: an Energy Cell buffers the network.
22. **Cables and Channels**: 16x `ae2:fluix_smart_cable`; 4x `ae2:fluix_covered_dense_cable` *(after: AE2 Storage)*
   > What: each ME device uses one channel. Normal cables carry 8 channels, dense cables 32. The controller sends 32 out of each face.
   > How: craft fluix cables, then smart cables (they show channel use as lines) and dense cables (check JEI).
   > Tip: build a dense-cable backbone from the controller and branch normal cables off it. Smart cables show you where channels run out.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Deep dive: if a device's light is off, it has no channel. Count devices on each normal cable (max 8). Drives, terminals, buses and interfaces all count. Plain cables, quartz fibre and energy cells don't.
   > How: the Network Tool (check JEI) shows the channel count of any cable when you right-click it.
23. **Storage Cells**: 2x `ae2:cell_component_1k`; `ae2:item_storage_cell_1k` *(after: AE2 Storage)*
   > What: cells are where the network actually stores things. Bigger components (4k, 16k, 64k, 256k) hold more.
   > Chemistry: certus and fluix are fictional, but the logic processors behind them echo real chips: doped silicon (Si).
   > How: craft components from processors and certus quartz, then put one in a cell housing (check JEI).
24. **Bigger Components**: `ae2:cell_component_16k`; `ae2:cell_component_64k` *(after: Storage Cells)*
   > What: each tier combines three of the last with a calculation processor and quartz glass, holding four times as many bytes.
   > How: 4k from 1k, 16k from 4k, 64k from 16k (check JEI). Put them in housings, or into the Matter Condenser.
   > Tip: a cell holds up to 63 different item types whatever its size, so use small cells for many odd items and big cells for bulk ores and dusts.
25. **Autocrafting**: `ae2:crafting_terminal` *(after: Storage Cells)*
   > What: pattern providers plus molecular assemblers turn whole chemical chains into one click.
   > How: a Crafting Terminal, some crafting storage, and patterns encoded in a Pattern Encoding Terminal (check JEI).
   > Tip: processing patterns can drive MI machines too: send the inputs, wait for the outputs. The Automation and Logic page walks through a full sulfuric acid line.
26. **Wireless Access**: `ae2:wireless_crafting_terminal` *(after: AE2 Storage)*
   > What: reach your ME network from anywhere in range of a Wireless Access Point.
   > How: check JEI. Link the terminal by putting it in the access point, and charge it in the Charger.
   > Tip: put the access point near the middle of your base for the best coverage.
27. **Universal Terminal**: `ae2wtlib:wireless_universal_terminal` *(after: Wireless Access)*
   > What: AE2 Wireless Terminals merges the crafting, pattern access and pattern encoding terminals into one Universal Terminal.
   > How: combine two wireless terminals in a crafting grid (check JEI); add more by crafting them in again.
   > Tip: a Magnet Card from the same mod pulls nearby drops straight into your network. A Quantum Bridge Card works across dimensions.
28. **Infinite Range**: `aeinfinitybooster:infinity_card` *(after: Wireless Access)*
   > What: the Infinity Booster Card removes the Wireless Access Point's range limit within one dimension.
   > How: a Nether Star, wireless boosters, eyes of ender and netherite ingots (check JEI). The star means fighting the Wither first.
   > Tip: put it in the Wireless Access Point, not the terminal.
29. **Across Worlds**: `aeinfinitybooster:dimension_card` *(after: Infinite Range)*
   > What: the Dimension Card lets a Wireless Access Point reach you in any dimension: the Nether, the Twilight Forest, the Moon.
   > How: four Infinity Cards, four Nether Stars and an eye of ender (check JEI).
   > Tip: the access point's chunk must stay loaded while you're away.
30. **ME Requester**: `merequester:requester` *(after: Autocrafting)*
   > What: the ME Requester keeps a set amount of an item in stock by ordering crafts automatically.
   > How: check JEI. Set "keep 64 HDPE" and it never runs out.
   > Tip: it needs autocrafting patterns for whatever it keeps in stock.
31. **Requester Terminal**: `merequester:requester_terminal` *(after: ME Requester)*
   > What: the Requester Terminal lists every ME Requester on the network, so you can edit all your stock rules from one place.
   > How: an illuminated panel, a logic processor and a Requester, shapeless (check JEI).
   > Tip: keep a stock rule for each acid and solvent: H₂SO₄, HCl and HNO₃ are inputs to almost everything late game.
32. **Entro Crystals**: `extendedae:entro_seed`; 8x `extendedae:entro_crystal` *(after: Autocrafting)*
   > What: entro crystals feed every ExtendedAE machine. They grow like certus, from Budding Entroized Fluix.
   > How: craft Entro Seeds (sand, ender dust, redstone, glowstone, sky dust), then right-click a placed Fluix Block with a seed to make it budding. Harvest the clusters.
   > Tip: Growth Accelerators work on budding entro too.
33. **Crystal Assembler**: `extendedae:machine_frame`; `extendedae:crystal_assembler` *(after: Entro Crystals)*
   > What: the Crystal Assembler makes ExtendedAE's blocks from several items (and sometimes a fluid) at once.
   > How: crush entro to dust in the Inscriber, drop it in water with a gold ingot and lapis for an entro ingot, then build a Machine Frame and the Assembler (check JEI).
   > Tip: it accepts pipes and patterns, so the network can drive it like any other machine.
34. **ExtendedAE**: `extendedae:ex_pattern_provider`; `extendedae:ex_drive` *(after: Crystal Assembler)*
   > What: ExtendedAE adds larger versions of AE2 blocks: the Extended Pattern Provider holds many more patterns, the Extended Drive many more cells.
   > How: made in the Crystal Assembler from the normal blocks plus concurrent processors (check JEI).
   > Tip: one extended provider can feed a whole row of chemical reactors.
35. **Wireless Connectors**: 2x `extendedae:wireless_connect` *(after: ExtendedAE)*
   > What: a pair of Wireless Connectors links two parts of your network without a cable between them.
   > How: made two at a time in the Crystal Assembler. Bind them with the Wireless Setup Kit (check JEI).
   > Tip: great for reaching a reactor room behind thick shielding.
36. **Assembler Matrix**: 8x `extendedae:assembler_matrix_frame`; `extendedae:assembler_matrix_crafter`; `extendedae:assembler_matrix_pattern` *(after: ExtendedAE)*
   > What: the Assembler Matrix is a multiblock that replaces walls of molecular assemblers: crafter blocks do the work, pattern blocks hold the patterns.
   > How: build a hollow box of frames and walls (or glass), with crafter, pattern and speed cores inside (check JEI for the rules).
   > Tip: it's for crafting-table recipes only. Processing patterns for MI machines still need pattern providers.
37. **Concurrent Processors**: 4x `extendedae:concurrent_processor` *(after: Crystal Assembler)*
   > What: concurrent processors go into nearly every Extended block: drives, providers, interfaces, inscribers and chargers.
   > How: build the Concurrent Press in the Crystal Assembler (eyes of ender, entro crystals and a Silicon Press), inscribe entro crystals with it, then assemble the prints with printed silicon and redstone (check JEI).
   > Tip: the Crystal Assembler can also make AE2's normal processors from their prints. One machine fed by pipes keeps all of them stocked.
38. **Extended Inscriber and Charger**: `extendedae:ex_inscriber`; `extendedae:ex_charger` *(after: Concurrent Processors)*
   > What: the Extended Inscriber and Extended Charger work on several items in parallel, so processors and charged certus stop being a bottleneck.
   > How: a normal Inscriber or Charger plus capacity cards and a concurrent processor, in the Crystal Assembler (check JEI).
   > Tip: the Circuit Slicer (also in JEI) cuts a whole storage block into nine prints at once: a gold block becomes nine printed logic circuits.
39. **Extended Interface and IO Port**: `extendedae:ex_interface`; `extendedae:ex_io_port` *(after: ExtendedAE)*
   > What: the Extended Interface stocks many more item types than a normal one. The Extended IO Port empties and fills cells far faster than AE2's IO Port.
   > How: both are made in the Crystal Assembler from the normal block plus cards and concurrent processors (check JEI).
   > Tip: an Extended Interface next to an MI machine can hold every input that machine needs, all at once.
40. **Extended Pattern Access**: `extendedae:ex_pattern_access_part`; `extendedae:wireless_ex_pat` *(after: ExtendedAE)*
   > What: the Extended Pattern Access Terminal lists every pattern provider on the network with search and filters. The wireless version works from your pocket.
   > How: a Pattern Access Terminal upgraded in the Crystal Assembler; add a wireless receiver and a dense energy cell for the wireless one (check JEI).
   > Tip: name your pattern providers in an anvil (Sulfuric Acid, Polyethylene) and the terminal groups them by name.
41. **Smarter Buses**: `extendedae:tag_storage_bus`; `extendedae:threshold_level_emitter` *(after: ExtendedAE)*
   > What: the Tag Storage Bus filters by item tag, so one bus can accept every dust or every ingot. The Threshold Level Emitter turns on at one amount and off at another.
   > How: a storage bus or level emitter plus processors, a book or redstone torches, in a crafting table (check JEI).
   > Tip: a threshold emitter on an MI Electrolyzer stops it flickering: on below 10,000 mB of hydrogen, off above 50,000 mB.
42. **MEGA Cells**: 4x `megacells:sky_steel_ingot`; `megacells:item_storage_cell_1m` *(after: Storage Cells)*
   > What: MEGA Cells adds 1M to 256M cells, bulk cells and bigger crafting storage.
   > Chemistry: sky steel is made by dropping charged certus, iron and sky stone into lava: heat drives the alloying, like a tiny smelter.
   > How: throw the ingredients into a lava pool for sky steel, then build the 1M component (check JEI).
43. **Sky Bronze and Sky Osmium**: 4x `megacells:sky_bronze_ingot`; 4x `megacells:sky_osmium_ingot` *(after: MEGA Cells)*
   > What: the same lava trick with copper gives sky bronze, and with osmium gives sky osmium. Both go into MEGA's larger parts.
   > Chemistry: bronze is really copper plus tin (Cu + Sn); here the sky stone plays the tin. Osmium (Os) is the densest natural element, 22.6 g/cm³.
   > How: drop charged certus, the ingot and a sky stone block into lava together. Each throw makes two ingots.
44. **Accumulation Processors**: 4x `megacells:accumulation_processor` *(after: MEGA Cells)*
   > What: the accumulation processor is MEGA's fourth processor, needed for every 1M+ part.
   > How: inscribe a singularity between the calculation and engineering presses to make the Accumulation Press, then print sky steel with it (check JEI).
   > Tip: keep the press. The Inscriber can copy it with an iron block, like the other presses.
45. **MEGA Crafting CPU**: `megacells:1m_crafting_storage`; 4x `megacells:mega_crafting_unit` *(after: Accumulation Processors)*
   > What: MEGA crafting storage and units build a separate, much larger crafting CPU.
   > How: check JEI. MEGA blocks only join other MEGA blocks, so build it as its own multiblock.
   > Tip: the Seed of a New World chain is huge. One big CPU saves splitting the job by hand.
46. **MEGA Pattern Provider**: `megacells:mega_pattern_provider` *(after: MEGA Crafting CPU)*
   > What: a pattern provider with many more pattern slots than the normal one.
   > How: made as a cable part and turned into a block in the crafting grid (check JEI).
   > Tip: put one on each multi-input MI machine, like the Chemical Reactor or the Large Diesel Generator's fuel line.
47. **Bulk Cells**: `megacells:bulk_item_cell`; `megacells:compression_card` *(after: MEGA Crafting CPU)*
   > What: a Bulk Item Cell holds a single item type in near-unlimited amounts. The Compression Card stores nuggets, ingots and blocks as one pool.
   > How: the bulk component needs a 1M component and accumulation processors; the card is an advanced card plus a matter ball (check JEI).
   > Tip: perfect for cobblestone (condenser feed), salt dust or coal coke.
48. **Four Million Bytes**: `megacells:cell_component_4m`; `megacells:mega_item_cell_housing` *(after: Accumulation Processors)*
   > What: MEGA components go up to 256M. They need MEGA cell housings, not AE2's.
   > How: the 4M component is 1M components, accumulation processors, ender dust and vibrant quartz glass (check JEI for the bigger ones).
   > Tip: big cells pay off for bulk stocks like stone dusts and plastics. Keep many small cells for rare items instead.
49. **MEGA Energy**: `megacells:mega_energy_cell`; `megacells:greater_energy_card` *(after: Accumulation Processors)*
   > What: the MEGA Energy Cell is eight dense cells around an accumulation processor. The Greater Energy Card gives portable tools and terminals far more charge.
   > How: both in a crafting table (check JEI). The card is an advanced card plus a MEGA energy cell.
   > Tip: one MEGA cell is plenty for a Quantum Computer's burst of crafting.
50. **Gas in the Network**: `appmek:chemical_storage_cell_1k` *(after: Storage Cells)*
   > What: Applied Mekanistics lets AE2 store and move Mekanism chemicals: H₂, O₂, Cl₂, HCl, SO₂ and the rest.
   > Chemistry: a 1k cell holds a lot of gas because the network stores amounts, not tanks. Real gases need pressure vessels.
   > How: a chemical cell housing (osmium, quartz glass, redstone) + a 1k component. Import buses on chemical tanks fill it.
   > Tip: processing patterns can pull stored SO₂ and O₂ straight from the cell to feed your sulfuric acid line.
51. **A Tank Farm in a Cell**: `appmek:chemical_storage_cell_64k` *(after: Gas in the Network)*
   > What: a 64k chemical cell replaces a room full of chemical tanks.
   > Chemistry: one mole of any ideal gas fills about 22.4 L at 0 °C and 1 atm. Stored as data, it fills nothing at all.
   > How: chemical housing plus a 64k component, or upgrade a smaller cell in the crafting grid (check JEI).
52. **Shielded Storage**: `megacells:radioactive_chemical_cell` *(after: A Tank Farm in a Cell, Fission)*
   > What: normal chemical cells refuse radioactive chemicals. MEGA's Radioactive Chemical Cell holds one, like nuclear waste or plutonium.
   > Chemistry: spent fuel stays dangerous because unstable nuclei keep decaying, giving off α, β and γ radiation for years.
   > How: check JEI for the radioactive component and cell.
   > Tip: a cell never leaks, unlike a broken tank. It's the safest place to keep waste before you reprocess it.
53. **Energy in a Cell**: 4x `appflux:charged_redstone`; `appflux:fe_1k_cell` *(after: Storage Cells)*
   > What: Applied Flux stores FE in AE2 cells and moves it through the network with Flux Accessors.
   > How: redstone crystal (redstone block, fluix and glowstone dropped in water) → charge it in the AE2 Charger → FE cell core and housing (check JEI).
   > Tip: the housing needs insulating resin, which needs silicon: a little chemistry even here.
54. **Flux Accessor**: `appflux:flux_accessor`; `appflux:induction_card` *(after: Energy in a Cell)*
   > What: a Flux Accessor pushes FE from your FE cells into any machine it touches. An Induction Card lets an I/O bus or interface do the same.
   > How: an energy acceptor, energy processors (iron block charged into the Energy Press, then inscribed), copper and glowstone (check JEI).
   > Tip: one FE cell plus accessors can replace a tangle of power cables around a dense machine room.
55. **Reaction Chamber**: `advanced_ae:reaction_chamber`; 2x `advanced_ae:shattered_singularity` *(after: The Matter Condenser)*
   > What: AdvancedAE's Reaction Chamber combines items and a fluid with lots of energy. Its first job: shattering singularities.
   > How: a matter condenser, a vibration chamber, fluix dust, glowstone and a bucket (check JEI). Feed it a singularity, ender dust, sky dust and lava.
   > Tip: it uses a lot of power per craft. Put it on its own Energy Acceptor.
56. **Quantum Alloy**: 4x `advanced_ae:quantum_alloy` *(after: Reaction Chamber)*
   > What: quantum alloy is AdvancedAE's top material, for the quantum computer and gear.
   > How: press a shattered singularity into quantum-infused dust, react it with water into Quantum Infusion, then react that with copper ingots, singularities and shattered singularities (check JEI).
   > Chemistry: copper (Cu) is the base for a reason: after silver it's the best electrical conductor of any metal.
57. **Directional Providers**: `advanced_ae:adv_pattern_provider` *(after: ExtendedAE)*
   > What: the Advanced Pattern Provider lets a processing pattern send each input to a chosen side of the machine.
   > How: an Extended Pattern Provider, a logic processor, an ender pearl and redstone (check JEI). Encode patterns in the Advanced Pattern Encoder.
   > Tip: ideal for machines with separate input faces, like a Mekanism machine that takes gas on one side and items on another.
58. **Quantum Computer**: `advanced_ae:quantum_core`; 8x `advanced_ae:quantum_structure`; `advanced_ae:quantum_multi_threader` *(after: Quantum Alloy)*
   > You remember thinking a thousand thoughts at once. The machine remembers how, too.
   > What: the Quantum Computer is a multiblock crafting CPU: huge storage, many parallel jobs, and accelerators that multiply speed.
   > How: a Quantum Core inside a shell of Quantum Structure blocks, with multi-threaders, accelerators and storage blocks (check JEI for size limits).
   > Tip: build it next to your main pattern providers so every chemical line can run at once.
59. **Quantum Processors**: 4x `advanced_ae:quantum_processor` *(after: Quantum Alloy)*
   > What: quantum processors go into the Quantum Computer's parts, quantum gear and AdvancedAE's best buses.
   > How: press a shattered singularity between the logic and engineering presses for the Quantum Press. Inscribe quantum alloy with it, then add redstone and printed silicon (check JEI).
   > Tip: copy the Quantum Press before you use it in automation, like the other presses.
60. **Quantum Armour**: `advanced_ae:quantum_helmet`; `advanced_ae:quantum_chestplate`; `advanced_ae:quantum_leggings`; `advanced_ae:quantum_boots` *(after: Quantum Processors)*
   > What: quantum armour is netherite armour rebuilt around quantum processors, with slots for AdvancedAE's armour cards.
   > How: each piece needs its netherite piece, quantum alloy plates, quantum processors and a quantum storage component (check JEI).
   > Tip: cards like Magnet, Night Vision and Step Assist are built on the Quantum Upgrade Base. Flight in this pack comes from chemistry (pylons, jetpacks, the Angel Ring), not from AE2.
61. **Import and Export Cards**: `ae2importexportcard:import_card`; `ae2importexportcard:export_card` *(after: Wireless Access)*
   > What: these cards go in a wireless terminal. The Import Card pushes chosen items from your inventory into the network; the Export Card keeps chosen items stocked in your inventory.
   > How: an import (or export) bus, redstone blocks, an advanced card and processors (check JEI).
   > Tip: set the Import Card to cobblestone, dirt and raw ores, and mining trips never fill your inventory.
62. **Packaged Extended Crafting**: `packagedexcrafting:basic_crafter` *(after: Packaged Automation, Crystaltine)*
   > What: Packaged ExCrafting adds crafters that run Extended Crafting recipes from packages: one for each table size, plus combination and ender crafting.
   > How: an auto table of the right size, an ME package component, crystaltine components, black iron and a redstone catalyst (check JEI).
   > Tip: encode the recipe in the Packaged Auto encoder, just like normal packages.
63. **The Ultimate Crafter**: `packagedexcrafting:ultimate_crafter` *(after: Packaged Extended Crafting, 9x9: Ultimate Table)*
   > What: the Ultimate Crafter runs 9x9 Ultimate Table recipes automatically from the network.
   > How: same recipe as the basic crafter, with an Ultimate Auto Table in the middle (check JEI).
   > Tip: the Seed of a New World is a 9x9 recipe. Feed it from the network and the capstone crafts itself once its ingredients exist.
64. **Co-Processors**: 4x `ae2:crafting_accelerator`; `ae2:crafting_monitor` *(after: Crafting CPU)*
   > What: each Crafting Co-Processing Unit lets a CPU run one more step at the same time. The Crafting Monitor shows what the CPU is making.
   > How: a crafting unit plus an engineering processor makes a co-processor; a crafting unit plus a storage monitor makes the monitor (check JEI).
   > Tip: co-processors only help if the machines can keep up. Ten acid patterns on one Chemical Reactor still run one at a time.
65. **A Bigger Plan**: 2x `ae2:16k_crafting_storage`; `ae2:64k_crafting_storage` *(after: Co-Processors)*
   > What: crafting storage limits how big a job a CPU can plan. Long chemical chains need far more than 1k.
   > How: a crafting unit plus a 16k or 64k cell component (check JEI). Add them to the CPU's solid box.
   > Tip: build two CPUs instead of one huge one, so a long job doesn't block a quick request.
66. **ME Interfaces**: 2x `ae2:interface` *(after: Crafting CPU)*
   > What: an interface keeps chosen items stocked in itself for pipes and machines to pull. A storage bus on an interface lets one network see into another.
   > How: iron, glass, an annihilation core and a formation core (check JEI). Set the items to keep in its top row.
   > Tip: a subnetwork for one chemical line, joined to the main network through an interface, keeps channels free.
67. **Pattern Access Terminal**: `ae2:pattern_access_terminal` *(after: ME Interfaces)*
   > What: the Pattern Access Terminal shows the patterns in every pattern provider, so you can add or swap them without walking to each machine.
   > How: an illuminated panel, an engineering processor and a pattern provider, shapeless (check JEI).
   > Tip: one terminal next to your Pattern Encoding Terminal makes a tidy crafting desk.
68. **Charged Certus**: `ae2:charger`; 8x `ae2:charged_certus_quartz_crystal` *(after: Certus Quartz)*
   > What: the Charger puts energy into certus crystals. Charged certus is the key to fluix, crystal growth and many AE2 recipes.
   > Chemistry: real quartz is piezoelectric: squeeze it and it makes a voltage, push a voltage into it and it flexes. AE2 imagines it can store the charge.
   > How: the Charger is iron and copper ingots (check JEI). Power it with FE and put certus crystals in.
   > Tip: a Crank on top of the Charger works too, slowly, if your power isn't up yet.
69. **Fluix**: 8x `ae2:fluix_crystal`; 4x `ae2:fluix_dust`; `ae2:fluix_block` *(after: Charged Certus)*
   > What: fluix crystals carry AE2's channels: every cable, core and most parts need fluix.
   > Chemistry: a reaction in solution: charged certus, nether quartz and redstone dropped together in water fuse into fluix. Real crystals also grow fastest from a seed in solution.
   > How: throw charged certus, nether quartz and redstone into a water block: you get two fluix crystals. Grind fluix in the Inscriber for dust; four crystals make a block.
