   > What: the Salvaging Table breaks affixed gear into materials of its rarity.
   > How: a smithing table, iron tools, copper, a lava bucket and gem dust (check JEI).
   > Tip: every affixed sword you don't want is a reforge for one you do.
4. **Gem Cutting**: `apotheosis:gem_cutting_table` *(after: Salvaging)*
   > What: the Gem Cutting Table upgrades gems to higher purity using matching gems and dust.
   > Chemistry: real gems are cut along cleavage planes, flat directions where the crystal's bonds are weakest.
   > How: planks, smooth stone, shears and gem dust.
5. **Divine Reforging**: `apotheosis:reforging_table` *(after: Gem Cutting, Into the Fire)*
   > You remember weapons that chose their wielders. These at least choose good affixes.
   > What: the full Reforging Table handles every rarity, up to mythic gear.
   > How: the Simple Reforging Table, netherite, nether bricks and arcane sands (check JEI).
6. **Better Bookshelves**: 4x `apothic_enchanting:hellshelf` *(after: Gem Dust, Into the Fire)*
   > What: Apothic Enchanting adds shelves that raise enchanting power, quanta and arcana. Hellshelves are the first step.
   > How: bookshelves, nether bricks and a blaze rod. Create: Enchantment Industry can automate enchanting later.
   > Tip: enchanting power above 30 unlocks enchantments beyond vanilla levels.
7. **Sigil of Socketing**: `apotheosis:sigil_of_socketing` *(after: Gem Cutting)*
   > What: adds a socket to gear in a smithing table, so you can slot in a gem.
   > How: gem-fused slate, amethyst, gunpowder and gem dust (check JEI).
   > Tip: a Sigil of Withdrawal pulls gems back out later.
8. **Augmenting**: `apotheosis:augmenting_table` *(after: Divine Reforging)*
   > What: the Augmenting Table improves or rerolls one affix at a time.
   > How: an enchanting table, a Nether Star, a godforged pearl and polished blackstone (check JEI).
   > Tip: save it for gear you plan to keep for the rest of the game.
9. **Bottled Monsters**: `minecraft:spawner` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: with Apothic Spawners a monster spawner can be picked up with a Silk Touch pickaxe and moved home.
   > How: find one in a dungeon or mineshaft, light it up, then mine it with Silk Touch. Check its tooltip after placing.
   > Tip: spawners are mob farms for drops you can't make chemically: bones, string, ender pearls, blaze rods.
10. **Spawner Runes**: 1x any of `or(item(apotheosis:spawner_rune)item(apotheosis:burning_spawner_rune)item(apotheosis:redstone_control_spawner_rune)item(apotheosis:ignore_players_spawner_rune)item(apotheosis:silent_spawner_rune)item(apotheosis:youthful_spawner_rune))` *(after: Bottled Monsters, Gem Dust)*
   > What: spawner runes change a spawner when you right-click it: spawn without players nearby, obey redstone, set mobs on fire, stay silent, and more.
   > How: a basic Spawner Rune is gem dust, gem-fused slate and spawner chains (check JEI for where chains come from). Each modifier rune adds one item, like campfires for Burning.
   > Tip: Redstone Control first, so you can switch the farm off when you don't need it.
11. **Elite Hunting**: kill 50x `minecraft:zombie` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: Apotheosis gives some monsters affixed gear and makes rare elites with a coloured name. Their drops can roll affixes and sockets.
   > How: kill 50 zombies. Pick up any named or glowing item they drop and read its tooltip.
   > Tip: elites hit hard. Gear up before poking one with a stick.
12. **Potion Charm**: `apotheosis:potion_charm` *(after: Gem Dust, The Brewer's Art)*
   > What: a Potion Charm holds a potion effect and applies it while switched on, using durability.
   > Chemistry: blaze powder is a reactive powder; here it fixes the potion so it lasts, a bit like a preservative.
   > How: three identical potions in the middle row and six blaze powder around them. Infusing it later makes it permanent (check JEI).
   > Tip: Night Vision or Haste charms are the most useful early.
13. **Rarity Materials**: 4x `apotheosis:luminous_crystal_shard` *(after: Salvaging)*
   > What: each rarity salvages into its own material: common scrap metal, uncommon timeworn fabric, rare luminous crystal, epic arcane sands, mythic godforged pearls.
   > How: salvage rare (blue) gear in the Salvaging Table until you have 4 luminous crystal shards.
   > Tip: reforging uses the material of that rarity, so sort your loot by colour before salvaging.
14. **Gate Pearl**: `gateways:gate_pearl` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: a Gate Pearl opens a Gateway that releases waves of a chosen mob. Beat every wave for rewards.
   > How: the Blaze gate is five blaze rods, an ender pearl and three nether bricks. Apotheosis adds tiered gates (Frontier and up); JEI shows them all.
   > Tip: a gate is a controlled mob farm: blaze rods, ender pearls and XP on demand.
15. **Close a Gateway**: checkmark *(after: Gate Pearl)*
   > What: the gateway closes when every wave is defeated and pays out its reward.
   > How: throw the pearl in an open area, stay close (leaving fails the gate) and kill each wave. Click the checkmark when it closes.
   > Tip: tiered Apotheosis gates hand out affix gear and rarity materials.
16. **Sigil of Withdrawal**: `apotheosis:sigil_of_withdrawal` *(after: Sigil of Socketing)*
   > What: pulls every gem out of an item without destroying them, so a good gem can move to new gear.
   > How: gem-fused slate, blaze rods, ender pearls, a lava bucket and gem dust (makes 4).
   > Tip: withdraw gems before salvaging or reforging old gear.
17. **Sigil of Enhancement**: `apotheosis:sigil_of_enhancement` *(after: Divine Reforging)*
   > What: upgrades a socketed gem to the next rarity at the Reforging Table.
   > How: gem-fused slate, gem dust and a godforged pearl (makes 4). Godforged pearls come from salvaging mythic gear.
   > Tip: save these for gems you'll keep: a mythic gem in endgame gear is worth it.
18. **Infusion**: `apothic_enchanting:infused_hellshelf` *(after: Better Bookshelves)*
   > What: Apothic Enchanting can 'infuse' items: enchanting a hellshelf at the right power makes an Infused Hellshelf.
   > How: put a hellshelf in the enchanting table with enough shelves around it. JEI's infusion page shows the exact Eterna, Quanta and Arcana it needs.
   > Tip: the table's three stats are shown on the screen: power, randomness and how many extra enchantments you get.
19. **Enchantment Library**: `apothic_enchanting:library` *(after: Infusion)*
   > What: the Library absorbs enchanted books and stores their enchantments as points, then pulls out any level you've collected.
   > How: four ender chests, four infused shelves and an enchanting table.
   > Tip: it only gives back levels up to the highest single book you fed it, so feed it every spare book.
20. **Endshelves**: 4x `apothic_enchanting:endshelf` *(after: Infusion, The End)*
   > What: endshelves push enchanting power past what hellshelves and seashelves allow.
   > How: end stone bricks, a bookshelf, an ender pearl and Infused Breath (dragon's breath infused at the enchanting table).
   > Tip: collect dragon's breath in glass bottles during the Ender Dragon fight.
21. **Scrap Tome**: `apothic_enchanting:scrap_tome` *(after: Better Bookshelves)*
   > What: a Scrap Tome in an anvil with enchanted gear strips off some of its enchantments into a book (the gear is destroyed).
   > How: eight books around an anvil makes eight tomes.
   > Tip: the Extraction Tome (infused) keeps the item; check JEI's infusion page.
22. **Gem-Fused Slate**: 8x `apotheosis:gem_fused_slate` *(after: Gem Dust)*
   > What: gem-fused slate is the backing for sigils and spawner runes.
   > Chemistry: deepslate is metamorphic rock: older stone squeezed and heated deep underground until its minerals recrystallised.
   > How: 8 deepslate around 1 gem dust makes 8.
23. **Working Sigils**: 1x any of `or(item(apotheosis:sigil_of_rebirth)item(apotheosis:sigil_of_unnaming))` *(after: Gem-Fused Slate)*
   > What: the Sigil of Rebirth fuels the Reforging Table; the Sigil of Unnaming removes an item's affix name.
   > How: Rebirth: 6 slate around 3 gem dust. Unnaming: 6 slate around 3 flint. Each makes 6.
   > Tip: the rarer sigils (Malice, Supremacy) come from Gateways, not the crafting grid.
24. **Gem Case**: `apotheosis:gem_case` *(after: Gem Cutting)*
   > What: a cabinet that stores gems by type and purity and can combine two of a kind into the next purity.
   > Chemistry: a ruby is corundum (Al₂O₃) with about 1% chromium. Less chromium and it's a pink sapphire.
   > How: glass on top, basalt around a Gem Cutting Table, and an ender chest below.
   > Tip: infused at the enchanting table it becomes the Gem Case of House Fabergé, which keeps the gems inside.
25. **House Fabergé**: `apotheosis:ender_gem_case` *(after: Gem Case, Infusion)*
   > What: the infused Gem Case. It keeps everything stored in the old one.
   > How: infuse a Gem Case at an enchanting table with very high stats (JEI's infusion page: 100 Eterna and Quanta).
   > Tip: you'll need endshelves or deepshelves to reach those numbers.
26. **Every Rarity**: `apotheosis:mysterious_scrap_metal`; `apotheosis:timeworn_fabric`; `apotheosis:arcane_sands`; `apotheosis:godforged_pearl` *(after: Rarity Materials)*
   > What: one material of each other rarity: common scrap metal, uncommon timeworn fabric, epic arcane sands and a mythic godforged pearl.
   > How: salvage gear of each colour. The pearl only comes from mythic gear: tiered Gateways and the toughest elites.
   > Tip: Divine Reforging, upgrade runes and the strongest sigils all spend these.
27. **God-Fused Pearl**: `apotheosis:god_fused_pearl` *(after: Every Rarity, Infusion)*
   > You remember something like this sitting in your crown. It was warmer then.
   > What: a godforged pearl infused at a maxed-out enchanting table, used for the Raven's table.
   > How: an enchanting table at 100 Eterna, about 59 Arcana and 10 Quanta (JEI's infusion page has the exact window).
28. **Enchanting Table of the Raven**: `apothic_enchanting:raven_enchanting_table` *(after: God-Fused Pearl)*
   > What: an enchanting table where you set the core stats by hand instead of building shelves.
   > How: an Apothic enchanting table, 2 god-fused pearls, 3 obsidian and a perfect Royalty gem (check JEI).
   > Tip: a late luxury: a good shelf room already does most of this.
29. **Spawner Chains**: `apotheosis:spawner_chain` *(after: Bottled Monsters)*
   > What: spawner chains are the binding for spawner runes. They only come from a monster spawner destroyed by an explosion.
   > Chemistry: TNT (C₇H₅N₃O₆) carries its own oxygen in its nitro groups, so it burns in microseconds and makes a shock wave.
   > How: find a spawner you don't want to keep and blow it up with TNT. Pick up the chains.
   > Tip: keep the good spawners: Silk Touch them home instead.
30. **Stranger Runes**: 1x any of `or(item(apotheosis:ignore_light_spawner_rune)item(apotheosis:ignore_conditions_spawner_rune)item(apotheosis:initial_health_spawner_rune)item(apotheosis:no_ai_spawner_rune)item(apotheosis:spawn_range_spawner_rune)item(apotheosis:echoing_spawner_rune)item(apotheosis:infused_spawner_rune))` *(after: Spawner Runes, Spawner Chains)*
   > What: more runes: spawn in daylight, ignore spawn conditions, weaken mobs, freeze their AI, change the range. Some need an Infused Spawner Rune.
   > How: a basic Spawner Rune plus the rune's item (Perpetual Twilight: 4 soul lanterns). The infused rune is a spawner rune infused at the table, or ringed with gem dust and bottles o' enchanting.
   > Tip: Stupor (no AI) makes a mob farm that can't fight back.
31. **Spawner Upgrade Runes**: 1x any of `or(item(apotheosis:frontier_spawner_upgrade_rune)item(apotheosis:ascent_spawner_upgrade_rune)item(apotheosis:summit_spawner_upgrade_rune)item(apotheosis:pinnacle_spawner_upgrade_rune))` *(after: Spawner Runes, Rarity Materials)*
   > What: four tiers of upgrade rune, from Frontiersman's (slightly better) to Thundering (the maximum).
   > How: Frontiersman's: a spawner rune with timeworn fabric, clocks and flint. Higher tiers use rarer materials; Thundering needs godforged pearls and a Nether Star.
   > Tip: save Nether Stars: the Seed of a New World needs them too.
32. **Curious Shelves**: 1x any of `or(item(apothic_enchanting:stoneshelf)item(apothic_enchanting:beeshelf)item(apothic_enchanting:melonshelf)item(apothic_enchanting:geode_shelf)item(apothic_enchanting:basic_bookshelf))` *(after: Better Bookshelves)*
   > What: the Stoneshelf, Beeshelf, Melonshelf, Geode shelf and Basic Bookshelf each nudge the table's stats in an odd direction.
   > Chemistry: a geode's calcite rind is CaCO₃, the same compound as chalk and limestone.
   > How: Stoneshelf: polished andesite and books. Geode shelf: calcite around a bookshelf and a budding amethyst. JEI has the rest.
   > Tip: every shelf's tooltip lists its Eterna, Quanta and Arcana: read them before you build.
33. **Hellshelf Upgrades**: 1x any of `or(item(apothic_enchanting:blazing_hellshelf)item(apothic_enchanting:glowing_hellshelf)item(apothic_enchanting:sightshelf)item(apothic_enchanting:sightshelf_t2))` *(after: Infusion)*
   > What: the Infused Hellshelf upgrades into Blazing (fire charges), Glowing (glowstone) or the Hellshelf of Sight, which shows more enchantment clues.
   > How: an Infused Hellshelf in the grid with the upgrade items (check JEI). Masterful Sight needs netherite and emerald blocks.
   > Tip: one Sightshelf shows much more of what the table will roll.
34. **Seashelves**: 4x `apothic_enchanting:seashelf` *(after: Better Bookshelves)*
   > What: seashelves are the second shelf family, with different stats from hellshelves.
   > Chemistry: sea water is about 3.5% dissolved salts, mostly NaCl with magnesium and sulfate ions.
   > How: prismarine bricks, a bookshelf, a water bottle and a pufferfish.
35. **Seashelf Upgrades**: 1x any of `or(item(apothic_enchanting:infused_seashelf)item(apothic_enchanting:crystal_seashelf)item(apothic_enchanting:heart_seashelf)item(apothic_enchanting:filtering_shelf))` *(after: Seashelves, Infusion)*
   > What: an Infused Seashelf, then Crystalline, Heart-Forged or the Seashelf of Aquatic Filtration, which keeps chosen enchantments out of the pool.
   > How: infuse a seashelf at the table, then craft it with prismarine crystals, a heart of the sea, or prismarine bricks and slabs (check JEI).
   > Tip: the filtering shelf is how you stop a table rolling the enchantment you never want.
36. **Deepshelves**: `apothic_enchanting:dormant_deepshelf`; `apothic_enchanting:deepshelf` *(after: Infusion)*
   > What: the deepshelf family pushes the stats high. It starts dormant and wakes with infusion.
   > How: Dormant Deepshelf: cracked deepslate tiles and books. Infuse it at the table to wake it.
   > Tip: upgrade it with echo shards or soul lanterns; the Deepshelf of Arcane Treasures allows treasure enchantments.
37. **Deepshelf Upgrades**: 1x any of `or(item(apothic_enchanting:echoing_deepshelf)item(apothic_enchanting:soul_touched_deepshelf)item(apothic_enchanting:treasure_shelf))` *(after: Deepshelves)*
   > What: Echoing and Soul-Touched deepshelves raise the stats further; the treasure shelf lets the table roll treasure enchantments.
   > How: a Deepshelf with an echo shard and candles, or a soul lantern and sculk. Treasure: 2 deepshelves, gold blocks, diamonds and an emerald block.
   > Tip: echo shards come from Ancient City chests.
38. **Sculkshelves**: `apothic_enchanting:warden_tendril`; 1x any of `or(item(apothic_enchanting:echoing_sculkshelf)item(apothic_enchanting:soul_touched_sculkshelf))` *(after: Deepshelf Upgrades)*
   > What: the strongest deepshelves need a Warden Tendril, which drops from a Warden.
   > How: kill a Warden (Ancient City; don't make a sound), then craft the tendril over an upgraded deepshelf with sculk and a sculk catalyst.
   > Tip: a Warden has 500 health and its sonic boom ignores armor. Plan the fight, or plan the escape.
39. **Endshelf Upgrades**: `apothic_enchanting:infused_breath`; 1x any of `or(item(apothic_enchanting:pearl_endshelf)item(apothic_enchanting:draconic_endshelf))` *(after: Endshelves)*
   > What: the top of the shelf ladder. The Pearlescent Endshelf adds end rods; the Draconic one is crowned with a dragon head.
   > How: infuse dragon's breath for Infused Breath (3 per bottle), then craft an Endshelf with end rods and ender pearls, or a dragon head and pearls.
   > Tip: dragon heads hang on End Ship bows. Bring the elytra home too.
40. **Better Tomes**: 1x any of `or(item(apothic_enchanting:other_tome)item(apothic_enchanting:improved_scrap_tome)item(apothic_enchanting:extraction_tome))` *(after: Scrap Tome, Infusion)*
   > What: the Tome of the Others enchants like a tool no other tome covers; Superior Scrapping and Extraction strip enchantments more gently (Extraction keeps the item).
   > How: Tome of the Others: 6 books and a blaze rod (makes 6). Infuse a Scrap Tome for Superior Scrapping, and that for Extraction.
   > Tip: Extraction tomes are the cleanest way to move a good enchantment to new gear.
41. **Library of Alexandria**: `apothic_enchanting:ender_library` *(after: Enchantment Library)*
   > What: the infused Enchantment Library stores more and gives back higher levels.
   > How: infuse an Enchantment Library at the enchanting table; it keeps the enchantments already inside (check JEI for the stats).
   > Tip: the real Library of Alexandria burned; keep this one away from your blaze farm.
42. **Ender Leads**: 1x any of `or(item(apothic_enchanting:flimsy_ender_lead)item(apothic_enchanting:ender_lead)item(apothic_enchanting:occult_ender_lead))` *(after: Better Bookshelves)*
   > What: the Flimsy Ender Lead captures animals; the infused Ender Lead captures most mobs; the Occult one can bind a mob to a spawner.
   > How: flimsy: an ender pearl, a lead and a gold ingot (shapeless). Infuse it for the Ender Lead; infuse that holding a witch for the Occult lead.
   > Tip: the easy way to move a villager across the world.
43. **Inert Trident**: `apothic_enchanting:inert_trident` *(after: Infusion)*
   > What: an inert trident infuses into a real trident at the enchanting table.
   > How: 3 nautilus shells, a heart of the sea and an iron ingot. Then infuse it (check JEI for the stats).
   > Tip: a Channeling trident in a thunderstorm calls lightning where it lands.

### Relics and Artifacts

*Found treasures and crafted curios: Relics, Artifacts and Reliquary.*

1. **Relics**: `reliquary:mob_charm_fragment` *(after: Iron)*
   > You remember a treasury. Most of it is scattered now, in chests and in the hands of monsters.
   > What: three mods of found and crafted treasures. Reliquary items are crafted from mob parts; Relics and Artifacts hide in chests and structures.
   > How: mob charm fragments drop from mobs. JEI shows the charm they build.
   > Tip: a Mob Charm stops that mob type attacking you.
2. **Alkahestry Tome**: `reliquary:alkahestry_tome` *(after: Relics)*
   > What: charged with redstone, the tome duplicates common items in a crafting grid.
   > Chemistry: alchemists searched for alkahest, a universal solvent. None exists (what would you keep it in?), but aqua regia, HCl + HNO₃, dissolves even gold.
   > How: check JEI for the tome and its recipes. Recharge it with redstone.
3. **Relic Hunter**: checkmark *(after: Relics)*
   > What: find any Relics or Artifacts item: a cloud in a bottle, running shoes, a leafy mantle, a mimic's treasure.
   > How: loot chests in dungeons, mineshafts and towers, and beware chests that bite. Click the checkmark when you have one.
   > Tip: Relics items level up as you use them; check their tooltips.
4. **Fortune Coin**: `reliquary:fortune_coin` *(after: Alkahestry Tome)*
   > What: pulls nearby items and XP toward you while active.
   > How: check JEI. Right-click to toggle it.
   > Tip: turn it off near your sorting system or it'll grab the items.
5. **A True Relic**: 1x any of `or(item(relics:chorus_staff)item(relics:experience_disperser)item(relics:ghostly_mantle)item(relics:glitchy_mantle)item(relics:hunting_belt)item(relics:jellyfish_necklace)item(relics:kinetic_belt)item(relics:leafy_mantle)item(relics:midnight_mantle)item(relics:pet_bone)item(relics:piglin_mask)item(relics:reflective_necklace)item(relics:rider_flute)item(relics:ring_of_the_seven_deadly_sins)item(relics:roller_skate)item(relics:shield_of_retaliation)item(relics:sphere_of_self_sacrifice)item(relics:springy_boot)item(relics:chef_hat)item(relics:clot_of_time)item(relics:cut_glass_boot))` *(after: Iron)*
   > You remember owning things no mortal smith made. A few of them seem to have survived.
   > What: Relics are found, never crafted: mantles, belts, necklaces, boots, a chef's hat, a ring of the seven deadly sins. Each has abilities that grow with use.
   > How: loot chests in dungeons, mineshafts, temples, villages and modded structures. Any one relic completes this quest.
   > Tip: read the tooltip: each relic says what it does and how it gains experience.
6. **Relic Growth**: checkmark *(after: A True Relic)*
   > What: relics earn experience when you use their abilities, and their levels make those abilities stronger.
   > How: keep the relic equipped and use it. Open its ability screen (the tooltip names the key) to spend levels. Click the checkmark after your first upgrade.
   > Tip: one well-levelled relic beats a drawer full of new ones.
7. **An Artifact**: 1x any of `or(item(artifacts:anglers_hat)item(artifacts:antidote_vessel)item(artifacts:aqua_dashers)item(artifacts:bunny_hoppers)item(artifacts:charm_of_shrinking)item(artifacts:charm_of_sinking)item(artifacts:chorus_totem)item(artifacts:cloud_in_a_bottle)item(artifacts:cowboy_hat)item(artifacts:cross_necklace)item(artifacts:crystal_heart)item(artifacts:digging_claws)item(artifacts:eternal_steak)item(artifacts:everlasting_beef)item(artifacts:feral_claws)item(artifacts:fire_gauntlet)item(artifacts:flame_pendant)item(artifacts:flippers)item(artifacts:golden_hook)item(artifacts:helium_flamingo)item(artifacts:kitty_slippers)item(artifacts:lucky_scarf)item(artifacts:night_vision_goggles)item(artifacts:novelty_drinking_hat)item(artifacts:obsidian_skull)item(artifacts:onion_ring)item(artifacts:panic_necklace)item(artifacts:pickaxe_heater)item(artifacts:plastic_drinking_hat)item(artifacts:pocket_piston)item(artifacts:power_glove)item(artifacts:rooted_boots)item(artifacts:running_shoes)item(artifacts:scarf_of_invisibility)item(artifacts:shock_pendant)item(artifacts:snorkel)item(artifacts:snowshoes)item(artifacts:steadfast_spikes)item(artifacts:strider_shoes)item(artifacts:superstitious_hat)item(artifacts:thorn_pendant)item(artifacts:umbrella)item(artifacts:universal_attractor)item(artifacts:vampiric_glove)item(artifacts:villager_hat)item(artifacts:warp_drive)item(artifacts:whoopee_cushion)item(artifacts:withered_bracelet))` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: Artifacts are simple, always-on curios: Running Shoes, Cloud in a Bottle, Digging Claws, a Lucky Scarf, Night Vision Goggles and many more.
   > How: found in chests underground and in structures, and dropped by Mimics. Any one artifact completes this quest.
   > Tip: a Cloud in a Bottle (double jump) and Running Shoes make early exploring much easier.
8. **That Chest Has Teeth**: kill 1x `artifacts:mimic` *(after: An Artifact)*
   > What: a Mimic looks exactly like a chest until you open it. It always drops an artifact.
   > How: they hide in mineshafts, dungeons and caves. If a chest stands somewhere odd, hit it before opening it.
   > Tip: Mimics are tough for their size; fight one with real armor, not a wooden sword.
9. **Divine Comedy**: `artifacts:whoopee_cushion` *(after: An Artifact)*
   > You remember the other gods laughing at something like this. You never admitted it was you.
   > What: the Whoopee Cushion. Equip it and crouch.
   > Tip: it does exactly what you think.
10. **Mob Ingredients**: 2x `reliquary:zombie_heart` *(after: Relics)*
   > What: Reliquary items are built from rare mob parts: zombie hearts, rib bones, catalyzing glands, slime pearls, molten cores and more.
   > How: they drop from their mobs (zombies drop zombie hearts). In this pack they can also be crafted: a zombie heart is rotten flesh in a ring of iron ingots.
   > Tip: a Looting sword makes the drops much more common than the iron recipe.
11. **Mob Charm Belt**: `reliquary:mob_charm_belt` *(after: Mob Ingredients)*
   > What: the belt holds Mob Charms, so you can be ignored by several mob types at once.
   > How: three leather and five mob charm fragments (check JEI). Each fragment is made from that mob's drops.
   > Tip: creeper and enderman charms are the most valuable around a base.
12. **Void Tear**: `reliquary:void_tear` *(after: Mob Ingredients, Ghast Tears)*
   > What: a Void Tear stores a huge stack of one item, and pulls more of it from your inventory.
   > How: a ghast tear, a nebulous heart, a slime pearl and lapis (shapeless).
   > Tip: it's also an ingredient for the Infernal Tear, Emperor's Chalice and Midas Touchstone.
13. **Lantern of Paranoia**: `reliquary:lantern_of_paranoia` *(after: Mob Ingredients)*
   > What: the lantern places torches from your inventory wherever it's dark enough for mobs to spawn.
   > How: iron ingots, glass, a slime pearl and a molten core (check JEI).
   > Tip: carry a stack of torches when caving and let it do the lighting.
14. **The Handgun**: `reliquary:handgun` *(after: Mob Ingredients)*
   > What: a pistol that fires magazines of special bullets: neutral, exorcism, blaze, ender, storm, seeker and more.
   > How: barrel, grip and hammer assemblies plus iron and a slime pearl. Bullets and magazines have their own recipes (check JEI).
   > Tip: Seeker bullets home in on targets; good against flying mobs.
15. **Phoenix Down**: `reliquary:phoenix_down` *(after: Mob Ingredients, Into the Fire)*
   > What: saves you from death, heals you, and gives you a few seconds of protection. It has several charges.
   > How: three Angelheart Vials and an Angelic Feather. Vials need milk, glass, fertile essence and an infernal claw (check JEI).
   > Tip: keep it in your inventory before boss fights and Nether trips.
16. **Gold Teeth**: 9x `relics:golden_tooth` *(after: Relic Growth)*
   > What: with the Piglin Mask's looting ability, kills drop golden teeth: bigger mobs, more teeth. Picking them up can also fire up its frenzy rank.
   > Chemistry: gold crowns last because gold barely reacts with anything in your mouth: it is the least reactive metal of all.
   > How: find a Piglin Mask, level its looting ability and fight. Three teeth craft into a gold ingot, or trade them to piglins.
   > Tip: it's mob-drop gold, like a zombified piglin farm: handy, but not ore.

### Equivalent Exchange

*A builder's toy for a demigod who has already mastered the elements.*

1. **The Philosopher's Stone**: `projecte:philosophers_stone` *(after: The Complete Periodic Table)*
   > You remember turning one thing into another with a thought. Now you know what it really costs.
   > What: the Philosopher's Stone transmutes blocks in the world and is the key to every ProjectE item.
   > Chemistry: alchemists spent centuries looking for a stone that turns lead into gold. Real transmutation needs a nuclear reaction, and you've already done that: it's how you made oganesson.
   > How: redstone dust and glowstone dust in a ring around one oganesson (this pack's recipe).
   > Tip: it isn't used up in crafting recipes, so one stone lasts forever.
2. **World Transmutation**: checkmark *(after: The Philosopher's Stone)*
   > What: right-click a block with the stone to turn it into a related block: stone and cobblestone, dirt, grass and sand, one wood or flower type into the next.
   > How: an outline shows what will change before you click; sneak-click for the reverse direction. ProjectE's keybinds change the area size and shape.
   > Tip: a whole hillside of stone into cobblestone (or back) takes seconds. Click the checkmark once you've tried it.
3. **Transmutation Table**: `projecte:transmutation_table` *(after: The Philosopher's Stone)*
   > What: the Transmutation Table turns items into EMC and EMC back into any item you've learned.
   > How: four obsidian in the corners, four stone on the sides, the Philosopher's Stone in the centre.
   > Tip: your EMC and your learned items belong to you, not the table: every table you open shows the same list.
4. **Burn to Learn**: checkmark *(after: Transmutation Table)*
   > What: placing an item in the table's burn slot destroys it, adds its EMC to your total and teaches you that item.
   > How: burn a stack of something cheap (cobblestone, logs, sand), then try to burn an iron ingot. The ingot has no EMC, so it can't be learned.
   > Tip: stone, wood, glass, terracotta, wool and other building materials all work. Click the checkmark when you understand the rule.
5. **Covalence Dust**: 8x `projecte:low_covalence_dust`; 8x `projecte:medium_covalence_dust`; 8x `projecte:high_covalence_dust` *(after: The Philosopher's Stone)*
   > What: three dusts used for ProjectE storage and repairs.
   > Chemistry: a covalent bond is two atoms sharing electrons. The name fits: these dusts bind items together.
   > How: low: charcoal and 8 cobblestone. Medium: an iron ingot and redstone. High: a diamond and coal. Each recipe makes 40.
   > Tip: covalence dust repairs tools in a crafting grid: the matching dust for the tool's material.
6. **Alchemical Chest**: `projecte:alchemical_chest` *(after: Covalence Dust)*
   > What: a large chest, and the base of the Alchemical Bag.
   > How: one of each covalence dust on top, stone, a diamond and stone in the middle, iron, a chest and iron on the bottom.
7. **Alchemical Bag**: 1x any of `or(item(projecte:white_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:orange_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:magenta_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:light_blue_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:yellow_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:lime_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:pink_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:gray_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:light_gray_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:cyan_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:purple_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:blue_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:brown_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:green_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:red_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:black_alchemical_bag))` *(after: Alchemical Chest)*
   > What: an Alchemical Bag shares its inventory with every bag of the same colour you own.
   > How: three high covalence dust on top, wool on each side of an Alchemical Chest, and three wool below. Dye the wool for a different colour.
   > Tip: keep one colour for building blocks so your supplies follow you between builds.
8. **Repair Talisman**: `projecte:repair_talisman` *(after: Covalence Dust)*
   > What: while it's in your inventory it slowly repairs your damaged tools and armor.
   > How: covalence dusts, string and paper (check JEI for the pattern).
9. **Transmutation Tablet**: `projecte:transmutation_tablet` *(after: Transmutation Table, Dark Matter)*
   > What: a portable Transmutation Table.
   > How: four Dark Matter blocks, four stone and a Transmutation Table. That's sixteen Dark Matter: a real project.
   > Tip: worth it for big builds far from home.
10. **The Law of Conservation**: checkmark *(after: The Philosopher's Stone)*
   > What: in this pack, EMC works on building blocks only. Metals, gems, dusts, ores and plates have no EMC.
   > How: read the second page, then click the checkmark.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > The rule: ProjectE normally gives every item an EMC value, so a pile of cobblestone can become diamonds. In a chemistry pack that would skip everything you've built.
   > Chemistry: matter isn't created or destroyed in a chemical reaction (Lavoisier, 1789). Iron comes from iron oxide, Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂. Copper comes from its ores. Gold comes from anode sludge and aqua regia. You can rearrange atoms; you can't conjure them.
   > So: ingots, nuggets, raw ores, dusts, gems, plates, gears, rods, wires and storage blocks are set to EMC 0. Nether Stars, the Dragon Egg and the Beacon are 0 too, because the Seed of a New World needs them.
   > Also removed: Energy Condensers, Collectors and Relays. They turn EMC into unlimited items or power.
   > What's left: a terraforming and building tool. Stone, wood, glass, sand, dirt and decoration are what a demigod reshapes the world with, and those still have EMC.
11. **Alchemical Coal**: 4x `projecte:alchemical_coal` *(after: The Philosopher's Stone)*
   > What: a dense fuel and the first step toward Dark Matter.
   > Chemistry: coal is mostly carbon. Packing more energy into less mass is what refining fuel is all about.
   > How: the Philosopher's Stone and four coal (shapeless). It must be real coal, not charcoal.
   > Tip: it also burns far longer than coal in a furnace.
12. **Mobius Fuel**: 4x `projecte:mobius_fuel` *(after: Alchemical Coal)*
   > What: the next fuel tier.
   > How: the Philosopher's Stone and four alchemical coal. That's 16 coal per Mobius Fuel.
   > Tip: automate coal now (Create crushing, MI quarries or a coal farm); the next steps need a lot.
13. **Aeternalis Fuel**: 8x `projecte:aeternalis_fuel` *(after: Mobius Fuel)*
   > What: the top fuel, and the main ingredient of Dark Matter.
   > How: the Philosopher's Stone and four Mobius Fuel. Each one is 64 coal; this quest asks for eight (512 coal).
   > Tip: packaged autocrafting (PackagedAuto or AE2) can do the whole chain while you build.
14. **Dark Matter**: `projecte:dark_matter` *(after: Aeternalis Fuel)*
   > You remember materials no forge could make. This one you made from coal and patience.
   > What: Dark Matter is ProjectE's strongest crafting material: tools, armor and rings.
   > How: eight Aeternalis Fuel around a diamond block. The diamonds come from real mining or synthesis; EMC can't make them here.
   > Tip: four Dark Matter make a Dark Matter Block, used by the tablet and the Dark Matter Furnace.
15. **Dark Matter Tools**: 1x any of `or(item(projecte:dm_pick)item(projecte:dm_axe)item(projecte:dm_shovel)item(projecte:dm_sword)item(projecte:dm_hoe)item(projecte:dm_shears)item(projecte:dm_hammer))` *(after: Dark Matter)*
   > What: Dark Matter tools never break and dig very fast. Their charge key widens what they mine.
   > How: like diamond tools, but Dark Matter replaces the head and diamonds the handle (the pickaxe is 3 Dark Matter and 2 diamonds).
   > Tip: charge the Dark Matter Hammer to mine a wider area: great for clearing land.
16. **Dark Matter Armor**: `projecte:dm_helmet`; `projecte:dm_chestplate`; `projecte:dm_leggings`; `projecte:dm_boots` *(after: Dark Matter)*
   > What: very strong armor that doesn't wear out.
   > How: shaped like diamond armor, all Dark Matter: helmet 5, chestplate 8, leggings 7, boots 4.
   > Tip: that's 24 Dark Matter. Automate the fuel chain first.
17. **Black Hole Band**: `projecte:black_hole_band` *(after: Dark Matter)*
   > What: while active, it draws nearby items toward you.
   > How: an Iron Band (eight iron around a lava bucket) between two Dark Matter, with string above and below.
   > Tip: switch it off near your storage system.
18. **Red Matter**: `projecte:red_matter` *(after: Dark Matter)*
   > What: the strongest ProjectE material, for Red Matter tools and armor.
   > How: three Dark Matter in the middle row with three Aeternalis Fuel above and three below.
   > Tip: each one is three Dark Matter plus 384 coal of fuel. Only for the truly committed.
19. **Rapid Reorganisation**: `projecte:nova_catalyst` *(after: Mobius Fuel)*
   > You remember reshaping mountains. The quick way was never the tidy way.
   > What: a Nova Catalyst: TNT and Mobius Fuel. A much bigger blast.
   > Chemistry: TNT is trinitrotoluene, C₇H₅N₃O₆. It carries its own oxygen, which is why it burns so fast.
   > Tip: never near your base. Ever.

## Exploration

### Other Worlds

*The End, the Otherside and the Undergarden.*

1. **The End**: visit `minecraft:the_end` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > You remember the edge of the world. It's closer than it used to be.
   > What: the End holds the dragon, End Cities, shulkers and azure silver ore. End Crystals power Just Dire Things' flight upgrade.
   > How: throw eyes of ender to find a stronghold, fill the portal frame and jump in.
   > Tip: bring blocks, a bow and slow-falling potions. YUNG's Better Strongholds make the hunt more interesting.
2. **Slay the Dragon**: kill 1x `minecraft:ender_dragon` *(after: The End)*
   > What: the Ender Dragon guards the End's central island. Beating it opens the gateways to the outer islands.
   > How: shoot or climb to the End Crystals on the obsidian pillars and destroy them first (the caged ones need a climb), then fight the dragon when it perches on the portal.
   > Tip: stay out of its purple breath and never look an enderman in the eye mid-fight. A bow and a stack of arrows do most of the work.
3. **The Dragon's Breath**: 4x `minecraft:dragon_breath` *(after: Slay the Dragon)*
   > What: the dragon's purple breath can be bottled and makes lingering potions.
   > Chemistry: the Dissolver splits one bottle into 8 xenon and 8 radon, two heavy noble gases. It gives no oganesson in this pack: element 118 has never been found in nature, so here it only comes from the Fusion Chamber.
   > How: catch the purple breath cloud in glass bottles during the fight, or respawn the dragon for another go.
   > Tip: crystals respawn the dragon when placed on the exit portal, if you need it again.
4. **An End City**: find structure `minecraft:end_city` *(after: Slay the Dragon)*
   > What: End Cities are tall purpur towers on the outer islands, guarded by shulkers. Some have an End Ship moored alongside.
   > How: throw an ender pearl into an End Gateway near the main island, then search the outer islands. The Explorer's Compass can find one.
   > Tip: shulker bullets make you float; carry milk or slow falling.
5. **End City Loot**: `minecraft:elytra`; 4x `minecraft:shulker_shell` *(after: The Dragon's Breath, An End City)*
   > What: End Cities hold elytra (on the end ships) and shulkers whose shells make shulker boxes.
   > How: take an End Gateway from the main island, then search the outer islands for purple towers.
   > Tip: the Angel Ring needs an elytra; shulker shells feed Silent Gear's tyrian steel.
6. **Rocket Boost**: 32x `minecraft:firework_rocket` *(after: End City Loot)*
   > What: firework rockets boost elytra flight. Thirty-two is a good start for a long trip.
   > Chemistry: gunpowder is black powder: about 75% potassium nitrate (KNO₃, the oxidiser), 15% charcoal and 10% sulfur. The nitrate supplies its own oxygen, so it burns fast even in a sealed tube.
   > How: paper + gunpowder (1–3 for longer flight) in the crafting grid. Creepers and the hunting page give gunpowder.
   > Tip: rockets with a firework star explode and hurt you; use plain ones for flying.
7. **The Egg**: `minecraft:dragon_egg` *(after: Slay the Dragon)*
   > One egg, one dragon, one world. You remember having a whole shelf of these.
   > What: the dragon leaves a single egg on top of the exit portal the first time it dies.
   > Tip: it teleports when you hit it. Push it off with a piston, or let it fall onto a torch to pick it up.
8. **An Ancient City**: checkmark *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: Ancient Cities sit deep below the Overworld in the deep dark. Each one's centre holds the frame of a portal to the Otherside.
   > How: the Explorer's Compass can find one. Sneak everywhere: shriekers summon the Warden. Click the checkmark once you're inside.
   > Tip: sneaking never triggers sculk sensors, and walking on wool doesn't either.
9. **The Warden**: kill 1x `minecraft:warden` *(after: An Ancient City)*
   > What: the Warden is the strongest regular mob in the game, and the key to the Otherside: with Deeper and Darker it drops the Heart of the Deep.
   > How: trigger shriekers three times to summon one (or let it find you). Fight from range; it's blind and tracks you by sound and smell.
   > Tip: its sonic boom goes through shields and armour. Break line of sight when it starts charging.
10. **The Otherside**: `deeperdarker:heart_of_the_deep`; visit `deeperdarker:otherside` *(after: The Warden)*
   > You remember a silence older than the world. You can hear it again.
   > What: beyond the Ancient City lies the Otherside, a dark dimension of sculk and echo trees.
   > How: defeat a Warden for its Heart of the Deep, then use it to light the portal frame in the city's centre.
   > Tip: the Warden is blind but hears everything. Fight from range and keep moving.
11. **Echoes of the Deep**: 4x `deeperdarker:reinforced_echo_shard` *(after: The Otherside)*
   > What: reinforced echo shards make Warden gear that rivals netherite.
   > How: check JEI for the recipe; echo shards come from Ancient City chests and Otherside loot.
   > Tip: Warden armour is a netherite smithing upgrade, so keep your netherite gear.
12. **The Ancient Temple**: find structure `deeperdarker:ancient_temple` *(after: The Otherside)*
   > What: the Otherside's great structure: a sculk-choked temple with traps and the best loot in the dimension.
   > How: the Explorer's Compass points the way. Step inside.
   > Tip: the temple is full of sculk; sneak, as you did in the Ancient City.
13. **Biomes of the Otherside**: find biome `deeperdarker:echoing_forest`; find biome `deeperdarker:overcast_columns`; find biome `deeperdarker:blooming_caverns` *(after: The Otherside)*
   > What: the Otherside has its own biomes: echo-tree forests, towering columns and caverns lit by blooming plants.
   > Chemistry: there's no sunlight down here; real cave and deep-sea ecosystems run on chemosynthesis, where microbes get energy by oxidising H₂S or CH₄ instead of from light.
   > How: Nature's Compass works in the Otherside. Visit all three.
14. **Soul Elytra**: `deeperdarker:soul_elytra` *(after: The Otherside, End City Loot)*
   > What: an upgraded elytra that boosts itself, no rockets needed.
   > How: an elytra, sculk bones (from Shattered), a soul crystal (from Stalkers) and soul dust (check JEI).
   > Tip: Stalkers and Shattered roam the Otherside; fight them at range.
15. **Warden Armour**: `deeperdarker:warden_chestplate` *(after: Echoes of the Deep)*
   > What: Warden armour is tougher than netherite.
   > How: netherite chestplate + reinforced echo shard + Warden upgrade template in a smithing table.
   > Tip: check JEI for where the Warden upgrade template comes from.
16. **Undergarden Metals**: 8x `undergarden:cloggrum_ingot`; 4x `undergarden:froststeel_ingot` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: new ores beneath the world: cloggrum (tough) and froststeel (slows what it hits). Utherium comes much later.
   > How: mine them in depthrock and shiverstone, then smelt. Utherium only grows deep in tremblecrust and dreadrock, and its clusters need the Infuser: see the Undergarden page.
   > Tip: run them through the Alchemistry Dissolver: what are these strange metals made of?
17. **Regalium**: 4x `undergarden:regalium_crystal` *(after: Undergarden Metals)*
   > What: regalium is the Undergarden's treasure: a rare crystal in depthrock and shiverstone.
   > How: smelt regalium ore. It also turns up in catacomb chests.
   > Tip: catacombs are also where the Forgotten Guardian waits.
18. **The Catacombs**: find structure `undergarden:catacombs`; kill 1x `undergarden:forgotten_guardian` *(after: Regalium)*
   > What: the catacombs are a buried tomb of the Undergarden's old builders. The Forgotten Guardian, a hulking armoured giant, still stands watch.
   > How: the Explorer's Compass can find one. Clear the halls, then fight the guardian.
   > Tip: it's slow; hit it, step back out of its swing, and repeat.
19. **The Forgotten Ingot**: `undergarden:forgotten_ingot` *(after: The Catacombs)*
   > You remember the old guardians and the oaths they swore. This one has forgotten its own.
   > What: the Forgotten Guardian drops forgotten nuggets; nine make a Forgotten Ingot for the strongest Undergarden tools.
   > How: find a catacomb, beat the guardian, and craft the nuggets into an ingot. The smithing template is in catacomb chests.
   > Tip: it hits hard; armour up and keep your distance between swings.
20. **Ruins and Camps**: find structure `undergarden:forgotten_vestige`; find structure `undergarden:denizen_camp` *(after: Undergarden Metals)*
   > What: forgotten vestiges are ruins left by the Undergarden's builders; denizen camps belong to the hostile Denizens who live there now.
   > How: explore until you find one of each (the Explorer's Compass helps) and step inside.
   > Tip: Denizens fight in groups; draw them out one at a time.
21. **Biomes Below**: find biome `undergarden:forgotten_field`; find biome `undergarden:frostfields`; find biome `undergarden:smog_spires` *(after: Undergarden Metals)*
   > What: the Undergarden's biomes range from frozen fields to spires that belch smog.
   > Chemistry: a smog is a mix of smoke and fog; real industrial smog is soot plus sulfur dioxide (SO₂), which forms sulfuric acid droplets in damp air.
   > How: Nature's Compass works here too. Visit all three.

### Exploration

*Go and see what the world has made without you.*

1. **A Plains Village**: find structure `minecraft:village_plains` *(after: Iron)*
   > You remember knowing every corner of this world by heart. For now, a compass will do.
   > What: villagers trade emeralds for crops, tools and enchanted books, and their beds and fields are free for the taking (politely).
   > How: plains villages generate in plains and a few grassy modded biomes. Walk into one. Nature's Compass and Explorer's Compass (the Find Anything quest, linked on the left) point you to any biome or structure on this page.
   > Tip: Towns and Towers adds a village style for most biomes (the optional villages next to this one), and villages often have a waystone. A cartographer villager sells maps to ocean monuments and woodland mansions.
2. **A Forest Village**: find structure `towns_and_towers:village_forest` *(after: A Plains Village)*
   > What: Towns and Towers builds a village style for each biome. The forest village is timber and cobblestone.
   > How: find one in a forest biome (Explorer's Compass: Towns and Towers) and walk in.
   > Tip: each biome style has its own loot chests.
3. **A Meadow Village**: find structure `towns_and_towers:village_meadow` *(after: A Plains Village)*
   > What: high meadows below the peaks get their own village style.
   > How: find a meadow biome on a mountainside and the village in it.
   > Tip: meadows are where bees and wildflowers are thickest.
4. **A Snowy Taiga Village**: find structure `towns_and_towers:village_snowy_taiga` *(after: A Plains Village)*
   > What: a village built for the cold, in the snowy taiga.
   > How: find a snowy taiga and the village in it.
   > Tip: bring leather boots for powder snow.
5. **A Swamp Village**: find structure `towns_and_towers:village_swamp` *(after: A Plains Village)*
   > What: vanilla never put villages in swamps. Towns and Towers does.
   > How: find a swamp and the village in it.
   > Tip: witches love swamps too; keep a milk bucket handy.
6. **A Desert Village**: find structure `minecraft:village_desert` *(after: A Plains Village)*
   > What: a sandstone village in the desert.
   > Chemistry: sandstone is sand grains (mostly quartz, SiO₂) cemented by minerals like calcite or iron oxides that precipitated from groundwater.
   > How: find a desert village (Explorer's Compass) and walk in.
7. **A Pillager Outpost**: find structure `towns_and_towers:pillager_outpost_forest` *(after: A Plains Village)*
   > What: pillagers build watchtowers. Towns and Towers gives each biome its own design.
   > How: find a forest outpost and walk in. Expect crossbow fire.
   > Tip: killing a pillager captain gives Bad Omen; in 1.21 you drink the ominous bottle it drops to start a raid.
8. **A Woodland Mansion**: find structure `minecraft:mansion` *(after: A Pillager Outpost)*
   > What: huge dark-oak mansions, very rare, deep in dark forests. Vindicators and evokers live inside.
   > How: a cartographer's woodland explorer map or the Explorer's Compass. Step inside.
   > Tip: evokers drop totems of undying; vindicators hit very hard.
9. **Better Dungeons**: checkmark *(after: Iron)*
   > What: YUNG's Better Dungeons adds catacombs, fortresses and spider caves underground.
   > How: find one (the Explorer's Compass lists them), clear it and loot it. Click the checkmark when done.
   > Tip: some dungeon chests hold Relics and Artifacts items.
10. **Zombie Catacombs**: find structure `betterdungeons:zombie_dungeon` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: YUNG's zombie dungeon: a tomb with spawners, coffins and loot.
   > How: find it with the Explorer's Compass (Better Dungeons) and step inside.
   > Tip: break or torch the spawners first; then loot at your leisure.
11. **Skeleton Fortress**: find structure `betterdungeons:skeleton_dungeon` *(after: Zombie Catacombs)*
   > What: YUNG's skeleton dungeon is a sprawling underground fort.
   > How: find it and step inside. Bring a shield.
   > Tip: torches on every spawner; skeletons will pick you off from the dark otherwise.
12. **Spider Caves**: find structure `betterdungeons:spider_dungeon` *(after: Skeleton Fortress)*
   > What: a natural-looking cave full of webs, cave spiders and their spawners.
   > Chemistry: real spider silk is a protein (spidroin) with crystalline β-sheets that make it, weight for weight, stronger than steel.
   > How: find one and step inside. A sword or shears cut webs fast.
   > Tip: cave spiders poison; carry milk.
13. **A Better Stronghold**: find structure `betterstrongholds:stronghold` *(after: Spider Caves)*
   > What: YUNG's Better Strongholds replaces the vanilla stronghold with a much larger, trapped maze. The End portal room is inside.
   > How: throw eyes of ender, or use the Explorer's Compass. Step inside.
   > Tip: mark your path with torches on one side; the halls all look alike.
14. **Better Mineshafts**: checkmark *(after: Iron)*
   > What: YUNG's Better Mineshafts are longer, with ore deposits, carts and loot.
   > How: explore one and loot a chest. Click the checkmark when done.
   > Tip: look for minecarts with chests along the tracks.
15. **An Old Mineshaft**: find structure `bettermineshafts:mineshaft_oak` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: YUNG's mineshafts come in styles for each biome. The oak style is the common one.
   > How: find one under a forest or plains (Explorer's Compass) and walk in.
   > Tip: the rails and planks are free building material.
16. **Mineshafts of the Caves**: find structure `bettermineshafts:mineshaft_dripstone`; find structure `bettermineshafts:mineshaft_lush` *(after: An Old Mineshaft)*
   > What: two mineshafts built into cave biomes: one among dripstone, one among moss and glow berries.
   > Chemistry: dripstone is calcium carbonate: water carrying dissolved Ca(HCO₃)₂ drips, loses CO₂, and leaves CaCO₃ behind, a millimetre at a time.
   > How: find a mineshaft under dripstone caves and one under lush caves.
17. **Trail Ruins**: find structure `minecraft:trail_ruins`; `minecraft:brush` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: half-buried ruins of an old people. Suspicious gravel hides pottery sherds and armour trims.
   > How: find the ruins (Explorer's Compass) and bring a brush (feather, copper ingot, stick).
   > Tip: brush slowly; breaking suspicious blocks destroys the loot.
18. **Trial Chambers**: find structure `minecraft:trial_chambers`; `minecraft:trial_key` *(after: A Better Stronghold)*
   > What: copper and tuff vaults deep underground. Trial spawners give keys; keys open vaults.
   > Chemistry: the halls show copper's patina: Cu weathers to green basic copper carbonate, Cu₂CO₃(OH)₂, unless you wax it.
   > How: find a chamber, beat a trial spawner's wave and take the key.
   > Tip: breezes deflect arrows; fight them up close.
19. **Temples**: find structure `minecraft:desert_pyramid`; find structure `minecraft:jungle_pyramid` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: a desert pyramid and a jungle temple, each with treasure and a trap.
   > Chemistry: the desert trap is TNT: trinitrotoluene, C₇H₅N₃O₆, which carries its oxygen inside the molecule.
   > How: find one of each. Don't stand on the pressure plate in the desert.
20. **Odd Little Houses**: find structure `minecraft:swamp_hut`; find structure `minecraft:igloo` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: a witch's hut in the swamp and an igloo on the snow. Some igloos hide a basement.
   > How: find one of each and step inside.
   > Tip: the igloo basement has a brewing stand and a golden apple for curing a zombie villager.
21. **A Ruined Portal**: find structure `minecraft:ruined_portal` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: broken Nether portals, with crying obsidian and a chest of gold.
   > Chemistry: obsidian forms when lava (molten silicate) cools so fast it can't crystallise: it's volcanic glass.
   > How: find one and stand inside it. Fill the missing blocks to repair the portal.
22. **A Shipwreck**: find structure `minecraft:shipwreck` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: sunken ships with supply, treasure and map chests. The map leads to buried treasure.
   > How: find a wreck (Explorer's Compass) and swim inside.
   > Tip: a potion of water breathing or a turtle shell helmet makes this easy.
23. **Buried Treasure**: find structure `minecraft:buried_treasure`; `minecraft:heart_of_the_sea` *(after: A Shipwreck)*
   > What: buried chests on beaches, each with a Heart of the Sea for a conduit.
   > How: follow a shipwreck's treasure map to the X and dig down.
   > Tip: the chest is usually right under the X, a few blocks down.
24. **Ocean Ruins**: find structure `minecraft:ocean_ruin_warm`; find structure `minecraft:ocean_ruin_cold` *(after: A Shipwreck)*
   > What: ruins on the sea floor: sandstone ones in warm water, stone bricks in cold.
   > Chemistry: warm-water coral reefs are calcium carbonate skeletons; more dissolved CO₂ makes seawater more acidic and dissolves them.
   > How: find one of each. Drowned guard them.
25. **Wreckage**: find structure `towns_and_towers:wreckage_ocean` *(after: A Shipwreck)*
   > What: Towns and Towers scatters its own wreckage across the oceans.
   > How: find it with the Explorer's Compass (Towns and Towers) and swim in.
   > Tip: boats are faster than swimming between ocean structures.
26. **An Ocean Monument**: find structure `minecraft:monument`; 4x `minecraft:wet_sponge` *(after: Buried Treasure)*
   > What: a prismarine temple guarded by guardians and three elder guardians. Its sponge rooms and gold block vault are the prize.
   > Chemistry: a sponge holds water by capillary action in its pores; dry it in a furnace to drive the water off.
   > How: find it with a cartographer's map or the Explorer's Compass. Bring water breathing and Respiration.
   > Tip: elder guardians give Mining Fatigue; kill all three to lift it (see the hunting page).
27. **A Nether Fortress**: find structure `minecraft:fortress` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: dark nether-brick bridges and halls. Blazes give blaze rods; wither skeletons drop skulls for the Wither.
   > How: fortresses run in long lines across the Nether; the Explorer's Compass finds them quickly.
   > Tip: nether wart grows in the fortress stairwells; take some for brewing.
28. **A Bastion Remnant**: find structure `minecraft:bastion_remnant` *(after: A Nether Fortress)*
   > What: blackstone castles full of piglins and gold. Some hide netherite upgrade templates and ancient debris.
   > Chemistry: gold doesn't tarnish because it's the least reactive metal: it won't oxidise in air, even at high temperatures.
   > How: wear one piece of gold armour so piglins stay calm, then step inside.
   > Tip: opening chests angers piglins anyway; piglin brutes ignore gold entirely.
29. **Nether Fossils**: find structure `minecraft:nether_fossil` *(after: A Nether Fortress)*
   > What: giant bone fossils in the soul sand valleys.
   > Chemistry: bone is mostly hydroxyapatite, Ca₅(PO₄)₃(OH): a calcium phosphate mineral, the same family as phosphate rock for fertiliser.
   > How: find a soul sand valley and walk into one of the bone arches.
30. **A Nether Dungeon**: find structure `betterdungeons:small_nether_dungeon` *(after: A Nether Fortress)*
   > What: Better Dungeons adds small dungeons to the Nether too, with spawners and loot.
   > How: find one with the Explorer's Compass and step inside.
   > Tip: fire resistance first; everything here burns.
31. **Ruins in the Fire**: find structure `minecraft:ruined_portal_nether` *(after: A Bastion Remnant)*
   > What: ruined portals turn up in the Nether as well, with the same gold chest.
   > How: find one in the Nether and stand inside it.
   > Tip: crying obsidian makes respawn anchors, which let you respawn in the Nether.
32. **Erupting Inferno**: find biome `biomesoplenty:erupting_inferno` *(after: A Bastion Remnant)*
   > What: a Nether biome of lava, ash and erupting vents.
   > Chemistry: volcanic gas is mostly water vapour, CO₂ and SO₂; the SO₂ is what makes volcanic air sting.
   > How: Nature's Compass finds it. Fire resistance is a must.
33. **Cliffs of Chalk**: find biome `regions_unexplored:chalk_cliffs`; find biome `regions_unexplored:towering_cliffs` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: two Regions Unexplored cliff biomes: white chalk and towering stone.
   > Chemistry: chalk is calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) made of the shells of tiny sea plankton. Heat it and it gives quicklime: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂.
   > How: Nature's Compass finds each one. Visit both.
34. **Hot Ground**: find biome `biomesoplenty:hot_springs`; find biome `biomesoplenty:volcanic_plains` *(after: Cliffs of Chalk)*
   > What: two Biomes O' Plenty biomes warmed from below.
   > Chemistry: hot springs carry dissolved minerals; when the water cools at the surface, silica and carbonates precipitate as terraces.
   > How: visit both (Nature's Compass).
35. **Wetlands**: find biome `biomesoplenty:bog`; find biome `biomesoplenty:marsh`; find biome `regions_unexplored:fen` *(after: Hot Ground)*
   > What: three kinds of wetland from the two biome mods.
   > Chemistry: waterlogged peat has almost no oxygen, so it barely rots; microbes there make methane (CH₄), the original "marsh gas".
   > How: visit all three. Bring a boat.
36. **Caves That Glow**: find biome `regions_unexplored:redstone_caves`; find biome `regions_unexplored:bioshroom_caves`; find biome `biomesoplenty:glowing_grotto` *(after: Wetlands)*
   > What: cave biomes lit by redstone, giant glowing mushrooms and glowing fungi.
   > Chemistry: real glowing fungi use the same chemistry as fireflies: luciferin oxidised by O₂ with the help of an enzyme, luciferase.
   > How: these are underground; Nature's Compass gives the location, then dig down.
37. **Useful Forests**: find biome `biomesoplenty:maple_woods`; find biome `regions_unexplored:eucalyptus_forest`; find biome `biomesoplenty:orchard` *(after: Cliffs of Chalk)*
   > What: three forests whose real trees give us chemicals.
   > Chemistry: maple sap is about 2% sucrose (C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁), boiled down 40:1 into syrup. Eucalyptus oil is mostly eucalyptol (C₁₀H₁₈O).
   > How: visit all three.
38. **Dry Country**: find biome `regions_unexplored:joshua_desert`; find biome `regions_unexplored:saguaro_desert`; find biome `regions_unexplored:outback` *(after: Hot Ground)*
   > What: Joshua trees, saguaro cacti and the red outback.
   > Chemistry: red desert soil is coloured by a thin coat of iron(III) oxide, Fe₂O₃, on every grain: the same rust that colours Mars.
   > How: visit all three. Carry water.
39. **Cold Places**: find biome `biomesoplenty:tundra`; find biome `regions_unexplored:icy_heights`; find biome `biomesoplenty:snowblossom_grove` *(after: Wetlands)*
   > What: three cold biomes from the biome mods.
   > Chemistry: ice floats because water expands about 9% when it freezes: hydrogen bonds lock the molecules into an open hexagonal lattice.
   > How: visit all three. Warm clothes not required, but recommended.
40. **Colour Fields**: find biome `regions_unexplored:poppy_fields`; find biome `biomesoplenty:jacaranda_glade`; find biome `regions_unexplored:wisteria_grove` *(after: Caves That Glow)*
   > What: biomes full of flowers: poppies, jacarandas and wisteria.
   > Chemistry: most red, purple and blue petals owe their colour to anthocyanins, pigments that change colour with pH (red in acid, blue in base).
   > How: visit all three. Collect the flowers for dyes.
41. **Strange Heights**: find biome `regions_unexplored:spires`; find biome `biomesoplenty:crag` *(after: Caves That Glow)*
   > What: tall rock spires and broken crags: two of the most dramatic landscapes in the pack.
   > Chemistry: rock spires are what's left when softer rock around them is weathered away by water, frost and slow acid rain (H₂CO₃ from dissolved CO₂).
   > How: visit both. Bring a water bucket for the way down.
42. **Dead Lands**: find biome `biomesoplenty:wasteland`; find biome `biomesoplenty:dead_forest` *(after: Caves That Glow)*
   > What: cracked wasteland and grey dead forest.
   > Chemistry: soil dies when it loses organic matter and nitrogen; your Haber-Bosch ammonia (N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃) is how real farms put nitrogen back.
   > How: visit both. A demigod might one day make them green again.
43. **The Origin Valley**: find biome `biomesoplenty:origin_valley` *(after: Strange Heights)*
   > Blocky trees, bright grass, a sky of old. You remember the world looking exactly like this, once.
   > What: a rare Biomes O' Plenty biome styled after Minecraft's earliest days.
   > Tip: there's a snowy version too, the wintry origin valley.

### The Undergarden

*A forgotten land under the world, opened with acid.*

1. **Depthrock**: 32x `undergarden:depthrock` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > Acid opened the way, and the dark below remembers you. You were the one who sealed it.
   > What: depthrock is the Undergarden's stone, the way deepslate is the Overworld's. Its ores (cloggrum, froststeel, utherium, regalium) all sit in it or in icy shiverstone.
   > Chemistry: dissolve depthrock in the Alchemistry Dissolver and it gives silicon dioxide (SiO₂), iron and aluminium, with rare traces of zirconium, gallium, dysprosium and tungsten.
   > How: the catalyst is copper ingots, stone, an ender pearl and a bucket of sulfuric acid (MI, Mekanism or ChemLib; this pack's recipe). Light the stone-brick frame and step through, then mine.
   > Tip: the Undergarden has no sun. Bring a stack of torches and mark your portal.
2. **Cloggrum Tools**: `undergarden:cloggrum_pickaxe`; `undergarden:cloggrum_sword` *(after: Depthrock)*
   > What: cloggrum is the first Undergarden metal: about as good as iron, and the base for every Forgotten tool later.
   > How: mine cloggrum ore (stone pickaxe or better), smelt the raw cloggrum, and craft tools as you would iron ones.
   > Tip: keep the cloggrum sword and pickaxe once you replace them: they're what the Forgotten template upgrades.
3. **Cloggrum Armour**: `undergarden:cloggrum_helmet`; `undergarden:cloggrum_chestplate`; `undergarden:cloggrum_leggings`; `undergarden:cloggrum_boots` *(after: Cloggrum Tools)*
   > What: a full set of cloggrum armour. The boots have a perk: scintling goo no longer slows you.
   > How: 24 cloggrum ingots for the set. Raw cloggrum also turns up in depleted mines.
   > Tip: scintlings leave sticky goo trails across whole caverns; the boots pay for themselves fast.
4. **Forgotten Tools**: `undergarden:forgotten_pickaxe`; `undergarden:forgotten_sword` *(after: Cloggrum Armour)*
   > What: Forgotten tools mine Undergarden blocks 1.5x as fast, Forgotten weapons hit non-boss Undergarden mobs 1.5x as hard. Only a Forgotten pickaxe can break dreadrock.
   > How: smithing table: Forgotten upgrade template + cloggrum tool + Forgotten Ingot. Ingots come from the Forgotten Guardian in the catacombs (see the Other Worlds page); templates from catacomb chests.
   > Tip: copy a template with 7 diamonds and a block of depthrock (makes 2). Do it before you use your last one.
5. **The Depths**: find biome `undergarden:depths` *(after: Forgotten Tools)*
   > Under the forgotten land there is an older one. You remember the floor you laid over it.
   > What: a layer of dreadrock seals the bottom of the Undergarden. Below it lie the Depths: infected caverns, puff mushroom forests and rogdorium groves.
   > How: dig down until you hit dreadrock, then break through it with a Forgotten pickaxe. Nothing else can mine it.
   > Tip: the Depths carry the Utheric Infection. Read the rogdorium quest before you stay long.
6. **Rogdorium**: 8x `undergarden:rogdorium` *(after: The Depths)*
   > What: rogdorium is a crystal found only in dreadrock. It's the key to the Infuser, and eating it holds back the Utheric Infection.
   > Chemistry: real poisoning by heavy metals is treated much the same way: a chelating agent such as EDTA binds the toxic metal ions so the body can flush them out.
   > How: mine dreadrock rogdorium ore with a Forgotten pickaxe (it drops rogdorium) or smelt the ore block.
   > Tip: carry a few rogdorium nuggets on every trip down; eat one when the infection meter climbs.
7. **Utheric Clusters**: 4x `undergarden:utheric_cluster` *(after: The Depths)*
   > What: mined utherium ore gives utheric clusters: utherium still full of the infection. The Infuser needs one to be built, and purifies the rest.
   > Chemistry: most real ores come out of the ground impure too: the metal is locked in a compound with sulfur, oxygen or arsenic, and refining is the work of pulling it free.
   > How: utherium ore sits in depthrock, shiverstone, tremblecrust and the Depths' dreadrock. Mine or smelt it; nine utheric shards also make a cluster.
   > Tip: mine extra: every utherium crystal you will ever make starts as one of these.
8. **The Infuser**: `undergarden:infuser` *(after: Rogdorium, Utheric Clusters)*
   > What: the Undergarden's own processing block. With rogdorium fuel it purifies; with utherium it corrupts.
   > Chemistry: the idea is old: purification is often just a reaction that removes one impurity, the way a blast furnace strips oxygen from iron ore.
   > How: an utheric cluster, rogdorium and five dreadrock (check JEI). It also gives armour a Rogdorium Infusion.
   > Tip: JEI's Infusing category lists every conversion, including which fuel slot it needs.
9. **Purified Utherium**: 4x `undergarden:utherium_crystal` *(after: The Infuser)*
   > What: utherium crystal is the Undergarden's weapon against rotspawn. Mined utherium ore only gives raw utheric clusters.
   > How: mine or smelt utherium ore for clusters (9 utheric shards also make one), then purify each cluster in the Infuser with rogdorium.
   > Tip: rotbeasts and rotbelchers drop utheric shards, so hunting them feeds the line.
10. **Utherium Gear**: `undergarden:utherium_sword`; `undergarden:utherium_chestplate` *(after: Purified Utherium)*
   > Rot fears what is pure. You remember forging blades for exactly this.
   > What: utherium weapons deal 1.5x damage to rotspawn; the armour is the Undergarden's best plain set.
   > How: craft them from utherium crystals like diamond gear (check JEI).
   > Tip: a worn-out utherium tool smelts back into a crystal, so nothing is wasted.
11. **Slingshot**: `undergarden:slingshot`; 16x `undergarden:depthrock_pebble` *(after: Depthrock)*
   > What: a ranged weapon that fires pebbles, goo balls, gronglets or rotten blisterberries.
   > How: twistytwigs (two wigglewood planks make four) and sticks. Pebbles drop from mogs and stoneborn, or stonecut depthrock.
   > Tip: it takes its own enchantments: Ricochet bounces shots off walls, Self Sling launches you instead.
12. **Froststeel**: `undergarden:froststeel_sword`; `undergarden:froststeel_chestplate` *(after: Cloggrum Tools)*
   > What: froststeel weapons give targets the Chilly effect, which slows them.
   > Chemistry: real steel gets brittle in deep cold: below its ductile-to-brittle transition temperature it cracks instead of bending, which is why ships' hulls once split in icy seas.
   > How: froststeel ore only forms in shiverstone, in the frozen biomes. It needs an iron pickaxe; smelt the raw froststeel.
   > Tip: a froststeel sword is great against fast rotspawn; slowed foes can't close the gap.
13. **The Forgotten**: kill 5x `undergarden:forgotten`; `undergarden:cloggrum_battleaxe` *(after: Cloggrum Armour)*
   > What: the Forgotten are armoured undead that guard the catacombs and vestiges. Some carry a cloggrum battleaxe.
   > How: kill five Forgotten. The battleaxe can't be crafted: it only drops from a Forgotten carrying one.
   > Tip: they hit hard but slowly. Shield up, then strike.
14. **Forgotten Battleaxe**: `undergarden:forgotten_battleaxe` *(after: The Forgotten, Forgotten Tools)*
   > What: the cloggrum battleaxe, upgraded with Forgotten metal.
   > How: smithing table: Forgotten upgrade template + cloggrum battleaxe + Forgotten Ingot.
   > Tip: make all six Forgotten tools if you want the mod's own completion advancement.
15. **Rogdorium Spear**: `undergarden:spear` *(after: Rogdorium)*
   > What: a spear you can stab with or throw, like a trident without the water.
   > How: one rogdorium on top of two sticks.
   > Tip: retrieve it after every throw; it doesn't come back on its own.
16. **Two Kinds of Gronglet**: `undergarden:rogdoric_gronglet`; `undergarden:utheric_gronglet` *(after: The Infuser)*
   > What: gronglets are little glowing growths. The Infuser can purify one with rogdorium or corrupt one with utherium.
   > How: collect two wild gronglets, then run one through each Infuser mode (JEI shows both).
   > Tip: gronglets also work as slingshot ammo. The mod asks if that is okay.
17. **Collector's Shelf**: `undergarden:cloggrum_block`; `undergarden:froststeel_block`; `undergarden:utherium_block`; `undergarden:regalium_block`; `undergarden:rogdorium_block`; `undergarden:forgotten_block` *(after: Utherium Gear)*
   > What: one storage block each of cloggrum, froststeel, utherium, regalium, rogdorium and Forgotten metal.
   > Chemistry: feed spares to the Dissolver: the Undergarden's metals are fiction, but what they break down into tells you what the pack thinks they are made of.
   > How: nine of each ingot or crystal in a crafting grid.
   > Tip: a Forgotten block and a carved gloomgourd summon a Forgotten Minion.
18. **Cloggrum Kit**: `undergarden:cloggrum_axe`; `undergarden:cloggrum_shovel`; `undergarden:cloggrum_hoe`; `undergarden:cloggrum_shield` *(after: Cloggrum Tools)*
   > What: the rest of the cloggrum toolset, plus a cloggrum shield for the Forgotten's heavy swings.
   > Chemistry: a real shield works by spreading a blow over a large area: the same force over more area means less pressure (P = F / A) on your arm.
   > How: the usual tool shapes with cloggrum ingots; the shield is cloggrum and planks (check JEI).
   > Tip: the axe, shovel and hoe are the three the Forgotten template turns into the rest of the Forgotten set.
19. **Froststeel Tools**: `undergarden:froststeel_pickaxe`; `undergarden:froststeel_axe`; `undergarden:froststeel_shovel`; `undergarden:froststeel_hoe` *(after: Froststeel)*
   > What: pickaxe, axe, shovel and hoe of froststeel.
   > Chemistry: cold slows chemistry down: as a rule of thumb, many reactions run about half as fast for every 10 °C cooler. That's why a fridge keeps food.
   > How: froststeel ingots in the usual tool shapes (check JEI).
   > Tip: raw froststeel has a blast furnace recipe, so smelt it there at double speed.
20. **Froststeel Armour**: `undergarden:froststeel_helmet`; `undergarden:froststeel_leggings`; `undergarden:froststeel_boots` *(after: Froststeel)*
   > What: the rest of the froststeel armour to go with your chestplate.
   > How: froststeel ingots in the usual armour shapes (check JEI). Froststeel ore only forms in shiverstone, in the frozen biomes.
   > Tip: compare it with cloggrum in your inventory before you commit: pick the set whose perks suit how you fight.
21. **Forgotten Kit**: `undergarden:forgotten_axe`; `undergarden:forgotten_shovel`; `undergarden:forgotten_hoe` *(after: Forgotten Tools, Cloggrum Kit)*
   > What: Forgotten axe, shovel and hoe: the same 1.5x speed on Undergarden blocks as the pickaxe.
   > How: smithing table: Forgotten upgrade template + cloggrum tool + Forgotten Ingot, once for each.
   > Tip: with the pickaxe, sword and battleaxe that makes all six Forgotten tools, which the mod has an advancement for.
22. **Utherium Tools**: `undergarden:utherium_pickaxe`; `undergarden:utherium_axe`; `undergarden:utherium_shovel`; `undergarden:utherium_hoe` *(after: Utherium Gear)*
   > What: the rest of the utherium toolset.
   > How: utherium crystals in the usual tool shapes (check JEI).
   > Tip: a worn-out utherium tool smelts back into a crystal.
23. **Utherium Armour**: `undergarden:utherium_helmet`; `undergarden:utherium_leggings`; `undergarden:utherium_boots` *(after: Utherium Gear)*
   > What: helmet, leggings and boots of utherium to go with your chestplate: the Undergarden's best plain set.
   > Chemistry: a crystal's strength comes from its lattice: every atom held by bonds in every direction, which is why diamond (carbon in a 3D lattice) is so hard.
   > How: utherium crystals in the usual armour shapes (check JEI).
   > Tip: the Infuser can still give this armour a Rogdorium Infusion.
24. **Small Change**: 9x `undergarden:cloggrum_nugget`; 9x `undergarden:froststeel_nugget`; 9x `undergarden:forgotten_nugget` *(after: Forgotten Tools)*
   > What: nuggets of cloggrum, froststeel and Forgotten metal. Forgotten nuggets are how the guardian pays out: nine make an ingot.
   > Chemistry: real nuggets only form from unreactive metals. Gold turns up native in rivers because it doesn't oxidise; iron almost never does.
   > How: break an ingot into nine in the crafting grid; Forgotten nuggets drop from the Forgotten Guardian.
   > Tip: a Forgotten nugget is also the heart of the Crumbling Catalyst.
25. **Crumbling Catalyst**: `undergarden:crumbling_catalyst` *(after: Small Change)*
   > What: a cheaper, crumbling cousin of the Catalyst: it lights an Undergarden portal frame and is used up doing it.
   > Chemistry: the name is a joke for chemists: a true catalyst is never used up by the reaction it speeds. This one is a reagent wearing a catalyst's name.
   > How: four cloggrum ingots, four depthrock and one Forgotten nugget in the middle (check JEI).
   > Tip: use it for a second portal near another base, and keep the real Catalyst safe.
26. **Ancient Armour**: 1x any of `or(item(undergarden:ancient_helmet)item(undergarden:ancient_chestplate)item(undergarden:ancient_leggings))` *(after: The Forgotten)*
   > What: the Forgotten wear ancient armour. It has no recipe: the only way to get a piece is from a Forgotten when it falls.
   > How: keep fighting Forgotten in catacombs and vestiges. Drops are rare; Looting helps.
   > Tip: any one piece completes this quest.
27. **Mysterious Totem**: `undergarden:denizen_totem` *(after: The Infuser)*
   > What: a carved totem like the ones in denizen camps.
   > How: purify an ancient root in the Infuser with rogdorium, or loot one from a denizen camp chest.
   > Tip: it's an axe-mined block, so break and move it with an axe.
28. **Woods Without Sun**: 8x `undergarden:smogstem_log`; 8x `undergarden:wigglewood_log`; 8x `undergarden:grongle_log` *(after: Depthrock)*
   > What: three kinds of tree that grow with no daylight at all.
   > Chemistry: real plants can't do that: photosynthesis (6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂) needs light. Underground life runs on chemosynthesis or on food that falls from above.
   > How: smogstem forests, wigglewood forests and the gronglegrowth each have their own tree.
   > Tip: wigglewood planks make the twistytwigs for the slingshot.
29. **Shard Torches**: 8x `undergarden:shard_torch` *(after: Depthrock)*
   > What: a torch tipped with an utheric shard. It lights the dark and hurts rotspawn that come close.
   > How: one utheric shard on a stick. Shards drop from rotbeasts and rotbelchers and sit in catacomb chests.
   > Tip: ring your portal and your base with them.
30. **A Depleted Mine**: find structure `undergarden:depleted_mine` *(after: Depthrock)*
   > What: old mines left by the Undergarden's builders. The chests still hold raw cloggrum, raw froststeel and cloggrum tools.
   > How: explore depthrock caverns until you find timber supports and rails; step inside.
   > Tip: a quick way to an early cloggrum pickaxe.
31. **Mushroom Bogs**: find biome `undergarden:blood_mushroom_bog`; find biome `undergarden:ink_mushroom_bog`; find biome `undergarden:veil_mushroom_bog` *(after: Depthrock)*
   > What: three bogs named after the giant mushrooms that grow in them. Each mushroom makes its own stew and dye.
   > Chemistry: a fungus is closer to an animal than a plant: its cell walls are chitin, (C₈H₁₃O₅N)ₙ, the same polymer as insect shells.
   > How: Nature's Compass works down here. Visit all three.
32. **Into the Depths**: find biome `undergarden:infected_depths`; find biome `undergarden:puff_mushroom_forest`; find biome `undergarden:rogdorium_grove` *(after: The Depths)*
   > What: the rest of the Depths: the infected depths, the puff mushroom forest and the rogdorium grove.
   > How: with a Forgotten pickaxe, tunnel through dreadrock to each one.
   > Tip: the rogdorium grove is the richest place for rogdorium; carry plenty out.
33. **Saplings of the Dark**: `undergarden:smogstem_sapling`; `undergarden:wigglewood_sapling`; `undergarden:grongle_sapling` *(after: Woods Without Sun)*
   > What: a sapling of each Undergarden tree, so you can farm their wood without the trip.
   > How: break the leaves of smogstem, wigglewood and grongle trees until each drops a sapling.
   > Tip: wigglewood leaves also drop twistytwigs, the slingshot's frame.
34. **Four Mushrooms**: `undergarden:blood_mushroom`; `undergarden:indigo_mushroom`; `undergarden:ink_mushroom`; `undergarden:veil_mushroom` *(after: Depthrock)*
   > What: the four small mushrooms of the Undergarden, each the seed of its own stew and dye.
   > Chemistry: real ink caps (Coprinus) digest their own gills into a black liquid as they ripen, and people once wrote with it: the black comes from the ripe spores.
   > How: they grow on the ground in the bogs and forests; the mushroom bogs have the most.
   > Tip: keep a few of each for the four stews.
35. **Mogmoss**: 4x `undergarden:mogmoss`; 4x `undergarden:blue_mogmoss` *(after: Depthrock)*
   > What: mogs, the Undergarden's mossy burrowers, drop mogmoss; the smog mogs of the smog spires drop the blue kind.
   > How: find mogs digging in the depthrock forests and smog mogs in the smog spires. Mogmoss makes rugs and slop bowls.
   > Tip: mogs also drop depthrock pebbles for the slingshot.
36. **Gronglets**: 2x `undergarden:gronglet` *(after: Depthrock)*
   > What: small glowing growths that hang on grongle trees in the gronglegrowth. The Infuser can purify or corrupt them.
   > How: break a wild gronglet to pick it up.
   > Tip: keep two: the Infuser quest later wants one of each kind.
37. **Scintling Goo**: 8x `undergarden:goo_ball` *(after: Depthrock)*
   > What: goo balls, the sticky stuff scintlings leave behind. They work like slime balls: sticky pistons, leads and goo blocks.
   > Chemistry: slime is a hydrogel: long, tangled polymer chains (glycoproteins, in a real snail) holding many times their weight in water.
   > How: break the goo trail blocks scintlings leave across the caverns; each drops goo balls. No need to hurt the snail.
   > Tip: cloggrum boots stop goo from slowing you down.
